    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

succeeded
2 validated the spec and the data
3 split the data
4 fitted quantile model 1
5 persisting the fitted estimators
6 fitted on the training data
7 evaluated the holdout through the score path
8 fitted quantile model 1
9 persisting the fitted estimators
10 fit complete
{'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}

What to notice:

  • Payloads are JSON. The spec travels as YAML text or a dict, the raw schema as a dict, and data only as references. This is exactly what the API will store and what a sandboxed runner will receive.
  • Submissions are idempotent. Re-submitting with the same nonce returns the same handle, so a retried API call never starts a second fit. adopt(nonce) finds a run after a restart.
  • Status is the source of truth. Events are for progress bars; status() and wait() decide whether a run succeeded. Failures come back as RFC 7807 problems with a stable code.
  • Cancellation is cooperative. cancel(handle) is checked between pipeline phases and inside long fits.

docs.title: Isolation levels
docs.text:
Every executor declares how strongly it isolates a run, and the platform refuses to send untrusted code to an executor that is not strong enough.

Executor Isolation For Status InprocExecutor NONE Notebooks, tests, your own trusted code available Local process / Docker PROCESS / GVISOR Local platform, CI v0.2 Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) MICROVM Hosted runs, one fresh sandbox per run v0.3

Never run untrusted code in-process

The in-process executor runs plugins with your permissions in your interpreter. It is for code you wrote or trust. Public plugins only ever run in the sandboxed executors.

See the roadmap for the sandbox design.

docs.title: Your first model
docs.text:
In this walkthrough you fit a demand model for three stores and two products, forecast the next four weeks (including a store that has not opened yet) and see the errors that stop dishonest answers. Everything runs in a notebook cell by cell; the complete script is docs/snippets/quickstart.py and the test suite runs it on every change.

flowchart LR
    D["1. Labelled data<br/><code>xr.Dataset</code>"] --> S["2. Schema<br/>dims, roles, policies"]
    S --> P["3. Spec<br/>pipeline + model"]
    P --> V["4. Static check<br/>no data touched"]
    V --> F["5. Fit<br/>evaluate, then refit"]
    F --> SC["6. Score<br/>forecast, new store"]
    SC --> B["7. Bundle<br/>write, read, verify"]

docs.title: 1. Labelled data
docs.text:
Your data is an xr.Dataset: every variable has named dims and every dim has coordinates (labels). Nothing downstream depends on the order of stores or products.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

Coming from pandas?

A long DataFrame with one row per store, sku and week becomes this dataset with df.set_index(["store", "sku", "week"]).to_xarray().

docs.title: 2. Describe it with a schema
docs.text:
A DataSchema says what each dim is and what may happen to it when you score:

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)
Dim Policy At score time store new_levels (pooled) Unseen stores are allowed and get the pooled prediction sku fixed Only the fitted products; anything else is UNSEEN_LEVELS week extend New weeks must continue the fitted range without gaps

If you skip the schema, mapi_sdk.infer_schema(data, targets=[...]) drafts one: time dims become extend, everything else fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the spec
docs.text:
A ModelSpec names the dataset, binds your names to the model's canonical names, picks a train/holdout split, lists the preprocessing steps and chooses the model.

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")
  • bind maps canonical names (what steps and models use) onto your dataset's names. Outputs come back under your names.
  • core.calendar adds week-of-year features; core.log1p models log(1 + units) and is inverted automatically on the way out.
  • tabular.regressor is a built-in quantile model (xgboost underneath) whose rows are stacked from the labelled dims; store and sku become categorical features.

docs.title: 4. Check it before fitting
docs.text:
The same static check the API runs before accepting a job: no data is read, and it takes milliseconds.

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)

A typo in a variable name, a split on a dim that does not exist yet, or a stateful step before the split would be reported here, each with a stable code and a JSON pointer such as /pipeline/1/with/vars/0.

docs.title: 5. Fit
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

With the default fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, fit_spec:

  1. fits every stateful step and the model on the first 44 weeks;
  2. scores the last 8 weeks through the score path, exactly like a forecast, and computes rmse, mape and coverage_80 in units sold (the log1p is undone);
  3. refits on all 52 weeks, so a forecast starts from the latest data, and links the evaluation fit in the bundle.

docs.title: 6. Forecast, including a new store
docs.text:
Supply the plan for the next four weeks: prices and promotions are future_required, the target is not needed. west has never been seen.

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

The result is an xr.DataTree. summary holds the statistics you asked for along a stat dim, with your dim names restored. Its attributes tell you how to read it:

Attribute Value here Meaning representation quantiles Per-cell quantiles: you can read them, not add them up output_space {"y_hat": "raw"} Inverted through every value step back to the raw data's space issues UNSEEN_LEVELS (info) west was scored with the pooled strategy

docs.title: 7. The errors that protect you
docs.text:
These requests fail before any model code runs, each with a stable code:

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))

MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE - forecasting needs future values of ['promo'] at stage 'raw'
CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED - cannot aggregate 'quantiles' output: Quantiles are marginal per cell; summing quantiles is not a quantile of the sum.
UNSEEN_LEVELS - 1 level(s) of 'sku' were not seen at fit and the dim's policy is 'fixed'

So how do I get a total over stores?

Use a model whose representation supports it. sklearn.tabular_bootstrap returns joint draws, which can be summed per draw, and Bayesian models return posterior draws. See Representations.

docs.title: 8. Save and reload the bundle
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

A bundle holds the spec, the binding, every step's state and context tail, the model's fitted groups and native artifacts (here: the xgboost model as JSON), and a manifest with the size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of every file. Nothing is pickled. See Bundles.

docs.title: The whole script
docs.text:
docs/snippets/quickstart.py 
"""Getting started: fit and score a labelled demand model in a notebook.

Every section between ``--8<--`` markers is included verbatim in the docs, and
``conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py`` runs this file top to bottom.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)
assert check.ok, check.errors

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks
assert set(bundle.metrics.values) == {"rmse", "mape", "coverage_80"}
assert bundle.metrics.n_holdout == 48

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'
assert set(summary["store"].values) == {"north", "south", "east", "west"}
assert summary.sizes["week"] == 4

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))
assert code_1 is ErrorCode.MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE
assert code_2 is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED
assert code_3 is ErrorCode.UNSEEN_LEVELS

from mapi_sdk import CoordPlan
from mapi_spec import load_score_request, validate_score_request

# What the API stores next to a model version: JSON only, no arrays, no plugin code.
meta = CoordPlan(load_score_request(FORECAST), bundle.resolved, bundle.fit_coords).metadata()
print(f"{len(meta.model_dump_json()) / 1024:.0f} KiB of metadata")

request = load_score_request(FORECAST + "output: {summary: [hdi_90], draws: 100}\n")
for issue in validate_score_request(request, meta):  # no data, no model: milliseconds
    print(issue.code, issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE /data - forecasting needs future values of ['price', 'promo'] ...
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/draws - draws were requested but the model's
#                                        representation is 'quantiles'
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/summary/0 - summary 'hdi_90' cannot be computed from
#                                            'quantiles' output
assert any(
    i.code is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED for i in validate_score_request(request, meta)
)

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

print(manifest.role, manifest.plugin["id"], manifest.spec_hash[:19])
# production tabular.regressor sha256:...
print(manifest.files["bundle.zarr.zip"])  # size, crc32c, md5 (GCS forms) and sha256
print(manifest.lineage["evaluation_bundle"])  # the train-only fit behind the metrics

tree = again.to_tree()  # the whole bundle as one xr.DataTree
print(sorted(tree.children))
# ['binding', 'fit_coords', 'model', 'native', 'preprocess', 'schema', 'spec']
print(sorted(tree["preprocess"].children))  # ['cal', 'logy']: one node per step
assert {"model", "preprocess", "native", "spec"} <= set(tree.children)

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Run the same fit and score as runs through an executor: Runs and executors.
  • Learn why the split happened where it did: Pipelines and stages.
  • Try a Bayesian model: the radon model or the marketing-mix model.

docs.title: Quickstart: zero to first model in 10 minutes v0.2
docs.text:
You will start the platform on your own machine, load a demo dataset, fit a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model from the web app, read its scorecard and plots, and score an 8-week forecast. No Docker and no cloud account are needed: PostgreSQL is embedded and object storage is a local emulator of Google Cloud Storage.

Step What happens Time on a laptop 1. Install Python and JavaScript dependencies 2–5 min the first time 2. Start the stack Database, object store, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox about 10 s 3. Load the demo Three datasets and a model spec, through the API about 40 s 4. Fit from the browser A sandboxed fit run, followed live 20–60 s 5. Inspect Scorecard, diagnostics, plots, provenance – 6. Score An 8-week forecast with the fitted preprocessing replayed about 10 s

We ran exactly these steps on a fresh clone while writing this page: from make dev to a scored forecast took under three minutes. The screenshots below come from that run.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• macOS or Linux, about 2 GB of free disk space;
  • uv (it installs Python 3.12 for you if needed);
  • Node.js 22 or newer with pnpm (corepack enable provides the pinned pnpm version);
  • git, and jq and curl if you want to follow the HTTP examples later.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url> modeling-api
cd modeling-api
make install          # uv sync --all-packages, then pnpm install

make install puts every Python package of the workspace into .venv and the web app's dependencies into node_modules. Nothing is installed globally.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
make dev

make dev runs every service in the foreground, each output line prefixed with its name, and prints all 6 services up when it is ready. Leave it running; Ctrl+C stops everything. The first start also queues a sandboxed describe run that exports the catalog of installed models and steps; it finishes in a few seconds.

Service Address Web app http://127.0.0.1:5173 API http://127.0.0.1:8000 (OpenAPI document at /openapi.json) Plot sandbox (a separate origin, on purpose) http://127.0.0.1:5174 GCS shim (signed URLs point here) http://127.0.0.1:4443

Port 8000 (or any other) already taken?

Export the matching variable before make dev, and in every other shell you use:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174

make dev, make seed, the CLI, the Python client and the web app all read the same variables. This page was produced on exactly these ports. Troubleshooting has more.

docs.title: 3. Load the demo
docs.text:
In a second shell:

make seed

API http://127.0.0.1:8000 is ok (version 0.4.0)
uploading eu_media_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v1 ready
uploading fx_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/fx_daily@v1 ready
uploading holidays_eu (7 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/holidays_eu@v1 ready
spec spec://default/eu-geo-mmm@r1: valid

make seed talks to the public API only. For each table it asks for a signed upload URL, sends the file straight to object storage, and starts a sandboxed ingest run that opens the file, checks it against its schema and stores an immutable, content-addressed version. Then it saves the model spec and validates it.

The data is the conformance corpus' E33 example: 30 weeks of daily spend per market and channel and daily revenue per market for NL, DE and UK (UK in GBP), an FX table and a holiday calendar.

Scoring needs the spend you plan for the coming weeks. Upload it with the CLI:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/     # the demo tables, score payloads and spec
uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future

docs.title: 4. Fit from the browser
docs.text:
Open http://127.0.0.1:5173, go to Build and click the eu-geo-mmm row.

The editor validated the spec on the server as it opened: every dataset:// reference, every step and the model settings resolve, and the panel on the right shows what each pipeline step does to the data. The split into training and holdout weeks sits after the weekly step, because a week only exists from that stage on.

Press Fit. The run page follows the run over server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the run's supervisor read its one-time bootstrap object and deleted it before any model code started.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is expected on a laptop: the local executor cannot run the model code as a separate user. Containers and the cloud executor can.
  • The progress bar and message come straight from the sampler.

The spec uses tiny sampler settings, so the fit takes well under a minute (the first one on a new machine also compiles PyTensor code). When it succeeds the platform checks every file the run wrote against the storage's own checksums, copies the files where runs cannot reach them and signs a manifest. Press Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The scorecard flags R-hat and effective sample size: two chains of 100 draws are not enough to converge, and each warning says what to do about it. The metrics come from the 8 holdout weeks, scored through the same code path a forecast uses, before the model was refitted on all the data (fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit).

Open Plots → Contribution by channel:

Every plot is a Vega-Lite or Plotly spec that the server sanitized, rendered inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from the plot sandbox's own origin. Provenance shows the signed manifest, every stored object with its generation, and the lineage.

docs.title: 6. Score a forecast
docs.text:
Press Score (top right). The form only offers the modes this model supports.

  1. Keep mode forecast, horizon dim time and 8 periods.
  2. Set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1.
  3. Leave the fx side table at the version the fit used; it covers the forecast weeks.
  4. Press Score.

Nothing was refitted: the run replayed the fitted preprocessing (currency conversion, weekly resampling, scaling, and the last weeks of spend each market carries into the adstock) and inverted the result back to weekly EUR. The result's output_space says so.

docs.title: Stop, and start again later
docs.text:
make stop             # or Ctrl-C in the make dev shell
make dev              # everything you loaded is still there (.local/)
make clean-local      # delete the local database and objects, start from scratch

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Tour every page of the web app

    Datasets and CSV mapping, revisions and dry-runs, run controls, the data tree, counterfactuals.

  • Do the same from the command line

    mapi datasets upload, mapi fit --remote @, mapi score, --json for scripts.

  • Or from Python

    mapi_client.Client: uploads, live events, model versions and xr.DataTree results.

  • Understand what just happened

    The control plane, the run sandbox, storage integrity and the event path.

docs.title: Administration v0.3
docs.text:
From v0.3 one deployment serves many organisations. This guide is for the people who look after it: who may do what, how compute is limited and paid for, and what to do when something goes wrong. The concepts behind it are in Tenancy and authentication and Quotas and cost; signing in is in Authentication.

There are three administrative jobs, and the platform keeps them apart:

Who Holds Works in Does Platform operator A verified e-mail listed in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in Admin console, mapi admin …, /v1/admin/* Creates and suspends tenants, sets trust tiers and quotas, flips kill switches, watches executors, reads every audit log. Never reads tenant content (datasets, specs, models, plots) Tenant admin The admin role, tenant-wide Members, Usage (Organisation), /v1/tenants/{tenant}/… Creates projects, adds and removes people, reads the tenant's bill and audit log Project admin The admin role in one project Members, Tokens, Usage Manages that project's members, endpoints, plugins and everyone's tokens there

Every example on this page is one walkthrough, docs/snippets/admin_tour.sh, which the test suite runs against a development stack (make dev). It signs in through the development identity provider twice: as admin@dev.local (a platform operator) and as analyst@dev.local (who becomes the new tenant's admin).

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
export MAPI_URL=$API
dev_login() {  # dev profile only: an ID token for one seeded account, valid for an hour
  python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))' "$API" "$1"
}
OPERATOR=$(dev_login admin@dev.local)          # a platform operator
TENANT_ADMIN=$(dev_login analyst@dev.local)    # becomes the new tenant's admin below
MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR mapi whoami

On a real deployment each person runs mapi login instead (see Authentication). Operator commands always need a sign-in: an API token never carries operator powers, even its owner's.

docs.title: Tenants
docs.text:
A tenant is an organisation: the boundary of billing, isolation and quotas. PostgreSQL row-level security keeps every tenant's rows apart, and every storage key starts with t/{tenant}/. Only operators create tenants:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin tenants create "$TENANT" --name "Acme Retail" --tier verified \
    --residency eu --admin-email analyst@dev.local --yes
mapi admin tenants ls
Field Values Effect id A lowercase slug (acme) Part of every reference (dataset://growth/eu_media_daily lives in a tenant's project) and storage key; it cannot change Trust tier internal, verified, public, self-hosted-trusted Where the tenant's runs may execute, and its default quotas (below) Status active, suspended, deleting suspended: people can read and download, but nothing can be created, changed or run. deleting: no access at all Data residency eu, us, asia or one region (europe-west1) Runs are placed only on executors in a matching region. Changing it applies to new runs only Admin e-mail Any address Invited as tenant admin. The invitation is claimed at that person's first sign-in with that verified e-mail

The Admin console (operators only; everyone else sees an explanation instead) lists every tenant with its tier, status and residency. New tenant and Edit do the same as the commands above. Suspending or deleting asks for a reason and for the tenant's id, typed out.

Suspending is the reversible way to stop an organisation: its people keep read access to their work, and every change, upload and run is refused with 403 FORBIDDEN. Operators can still act on the tenant.

mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status suspended --reason "contract ended" --yes
mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status active --yes

docs.title: Trust tiers
docs.text:
The tier decides where a tenant's code may run, and this is enforced by the dispatcher in code, never by tenant configuration: a run whose executor does not meet its tenant's requirement is never submitted. The dispatcher fails it with INFRA_ERROR and a detail naming the requirement (for example verified tenants require an executor with isolation >= gvisor and enforced egress/DNS). The tier also sets the tenant's default quotas until an operator overrides them.

Tier Executor must provide vCPU-s / day vCPU-s / month Concurrent runs Fan-out tasks Largest class Storage Egress / month Requests / min internal isolation ≥ process — — 100 1,000 — — — 6,000 self-hosted-trusted isolation ≥ process — — — — — — — — verified isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 86,400 1,000,000 20 256 L 100 GiB 100 GiB 600 public isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 3,600 36,000 2 16 S 2 GiB 5 GiB 60

Platform-wide (global) defaults: concurrent_runs = 700. A dash means no limit at that level.

Which executors can take verified and public tenants today

Shared tiers need an executor with gVisor or microVM isolation and enforced egress and DNS. In v0.3 that is:

  • cloudrun-jobs, once MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED=true. It is false by default, because the DNS response policy has not yet been verified against a real Cloud Run Jobs execution (the first item of the M0 checklist). Until then, verified and public runs fail at dispatch rather than run somewhere weaker.
  • docker-gvisor, only with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=none, which needs an HTTPS bootstrap URL; with the local GCS shim it is not available.

internal and self-hosted-trusted tenants run anywhere, including local-process (which refuses to start at all under MAPI_PROFILE=multi-tenant).

docs.title: Projects and members
docs.text:
A project is a workspace inside a tenant and the unit of access control. Tenant admins create projects and decide who works in them; there is no CLI command for members yet, so the walkthrough uses the HTTP API:

as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects" \
    -d '{"id": "growth", "name": "Growth marketing"}' | jq -c '{tenant_id, id, name}'
as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    -d '{"email": "viewer@dev.local", "role": "runner"}' | jq -c '{project_id, email, role}'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t(tenant-wide)"'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t\(.project_id // "(tenant-wide)")"'

A membership grants one role, either on one project or tenant-wide (on the tenant and every project in it). In a project, a person's effective role is the higher of the two. Membership is read at every request, so removing someone from a project immediately disarms their sessions and their tokens there.

Members shows the project's members (or, with Organisation, the tenant-wide grants). Admins change a role in place, remove a member, or Add member by e-mail: an address nobody has signed in with yet becomes an invitation, claimed at first sign-in. A grant marked organisation comes from a tenant-wide membership and is changed there.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
There are four roles, each including the one before it. Running sits above editing on purpose: compute costs money, so someone can be trusted to edit a spec without being able to start a 200-task sweep.

Role Adds viewer Read everything in the project; validate specs; mint tokens for themselves editor Create and change datasets, specs and saved plots runner Spend compute: submit, cancel and retry runs, score models and endpoints, render plots admin Manage members, endpoints, plugins and other people's tokens; delete things

The complete matrix, generated from mapi_spec.tenancy.PERMISSIONS (the table every component checks). tenant-wide means only a tenant-wide grant counts; a pair that is not listed is denied to everyone:

Resource Action viewer editor runner admin Operator tenant read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ update ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ delete ✓ manage (tier, status, residency, identity verification) ✓ tenant_member read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ tenant-wide delete ✓ tenant-wide project read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ delete ✓ tenant-wide member read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ token read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ delete (own tokens; manage covers everyone's) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ manage (list and revoke other members' tokens) ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ run read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ delete ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ manage (override a promotion gate; sessions only) ✓ plot read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ run (render) ✓ ✓ delete (saved plots) ✓ ✓ ✓ embed read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ ✓ ✓ webhook read ✓ create ✓ update (includes rotating the secret and replaying deliveries) ✓ delete ✓ plugin read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ delete ✓ usage read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ billing read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ audit read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ quota read ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ kill_switch read ✓ update ✓ executor read ✓ update ✓ event create — — — — internal services only tenant_deletion read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide cancel (within the grace period) ✓ tenant-wide manage (purge, retry) ✓ tenant_export read ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ tenant-wide

The Permissions reference has the same matrix with the token scopes and the operators' permissions side by side.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs (the Python client, the CLI in CI, Atlas, BI exports) use API tokens. A token is minted by a person in one project, acts as that person narrowed by its scopes, and is bound to that project. Anyone with a role can mint tokens for themselves; project admins can list and revoke everyone's.

export MAPI_TOKEN=$TENANT_ADMIN
mapi use "$TENANT/growth"
mapi tokens create nightly-report -s models:read --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 60 \
    --budget 3600 --budget-period day > nightly-report.token   # the secret, once
mapi tokens ls

New token asks for a name, the scopes, optional endpoint aliases, an expiry (default 90 days, at most 365), a requests-per-minute limit and a vCPU-second budget per day or month. It names your role, which is the most any of your tokens can do.

The secret is shown once. The server stores only an HMAC of it, so a lost token is revoked and replaced, never recovered. Revoking takes effect on the next request.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Scopes only narrow: a token can never do more than its owner's role, and both must allow an action. admin covers everything the owner's role allows. Generated from mapi_spec.tokens.scope_allows:

Resource Action models:read runs:create score:* datasets:write plugins:publish endpoints:promote webhooks:manage project read ✓ ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ run read ✓ ✓ create ✓ cancel ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ plot read ✓ ✓ run ✓ webhook read ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ plugin read ✓ create ✓ delete ✓ usage read ✓ ✓

score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:geo-mmm-prod), score:* every endpoint of the project. Tenant-level actions (members, the bill, the audit log) and operator actions are never reachable with a token.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text:
Compute is limited in vCPU-seconds, at three levels checked in order: the token's own limits, the tenant's policy (or its tier's defaults, above), and platform-wide limits that protect the cloud project. The first limit a request would exceed answers 429 with QUOTA_EXCEEDED or RATE_LIMITED, a detail naming the level and the limit, and Retry-After when it resets (Quotas and cost explains every limit). Operators override a tenant's defaults:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin quotas set tenant "$TENANT" --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 \
    --concurrent-runs 40 --max-fanout-tasks 256 --storage 200GiB \
    --note "private beta customer" --yes
mapi admin quotas ls

set replaces the policy: limits you leave out are removed, and the tier default applies to them again. mapi admin quotas rm tenant acme removes the override.

docs.title: Cost and usage
docs.text:
Every run is estimated when it is submitted (and checked against the quotas with that estimate), then metered when each attempt ends: vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds of its resource class, at the deployment's versioned price table, written to an append-only cost ledger. Amounts are exact integer micros of a currency, and each names the price table it used. A run's page and mapi runs get show its cost; usage pages add it up.

mapi usage --group-by resource_class             # the selected project, this UTC month
mapi usage --tenant "$TENANT" --period day       # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)

Usage shows a project's (or, with Organisation, the whole tenant's) cost, compute, runs and memory for a UTC day or month; a daily chart; how close each quota is (warnings at 70 % and 90 %); and the totals by token and by resource class. Anyone in a project sees its usage; the tenant-wide view needs a tenant-wide admin. The amounts are an estimate of compute cost at list prices, not an invoice.

docs.title: Kill switches
docs.text:
Two platform-wide switches stop compute fast. Both are audited and need a reason:

Switch Effect Uploaded code (untrusted_execution_enabled) Off: no run of tenant-uploaded plugin code is accepted or leased. Built-in models keep working Global spend cap Once the platform's spend in the current UTC day or month reaches the cap, no new compute starts except for internal tenants 
mapi admin kill-switches set --spend-cap 500 --spend-cap-period month \
    --reason "private beta budget" --yes
mapi admin kill-switches get

Turning off uploaded code is the first step of the sandbox-escape runbook (ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md). Spend opens a ticket at 70 % of the cap and pages at 90 % (Observability).

docs.title: Executors
docs.text: Executors in the admin console (and mapi admin executors ls) show each execution backend's health, isolation, resource classes, running and queued work, failures in the last hour, its jobs.run rate against the limit, and whether it has passed the executor conformance suite. trusted tenants only marks an executor that verified and public tenants can never be placed on.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Security-relevant actions are appended to an audit log: sign-ins (and failed ones), tenant, project and membership changes, token creation, revocation and failed use, quota and kill-switch changes, quota denials, run creation and cancellation, integrity failures, artifact links and dataset downloads, and refused run events. Each entry records who (and whether as an operator), what, on which resource, the outcome and a problem code. IP addresses and user agents are kept only as keyed hashes: entries can be correlated, never reversed.

mapi admin audit --tenant "$TENANT" -n 10        # operators: any tenant
# tenant admins: their own tenant's log
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/audit?limit=5" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.ts)  \(.action)  \(.resource_kind):\(.resource_id)  \(.outcome)"'

Tenant admins read their own tenant's log (GET /v1/tenants/{tenant}/audit); operators read everyone's in the Audit log tab or with mapi admin audit, filtered by tenant, project, actor, action, outcome and time.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Authentication: browser sign-in, the development IdP, Identity Platform, API tokens and the CLI.
  • Permissions: the generated matrices.
  • CLI reference: every mapi admin and mapi tokens option.
  • HTTP API: multi-tenant API: the endpoints.
  • Observability: the metrics, alerts and runbooks behind the kill switches and quotas.

docs.title: Optimise a budget with Atlas v0.4
docs.text:
Atlas optimises budget allocations against any model that has its model interface. mapi_client.atlas.RemoteModel gives an endpoint that interface: each candidate allocation the optimiser tries is scored by the endpoint's current model version, so the fitted posterior - not a local copy - decides where the next euro goes, and promoting a better model changes the optimiser's answers without touching its code.

The examples come from docs/snippets/atlas_budget.py, which runs offline against a stand-in endpoint with a concave response whose optimum is known in closed form, so the page can check that the optimiser finds it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install 'mapi-client[atlas]'                         # the client and the xarray runtime
pip install git+https://github.com/redam94/optimizer-framework   # Atlas itself

The atlas extra installs only what the adapter needs (xarray and the SDK's wire format). Atlas is installed separately: it is AGPL-licensed, so the Apache-2.0 client never imports it - RemoteModel matches Atlas's interface structurally (predict(x) -> xr.DataArray, contributions(x) -> xr.Dataset, model_type, required_dimensions) and works with any code written against atlas.core.interfaces.ModelProtocol.

Give the program a token that can only score this endpoint:

mapi tokens create budget-optimiser -s score:budget-planner --rate-limit 600

docs.title: Wrap the endpoint
docs.text:
from mapi_client.atlas import RemoteModel

model = RemoteModel(
    api,
    endpoint="budget-planner",
    batch_dim="scenario",  # the model scores every scenario independently
    output="mean",  # or "draws" for risk-aware objectives
)
x = model.allocation({"tv": 4000.0, "search": 4000.0, "social": 2000.0})
print(float(model.predict(x)))  # the KPI (revenue) of this allocation

8634.97622707262
  • KPI. predict returns the endpoint's output variable - the only one, or the one named like the target; set kpi= (e.g. "y_hat") when there are several - summed over every other dim (reduce="sum"; "mean" and "none" too). It reads one summary statistic, chosen by the endpoint's representation: the mean of a Bayesian (draws), point or moments model, the median of a quantile model such as tabular.regressor, the point of an interval model (stat= overrides it). Summing per-cell medians is an approximation; prefer endpoints with draws for totals across many cells. With output="draws" (and draws=100, at most 300) a draws endpoint returns posterior draws along a sample dim instead, for risk-aware objectives (a quantile, an expected shortfall).
  • Allocations. allocation({"tv": 4000, ...}) builds the payload from a budget per channel (spend_var= and channel_dim= name them; by default the endpoint's only spend variable along channel). With base= - a dataset holding the other inputs (controls, prices, the weeks of the plan) - each channel's flighting across weeks and markets is kept and rescaled to its budget, and every input the allocation lacks is sent from the base.
  • Scoring. Every payload is first transposed to the dim order of the endpoint's input schema (the server checks each variable's dims in order; Client.endpoint(alias) does the same unless conform=False). Candidates go inline as XrJSON in the call's data (payload_field="scenario" for counterfactual endpoints); call={"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {...}} adds any other EndpointScoreCall field. Each call waits with Prefer: wait=60 and collects slow runs with the same idempotency key.
  • contributions(x) returns every output variable of the endpoint for x, unreduced - including the decomposition variables an MMM returns.

docs.title: Batching, caching and rate limits
docs.text:
An optimiser evaluates many nearby allocations - finite differences, line searches, populations. RemoteModel keeps that cheap:

  • Batching. predict_batch(xs) scores a list of allocations. With batch_dim= - a dim of the endpoint's input that accepts new coordinates (a categorical dim with policy new_levels, or an integer/index dim with extend) and that the model scores independently, such as a scenario dim - up to max_batch (64) candidates are stacked along it into one score request and split again from the result. Without batch_dim each candidate is its own request. Only batch along a dim the model really treats independently: a hierarchical model's geo dim does not qualify (new markets are pooled). The endpoint's schema is checked first, and a dim it cannot extend is refused.
  • Caching. Results are cached by the exact payload (an LRU of cache_size=1024), so re-evaluating a point costs nothing; cache_info() reports hits, misses and requests.
  • Rate limits. The client already waits out short 429 RATE_LIMITED answers. When the server asks for a longer wait, RemoteModel retries up to rate_limit_retries (5) times with exponential backoff (backoff=1 s, doubling, capped at max_backoff=60 s, honouring Retry-After) and the same idempotency key. QUOTA_EXCEEDED is raised at once: waiting will not help until the quota window resets.

docs.title: Optimise
docs.text:
Atlas's OptimizerProtocol is optimize(model, constraints, config) -> OptimizationResult. This SLSQP optimiser keeps the total budget fixed and scores each iteration's point and its central finite differences in one batched request:

from scipy.optimize import minimize


class BudgetOptimizer:
    """An Atlas optimiser (``OptimizerProtocol``): maximise ``model.predict`` with a fixed
    total. Each iteration scores the point and its finite differences in one batch."""

    def optimize(
        self, model: Any, constraints: Mapping[str, Any], config: Mapping[str, Any]
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        channels, total, h = list(config["channels"]), float(constraints["total_budget"]), 1e-4

        def budget(w: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
            return {c: total * max(float(v), 0.0) for c, v in zip(channels, w, strict=True)}

        def objective(w: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:
            steps = [np.zeros_like(w)] + [s * h * np.eye(len(w))[i]
                                          for i in range(len(w)) for s in (1, -1)]
            values = model.predict_batch([model.allocation(budget(w + e)) for e in steps])
            f = [float(v) for v in values]
            grad = [(f[1 + 2 * i] - f[2 + 2 * i]) / (2 * h) for i in range(len(w))]
            return -f[0], -np.asarray(grad)

        res = minimize(
            objective, np.full(len(channels), 1 / len(channels)), jac=True, method="SLSQP",
            bounds=[(h, 1 - h)] * len(channels),
            constraints=[{"type": "eq", "fun": lambda w: float(np.sum(w) - 1)}],
        )  # fmt: skip
        return {"optimal_budget": budget(res.x), "optimal_value": float(-res.fun)}


result = BudgetOptimizer().optimize(
    model, {"total_budget": 10_000}, {"channels": ["tv", "search", "social"]}
)
print({c: round(v) for c, v in result["optimal_budget"].items()})
print(model.cache_info())

{'tv': 5750, 'search': 2500, 'social': 1750}
CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=71, requests=11, size=71)

71 candidate allocations cost 11 score requests. The optimum matches the closed form (a_c / (b_c + x_c) equal across channels). With a real endpoint, each request is one sandboxed score run, so the wall time is dominated by run start-up; batching is what keeps a gradient optimiser to a few minutes.

docs.title: With Atlas installed
docs.text:
Code that checks isinstance(model, AbstractModel) accepts RemoteModel once it is registered as a virtual subclass (this imports Atlas, so call it only where Atlas is installed):

    from atlas.core.interfaces import AbstractModel
    from mapi_client.atlas import register_with_atlas

    register_with_atlas()  # RemoteModel becomes a virtual subclass of AbstractModel
    assert isinstance(model, AbstractModel)

Atlas optimisers can then return Atlas's own OptimizationResult. In this repository, make test-atlas runs the adapter's tests with Atlas installed from a sibling checkout (ATLAS_DIR=../optimizer-framework) into a throwaway environment overlay - Atlas is never a locked dependency of the platform.

Against a running stack (a tabular.regressor fitted on 1,800 rows of the same concave response, promoted to an endpoint), this optimiser found tv 5534, search 2233, social 2233 - the closed form is 5750 / 2500 / 1750; the gap is the gradient-boosted model's own error - from 98 candidate allocations in 14 batched score requests, in about 140 seconds.

Optimising in the sandbox

RemoteModel drives the optimiser from your machine, one score run per batch. For long optimisations the plan's in-sandbox optimize job (M4) runs Atlas next to the model, without a network round trip per batch.

docs.title: Authentication v0.3
docs.text:
A v0.3 deployment answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to anyone it does not know. There are three ways in, one per kind of caller:

Caller Signs in with Sends Reference A person in a browser The organisation's identity provider (OpenID Connect) An HttpOnly session cookie; the app never sees a token Browser sign-in A person in a terminal mapi login: the same provider, from the command line The provider's ID token as Authorization: Bearer The command line A program Nothing: a person mints it an API token Authorization: Bearer mapi_… API tokens

Whichever way, the caller is a user (usr_…) with roles in projects, and every request is checked against those roles at that moment (Administration). This page is for the people who sign in and set up sign-in; the protocol details (cookies, CSRF, PKCE, JWKS, the database roles) are in Authentication and tenant isolation.

docs.title: Browser sign-in
docs.text:
Opening the web app without a session shows Sign in to your workspace. Continue to sign in goes to the API's /auth/login, which sends the browser to the identity provider; after the provider's own sign-in the browser comes back to the page it started on.

The API does all the OpenID Connect work (authorization code with PKCE, a nonce, ID-token verification against the provider's keys) and keeps the tokens to itself: the browser holds only two cookies, a __Host- session cookie that scripts cannot read and a CSRF token. A session ends after 2 hours idle or 12 hours in all, or at Sign out.

Once signed in, the project switcher at the top left lists every tenant and project you have a role in, with that role and the tenant's trust tier. Everything the app shows and does happens in the selected project (it is sent as X-Mapi-Project on every request). The avatar menu shows who you are; a shield marks a platform operator.

The first sign-in of a person creates their user from the provider's (issuer, subject) and, if the provider says the e-mail is verified, claims every invitation sent to that address (a tenant admin's Add member, an operator's --admin-email). Someone with no membership yet sees You are not in a project yet.

docs.title: The development IdP
docs.text:
make dev (and Docker Compose) run the servers in the dev profile, which mounts a small OpenID provider inside the API at /dev/idp. Sign-in then works offline, through exactly the same code path as a real provider: RS256-signed ID tokens, PKCE, single-use codes.

There are no passwords: whoever can reach a dev API can sign in as any listed account. The accounts come from MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS:

Account Gets at start-up admin@dev.local Admin of the default tenant and a platform operator analyst@dev.local runner in default/default viewer@dev.local (and any further addresses) viewer in default/default

Scripts sign in without a browser with mapi_client.oidc.dev_idp_login(api_url, email), which runs the same flow and returns an ID token valid for an hour. make seed, the end-to-end tests and the walkthroughs on this page use it; a server in any other profile answers 404, so it cannot be pointed at production. The walkthrough below is docs/snippets/auth_tour.sh, run by the test suite against make dev:

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'anonymous: %{http_code}\n' "$API/v1/me"      # 401: sign in first
# dev profile only: what `mapi login` gets from a real identity provider, without a browser
ID_TOKEN=$(python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], "analyst@dev.local"))' "$API")
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" \
  | jq -c '{email: .principal.email, auth, operator,
            projects: [.tenants[].projects[] | "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id) \(.role)"]}'

anonymous: 401
{"email":"analyst@dev.local","auth":"session","operator":false,"projects":["acme/growth admin","acme/retail admin","default/default runner"]}

MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant make dev turns sign-in off altogether: the v0.2 behaviour, where every request acts as the local administrator of default.

docs.title: Setting up a real identity provider
docs.text: The API signs people in with any OpenID Connect provider that offers the authorization-code flow: it needs an issuer whose /.well-known/openid-configuration lists an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint and a JWKS.

docs.title: Google accounts
docs.text:
The default of the Google Cloud deployment and the simplest choice for an organisation on Google Workspace:

  1. In the Google Cloud console (APIs & Services → Credentials) create an OAuth client ID of type Web application, with the authorized redirect URI https://<your app domain>/auth/callback.
  2. Give Terraform its id (oidc_client_id in terraform.tfvars) and its secret as the ephemeral variable TF_VAR_oidc_client_secret with oidc_client_secret_version = 1 (step 4 of the deployment). Outside Terraform, set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET on the API.
  3. List the operators' e-mails in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, and create each organisation's tenant with an --admin-email (Administration).

MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS='{"hd": "acme.com"}' pre-selects a Workspace domain in Google's account chooser. It is only a hint: who may do what is decided by memberships, never by the e-mail domain.

docs.title: Identity Platform
docs.text:
Terraform also enables Identity Platform in the control project (infra/terraform/modules/control/identity.tf): it registers the app's domain as an authorized domain, turns off anonymous and (by default) e-mail/password sign-in, and is where SAML and OIDC providers for enterprise single sign-on are added, in the console or with google_identity_platform_*_idp_config resources kept outside the module (their secrets do not belong in its state).

Known gap in v0.3

The API's sign-in cannot use Identity Platform's own tokens yet. Those (issuer https://securetoken.google.com/<project>) are obtained with Identity Platform's client SDK, and that issuer offers no authorization-code endpoint for the API to redirect to. Until that adapter exists, point MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER at Google (above) or directly at the organisation's own OpenID provider (below). The Identity Platform configuration that Terraform creates is harmless meanwhile.

docs.title: Other providers
docs.text: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0 and any other standard provider work the same way: register a web client with the redirect URI https://<your app domain>/auth/callback, then set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER to its issuer (and MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL if its discovery document is not under the issuer), MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET. ID tokens must be signed with an asymmetric algorithm (MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS, default RS256,ES256).

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
mapi login signs in with the same provider, from the terminal:

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • With a browser, it opens the provider's page and listens once on 127.0.0.1 for the redirect (authorization code with PKCE).
  • --device prints a short code to enter on another device (providers that support the device flow).
  • --with-token stores an API token read from standard input instead (CI).

It keeps the sign-in in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600) and sends the provider's ID token as Authorization: Bearer. The API accepts such a token only when its audience is one of MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS (default mapi-cli): register the CLI with your provider as a public installed app client with a loopback redirect, PKCE and the openid email scopes. Google's installed-app clients need a client secret, which the CLI reads from MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and never prints.

Against the development IdP:

mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost \
           --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp

Then choose where commands act with mapi use <tenant>/<project> (or --project, or MAPI_PROJECT); mapi whoami shows who you are, how you are signed in and your projects. See The command line.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs never sign in. A person mints them a token in one project, with only the scopes it needs; the token then acts as that person, narrowed by its scopes, and only in that project. In the web app it is Tokens → New token (Administration); from the CLI, mapi tokens create; over HTTP:

CREATED=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" \
  -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "auth-guide", "scopes": ["models:read"], "expires_in_days": 1}')
TOKEN=$(jq -r .secret <<<"$CREATED")             # shown once: store it now
TOKEN_ID=$(jq -r .token.id <<<"$CREATED")
jq -c '.token | {id, display, scopes, project: "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id)", expires_at}' \
  <<<"$CREATED"

{"id":"tok_01m50mxfqh4k95ed2dv2jc005v","display":"mapi_hhb9gjzf_…","scopes":["models:read"],"project":"default/default","expires_at":"2026-10-16T20:44:02.161164Z"}

The secret (mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>) is in the response once. The server keeps only an HMAC of it; listings show the prefix (mapi_hhb9gjzf_…). The built-in checksum lets clients and secret scanners reject a mistyped or made-up token without asking the server.

A program sends it as a bearer. The token is bound to its project, so it needs no X-Mapi-Project header:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{auth, operator}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/runs?limit=2" \
  | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.id) \(.kind) \(.state)"'   # bound to its project: no header needed

The Python client takes it as Client(token=…) or MAPI_TOKEN, the CLI as --token, MAPI_TOKEN or mapi login --with-token (Python client). Both refuse to send a token over plain HTTP to anything but a loopback address.

docs.title: What a token cannot do
docs.text:
Scopes only narrow. A models:read token cannot start a run even when its owner is a runner; it cannot act in another project; and no token carries operator powers:

# models:read cannot spend compute, even though its owner is a runner
curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"kind": "fit", "spec": "spec://default/eu-geo-mmm"}' \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
# a token never acts outside its project, or as an operator
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth' "$API/v1/runs" \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/admin/tenants" | jq -c '{status, code}'

{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}

Tokens expire (default 90 days, at most 365). Revoking one, or removing its owner from the project, stops it at the next request:

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'revoke: %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/v1/tokens/$TOKEN_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{status, code}'   # at once

revoke: 204
{"status":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}

Failed uses of a known token (a wrong secret, an expired or revoked token) are written to the audit log as token.auth_failed; no error ever echoes the token back.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: Browser session mapi login API token Identity The person The person The person who minted it Projects Every project with a role (choose one per request) Same Only the one it was minted in Permissions The role The role The role and the scopes Operator powers Yes, for operators Yes, for operators Never Needs CSRF token Yes, for changes No No Ends 2 h idle, 12 h total, sign-out mapi logout; the CLI renews the ID token with a refresh token when the provider issued one, otherwise mapi login again Expiry or revocation

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Administration: tenants, members, roles, tokens, quotas and audit.
  • Authentication and tenant isolation: the operator's view, with cookies, CSRF, row-level security and Pub/Sub push authentication.
  • Tenancy and authentication: the concepts and the request-authorization pipeline.

docs.title: The command line v0.2
docs.text:
mapi (package mapi-cli, Apache-2.0) works in two places:

  • locally, without any server: scaffold a spec, check it, fit it and score it in your own Python process with the installed plugins (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec);
  • remotely, against the HTTP API of a running platform: upload datasets, fit, follow runs and score model versions (datasets, runs, and --remote on check, fit, score and catalog).

Every command and option is listed in the generated CLI reference. The examples on this page are scripts that the test suite runs: the local ones in the default suite, the remote ones in make e2e.

Running the commands

make install puts mapi into the workspace environment. Either activate it (source .venv/bin/activate) or prefix every command with uv run (uv run mapi --help).

docs.title: Without a server
docs.text:
Scaffold a spec from a template. --with-data also writes the matching conformance fixture's sample data (it needs the mapi-conformance package, which the workspace has):

mapi new tabular -o spec.yaml --with-data     # an XGBoost demand model plus its sample data
Template What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Hierarchical geo MMM (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend and seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02

Check it statically against the installed plugins and the data's schema. --stages prints the schema after every pipeline step; the exit status is 1 when there are errors, so it works in CI:

mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --stages

Fit in-process. The bundle (zarr zip, sidecars, plots, metrics and the evaluation bundle of evaluate_then_refit) goes to bundles/<name>/; --side-table NAME=PATH supplies side tables:

mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip       # in-process: writes bundles/<name>/
ls bundles/tabular

mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/<name> --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip scores a local bundle with a ScoreRequest document.

Local means trusted

Local fit and score import and run the plugins in your own process (isolation NONE), exactly like a notebook. Use them with code and data you trust. On the platform, the same work runs in a sandbox.

Inspect the catalog of installed plugins, and upgrade spec documents across apiVersions:

mapi catalog models
mapi --json catalog steps | jq -r '.steps[].id' | head -n 5
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check           # exit 0: already the current apiVersion

mapi plugin init NAME scaffolds a plugin package (model, entry point, contract-kit tests) and mapi plugin test NAME runs its tests; see Write a plugin.

docs.title: Against a running platform
docs.text: Start the stack first (make dev, then make seed; see the quickstart).

docs.title: Choosing the API
docs.text:
Every remote command resolves the API the same way as the Python client, first match wins:

  1. --url and --token (global options, before the command: mapi --url http://… runs ls);
  2. MAPI_URL (falling back to MAPI_API_URL, the name make dev uses), MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE;
  3. the selected profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml if set);
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.
# ~/.config/mapi/config.toml
profile = "local"

[profiles.local]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

[profiles.other-ports]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:18000"
timeout = 60

mapi config show prints the resolved URL, profile, project and credentials and where each value came from (never a token: an API token appears as mapi_<prefix>_…, a sign-in as who signed in and until when); mapi config path prints the file's location. mapi config set KEY VALUE and mapi config unset KEY change the selected profile (--profile, else MAPI_PROFILE, else the file's default). They rewrite the file with mode 0600 and do not keep comments. Secrets cannot be set this way: use mapi login --with-token. --remote @ on check, fit, score and catalog means "the configured API"; --remote URL overrides it for one command.

Tokens

v0.2 is single-tenant and has no authentication: the API listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The client sends MAPI_TOKEN as a bearer token when one is set, and refuses to send it over plain HTTP to anything but a loopback address.

docs.title: Sign in and choose a project v0.3
docs.text:
A multi-tenant API (v0.3) needs credentials and a project (Tenancy and authentication).

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • mapi login opens the identity provider in your browser (OpenID Connect, authorization code with PKCE, redirected to a one-off listener on 127.0.0.1). --device signs in with a code typed on another device instead, and --no-browser only prints the address. --issuer, --client-id and --discovery-url are saved in the profile, so later logins need none of them. Against a local MAPI_PROFILE=dev stack, use mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp and pick an account on the page that opens. The sign-in is kept in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600) and renewed automatically with its refresh token. It is only ever sent to the API it was made for.
  • mapi login --with-token reads an API token from stdin, checks its checksum (a typo is caught before any request), verifies it with GET /v1/me and saves it in the profile (the config file is rewritten with mode 0600). An API token in the profile or in MAPI_TOKEN takes precedence over a browser sign-in.
  • mapi whoami shows who you are, how you signed in, and every project you can act in with your role there.
  • mapi logout forgets the sign-in (revoking its refresh token at the identity provider) and the profile's token; --revoke also revokes that token on the server.

Every v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) now lives in a project. mapi use checks that you are a member and saves the selection in the profile; the CLI sends it as X-Mapi-Project on project-scoped requests only. --project or MAPI_PROJECT override it for one command or one shell. An API token acts in its own project only.

mapi use acme/growth                            # sent as X-Mapi-Project from now on
mapi --project acme/retail runs ls              # another project, for one command
mapi use                                        # show the selection and where it came from

docs.title: Tokens, usage and cost v0.3
docs.text:
mapi tokens create atlas-optimiser -s score:geo-mmm-prod -s models:read \
    --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 120 > atlas.token   # the secret, once, on stdout
mapi tokens ls
mapi tokens revoke tok_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0      # asks first; --yes for scripts
mapi usage --group-by resource_class            # this month: cost, compute, quota headroom
mapi usage --tenant acme --period day           # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)
mapi runs get run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0    # includes the run's metered cost

mapi tokens create prints the new token's secret once, alone on stdout, so redirecting it to a file captures exactly the token; --save stores it in the profile instead. Nothing else ever prints a token: listings, whoami and config show use the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_…. mapi usage shows the exact cost of the period (integer micro-units of the currency, priced by a named price table), the vCPU- and GiB-seconds behind it, and how much of each quota is used and when it resets. mapi runs get and mapi runs ls show each run's cost (~ while it is still an estimate).

When the API answers 429, the client handles it: RATE_LIMITED is waited out (the server's Retry-After, then exponential back-off) and retried; QUOTA_EXCEEDED stops at once with the reason, when the quota resets (retry after 1h 30m) and, with --json, retry_after_seconds.

docs.title: Operators v0.3
docs.text:
Platform operators manage tenants, quotas, kill switches and executors with mapi admin. Each change shows a before-and-after table and asks for confirmation (--yes skips it, for runbooks); the server audits it. Kill-switch changes need --reason.

mapi admin kill-switches set --untrusted-code off --reason "incident 2026-10-15"
mapi admin quotas set tenant acme --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 --concurrent-runs 40 \
    --storage 200GiB --note "beta customer"
mapi admin tenants update acme --status suspended --reason "payment overdue"
mapi admin executors ls
mapi admin executors disable cloudrun-jobs --reason "incident 2026-10-15: contain"
mapi admin audit --tenant acme --action token.create --since 2026-10-01

mapi admin quotas set replaces the whole policy of a subject: limits you leave out are removed (the tier defaults and the other levels still apply).

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
mapi datasets upload creates the dataset if it does not exist, sends the file to the signed URL the API returns, starts the sandboxed ingest run and waits until the version is ready. CSV and Parquet files need --mapping mapping.yaml, an IngestMapping with the column of each dim and variable:

python scripts/seed.py --export demo/      # the E33 tables, score payloads and spec
mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future
mapi datasets ls

docs.title: Fit and follow
docs.text:
mapi fit SPEC --remote @ creates the spec (or adds a revision when the text changed), submits a fit run and follows its event stream until it ends, printing warnings, diagnostics and metrics as they arrive. --no-wait returns after submitting; mapi runs watch RUN follows any run later.

mapi check demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @   # the server's static validation
mapi fit demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @     # create or revise the spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --kind fit --limit 3

mapi runs cancel RUN requests cancellation, and mapi runs retry RUN --resource-class L starts a new run from a failed one.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
cat > forecast.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
data: dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest
side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90]}
EOF
# the CLI has no `models` command yet: take the model id and version from the API
# (with the same credentials as the CLI when MAPI_TOKEN is set)
AUTH=(-H "X-Mapi-Project: ${MAPI_PROJECT:-default/default}")
[ -z "${MAPI_TOKEN:-}" ] || AUTH+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN")
MODEL=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}/v1/models" \
  | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
mapi score forecast.yaml --remote @ --model "$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")" \
  --version "$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")" -o forecast.zarr.zip

mapi score --remote @ sends Prefer: wait=60 (change it with --wait), follows the run if it takes longer, prints the outputs with their sizes and CRC32C, and with -o downloads the result tree, checking it against that CRC32C.

docs.title: Endpoints, webhooks and sharing v0.4
docs.text:
mapi endpoints promote geo-mmm-prod model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3   # asks first; --yes skips
mapi endpoints ls
mapi endpoints schema geo-mmm-prod --example > call.json           # a valid score call
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod call.json -o result.zarr.zip
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --mode forecast --periods 8 --draws 100
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --data plan.nc                   # inline XrJSON (≤ 5 MB)
mapi endpoints snippets geo-mmm-prod -l python > score.py
mapi endpoints rollback geo-mmm-prod --reason "v3 over-forecasts"

promote goes through the promotion gate: a warning scorecard needs --override --reason TEXT from a signed-in project admin, a failing one is blocked. Promotions and rollbacks change what every integration calling the alias receives, so both show the current version and ask before acting. score sends a JSON EndpointScoreCall (a file, - for stdin, or --example), with flags for the mode, the horizon, --data/--scenario (a dataset:// reference, an XrJSON .json, a .zarr.zip or a netCDF file, sent inline) and --draws; it waits like mapi score --remote and -o downloads the result tree. With one --language, snippets prints only the code.

mapi webhooks create https://hooks.example.com/mapi -e endpoint.promoted -e run.failed > hook.secret
mapi webhooks ls
mapi webhooks deliveries WEBHOOK_ID --status failed
mapi webhooks replay WEBHOOK_ID DELIVERY_ID
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID --enable           # back on after --inactive or an auto-disable
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID -e run.failed --description "on-call"
mapi webhooks rotate WEBHOOK_ID > hook.secret      # asks first; the old secret signs for 24 h
mapi webhooks rm WEBHOOK_ID                        # asks first

Like tokens, a webhook's signing secret is printed once, alone on stdout, by create and rotate; listings show whsec_…<last 4>. update changes the events (-e replaces the whole list), --url or --description, and --enable/--disable switches deliveries on or off: a webhook created with --inactive, or disabled automatically after repeated failures, goes back on with --enable, which also resets its failure count. Delivery responses are the receiver's text and are printed with control sequences removed. Verifying deliveries is described in Receiving webhooks.

mapi plots render --model MODEL_ID --version 3 --plot mmm.response_curves -f pdf -o curves.pdf
mapi plots render --saved PLOT_ID --width 1200
mapi plots embed PLOT_ID --expires-in-days 30 --allow-origin https://bi.example.com
mapi plots embeds PLOT_ID
