mapi plots revoke PLOT_ID EMBED_ID                 # asks first

render draws the plot in the sandbox (vl-convert) and downloads the file; embed prints the link - which carries its token - once (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Guided mode and business priors v0.4
docs.text:
mapi guided templates [geo_mmm]
mapi guided detect geo_mmm --csv media.csv          # or --dataset dataset://growth/media@v2
mapi guided draft geo_mmm --name eu-geo-mmm --dataset eu_media --csv media.csv --detect \
    -a spend=tv_spend,search_spend -a holdout_periods=8 --yaml-out spec.yaml
mapi priors preview --beliefs beliefs.yaml --spec SPEC_ID --revision 2 -o priors.json

detect and draft --csv profile the file locally - types, counts, ranges and a few sample values per column - and send only those summaries, as the web app does. --detect pre-fills every answer detection is sure of; -a QUESTION=VALUE answers (or overrides) one, with a,b,c for lists and JSON for numbers. A draft stores nothing: review spec.yaml, then upload the data with the mapping (--mapping-out) and fit. priors preview turns ROI or contribution-share ranges into model priors in a sandboxed run and shows what the model then believes, per channel (Guided modelling).

docs.title: Sign-up and your workspace v0.4
docs.text:
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example signup --email ana@acme.example --name "Ana Analyst" --accept-terms
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example verify-email mev_…   # the token from the e-mail link
mapi tenant status                                       # verification, any scheduled deletion
mapi tenant export -o acme-export.zip                    # GDPR export, waited for and downloaded
mapi tenant delete                                       # type the tenant id to confirm
mapi tenant delete --cancel                              # within the grace period

signup and verify-email send no credentials. tenant delete explains what is purged and kept, and asks you to type the tenant id; scripts pass --confirm TENANT. The tenant is --tenant, else the selected project's, else your only one (Deleting and exporting data).

docs.title: Scripting with --json
docs.text:
--json (a global option) prints one JSON document on stdout instead of tables; runs watch --json prints one JSON event per line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1, and usage errors exit with 2.

RUN=$(mapi --json runs ls --kind score --limit 1 | jq -r '.[0].id')
mapi --json runs get "$RUN" | jq '{state, attempt, kind}'
mapi runs logs "$RUN" | tail -n 5

Text that came from the server, a plugin or a run log is printed with ANSI and control sequences removed, so a hostile log line cannot rewrite your terminal.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev: database migrations, then the API and the orchestrator in one process, with an embedded PostgreSQL unless DATABASE_URL is set and an in-process GCS shim unless one already listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. It is the smallest way to get an API for the CLI or the client. For the web app as well, use make dev (Local deployment).

docs.title: Conformance corpus
docs.text:
The corpus is how the platform defines "supported": a set of small, realistic modelling problems (ports of pymc-challenges and of the plan's examples) that must keep working, end to end, on every change. Each fixture goes through exactly what a user's model goes through:

  1. validate – the spec is checked statically against the step, model and plot catalogs, as the API does before accepting a run;
  2. fit – a fit run on the in-process executor, honouring fit.mode (evaluate_then_refit included);
  3. score – every request in score_requests.yaml as a score run; requests that must fail are checked for their typed error code (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, UNSEEN_LEVELS, ...);
  4. evaluate – the holdout scored through the score path; the metrics must equal the ones computed at fit time;
  5. contract – the full check_model contract kit;
  6. plots – the spec's outputs.plots rendered from real outputs;
  7. expectations – the fixture's own checks (recovered effects, terminal state, ...).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
python -m mapi_conformance list
python -m mapi_conformance run                         # every fixture at size tiny
python -m mapi_conformance run --fixture e24 --fixture c08
python -m mapi_conformance run --size full --json corpus.json
make conformance                                       # the same as `run` at size tiny
make conformance FIXTURE=e33                           # one fixture
make conformance-full                                  # every fixture at size full
python -m mapi_conformance list --deferred             # plus the plan fixtures not ported yet

The runner prints one row per fixture and exits non-zero if any step failed:

fixture           model                           validate  fit  score   evaluate  contract  plots   expectations  ...  result
----------------  ------------------------------  --------  ---  ------  --------  --------  ------  ------------       ------
e02               tabular.hierarchical_glm@1.0.0  ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
c08               ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0             ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e24               ts.gaussian_hmm@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 15/15  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
xgb_store_demand  tabular.regressor@1.0.0         ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 16/16  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e33               mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0      ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 16/16  ok 4/4  ok                 PASS
pymc_marketing    mmm.pymc_marketing@1.0.0        ok        ok   ok 4/4  ok        ok 16/16  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS

--size tiny (the default, used by pytest -m conformance) keeps data small and MCMC short; --size full uses the spec's own fit settings and larger data.

docs.title: Through a running stack
docs.text:
The default runner skips the control plane. --stack drives the same fixtures through the API of a running stack (make dev), as a user does: spec → ingest → fit → score.

  1. The data, side tables and score payloads are uploaded as dataset versions (signed PUT, then a sandboxed ingest run).
  2. The spec, pointed at the uploads, is validated, created and fitted through the dispatcher, the runner and FINALIZING.
  3. Every score request runs against the registered model. An expected typed error may come from the failed run or from the API refusing the request up front.
  4. The holdout metrics and stored plots are checked on the model version.
  5. The bundle is downloaded through signed URLs with every hash verified, and goes through the fixture's check_fit.
python -m mapi_conformance run --stack http://127.0.0.1:8000 --fixture e33 --fixture xgb_store_demand
uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_corpus_stack.py   # E33, xgboost and sklearn (`make e2e`)

The contract kit does not run in this mode; it needs the plugin in-process.

docs.title: The fixtures
docs.text: Fixture Model Exercises e02 tabular.hierarchical_glm long layout, shuffled county labels, hyperprior new counties, LOO, CRN counterfactual c08 ts.hsgp_trend sentinel codes, max_extension from anticipated coords, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, contiguity e24 ts.gaussian_hmm padded + mask, terminal state, forecast and filter, relabelling, invalid LOO xgb_store_demand tabular.regressor pooled new stores, quantile aggregation refused, future-required covariates sklearn_store_demand sklearn.tabular_conformal the same panel with plain scikit-learn (histogram boosting, skops): split-conformal intervals, interval aggregation refused, pooled new stores e33 mmm.hierarchical_geo FX (supplied) and holiday (pinned) side tables, split after resample, per-market lag context, new market from the hyperprior, weekly EUR plan via inputs_stage, CRN counterfactual (intervention and baseline-vs-scenario), derived quantities in EUR pymc_marketing mmm.pymc_marketing a model that owns scaling, carry-over and units; a scoring window equals the same weeks of the full series e84_lite choice.multinomial_logit a ragged household × trip panel with a text target, last_per_group split, products off the shelf, new households from the fitted spread, a price-rise counterfactual, next trips, categorical holdout metrics (hit rate against the naive guess, log score, Brier) guided_mmm mmm.hierarchical_geo the geo_mmm Guided template's draft with business priors (ROI, contribution share, baseline share) translated at fit time and a lift test in the likelihood, both true to the simulation; ROI, baseline share and lift checked against the truth; a forecast and the channel-off preset

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text:
The plan's corpus also lists fixtures that need plugins or run kinds that do not exist yet. They are listed in mapi_conformance.fixtures.DEFERRED with the reason, and a test keeps the plan's list, the fixtures and the deferrals in step:

Plan fixture Waits for E13 state-space a state-space plugin with the filter mode (vetted plugins, M4) E82-slim GP Bayesian optimisation the recommend mode and Campaign runs (M6) E45 a plugin for its model (vetted plugins, M4)

docs.title: Porting time
docs.text:
The M0 exit criteria ask for the porting time of every fixture (target: under one day each, model plugin plus fixture). It measures human effort, so it cannot be derived from the code or from commit timestamps; record it here when a fixture is ported or re-ported.

Fixture Porting time Recorded e02 not measured yet – c08 not measured yet – e24 not measured yet – xgb_store_demand not measured yet – sklearn_store_demand not measured yet – e33 not measured yet – pymc_marketing not measured yet –

docs.title: Add a fixture
docs.text:
Create a package conformance/src/mapi_conformance/fixtures/<id>/ and list <id> in fixtures/__init__.py.

data.py generates the data:

def generate(seed: int = 0, size: str = "tiny") -> tuple[xr.Dataset, dict[str, xr.Dataset]]:
    """The dataset and its side tables (name -> dataset)."""

def schema() -> DataSchema:            # optional: the raw schema (else inferred)
    ...

def payload_new_store(data, seed, size) -> xr.Dataset:   # optional payload builders
    ...

spec.yaml is an ordinary ModelSpec with the fit settings of a full run.

score_requests.yaml lists the requests to score. apiVersion, kind and model are filled in for you:

- name: forecast_with_new_store
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}}
  payload: new_store          # none | fit_data | "tail:<n>" | a payload_<name> builder
  drop_targets: true          # remove target variables from the payload (default)
  side_tables: true           # pass the fixture's side tables to the run (default)
  expect: {vars: [y_hat], sizes: {week: 4}, issues: [UNSEEN_LEVELS], groups: [summary]}
- name: quantiles_are_not_summed
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}, output: {aggregate: {over: [store_id]}}}
  payload: new_store
  expect_error: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED

expectations.py (optional) adds fixture-specific checks; raise AssertionError to fail:

TINY_FIT = {"tune": 150, "draws": 100, "chains": 2}       # fit overrides at size tiny
TINY_SETTINGS = {"m": 20}                                  # model-settings overrides
MODEL_CHECKS = None                                        # or a subset of check_model checks

def check_fit(bundle, data): ...
def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data): ...
def check_evaluate(tree, bundle, data): ...

A hook that declares a keyword ctx parameter also receives a FixtureContext: the seed, size, registry, side tables and results, the trees of the score requests that succeeded before this one. Use it to compare requests, as E33 does when it checks that a weekly EUR plan forecasts exactly what the raw daily path forecasts:

def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data, *, ctx):
    if name == "weekly_eur_plan" and "forecast_8w" in ctx.results:
        ...

A side table with score_policy: supplied must be named in each score request that replays its step (request.side_tables); the runner supplies the data under that name.

From Python, mapi_conformance.run_fixture("e24") returns a FixtureReport and run_corpus() a CorpusReport with .table() and .to_json().

docs.title: Deleting data and exporting it v0.4
docs.text: A tenant admin can export everything the workspace stored (GDPR access) and delete the whole workspace (GDPR erasure). Both need a signed-in session of a tenant admin: API tokens never administer a tenant. The HTTP operations are in the HTTP API reference; the settings are in the configuration reference.

docs.title: Export first
docs.text:
# queue the export (everything by default: metadata, datasets, models, audit, usage)
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
# poll it; once "ready", download_url is a signed link valid for 15 minutes
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports/exp_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0"
# every export of the workspace, newest first (any admin, any browser)
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports"

Settings > Data shows the newest export from that list, so another admin (or another browser) sees an export that is still being built and can download a finished one; the Python client has client.tenants.exports("acme").

The orchestrator builds the archive in the background (usually within a minute). It is a zip:

Path Content README.txt, manifest.json What is inside, with the size and SHA-256 of every file metadata/<table>.jsonl Every record of the workspace, one JSON object per line: projects, members, API tokens, datasets and versions (schemas, profiles), specs and revisions (YAML), runs, models and versions, plots, endpoints, webhooks…, up to MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES (256 MiB) in total; a table cut short is listed under skipped with the rows written datasets/<dataset>/v<n>/... The stored dataset objects, byte for byte, up to MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES (256 MiB) in total; the rest is listed in manifest.json under skipped with sizes and checksums models/<model>/v<n>/manifest.json, model_version.json The signed bundle manifest, lineage, diagnostics, scorecard and metrics of every model version audit/audit_events.jsonl, usage/cost_ledger.jsonl The workspace's audit log and metered usage

Credentials are never exported: token hashes, signing keys, nonces and webhook secrets are [redacted]. Records are read through the workspace's own row-level-security session, so an archive can only contain its own workspace's rows. One export runs at a time, at most MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY (3) a day (429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED otherwise); an archive is deleted after MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S (7 days). A suspended workspace, including one whose deletion is scheduled, can still export.

docs.title: Request the deletion
docs.text:
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"confirm": "acme", "reason": "closing the account"}'

confirm must repeat the tenant id. A deployment can also demand a recent sign-in (MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S: older sessions get 401 and sign in again). The platform's own tenant cannot be deleted.

The deletion is scheduled for the end of a grace period (MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S, 7 days). At once:

  • the workspace is suspended: everything stays readable, nothing new can be created or run, and nothing spends compute;
  • its unfinished runs are cancelled.

Until the grace period ends the admin can still export, and can cancel:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X DELETE "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion"

Cancelling gives the workspace back the status it had (unless an operator changed it in the meantime). The audit log records tenant.deletion_request and tenant.deletion_cancel.

docs.title: What happens when the grace period ends
docs.text:
The deletion becomes deleting. This cannot be undone:

  1. The tenant's status becomes deleting: every request for it is refused, for its members and its tokens alike (operators can still read the deletion's progress).
  2. Its API tokens are revoked, and the browser sessions of people who belong to no other workspace are ended. Components that hand out links (webhooks, embed links) revoke theirs.
  3. Unfinished runs are cancelled again, and the purge waits for them to stop (at most MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S, one hour). A run that still has not stopped after that could keep uploading results under the workspace's prefix while its signed upload links are valid (its timeout plus 30 minutes), so the purge then waits for those links to expire before it deletes anything; the queue store's detail says until when.
  4. Exports that are queued or still being built are cancelled (state failed). The purge waits for a build in progress to end (at most its MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S lease); a cancelled build never uploads its archive, and deletes one that landed after the purge listed the objects.

Then the purge goes store by store, and GET /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion shows each one's progress:

Store What is purged queue Background jobs of the tenant's runs and their bootstrap objects database Every record of the workspace in every table, children before parents. People who belonged only to this workspace are deleted too object_store Every object under t/<tenant>/ in the quarantine, runs, bundles and data buckets: uploads, run scratch, model bundles, dataset versions, export archives logs Not purged (see below) webhooks The tenant.deletion.completed webhook is sent to the endpoints registered before the purge

When every store is done the deletion is purged, and the audit log gets the tombstone event tenant.purged (by tenant id, without content).

docs.title: What is kept, and why
docs.text: Record Kept Audit log 1 year after deletion, pseudonymised: actor ids and keyed digests of client addresses, no content Cost ledger 7 years for tax law: amounts and run ids, no content The deletion's own record Its ids, dates and counts per store The tenant id A tombstone row (status deleting, no name) so the id is never reused Sign-up records Only the keyed digests used against repeated abuse; the e-mail, name and organisation are erased Platform logs Not purged: see below

docs.title: Retention locks
docs.text: Model bundles live in a bucket with a retention policy (Terraform bundle_retention_days, 30 days; locked in production). An object younger than that cannot be deleted by anyone. The purge records each such object with the time it may be deleted (time_created plus MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS), shows object_store as running with a plain explanation, and resumes on its own when the retention expires. Everything else is gone already, and the workspace stays inaccessible.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Cloud Logging entries cannot be deleted one by one, so a deletion does not purge logs. The platform keeps tenant content out of them: structured log lines carry tenant, project, run and request ids and keyed digests of client addresses, never request bodies, data or tracebacks of tenant code. They expire with their bucket's retention: Terraform sets the control project's _Default log bucket to log_retention_days (30 days by default, infra/terraform/modules/control/logging.tf). The run-event sink only forwards events to Pub/Sub and stores nothing. So 30 days after a deletion, its logs are gone too.

docs.title: When a store fails
docs.text:
A failing store makes the deletion failed. The orchestrator retries it with back-off (5 minutes doubling up to 6 hours) up to MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS (8) times; after that an operator looks at last_error in the logs and restarts it:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST \
  "$API/v1/admin/tenants/acme/deletion/retry"

The purge is idempotent: a retry starts where the last pass stopped.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text:
• The scheduler runs in the orchestrator (mapi-server worker) every MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S; purges and exports run as procrastinate jobs on the lifecycle queue, one at a time per deletion or export, and are re-queued if a worker dies.
  • An export build may take MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S (one hour) and then fails. An export still running five minutes after that belongs to a process that died (an OOM kill, a lost orchestrator): the scheduler builds it once more, and fails it if that build dies too, so a workspace can always ask for a new export. The archive is built in memory, so size the orchestrator for MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES plus MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES.
  • Database rows are deleted through the tenant's own row-level-security session wherever the request-path role may delete them, so a purge cannot touch another tenant's rows.
  • Components that own credentials or links of a tenant register a mapi_server.services.trust.TenantRevoker; the webhooks component provides the DeletionNotifier that sends tenant.deletion.completed.

docs.title: Endpoints and webhooks v0.4
docs.text:
An endpoint gives a model version a stable name, endpoint://<project>/<alias>, that other applications call. A better version can then be promoted, or a bad one rolled back, without changing any of them. A webhook tells another application when something happens in a project: a run finished, a model version is ready, an endpoint changed.

This guide does both with curl. The concepts behind them (the promotion gate, signatures, the SSRF policy) are in Integrations, and every operation is listed in the HTTP API reference.

The examples assume MAPI_TOKEN holds an API token, MAPI_PROJECT the <tenant>/<project> it acts in, and API the base URL:

export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
api() { curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: $MAPI_PROJECT" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$@"; }

docs.title: Promote a model version
docs.text:
PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} creates the alias, or points it at another version. Name the version by reference or by id:

api -X PUT "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod" \
  --data '{"model": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3", "expected_revision": 0}'

{
  "alias": "geo-mmm-prod",
  "ref": "endpoint://growth/geo-mmm-prod",
  "model_ref": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3",
  "revision": 1,
  "evaluation_policy": {"fit_mode": "evaluate_then_refit", "schema_change": "block"},
  "gate": {"outcome": "allowed", "scorecard_overall": "pass", "reasons": []},
  "overridden": false
}

expected_revision makes the call safe against a colleague promoting at the same time: 0 means "the alias must be new", N means "it must still be at revision N" (409 CONFLICT otherwise). Sending the same body again changes nothing.

The promotion gate decides whether the version may serve:

The version Answer Its scorecard passes, it was fitted with evaluate_then_refit, and it takes the input the endpoint's callers send Promoted Its scorecard warns, or it has none; it was never scored on a holdout (no data.split), or a check its guided template asks for could not run (NOT_EVALUATED) 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED, unless a project admin overrides Its scorecard fails, the fit was interrupted, or it was fitted train_only 409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED It expects different input (a dim removed, a new required variable, ...) Blocked by default; the endpoint's schema_change policy can make it warn or allow

Relaxing the endpoint's evaluation_policy (schema_change from block to warn or allow, or fit_mode to train_only) disarms the gate as an override does, so only a signed-in project admin may send a laxer policy; an endpoints:promote token gets 403 FORBIDDEN (the same or a stricter policy is fine). The promotion's audit event records the policy before and after.

Each refusal lists the gate's reasons in the problem's errors, with the scorecard check that caused it:

{
  "code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED",
  "status": 409,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED", "severity": "warning",
     "message": "Holdout error: Forecasts were off by 14%.",
     "context": {"gate_code": "SCORECARD_WARN", "check": "holdout.mape"}}
  ]
}

Evaluated, then refitted. An endpoint serves versions whose fit evaluated the holdout and then refitted on all the data (fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, the default of every spec), so forecasts start from the full history. Both happen inside the one fit run; the version's lineage links the evaluation. To serve an exploration fit, give the endpoint the policy {"fit_mode": "train_only"}.

docs.title: Overriding
docs.text:
An override is a human decision. A signed-in project admin sends override: true with a reason, from the web app or a session; no API token can override, whatever its scopes:

{"model_version_id": "mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0", "override": true,
 "reason": "Holdout MAPE is high because of the strike in week 41; accepted by the CMO."}

The reason is kept in the endpoint's history and in the audit log (endpoint.promote_override), next to the checks that warned.

docs.title: History and rollback
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/history"
api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/rollback" \
  --data '{"reason": "v4 over-forecasts after the price change"}'

A rollback points the alias at the version of an earlier revision (by default the last one that served another version; to_revision picks one). It is a new revision, audited with its reason; the gate is not run again. DELETE /v1/endpoints/{alias} removes the alias and its history - model versions stay.

docs.title: Score an endpoint
docs.text:
Ask the endpoint what it expects. The answer has the input schema frozen at promotion and an example body that validates:

api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/schema" | jq .example

{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
 "future_covariates": "carry_last", "output": {"kind": "expected", "summary": ["mean", "hdi_90"]}}

Then score. Prefer: wait=60 waits up to a minute: 200 with links to the outputs if the run finished, 202 with the run otherwise. A finished answer also carries the numbers inline in summary: one table per output, the coordinate columns then one column per statistic (the mean and the 90% HDI by default), so a spreadsheet or a shell script needs no zarr or Arrow reader. A result above 100,000 cells is cut short (truncated); score.zarr.zip always has everything.

"summary": {"tables": [{"variable": "revenue",
                        "columns": ["geo", "time", "mean", "hdi_90_lower", "hdi_90_upper"],
                        "rows": [["de", "2026-01-05", 1520.4, 1402.1, 1633.9]]}],
            "truncated": false}

api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score" \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H 'Idempotency-Key: plan-2026-11' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last"}'

To collect a result that took longer, send the same call again with the same Idempotency-Key: it answers for the run the first call started, waiting again if you ask. This works with the narrowest token there is, score:<alias>, which can read and score one endpoint and nothing else.

docs.title: Inline data
docs.text:
data and scenario can be dataset:// references, or small datasets sent inline as XrJSON (the shape of xr.Dataset.to_dict(), up to 5 MB each), so scripts and spreadsheets need no upload. A caller that cannot read datasets (a score:<alias> token) sends data inline or names the dataset the endpoint's model was fitted on; any other reference, and a missing one, gets the same 403 FORBIDDEN, so such a token can neither score the project's other datasets nor find out which exist:

{
  "mode": "predict",
  "data": {
    "coords": {
      "market": {"dims": ["market"], "data": ["de"]},
      "channel": {"dims": ["channel"], "data": ["search", "tv"]},
      "date": {"dims": ["date"], "data": ["2025-12-30"]}
    },
    "data_vars": {
      "spend_local": {"dims": ["market", "channel", "date"], "data": [[[1200.0], [5300.0]]]}
    }
  }
}

Before anything runs, the server checks the payload against the endpoint's input contract - every variable must be one the endpoint takes, with its dims; coordinates must be dims of the input; a predict call must send every input - and then runs the usual coordinate checks (modes, horizon, unseen levels, future covariates). It reads only the payload's coordinates for that: the values are decoded inside the sandboxed score run, never by the API. The score run gives each coordinate the type of the model's dim (dates arrive as ISO strings), so an inline payload scores exactly like the same rows uploaded as a dataset.

The input contract (GET …/schema → snapshot.input_schema) names dims and variables the way the spec does after data.bind: if the spec binds time: week and y: revenue, an inline payload sends a time dim, not week. The score run renames the payload to the dataset's own names before scoring, and results come back under the dataset's names, as for any score. POST …/validate runs the same checks and answers 200 with the issues, without running anything.

Bodies above 10.25 MB are refused with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; upload larger data as a dataset and reference it.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/snippets?language=python&language=curl"

returns ready-to-run code for Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Google Sheets (Apps Script) and Atlas, with this server's address and the endpoint's example payload. base_url= puts another address in (a public one, behind a proxy). Snippets read the token from MAPI_TOKEN and never contain a secret. From Python, Client().endpoint("geo-mmm-prod").score(ds) sends an xr.Dataset and returns one (The Python client); the CLI has mapi endpoints score, and Atlas optimises budgets against an endpoint.

docs.title: Tokens for integrations
docs.text:
Scope For score:geo-mmm-prod An application that scores this endpoint (reads its schema and snippets too) score:* Every endpoint and model of the project endpoints:promote CI that promotes passing versions and rolls back (never overrides) webhooks:manage Managing webhooks from a script

Every call counts against the token's own rate limit (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After) and every score run against its vCPU-second budget (429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED), on top of the tenant's.

docs.title: Subscribe
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks" \
  --data '{"url": "https://hooks.example.com/mapi",
           "events": ["run.succeeded", "run.failed", "endpoint.promoted"]}'

The answer holds the signing secret, whsec_…. It is the only time you see it: store it with the receiver. Managing webhooks needs the project admin role (or a webhooks:manage token of an admin): deliveries reveal what a project is doing.

The URL must be https on port 443 or 8443 and name a public host: the server resolves it and refuses (422 WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED) any host with a private, loopback, link-local, metadata or otherwise internal address. It checks again at every delivery and connects only to the address it checked, so a DNS answer that changes later cannot point a delivery inside the platform.

docs.title: What a delivery looks like
docs.text:
POST /mapi HTTP/1.1
Host: hooks.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: mapi-webhooks/1
Mapi-Signature: t=1792000000,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd
Mapi-Event-Id: evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0
Mapi-Event-Type: run.succeeded
Mapi-Webhook-Id: whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0
Mapi-Delivery-Id: whd_01jaf3m1n2p3q4r5s6t7v8w9x0

{"api_version":"v1","created":"2026-10-15T09:30:00Z","data":{"kind":"fit","model_version_id":"mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0","run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"succeeded"},"id":"evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0","project":"growth","tenant":"acme","type":"run.succeeded"}
Event data run.succeeded, run.failed run_id, kind, state, model_version_id; failures add failure_class and code model.version.ready model_id, model_version_id, ref, scorecard_overall endpoint.promoted alias, ref, revision, model_version_id, overridden, action (promote or rollback) score.completed run_id, model_version_id, outputs (names), and endpoint (alias, ref, revision) when it came through one tenant.deletion.completed deletion_id, requested_at, completed_at

Events are recorded in the same database transaction as what caused them, so an event is sent if and only if it happened. Delivery is at least once: deduplicate on Mapi-Event-Id. Envelopes carry ids and states, never data, signed URLs or secrets; fetch results with the API.

No plot attachments. Webhooks do not attach rendered plots (the platform plan had them as an option). A receiver is a third party reached over the internet, often a chat or automation service that logs or forwards what it gets, so a chart - or a signed link to one - in the body would publish model results beyond the project. A receiver that wants a chart renders it with its own token when the event arrives: on model.version.ready, call POST /v1/plots:render with {"source": {"model_id": ..., "version": ..., "plot_id": "core.ppc_fan"}, "format": "png"} and Prefer: wait=60, then download the PNG from the answer's link (render runs need a token with runs:create).

docs.title: Verify it
docs.text:
Recompute the HMAC over the raw body before parsing it, compare in constant time, and refuse timestamps more than five minutes away from your clock:

PythonNode 
from mapi_client.webhooks import verify
from mapi_spec.errors import MapiError

def handle(raw_body: bytes, headers: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    try:
        event = verify(headers, raw_body, SECRET)  # a WebhookEnvelope
    except MapiError:
        return 401
    ...

Receiving webhooks has complete FastAPI and Flask receivers.

import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verify(rawBody, header, secret, now = Date.now() / 1000) {
  const parts = Object.groupBy(header.split(","), (p) => p.split("=")[0]);
  const t = Number(parts.t?.[0]?.split("=")[1]);
  if (!Number.isInteger(t) || Math.abs(now - t) > 300) return false;
  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  return (parts.v1 ?? []).some((p) => {
    const got = Buffer.from(p.split("=")[1] ?? "", "hex");
    return got.length === 32 && crypto.timingSafeEqual(got, Buffer.from(expected, "hex"));
  });
}

Answer any 2xx quickly and do the work afterwards: the platform waits at most 5 seconds and reads at most 256 KiB of the answer. Redirects are not followed.

docs.title: Retries, failures and replays
docs.text:
A delivery that does not get a 2xx is retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours (each with up to 10% jitter), 8 tries in all. An event that still could not be delivered counts as one failure of the webhook; after 20 such events in a row the webhook is disabled and says why (disabled_reason). A receiver that answers 410 Gone disables it at once. Both are audited (webhook.disabled). Fix the receiver, then turn it back on:

api -X PATCH "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0" --data '{"active": true}'

or, from the command line, mapi webhooks update whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0 --enable.

The delivery log has every delivery with its status (pending, retrying, succeeded, failed, blocked), the last response code, duration and the start of the answer:

api "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0/deliveries?status=failed"
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0/deliveries/whd_01jaf3m1n2p3q4r5s6t7v8w9x0:replay"

A replay sends the same event again (same event id) as a new delivery.

docs.title: Rotate the secret
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0:rotate-secret"

returns the new secret, once. For 24 hours deliveries carry two v1 signatures, one per secret, so the receiver can switch over without dropping any.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
Deliveries are sent by the worker (mapi-server worker), never by the API: a relay loop looks for due deliveries every MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S and hands each try to the webhooks procrastinate queue. Retries are scheduled in the database, so a worker that dies mid-delivery only delays it. The settings are in the configuration reference; the metrics (mapi_webhook_deliveries_total, mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total, mapi_webhooks_disabled_total, mapi_endpoint_promotions_total, mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total, ...) are listed in Observability.

For development, a receiver on your own machine is not a public host. Allow it explicitly - these settings are refused in the multi-tenant profile:

export MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST=localhost
export MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP=true   # only for the allow-listed hosts

docs.title: Your first model in the web app v0.2
docs.text:
This guide fits a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model (the corpus' E33 example) on the local stack and then uses it, entirely from the browser:

  1. upload daily spend and revenue per market and channel, an FX table and a holiday table;
  2. paste the model spec into the editor and let it validate as you type;
  3. fit it and follow the sampler live;
  4. read the sanity scorecard, the posterior predictive check and the channel decomposition;
  5. score an 8-week forecast, a market the model has never seen, and a weekly budget in EUR.

It takes about ten minutes, most of it reading. The fit itself uses tiny sampler settings and finishes in under a minute on a laptop.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Start the stack and leave it running (Local development):

make install
make dev                      # PostgreSQL, GCS shim, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

Port 8000 taken?

Move the API with export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010 before make dev. Every other command in this guide (make seed, make e2e) reads the same variable. The other three ports move the same way; see Port conflicts.

This guide clicks through every step, including the uploads. For the short path (make seed loads the data and the spec for you) see the quickstart; for every page of the app, The Expert web app.

Then write the demo files to a folder. Nothing is uploaded yet:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/
File What it is Upload it as eu_media_daily.zarr.zip 30 weeks of daily spend_local(market, channel, date) and revenue_local(market, date) for NL, DE and UK (UK in GBP) eu_media_daily fx_daily.zarr.zip Daily EUR per GBP, covering the fit window and the forecast horizon fx_daily holidays_eu.zarr.zip A daily holiday indicator holidays_eu eu_media_future.zarr.zip Planned daily spend for the 8 weeks after the data (no revenue) eu_media_future eu_media_future_fr.zarr.zip The same weeks plus FR, a market the model has not seen eu_media_future_fr eu_media_weekly_plan.zarr.zip A planner's budget: weekly spend in EUR eu_media_weekly_plan eu_media_window.zarr.zip The last four weeks of the data, for counterfactuals eu_media_window eu-geo-mmm.yaml The model spec, pointing at dataset://default/<name>@latest (paste it)

make seed does steps 1 and 2 for you through the HTTP API. This guide clicks through them.

docs.title: 1. Upload the data
docs.text:
Open Datasets → New dataset, name it eu_media_daily and create it. The upload panel opens: choose eu_media_daily.zarr.zip and press Upload and ingest. The browser sends the file straight to object storage through a signed URL; a sandboxed ingest run then opens it, checks it and stores an immutable, content-addressed version. The page refreshes on its own until the version is ready.

The schema came with the file: market allows new levels at score time (with a hyperprior), channel is fixed, and date may be extended into the future. revenue_local is the target, spend_local is spend, both in local currency. A CSV upload would ask you for the same mapping column by column.

Repeat for the other six files, using the names in the table above.

docs.title: 2. Write and validate the spec
docs.text:
Open Build → New spec, select everything in the editor and paste eu-geo-mmm.yaml. The editor validates as you type: the server resolves every dataset:// reference and step, checks the settings and propagates the schema through the pipeline without running anything. Problems appear as squiggles at the exact YAML path.

The pipeline panel shows what each step does to the data. to_eur converts both spend and revenue to EUR with the fx side table, weekly resamples days to weeks (only from this stage on does a week exist, so the train/holdout split sits right after it), and scale_spend, scale_y and lags learn state from the training weeks only. Open Schema after this step on any card to see the variables and dims at that stage.

Press Save spec. The spec becomes revision r1 of spec://default/eu-geo-mmm. (If you ran make seed before, that name is taken: change metadata.name first, or open the seeded spec under Build instead.)

docs.title: 3. Fit it
docs.text:
Press Fit. The run page follows the run over server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the run's supervisor read its one-time bootstrap object and deleted it, so the credentials it held are gone before any model code runs.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is expected on a laptop: the local executor cannot drop to a separate user for the model code. Containers and Cloud Run do.
  • The progress bar and message come straight from the sampler (chain 1/2: sampling 39/100).

fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit makes the run fit the training weeks, score the 8 holdout weeks through the normal scoring path, then refit on all the data, so the model you use has seen the latest weeks while its metrics are honest. When the run succeeds, the platform checks every file the run claims to have written against the storage's own checksums, copies them where the run cannot reach, and signs a manifest. Press Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 4. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The Overview tab opens on the sanity scorecard, the holdout metrics and what the model can do.

With 2 chains of 100 draws the sampler has not converged: R-hat above 1.01 and fewer than 200 effective samples are flagged as warnings, each with a suggested action. That is the point of the tiny settings; raise tune and draws (and use more chains) for a model you mean to use. Diagnostics lists the same checks per variable.

Plots has the recipes the spec asked for. Every plot renders inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from a separate origin (port 5174), so even a malicious plot spec could not read the app, its cookies or your data.

Fit and forecast compares the model's predictions for the holdout weeks with what happened: the line is the median, the bands are the 50% and 90% intervals, the dots are the actual weekly EUR revenue.

Contribution by component splits revenue over time into the baseline, each channel, seasonality and holidays, in EUR, with the totals and their uncertainty below. Response curves shows what an extra euro of spend returns per channel, and Sampler convergence has the trace and rank plots behind the scorecard. Provenance shows the signed manifest, every stored object with its generation, and the lineage: data and side table versions, spec hash, plugin, seed and library versions.

docs.title: 5. Score it
docs.text:
Press Score. The form only offers what this model supports, and the fitted preprocessing is replayed exactly: nothing is refitted.

An 8-week forecast. Keep mode forecast with 8 periods along time, set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1 and press Score. The fx side table defaults to the one the fit used; it covers the horizon, so the planned local-currency spend can be converted to EUR. The result shows a fan per market, then the outputs: the result tree (score.zarr.zip), its summary as a table, and a quick chart you can re-plot by any column.

A new market. Score again with dataset://default/eu_media_future_fr@v1. FR was never seen in training; its effects are drawn from the hierarchical prior over markets, so its band is visibly wider than the others'. The result's issues record an UNSEEN_LEVELS note saying so.

A weekly plan in EUR. Planners think in weekly euros, not daily local currency. Set Inputs enter at stage to weekly and Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_weekly_plan@v1. The request enters the pipeline after to_eur and weekly, so no FX table is needed. Because this plan is the same spend as the daily file, the forecast is identical to the first one, which is exactly what replaying the preprocessing promises.

A counterfactual. Choose mode counterfactual, set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_window@v1, add an intervention spend_local where channel=tv, multiply by 1.2, choose Predictive output and set Draws to 100 (with 0 draws you get the means, but not the uncertainty of the change). The result holds the baseline, the scenario and their difference, computed with common random numbers so the delta is not drowned in sampling noise.

docs.title: What was checked along the way
docs.text:
The same flow runs as two automated suites against the running stack (make e2e):

  • tests/e2e/test_m1_stack.py drives it through the Python client. It also verifies the manifest signature, that every bundle object sits in the bundles bucket at its signed generation, that the bundle reads back with all hashes intact, that the bootstrap object is gone, and that forged run events are refused.
  • apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts clicks through the pages above with Playwright and checks that the plot frame is an opaque origin with no access to its parent.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Marketing-mix models: the model, its priors, derived quantities and budget plots.
  • Spec format and the steps used here.
  • Web app and plot sandbox: every page and how plots are isolated.

docs.title: From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft v0.4
docs.text:
This guide follows the Guided data path over the HTTP API: pick a template, let the platform suggest which column answers which question, turn the answers into a draft (an ingest mapping plus a ModelSpec), upload the data with that mapping and save the spec. The web app's Guided screens and the Python client make exactly these calls. The concepts are in Guided mode.

Every call is project-scoped: send X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project> (or use a token bound to the project). The examples use the single-tenant development server.

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser or client
    participant API as API (JSON only)
    participant S as Sandbox (ingest run)
    B->>API: GET /v1/guided/templates
    B->>B: profile the file locally (ColumnProfile per column)
    B->>API: POST /v1/guided/detect-roles {template_id, columns}
    API-->>B: RoleSuggestions (answers pre-filled, reasons)
    B->>API: POST /v1/guided/drafts {answers, columns}
    API-->>B: GuidedDraft (mapping, spec, YAML, issues)
    B->>API: POST /v1/datasets/{id}/uploads, PUT the file, POST …/versions {mapping}
    API->>S: ingest run (parse, caps, columns.json)
    B->>API: POST /v1/specs {yaml}

docs.title: 1. Pick a template
docs.text:
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/templates | jq '.items[] | {id, title, plugin}'
Template Built-in model Data it expects geo_mmm mmm.hierarchical_geo one row per market and week: the result, one spend column per channel, optional controls weekly_forecast ts.hsgp_trend one row per week (or day): the series to forecast store_demand tabular.regressor one row per store and week: units sold and the drivers (price, promotions) customer_choice choice.multinomial_logit one row per household and shopping trip: the product chosen and one price (and promotion) column per product

GET /v1/guided/templates/{id} returns one template with its questions, the spec template, the scorecard checks and the x-ui-level of every field.

docs.title: 2. Let the platform suggest the answers
docs.text:
The browser profiles the upload locally, so nothing hostile reaches the servers just to be previewed, and sends one ColumnProfile per column:

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/detect-roles -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "template_id": "geo_mmm",
  "columns": [
    {"name": "Week", "dtype": "date", "n_rows": 520, "n_distinct": 104, "detected_freq": "W-SUN"},
    {"name": "Region", "dtype": "string", "n_rows": 520, "n_distinct": 5},
    {"name": "Revenue", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 10, "max": 90000},
    {"name": "TV_Spend", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 0, "max": 50000},
    {"name": "Search_Spend", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 0, "max": 20000},
    {"name": "avg_price", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 1, "max": 3}
  ]}' | jq '.questions[] | {question_id, answer}'

Each question comes back with ranked candidates, a confidence and a reason_plain ("named like a revenue column; never negative"). The heuristics look at names (split into words, matched against each question's keywords), types, the number of distinct values (labels suit dims), ordered dates and trip numbers, negative or constant values (bad spend candidates) and mostly empty columns. A column answers at most one question; required questions without a good candidate come back as warnings in issues.

docs.title: From a stored dataset
docs.text: Instead of columns, name a stored version: {"template_id": "geo_mmm", "dataset": "dataset://growth/eu_media@v2"}. Every ingest run since v0.4 writes columns.json - the profile of each uploaded column, computed in the sandbox - and detection reads it (also downloadable as GET /v1/datasets/{id}/versions/{v}/artifacts/columns.json). For an MFF upload the profiles are those of the pivoted table: Period, the key columns that vary and one column per VariableName, so TV_Spend answers the spend question. Versions ingested before v0.4 (and zarr or netCDF uploads) fall back to their dims and variables, read from the stored schema and summary. Either way the API reads only JSON metadata, never the data.

docs.title: 3. Turn the answers into a draft
docs.text:
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/drafts -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "template_id": "geo_mmm", "name": "eu-geo-mmm", "dataset": "eu_media",
  "answers": {"kpi": "Revenue", "date": "Week", "geo": "Region",
              "spend": ["TV_Spend", "Search_Spend"], "controls": ["avg_price"]},
  "columns": [ ...the same profiles... ]}'

The GuidedDraft holds:

  • mapping: the IngestMapping for the upload. Column names become safe dataset names (Avg Price → avg_price); spend columns become one spend variable along a new channel dim, labelled from the names (TV_Spend → tv; for the choice template price_cola and promo_cola both label product cola).
  • spec and yaml: the ModelSpec for the project, with fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit.
  • issues: answer warnings (a column whose type does not fit the question) and the static validator's findings. The draft is validated against the catalog with the schema its mapping promises, before any data exists - for example a control named Fourier would clash with the seasonality the template adds (/pipeline/4).

Impossible answers are 422 GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID pointing at /answers/<question>: a missing required answer, a column used twice, two columns that would get the same dataset name, a choice or number out of range.

For an MFF upload send "format": "mff": the answers then name Period, the MFF key columns and VariableName values, and the mapping uses the mff preset.

Nothing is stored. Upload the data with the draft's mapping and save the spec:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/datasets/$DS/versions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"upload_id\": \"$UPLOAD\", \"mapping\": $(jq .mapping draft.json)}"
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/specs -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"yaml\": $(jq .yaml draft.json)}"

docs.title: File formats and presets
docs.text:
Every upload is parsed in a sandboxed ingest run. Tabular uploads are CSV (comma, semicolon, tab or | separated, UTF-8, optionally gzip-compressed) or Parquet; zarr_zip and netcdf are self-describing.

Mapping What the ingest does dims, vars, wide one column per dim and variable; wide gathers one column per label into one variable along a new dim. Wide variables sharing a dim must use the same labels preset: mff (or format: mff) pivots the MFF long table: Period becomes the time dim, key columns with several values become dims, every VariableName a variable. With vars/wide, those pick and rename the pivoted variables like CSV columns. mff.combine joins key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) preset: bayesinsight an MFF table restricted to what BayesInsight's metadata.json allows: the allowed_* key values and the start_period/end_period range; necessary_variables must be present. A weekly period's weekday comes from the data preset: meridian Google Meridian's CoordToColumns contract on a wide table: time, geo, kpi (target), revenue_per_kpi, population, controls, and media/media_spend (and reach and frequency) along channel

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The ingest checks what a file declares before a parser allocates anything, and every cell after parsing (IngestJob sets the limits; the server's defaults are below).

Limit Default Checked rows 50 million CSV: parsing stops one row past it; Parquet: from its metadata columns 4,096 the CSV header or Parquet schema; MFF: distinct variables characters per cell or column name 4,096 (names: 256) every header and text cell decompression ratio 50 × the stored size gzip CSV (streamed), Parquet, zip archives, netCDF (decoded bytes); files that decode to less than 64 MiB are never refused for their ratio uncompressed size the ingest run's scratch budget: 3 GiB (class S), 6 GiB (M), 12 GiB (L) the same, as an absolute size; the class is the smallest whose dataset cap holds the upload dataset size 250 million values, and 8 bytes per value within the scratch budget the dense dataset a table pivots to (every combination of the dim labels, times the variables), checked before it is built (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE)

Dates with a UTC offset or a time zone (2024-01-07T00:00:00+01:00, a tz-aware Parquet timestamp) are read as the local date and time they name, the offset dropped, so midnight labels stay on their day; the ingest reports it as an info issue.

bzip2, xz and zstd compressed uploads are refused. Every refusal is one plain-language message and a suggested action, for example:

Problem Message Suggested action a mapped column is missing column 'week' (dim 'week') is not in the upload Did you mean 'Week'? repeated rows 52 rows repeat a (week) combination Columns such as 'Region' vary within a combination: map them as dims too, or aggregate the rows first. text in a spend column column 'TV' ('spend' for 'tv') has 3 cells that are not numbers Use plain numbers without currency signs or thousands separators. not UTF-8 the upload is not UTF-8 text Save the file as 'CSV UTF-8' (in Excel: File > Save As > CSV UTF-8). a decompression bomb the gzip file expands to more than … bytes Upload the CSV uncompressed, or split it into several files. dims that rarely repeat the mapped dims span 100,000 store x 100,000 day = 10,000,000,000 combinations, so the dataset would hold … values Most combinations have no row: map fewer columns as dims (keep the others as variables), use a long layout with one id dim, or split the upload.

A failed ingest marks the dataset version failed; its issues carry the messages and the run's events carry them as diagnostics with message_plain and suggested_action. Cell values are only ever quoted in untrusted_text.

docs.title: Import a BayesInsight model
docs.text:
A BayesInsight project imports as a draft for the built-in geo MMM (the default target) or, with "target": "mmm.bayesinsight", for the dedicated BayesInsight model (below):

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/import/bayesinsight -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{
  \"name\": \"bi-import\", \"dataset\": \"bi_mff\",
  \"model_def\": $(cat model_def.json), \"metadata\": $(cat data/metadata.json)}"

The mapping uses the bayesinsight preset: the media variables become spend along channel, the controls and the KPI become variables, and the key columns of row_ids (without Period) are joined into one geo dim. The spec carries every feature that has an equivalent, with BayesInsight's own distributions where they exist:

BayesInsight Geo MMM spec adstock: delayed / geometric adstock.kind, 12 lags (BayesInsight's l_max) adstock_prior (Delayed) alpha ~ Beta(mu=retention_rate_mean, nu=retention_rate_std), theta ~ Exponential(lag_max), per channel media_transform: hill / linear saturation.kind: hill / none media_transform_prior (Hill) half ~ LogNormal(log K_ave, log(K_std / K_ave + 1)); slope ~ Gamma with the mean and sd of BayesInsight's 1 + Exponential media random_coeff_dims pooling: partial (fixed_ind_coeff_dims: none; neither: complete) normalization: Global Standardize a core.standardize step over time and geo season core.fourier with its period and n_fourier localtrend a core.trend control (warned: an approximation)

Everything without an equivalent is listed as an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning at its pointer, so nothing is dropped silently: non-Normal likelihoods, coefficient and intercept priors (stated in KPI units, which mean something else on the mean-scaled KPI - state them as business priors instead), Weibull adstock, S-shaped curves, sign constraints on controls, time and non-linear transforms, and per-dim random effects of controls. A model that cannot run at all is 422 IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED: no single exog KPI, no media variable, variable names that do not match the metadata's row_ids, or variables split into several series by a key column that is not a row id.

docs.title: Importing for mmm.bayesinsight
docs.text:
"target": "mmm.bayesinsight" drafts the dedicated built-in model instead, which fits BayesInsight's model as model_def.json defines it - nothing above needs an equivalent:

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/import/bayesinsight -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{
  \"name\": \"bi-sales\", \"dataset\": \"bi_mff\", \"target\": \"mmm.bayesinsight\",
  \"model_def\": $(cat model_def.json), \"metadata\": $(cat data/metadata.json)}"
  • Data. The bayesinsight preset with every row id besides Period as a panel dim of its own (Geography → geo, Product → product, kept even with a single label, as BayesInsight keeps it). A panel dim is new_levels (pooled), or fixed when some coefficient is estimated separately per level of it (fixed_ind_coeff_dims). Variables keep their MFF names, made safe (Sales → sales).
  • Spec. The KPI is bound to y, the media get a 12-lag core.lag_tensor with pad: nan, and model.settings carries model_def plus the map from every analytic name (TV_Total_Total_Total) to its variable. Priors stay in the KPI's own units.
  • Issues. What the plugin cannot run falls back to BayesInsight's own default with an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning at its pointer: an MvNormal likelihood (fitted with independent Normal errors), time transforms, priors with unknown families or parameters, coefficient dims that are not row ids, keys a variable type does not have. Faithful but surprising behaviour is an info issue: a KPI without a likelihood is fitted as Poisson, random_coeff_dims with partial_pooling_sigma: 0 pool nothing, signs on controls are enforced, and carry-overs and curves that BayesInsight's code cannot run are fitted as documented in the models reference.
  • Refusals (422 IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED): no single exog KPI, no media or control variable, names that do not match the row ids, a series split by a key column that is not a row id, or a variable whose safe name is taken.

The draft is validated against the catalog like the geo MMM's.

docs.title: Locking a project to Guided mode
docs.text:
A project admin locks a project in the web app (Settings > Mode > Lock … to Guided mode) or with PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project} {"guided_locked": true} (audited as project.guided_lock). Members below admin then see the Guided screens only, and their spec writes (POST /v1/specs and new revisions) must stay Guided specs:

  • the spec names its template in metadata.labels.guided (drafts do) and uses that template's plugin;
  • fields the template marks advanced or hidden keep their values: a revision may not change them from its parent, and a new spec has the template's values wherever the template fixes them (for geo_mmm: the pipeline, the adstock and saturation settings, the fit settings and the execution block);
  • answers, basic settings (such as pooling), business priors and lift tests may change.

Anything else is 403 FORBIDDEN with one issue per offending pointer and the suggestion to ask an admin. Admins, POST /v1/specs:validate, runs and scoring are not affected, and the lock does not reach integrations' score calls.

docs.title: Guided modelling: priors, lift tests and the scorecard v0.4
docs.text:
This guide explains what happens behind the Guided-mode tasks of Guided mode when the model is a marketing-mix model (mmm.hierarchical_geo): how beliefs in business units become model-space priors, how experiment results calibrate a fit, how the sanity scorecard is measured, and which views the what-if sliders, forecasts and counterfactuals read. Everything that touches data runs in the sandbox; the control plane only validates JSON.

Task Where it runs What it writes Business priors → model-space priors a translate_priors run priors.json (PriorTranslationResult), plots.json Lift-test calibration inside the fit the posterior (lift_tests__model), learned.calibration Sanity scorecard at the end of the fit scorecard.json (Scorecard), stored on the model version What-if sliders at the end of the fit ui/grids/response_curves.json (ResponseGridView) Forecast a forecast score run ui/guided/forecast.json (ForecastView) and a fan chart with the split line Counterfactual a counterfactual score run ui/guided/counterfactual.json (CounterfactualView)

docs.title: Business priors
docs.text:
A business prior states a belief about one channel in the units people think in:

calibration:
  business_priors:
    channels:
      tv:     {roi: [1.5, 4.0], credibility: 0.8}           # "80% sure each euro returns 1.5 to 4"
      search: {contribution_share: [0.05, 0.15], credibility: 0.9}
    baseline_share: {share: [0.5, 0.8], credibility: 0.8}   # KPI without any media

docs.title: From beliefs to priors: the math
docs.text:
The model's contribution of channel c over the fit window, in KPI units, is

C[c] = sum over geos g and periods t of  kpi_scale[g, t] * beta[g, c] * S[g, c, t]

where kpi_scale converts model units to KPI units (the pipeline's fitted scaling, read through its inverse), beta[g, c] is the channel effect in geo g and S the carried-over, saturated spend, a function of the adstock and saturation parameters. The two business quantities are

ROI[c]   = C[c] / spend[c]       spend[c]: the channel's total spend over the window
share[c] = C[c] / Y              Y:        the observed KPI total over the window

The translation gives the median channel effect a log-normal prior, beta_channel[c] = exp(mu[c] + sigma[c] * eps[c]). With partial pooling beta[g, c] = beta_channel[c] * exp(beta_sigma[c] * z[g, c]), so

log ROI[c] = mu[c] + sigma[c] * eps[c] + log K[c] - log spend[c]
K[c]       = sum over g, t of  kpi_scale[g, t] * exp(beta_sigma[c] * z[g, c]) * S[g, c, t]

(Without pooling every geo draws its own effect and the log-sum runs over geos; with complete pooling z = 0.) Two facts make the solve exact up to Monte Carlo error:

  • mu[c] only shifts log ROI[c]: every term is proportional to exp(mu[c]);
  • K[c] depends only on the other priors (adstock, saturation, pooling spread), which are independent of beta_channel, so it is sampled once, with common random numbers.

The stated range [L, H] held with credibility p fixes the q = (1 - p) / 2 and 1 - q quantiles of log ROI[c]. Write R(sigma) for log ROI[c] with mu[c] = 0. Then

  1. sigma[c] solves Q[1 - q](R(sigma)) - Q[q](R(sigma)) = log(H / L) by bisection, vectorised over channels (the interval widens with sigma);
  2. mu[c] = (log L + log H) / 2 - (Q[q] + Q[1 - q])(R(sigma[c])) / 2 centres it.

A share range works the same way with Y in place of spend[c]. Edge cases are reported as issues, never hidden:

  • if the other priors alone already make the interval wider than stated, sigma[c] stops at its floor (0.02) and a warning says so - the reported coverage shows by how much the range is missed;
  • a range starting at 0 is read as [H / 20, H] (a log-normal has no mass at zero);
  • a channel the data does not have, or a ROI for a channel without spend, is an error.

Channels without a belief keep their prior, refitted as the log-normal with the same 5% and 95% quantiles, so beta_channel stays one per-channel log-normal.

The baseline share (intercepts plus controls) is linear in the population mean of the geo intercepts m: B = a * (m + s * eps) + E, so the same two-step solve runs in linear space and gives intercept: {distribution: Normal, mu: m, sigma: s}. When the geo spread and the control effects alone are wider than the stated range, their priors (intercept_sigma, gamma_control) are narrowed by a common factor first, and an info issue says by how much.

Amounts only translate through linear preprocessing (mean_scale, max_abs_scale, currency conversion). A log1p or standardize step on the KPI or spend refuses the translation with CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

docs.title: The prior-translation run
docs.text:
Ask for a translation while drafting - from an unsaved document or a saved revision:

curl -X POST "$MAPI/v1/guided/prior-translations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spec_id": "spc_…", "revision": 2, "draws": 500,
       "business_priors": {"channels": {"tv": {"roi": [1.5, 4.0], "credibility": 0.8}}}}'

The API checks the beliefs statically first (channels against the dataset's levels, shares that cannot add up, BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID; a model without the business_priors capability, CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED) and answers 202 with the queued run. The run fits the pipeline's preprocessing on all of the data (the scales a production refit learns), solves, and samples the translated priors afresh for the preview:

GET /v1/guided/prior-translations/{run_id} returns, once done, the PriorTranslationResult:

  • priors: the model-space priors in the settings.priors form, to write at apply_at (/model/settings/priors; mapi_spec.calibration.apply_prior_translation does it and records the run in calibration.prior_translation_run);
  • preview: ROI and contribution-share distributions per channel, the baseline share and a KPI fan in business units against the observed KPI;
  • coverage: the prior mass inside each stated range - close to the stated credibility when the translation is faithful;
  • issues: everything above in plain words, plus lift tests whose implied ROI falls outside the prior's 90% range.

The run's plots (GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots) are mmm.prior_beliefs (each channel's prior interval over the range you stated) and core.prior_predictive (the KPI the priors can generate, against your data).

A spec that carries business_priors without a recorded translation run is translated at fit time instead, with the same solve over the training data's scales; the priors used are in the model's learned.calibration.translated_priors.

docs.title: Business priors for mmm.pymc_marketing
docs.text:
The pymc-marketing adapter takes business priors too. pymc-marketing scales the KPI by its maximum (target_scale) and each channel by its maximum, and every curve it offers here is beta * g(adstock(x)) (or adstock(beta * g(x)) with adstock_first: false), beta being its saturation_beta prior over (*dims, channel). A channel's contribution in KPI units is therefore

C_c = target_scale * sum over panel cells k of beta[k, c] * A[k, c],
A[k, c] = sum over periods t of g(...)[t, k, c]

and A depends on the adstock and curve priors only. The translation draws A from pymc-marketing's own model - prior draws of channel_contribution / beta - so its scaling, carry-over padding and curves are exactly the fit's, and then solves as above for a log-normal saturation_beta with one mu and sigma per channel (drawn independently per panel cell, as pymc-marketing draws it): a bisection on sigma matches the range's width at its credibility, mu centres it. The baseline share is linear in the intercept (intercept ~ Normal(m, s) per cell, B = a (m + s zbar) + E with a = target_scale * T * cells / Y and E the controls' and seasonality's share). pymc-marketing's default seasonality prior (Laplace(0, 1) on the scaled KPI) is wide, so when E alone spreads the baseline share over more than 80% of the range, the gamma_control and gamma_fourier priors are narrowed by a common factor first - their contributions are linear in them, so the spread shrinks by the same factor - and an info issue says by how much.

The priors land in the adapter's settings.priors (saturation_beta, intercept, gamma_control, gamma_fourier, in pymc-marketing's scaled units), which it hands to pymc-marketing as model_config priors; the preview, coverage and plots are the same as for the geo MMM.

docs.title: mmm.bayesinsight: no business priors
docs.text: The BayesInsight model's coefficient priors are already statements in the KPI's own units (coeff_prior in model_def.json), so it does not declare business priors: state the ROI you believe directly as the media coefficient's prior. It does take lift tests (below).

docs.title: Lift tests
docs.text:
A lift test is calibration data: extra spend on one channel (optionally in one geo) during a window, and the incremental KPI it caused, with its uncertainty:

calibration:
  lift_tests:
    - id: tv-holdout-2026q2
      channel: tv
      geo: DE
      start: 2026-04-06
      end: 2026-05-03
      spend_delta: -120000      # TV off: the spend removed
      kpi_delta: -260000        # the revenue lost
      ci: [-380000, -140000]    # or se: 73000
      ci_level: 0.9

The fit adds one observation per test,

kpi_delta ~ Normal(lift, se)
lift      = sum over the test's geos g and periods t in W of
            kpi_scale[g, t] * beta[g, c] * (S[g, c, t](x + dx) - S[g, c, t](x))

where W are the model periods whose label lies in the window and dx is the extra spend in model units, spread over the window's cells in proportion to the channel's actual spend there (evenly when there was none) and carried over through the lag tensor within the window. Carry-over after the window is not counted: tests report the lift measured during the test. (pymc-marketing's add_lift_test_measurements uses the saturation curve alone; this version also carries the extra spend over.) The model's implied lift per draw is kept as lift_tests__model(lift_test); the KPI likelihood alone stays in log_likelihood, so elpd_loo is unchanged in meaning.

Tests are checked three times, each time where the information is:

  1. at submit, against the dataset version's summary: the channel and geo exist and the window lies inside the data (SCHEMA_INVALID at /calibration/lift_tests/<i>/…);
  2. in the sandbox, before fitting, against the raw data itself;
  3. at the model stage: the window must cover at least one model period, and a holdout (negative spend_delta) may remove at most the spend the data shows.

During evaluate_then_refit, a test whose window lies after the training periods, or that the end of the training periods cuts, is skipped by the evaluation fit (logged) and used by the production refit.

mmm.pymc_marketing accepts lift tests too, through pymc-marketing's own add_lift_test_measurements: each test becomes rows of its window's average spend, extra spend, lift and sigma per period, conditioned on the saturation curve (a Gamma on the absolute lift, pymc-marketing's model). With panel dims, a test must name its geo.

mmm.bayesinsight observes each test under its own likelihood: channel names a media variable (its analytic name, TV_Total_Total_Total, or its model-stage name), geo a label of the first panel dim (the test then covers every level of the other panel dims there), and

lift = sum over the test's cells p and periods t in W of
       mean(eta[p, t] + d_eta[p, t]) - mean(eta[p, t]),
d_eta[p, t] = coef[p] * sum over lags l of w[l] * (f(z + dz)[p, t, l] - f(z)[p, t, l])

with mean the likelihood's mean function (the identity for a Normal KPI, exp and the zero-inflation share for counts, exp(. + sigma^2 / 2) for a log-normal), f the media curve and z the indexed media - so the extra spend goes through BayesInsight's curve, then its carry-over, then the link. The extra spend is spread and carried over within the window as above; the implied lift is kept as lift_tests__model.

docs.title: The sanity scorecard
docs.text:
At the end of every fit the runner measures each check of the catalog it can answer and writes scorecard.json; the finalizer stores it on the model version (GET /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v} → scorecard) and the promotion gate reads it. A guided spec (metadata.labels.guided: <template>) runs its template's checks with its thresholds; any other spec runs the whole catalog.

Metric Measured on r_hat_max, ess_bulk_min the production posterior's free parameters (the plugin's convergence diagnostics) divergence_rate sample_stats.diverging, as a share of all draws mape, coverage_90 the holdout, through the score path (needs them in evaluate.metrics). metrics.json reports mape in percent (1.4 is 1.4%); the check compares it as a fraction (0.014 against 0.10/0.25) accuracy_lift choice models: the holdout hit rate (the most likely product is the one bought) minus that of always guessing the holdout's most common product (accuracy, accuracy_naive; the customer_choice template evaluates them) negative_roi_share, roi_max the response_curves grid at the actual spend: per channel the share of draws with a negative return, and the largest posterior-mean ROI max_channel_share, baseline_share a channel's (or the baseline's) share of baseline + every channel, posterior mean prior_overlap_max the overlap of prior and posterior draws of the model's media parameters (PyMCModel.prior_overlap_vars, forward-sampled at fit time; cheap) missing_fraction the raw dataset's numeric variables history_years the model stage's time dim, in years: its periods over the periods in a year at the dim's frequency (or the one its dates follow), so 105 days and 15 weeks both count as about 0.3 years spend_cv_min the raw spend per channel over time

A check that cannot be measured - no holdout split, no response curves, a non-MCMC model - is listed in skipped with the reason. Every item carries message_plain, message_expert (what was measured, on which parameter or channel), a suggested_action when it is not a pass and a docs_anchor back to the catalog.

docs.title: What-if grids and "Run exact"
docs.text:
Fits with response_curves write ui/grids/response_curves.json: per thinned draw (up to outputs.ui_draws, at most 500), channel and spend multiplier, the channel's total contribution over the fit window in KPI units, plus the spend at every grid point, the actual spend, the baseline (intercepts and controls) and the per-geo grids when they fit the size cap. The sliders interpolate it per draw (the contract).

"Run exact" compiles the scenario into a counterfactual score request with one multiply intervention per changed channel. At grid points the two agree per draw to float precision: the grid is computed from the same fitted curves, and linear preprocessing passes the multiplier through unchanged (packages/runner/tests/test_guided.py checks it).

docs.title: Future covariates
docs.text:
A forecast needs the future values of its covariates - spend, prices. Guided forecasts do not ask for an upload: ScoreRequest.future_covariates says how the runner extends the ones the payload lacks, per series, from the fitted history (the server passes the model's fit dataset to the score run as its history input):

Policy Future values supplied (default for API callers) from the request's data or scenario; missing ones are MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE carry_last (default in Guided mode) the last observed value of each series seasonal_naive the value one year earlier by date (52 weeks, 12 months, 365 days...), so the last observed year repeats even after a gap; a missing value steps back another year, and one missing in every year (or a history shorter than a year) falls back to carry_last with a warning zero zero - "no spend planned"

Values the payload does supply are never replaced, and interventions apply after the fill, so budget × k over a horizon scales the carried-forward spend. The score result's issues name what was filled.

docs.title: Forecast and counterfactual views
docs.text:
A forecast score run writes ui/guided/forecast.json (mapi.forecast/v1): the actual KPI over the fitted history (fan.observed), then the forecast quantiles after split_at (fan.values), summed over geos per draw before the quantiles are taken, and the KPI total over the horizon. Its core.ppc_fan plot shows the history and the dashed split line.

A counterfactual score run - for example a preset from mapi_spec.whatif.counterfactual_request such as channel off or budget × k - writes ui/guided/counterfactual.json (mapi.counterfactual/v1): the scenario, baseline and change totals, the change as a share of the baseline and a per-period band of the change. Scenario and baseline share their noise (common random numbers), so the change is precise even when the totals are uncertain.

Both views exist only for models whose outputs are posterior draws; other representations cannot be summed across geos.

docs.title: Your first analysis in Guided mode v0.4
docs.text:
Guided mode takes you from a spreadsheet to a trustworthy answer without writing YAML or knowing statistics: you pick what you want to learn, answer a few questions about your columns, say what you already believe, and the platform fits a model in a secure sandbox and explains what it found in plain words. Behind every screen sits the same ModelSpec that Expert mode edits (see Guided mode for the concepts).

This tutorial walks through a geo marketing mix: weekly revenue and media spend per market. It takes about ten minutes. To follow along without your own data, use the sample in the repository, apps/web/e2e/fixtures/guided-geo-mmm.csv (40 weeks, two markets, TV, search and social spend and an average price). The screenshots come from the web app in mock mode (pnpm --filter @mapi/web dev:mock), so the numbers are illustrative.

Every step has its own address

An analysis is saved as soon as its data is uploaded. Each step has its own URL (/guided/<analysis>/<step>), so you can bookmark it, send it to a colleague, close the browser during a fit, and pick up later from Guided → Continue where you left off.

docs.title: 1. Choose what you want to learn
docs.text:
A workspace you signed up for opens here. Elsewhere, switch the header to Guided (the choice is remembered for your account) or open Guided in the sidebar or from Start a guided analysis on Home. Each card is a template: the question it answers, the data it needs and what you can do with the result.
