Template Use it for Geo marketing mix What each channel adds to your results per market, ROI per channel, what-if budgets Weekly forecast One weekly or daily series, forecast with a likely range Demand by store Units per store and week from prices and promotions, with low and high estimates Customer choice Which product shoppers pick on each trip, and how prices shift the choice

Pick Geo marketing mix.

docs.title: 2. Your data
docs.text:
Give the analysis a name, then drop your file on the page (CSV or Parquet). Your file is read in your browser first: the page profiles every column (type, range, how often the dates repeat) and sends only that profile to the platform, which suggests which column answers which question. Nothing is uploaded until you press Upload and continue.

  • Each question shows the suggested column, how sure the suggestion is and why ("named like a revenue column; never negative"). Change any answer that is wrong; columns another question already uses are not offered twice.
  • The preview on the right labels each column with its role and draws a small line per series you picked, added up per week, so a column of zeros or a broken week is easy to spot.
  • MFF long tables (Period, Geography, VariableName, VariableValue, as BayesInsight uses) and Google Meridian tables (time, geo, kpi, <channel>_spend) are recognised automatically and the answers filled in from their standard names.
  • Parquet files are opened only inside the sandbox, so for them you type the column names.
  • More options holds the settings most people never change, such as how many of the latest weeks to hold back to test the model.

When every required question is answered the panel says Everything the model needs is answered. Upload and continue then creates the dataset, uploads the file to storage, starts the sandboxed check of the data and saves the analysis.

docs.title: 3. What you believe
docs.text:
If you already know something about your channels - from earlier studies, industry benchmarks or experiments - say so here. Everything on this step is optional.

  • Return on spend or Share of results: describe each channel either way. A range of 1.5 to 4 means "every euro spent brings back between 1.5 and 4 euros". How sure? sets how firmly the model should hold to the range.
  • Channels start unticked: without a view, the data decides alone. Tick a channel to give it a range (it starts from a wide, sensible one).
  • Results without any media (optional) is the share of results that would happen anyway.
  • Experiments you have run take lift tests or geo holdouts: the channel and market, the dates, how much spend changed and the measured change in results with its uncertainty. The model treats each as extra evidence.

Preview what this means runs a quick simulation in the sandbox and shows what your beliefs imply before any fitting: the range the model now believes for each channel you ticked (the shaded bar is the range you gave) and the results it would expect week by week. A sentence per channel says how much of the model's belief falls inside your range. Channels you left unticked are named below the charts but not drawn: the model starts them from a deliberately wide default, which is not a belief. If the expected results are far from your usual numbers, a belief is probably off.

Save and continue stores the beliefs in the analysis. If you previewed exactly these beliefs, the fit reuses the translation; otherwise it translates them itself.

docs.title: 4. Fit the model
docs.text:
Press Fit the model. The page follows the run live: what is happening in plain words, a progress bar, roughly how long is left and a Cancel button.

The model is first fitted without the latest weeks, to measure how well it forecasts weeks it has not seen, and then refitted on everything. You can leave the page; the fit carries on. Technical details opens the run in Expert mode.

docs.title: 5. Results and the sanity scorecard
docs.text:
• Headline numbers: how much of your results media drove, the channel with the best return, the forecast error on the held-back weeks and how many weeks fell inside the 90% range (close to 90% means the ranges are honest).
  • Per channel: spend, return per 1 spent and share of results. The bold number is the best estimate; the bracket and the bar show where the true value lies with 90% probability.
  • Charts: the model against your actual results, and how much each channel adds as its spend grows (the dot is what you actually spent).

The sanity scorecard groups its checks by the question they answer: did the model settle, does it forecast well, are the numbers believable, is the data good enough. Each check is Pass, Check or Fail, says what it found in plain words and, when it is not a pass, what to do about it.

Inspect in Expert mode opens the model's diagnostics for a closer look. The checks and their thresholds are listed in Guided mode.

If a check under Did the model settle? says Check or Fail, the page offers Fit again, more carefully: the same data and beliefs, fitted with longer and more careful sampling (it takes about twice as long). This usually fixes those checks; the settings it changes are hidden in Guided mode, so the button is the way to change them. In a project locked to Guided mode, a project admin presses it.

docs.title: 6. What if…
docs.text:
• Change the budget: move a channel's slider to spend more or less over the same period. The change in results updates as you move, with the range of likely outcomes. It is answered in your browser from response curves the fit precomputed for every posterior draw, so the range stays honest when several channels move at once.
  • Run exact asks the full model the same question (a real score run) and shows its answer under the instant one; they should be close.
  • Quick scenarios: what if a channel were turned off, or every budget changed by a percentage.
  • Forecast: how results may develop over the next weeks (or days, for daily data) if you carry on as in the latest ones, with the split between history and forecast marked. A weekly forecast reaches as far as the horizon you answered when you set it up; further needs a new fit with a longer horizon.

The sliders cover the range the fit precomputed (from nothing to three times what you spent).

docs.title: 7. Share
docs.text:
• Put the model live gives other tools a stable address (an endpoint) to ask the model questions. Before you press the button the page explains the promotion gate: a model whose checks all passed goes live straight away; one with checks to look at needs a project admin, who approves it with a short reason that is kept in the audit log; a model with a failed check cannot go live. See Integrations.
  • Share a chart creates a read-only link to one chart for a slide, a Notion page or a dashboard. The link is shown once, expires, and can be revoked. Only charts the platform itself drew can be shared (Embed a chart).
  • Once the model is live, Code for this endpoint opens its page in the Integrations hub on the Snippets tab (Google Sheets, Python, a notebook cell and more), and Create a token for it a key that may score only this endpoint (Connect Google Sheets uses both). The chart link can be revoked later under Plots and links.
  • Open the Integrations hub for spreadsheets, BI tools, scheduled exports and webhooks. In a project locked to Guided mode the hub stays in the navigation.

docs.title: View as YAML and Expert mode
docs.text:
Every step has View as YAML: the specification your answers produced, read-only. Edit in Expert opens it in the Expert editor, where any setting can change. Back in Guided mode (the Back to Guided mode link in the editor), your changes are kept as they are and the analysis shows Advanced settings applied, listing what was changed.

Projects locked to Guided mode

A project admin can lock a project to Guided mode. Members below admin then see only Guided screens - no Expert switch and no Expert pages in the navigation - and can change only the basic settings, their answers and their beliefs. See the persona lock.

docs.title: On a phone
docs.text: Every Guided screen works on a phone: the steps collapse to "Step 4 of 6" with a progress bar and the panels stack.

docs.title: What happens behind the screens
docs.text:
Step Calls Templates GET /v1/guided/templates Your data POST /v1/guided/detect-roles, POST /v1/guided/drafts, then POST /v1/datasets, the upload, POST /v1/datasets/{id}/versions and POST /v1/specs What you believe POST /v1/guided/prior-translations (preview), POST /v1/specs/{id}/revisions Fit POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (live progress), POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel Results GET /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v} (scorecard, metrics), its plots and ui/grids/response_curves.json What if… POST /v1/guided/requests:compile, then POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score Share PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}, POST /v1/plots, POST /v1/plots/{id}/embeds

From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft and Guided modelling make the same calls with curl.

docs.title: The HTTP API v0.2
docs.text:
Everything the web app, the CLI and the Python client do is a call to the versioned /v1 HTTP API. This guide does the main flow with curl and jq, so you can see every request. The script is docs/snippets/http_tour.sh; make e2e runs it against a live stack. The outputs below are from one of those runs, shortened.

Where What HTTP API reference Conventions, errors, pagination, idempotency, SSE and every endpoint with its DTOs OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, browsable, with every schema and example GET /openapi.json on a running API The same document, served by the API itself Error codes Every stable error code and its HTTP status

Start the stack and load the demo first: make dev, make seed, uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/ and uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future (see the quickstart).

From v0.3, make dev requires sign-in. Set MAPI_TOKEN to an API token (the web app's Tokens page, or mapi tokens create) and MAPI_PROJECT to the <tenant>/<project> it acts in. The script's api function then adds Authorization: Bearer … and X-Mapi-Project to every API call. It never sends them to signed storage URLs, which carry their own authorization. See authentication.

docs.title: Health and the catalog
docs.text:
API=${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}
api() {  # curl the API; signed in when MAPI_TOKEN is set (every multi-tenant stack, v0.3)
  if [ -n "${MAPI_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
      -H "X-Mapi-Project: ${MAPI_PROJECT:-default/default}" "$@"
  else
    curl -s "$@"
  fi
}
curl -s "$API/readyz" | jq -c '{status, version, checks: .checks | map_values(.status)}'
api "$API/v1/catalog/models" \
  | jq -r '.items[].manifest | "\(.id)@\(.version)  \(.capabilities.representation)"'

{"status":"ok","version":"0.4.0","checks":{"postgres":"ok","object_store":"ok","catalog":"ok"}}
mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0  draws
mmm.pymc_marketing@1.0.0  draws
sklearn.tabular_bootstrap@1.0.0  draws
…
ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0  draws

/healthz says the process is alive; /readyz checks PostgreSQL, the object store and the catalog, and answers 503 with the same body when one is not ready. The catalog is what the runner image provides, exported by a sandboxed describe run; specs are validated against it.

docs.title: Upload a CSV
docs.text:
Data never passes through the API. You create a dataset, ask for an upload session, and PUT the bytes to the signed URL it returns:

DS=$(api "$API/v1/datasets?limit=200" | jq -r '.items[] | select(.name == "weekly_sales") | .id')
if [ -z "$DS" ]; then
  DS=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name": "weekly_sales", "description": "a CSV upload from the HTTP guide"}' | jq -r .id)
fi
echo "dataset $DS"
printf 'week,sales\n2026-01-04,120\n2026-01-11,131\n2026-01-18,127\n2026-01-25,140\n' > sales.csv
SIZE=$(wc -c < sales.csv | tr -d ' ')
UP=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/uploads" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"filename\": \"sales.csv\", \"content_type\": \"text/csv\", \"size_bytes\": $SIZE}")
HEADERS=()  # the signed URL binds these headers: send them exactly
while IFS= read -r h; do HEADERS+=(-H "$h"); done \
  < <(jq -r '.upload.headers | to_entries[] | "\(.key): \(.value)"' <<<"$UP")
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'PUT %{http_code}\n' -X PUT "${HEADERS[@]}" \
  --data-binary @sales.csv "$(jq -r .upload.url <<<"$UP")"

dataset ds_01m4zy65cdbxtaa4vgsvpeb4rt
PUT 200

The URL is a V4-style signed URL for one object in the quarantine bucket, valid for an hour. Send the headers from upload.headers exactly, because they are part of the signature: content-type must be the one you declared, x-goog-content-length-range caps the size at size_bytes, and x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 makes the object write-once, so a second PUT to the same URL is rejected.

Then turn the upload into a dataset version. For CSV and Parquet the mapping names the column of every dim and variable, with its kind, score-time policy and role:

MAPPING='{
  "format": "csv",
  "dims": {"week": {"column": "week", "spec": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"}}},
  "vars": {"sales": {"column": "sales", "role": "target", "units": "units"}}
}'
DV=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"upload_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$UP"), \"mapping\": $MAPPING}")
V=$(jq -r .version <<<"$DV")
STATUS=ingesting
while [ "$STATUS" = ingesting ]; do  # a sandboxed ingest run parses and checks the file
  sleep 1
  STATUS=$(api "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq -r '.status // "ingesting"')
done
api "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq '{ref, status, dims: .data_schema.dims | keys}'

{
  "ref": "dataset://default/weekly_sales@v1",
  "status": "ready",
  "dims": ["week"]
}

POST …/versions answers 202 with the version in status ingesting and the id of the sandboxed ingest run that parses the file. It accepts an Idempotency-Key: a retried request with the same key and body returns the same version instead of ingesting twice.

docs.title: Validate and fit a spec
docs.text:
jq -Rs '{yaml: .}' demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml \
  | api -X POST "$API/v1/specs:validate" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- \
  | jq '{valid, issues: [.issues[] | {code, pointer}], stages: [.stages[] | .name]}'

{
  "valid": true,
  "issues": [],
  "stages": ["raw", "to_eur", "weekly", "scale_spend", "scale_y", "lags", "season", "hols"]
}

POST /v1/specs:validate answers 200 even for an invalid spec: the verdict is in valid and every problem is in issues with its code and JSON pointer. Non-2xx statuses are kept for requests that cannot be validated at all (unparseable YAML, too large).

SPEC=$(api "$API/v1/specs?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
RUN=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"kind\": \"fit\", \"spec_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$SPEC"), \"revision\": $(jq .latest_revision <<<"$SPEC")}" \
  | jq -r .id)
echo "run $RUN"

POST /v1/runs answers 201 with the run in state created or queued. The same Idempotency-Key with the same body answers 200 with the same run; with a different body, 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Generate one key per user intent and reuse it on retries.

docs.title: Follow the run
docs.text:
# server-sent events: a snapshot, the persisted events, live progress, then `end`
api -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "$API/v1/runs/$RUN/events" | grep '^event:' | uniq -c
api "$API/v1/runs/$RUN" | jq '{state, output_model_version_id}'

   3 event: snapshot
   1 event: state
   1 event: warning
   2 event: state
   6 event: progress
   1 event: state
   5 event: diagnostic
   3 event: metric
   1 event: state
   1 event: complete
   1 event: state
   2 event: snapshot
   1 event: end
{
  "state": "succeeded",
  "output_model_version_id": "mv_01m4zy6yc82qy97jzjmv9phv1j"
}

With Accept: text/event-stream the events endpoint is a live stream: a snapshot of the run first, then the persisted events (each with an id:), live progress and log frames (no id, never replayed), a fresh snapshot on every state change, and end when the run is terminal, after which the server closes the stream. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID: <id> to resume exactly after the last persisted event. Without that Accept header the same URL returns the persisted events as a JSON page. See Run events.

docs.title: Read the model version
docs.text:
MODEL=$(api "$API/v1/models?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
M=$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")
MV=$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")
api "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV" \
  | jq '{ref, scorecard: .scorecard.overall, metrics, signed: .manifest.signature.alg}'

{
  "ref": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
  "scorecard": "warn",
  "metrics": {"mape": 7.59, "elpd_loo": 183.47, "coverage_90": 0.875},
  "signed": "KMS-EC-P256-SHA256"
}

GET …/artifacts/{name} returns a signed GET URL for any bundle object or ui/ view. It is minted only after the server has verified the version's signed manifest; each link is pinned to an object generation, supports HTTP Range requests and expires after 15 minutes.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
RES=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"request": {
        "apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
        "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest",
        "mode": "forecast",
        "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
        "side_tables": {"fx": "dataset://default/fx_daily@latest"}}}')
jq '{done, state: .run.state, outputs: [.outputs[] | {name, size, crc32c}]}' <<<"$RES"
curl -s "$(jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.name == "result.json") | .url' <<<"$RES")" \
  | jq '{mode, representation, output_space}'

{
  "done": true,
  "state": "succeeded",
  "outputs": [
    {"name": "plots.json", "size": 4122, "crc32c": "d8PGZA=="},
    {"name": "result.json", "size": 406, "crc32c": "PonvmQ=="},
    {"name": "score.zarr.zip", "size": 9396, "crc32c": "Uwymhw=="},
    {"name": "ui/summary.arrow", "size": 27266, "crc32c": "hxiS8w=="}
  ]
}
{
  "mode": "forecast",
  "representation": "draws",
  "output_space": {"contributions": "weekly", "y_hat": "weekly"}
}

Prefer: wait=60 holds the request until the score run finishes (at most 60 seconds) and answers 200 with done: true and signed links to the outputs. If it takes longer the answer is 202 with done: false: repeat the request with the same Idempotency-Key to get the same run's result, or follow the run. The response header Preference-Applied says which wait the server used. Over HTTP the ScoreRequest needs its apiVersion and kind (the Python client fills them in).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"request": {"apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
       "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest", "mode": "filter",
       "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest"}}' | jq '{status, code, detail}'

{
  "status": 422,
  "code": "MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED",
  "detail": "validation failed with 2 errors; first at /mode: model 'mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0' does not support mode 'filter'"
}

Every error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json) with a stable code, an HTTP status, and every individual problem in errors[] with a JSON pointer. Tracebacks and plugin messages only ever appear in an untrusted_text field; render them as text. The score request above was rejected statically: no run was created.

docs.title: Other clients
docs.text: The OpenAPI document is generated from the server itself (apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py writes apps/web/openapi.json, and CI fails if it drifts), so any OpenAPI generator produces a typed client. The web app's TypeScript client is generated that way (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch). For Python, use mapi_client.

docs.title: The Integrations hub v0.4
docs.text:
Integrations in the web app's sidebar (G then I) is where a fitted model leaves the platform: a spreadsheet scores it, a dashboard embeds its chart, your pipeline hears when a fit is ready. Everything on these pages is one or two calls of the HTTP API; the concepts behind them - the promotion gate, signed webhooks, embed links for platform recipes only - are explained in Integrations, and Endpoints and webhooks does the same with curl.

The hub has four tabs: Overview (the Guided cards and the developer entry points), Endpoints, Webhooks and Plots and links. Guided mode's last step, Share, leads here: an endpoint or chart link made there is listed in the hub straight away, and its Code for this endpoint button opens the endpoint's snippets. In a project locked to Guided mode, the hub stays in the navigation.

docs.title: Overview: connect in a few steps
docs.text:
Three cards cover the common cases without reading any API documentation:

Card What you get You need Google Sheets The Apps Script that scores an endpoint from a sheet - the rows of a sheet named Input (a header row with the endpoint's dims and inputs, one row per coordinate), or the example call - and writes the answer's summary (mean and 90% interval per coordinate) to a sheet named Result, with the steps to install it An endpoint; a token from Create a token (it can only score that endpoint) BI dashboard A read-only, expiring embed link for Looker Studio, Power BI or Notion (Slack shows a link as a card without the chart: post the PNG there) A saved plot of a platform recipe Webhook A signed call to your URL when a model is ready or a run fails The project admin role

Below them, For developers links to the endpoints, to scoped tokens and to the server's own interactive API documentation (/docs) and OpenAPI 3.1 document (/openapi.json).

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text: The Endpoints tab lists the project's endpoints: the alias, the model version it serves, its revision, the gate it passed and when it was promoted. Click one to open its page.

docs.title: Promoting through the gate
docs.text:
Promote a model (project admins) asks for the endpoint's name, a model and a version. The dialog shows the version's sanity scorecard and the expected gate; Promote asks the server, which decides:

The gate says The dialog What to do Passes The endpoint page opens on the new revision - Needs an override (409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED) The reasons, each with its check (holdout.mape), and an Override reason field A project admin signed in to the app writes why and clicks Override and promote; the override is audited as endpoint.promote_override. No API token can override Blocked (409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED) The reasons; no override A failing scorecard, an interrupted fit, a train_only fit or a breaking input change: fix it and promote a new version

The server also checks what the app cannot see - that the version was refitted on all data after its holdout evaluation, and that its input contract still matches what callers send - so an expected Passes can still come back blocked. Description and evaluation policy sets the endpoint's EvaluationPolicy: accept exploration fits too, and block, warn about or allow input-contract changes. If someone else promoted the endpoint while the dialog was open, the server refuses the stale revision and the dialog says so.

docs.title: An endpoint's page
docs.text:
• Version and history: the version served now (linked to its model page), who promoted it and how, the gate's reasons, and every promotion and rollback with its reason. Roll back returns to the previous revision's version, Roll back here to any earlier one; both ask for a reason, which is audited. The gate is not re-run on a rollback: that version passed it before. Delete endpoint needs the alias typed out; integrations calling it get 404.
  • Schema and Try it: the input contract frozen at promotion (score modes, the dim a forecast extends, dimensions and variables) and the example call. Validate runs the server's static checks (POST …/validate), Score a real score run (POST …/score with Prefer: wait=30, runner role) - edit the call first to try your own.
  • Snippets: ready-to-run code for Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, Atlas and Notebook (a Jupyter or marimo cell that returns an xarray.Dataset), generated by the server with the example call, shown and copied exactly as the server wrote it, each with what to install first. Snippets never contain a secret: they read the token from MAPI_TOKEN.

Token for this endpoint (and Create a score:… token on the Snippets tab) opens the Tokens page's New token dialog prefilled for a score:<alias> token: it can read and score that endpoint and nothing else, with a 120 requests-per-minute limit to start from.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
The Webhooks tab (project admins; others see why it is empty) lists every webhook with its events, status and last delivery. New webhook asks for an https URL, a description and the events to send. The platform refuses URLs on private or internal addresses (WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED), and says so under the URL field.

The signing secret is shown once, right after creation: copy it into your receiver's configuration (the dialog's Done stays disabled until you copy it or tick that you stored it). The dialog also shows the few lines that verify a delivery's Mapi-Signature.

A webhook's page has:

  • Settings: enable or disable it, change its events, Rotate secret (the new secret is shown once; the old one keeps signing for 24 hours).
  • Delivery log: every try, newest first - the event, its status (Delivered, Retrying, Failed, Blocked, Pending), the attempt number, your receiver's response code and the time it took. Details shows the error, the next retry and the first KiB of your receiver's answer (as untrusted text). Replay sends a delivery again; Resend newest replays the newest one, so you can check a receiver you just fixed. There is no synthetic test event: a new webhook gets its first delivery from the next subscribed event in the project (a fit or score finishing, a version ready, a promotion).
  • A webhook that kept failing (20 consecutive failed events, or a 410 Gone) is disabled automatically: the page says why. Fix the receiver, then switch it back on (here, or with mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID --enable); that resets the failure count.

docs.title: Plots and links
docs.text:
The Plots and links tab keeps the plots you report on:

  • Save a model plot picks a model, a version and one of its plots. The Share button in a model version's plot gallery opens the same dialog prefilled. A saved plot keeps pointing at that version, so a link to it never changes when the model is refitted.
  • Download renders PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox (a render run, runner role; slow formats are followed until they finish) and checks the file's checksum before saving it. Plotly figures need kaleido and a Chrome in the runner image: when the server answers MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, the Plotly download buttons are disabled with the server's reason.
  • Create link makes a tokenised, read-only, expiring link - 7 to 365 days, 30 by default - optionally limited to the sites that may frame it (https origins). Only plots of the platform's own recipes can be shared; others say why the button is disabled. The link and its <iframe> code are shown once; the table below each plot lists its links with their status, expiry and view count, and Revoke ends one at once (viewers then see "This link has expired").

See Sharing plots for what the embed page does and does not load.

docs.title: Sign-up and e-mail verification
docs.text:
When the server allows self-service sign-up, the sign-in screen links to Create a workspace (/signup), a page that works without a session:

  1. Enter a work e-mail, your name, optionally the organisation (it names the workspace) and accept the terms: the terms of service and the acceptable-use policy open in a new tab (/terms and /acceptable-use, or the installation's own documents set with VITE_TERMS_URL and VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL). Disposable e-mail addresses are refused at the e-mail field; a server with sign-up closed says so.
  2. Check your inbox: the answer is the same whether or not the address already has an account. The link works once, for 24 hours; Send the link again replaces it. On a development server the page links straight to the mail in the outbox (make outbox).
  3. The link opens /verify-email, which removes the token from the address bar and asks you to Confirm and create my workspace. That creates a public-tier workspace with a default project and makes you its admin; Sign in then goes through the usual identity-provider flow and opens the new workspace in Guided mode. An expired or reused link explains how to get a new one.

docs.title: Settings > Data
docs.text:
Organisation admins find a Data section at the bottom of Settings:

  • Export your data packs everything the organisation stored - workspace records (credentials redacted), datasets, model manifests, the audit log and the cost ledger, as you choose - into one archive. The page follows the export and offers Download archive; the link lasts 15 minutes, so reload the page for a fresh one. Exports work while the organisation is suspended.
  • Delete the organisation needs the organisation id typed out. The organisation is suspended (read-only) at once and its runs are cancelled; for 7 days a banner on every page says when the purge starts, and Cancel the deletion restores it. Then every store is purged, with the progress shown per store. The audit log (pseudonymised) and the cost ledger (amounts only) are kept for their legal retention - see Deleting and exporting data.

docs.title: Admin console additions
docs.text:
Platform operators get two more things in Admin:

  • Sign-ups: the review queue of sign-ups a Sybil heuristic flagged (same network address, same browser, a repeated address, a burst from one domain), with the reasons in plain words. Approve clears the flag; Reject suspends the workspace the sign-up created. Both need a reason, which is audited.

  • Trust on each tenant row: its e-mail and identity verification and whether uploaded code is allowed, Mark identity verified (with the method and a reason) or withdraw it, and its deletion's status per store, with Retry the purge after a failure.

  • Promotions: the endpoint promotions that needed attention, across tenants and newest first - admin overrides of the scorecard gate (with the reason and the failing checks) and refused promotions (blocked, or needing an override). Nothing waits in a queue: the gate decides each promotion at once. The rows come from the audit log (endpoint.promote_override, and endpoint.promote with the outcome denied).

docs.title: Marketing-mix models
docs.text:
mapi-plugin-mmm ships two marketing-mix models (MMMs) as built-in plugins:

Plugin What it is Use it when mmm.hierarchical_geo A hierarchical geo MMM written for the platform (PyMC) You have several markets, want new markets and budgets scored honestly, and want response curves and marginal costs in your own currency mmm.pymc_marketing An adapter around pymc-marketing's MMM You already use pymc-marketing and want its model behind the platform: versioned bundles, forecasts, counterfactuals and plots

Both are registered through the mapi.models entry point, so a spec only has to name them: use: mmm.hierarchical_geo@^1.3.

docs.title: From daily spend in local currency to weekly EUR decisions
docs.text:
A typical European media dataset is daily, per market and channel, in each market's own currency. The platform's preprocessing turns that into the weekly EUR panel the model fits, and remembers every learned step so scoring replays exactly the same work:

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: eu-geo-mmm, project: growth}
data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/eu_media_daily@latest
  side_tables:
    fx:       {ref: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest, score_policy: supplied}
    holidays: {ref: dataset://shared/holidays_eu@v3, score_policy: pinned}
  bind:
    dims: {geo: market, channel: channel, time: date}
    vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8, after_step: weekly}   # weeks exist after `weekly`
pipeline:
  - id: to_eur
    use: core.fx_convert@^1
    with: {vars: [y, spend], table: fx, table_along: date, currency_dim: geo,
           currencies: {UK: GBP}, default_currency: EUR}
  - {id: weekly,      use: core.resample@^1,   with: {dim: time, freq: W-SUN, how: sum}}
  - {id: scale_spend, use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: scale_y,     use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: lags,        use: core.lag_tensor@^1, with: {vars: [spend], along: time, within: [geo], l_max: 6, pad: first}}
  - {id: season,      use: core.fourier@^1,    with: {along: time, period: 52.18, order: 3, out: fourier}}
  - {id: hols,        use: core.holidays@^1,   with: {table: holidays, table_along: date, along: time}}
model:
  use: mmm.hierarchical_geo@^1.3
  settings:
    pooling: partial
    adstock: {kind: geometric, l_max: 6}
    saturation: {kind: logistic}
    priors:
      beta_channel: {distribution: HalfNormal, sigma: 1.0, dims: [channel]}
      lam:          {distribution: Gamma, alpha: 3, beta: 1, dims: [channel]}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: nutpie, tune: 1000, draws: 1000, chains: 4, seed: 7}
outputs:
  derived: [contributions, response_curves, marginal_cost]
  plots: [core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves]
evaluate: {metrics: [elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape]}

What the platform does with this, without a line of model code:

  • Binding. Your names (market, revenue_local) become the model's canonical names (geo, y) and are reversed on every output.
  • Split at the right stage. The holdout is the last 8 weeks, cut after resampling, so no partial week leaks into training.
  • Evaluate, then refit. The model is fitted on the training weeks, scored on the holdout through the scoring path (the same code a forecast uses), then refitted on all weeks so forecasts start from the latest data.
  • Context. lag_tensor stores each market's last weeks of spend; a forecast prepends them, so carry-over from last month's TV burst reaches next month's sales.
  • Original units. Predictions and contributions come back in weekly EUR: the scaling steps are inverted, and the inversion stops at the weekly resample (daily values cannot be recovered from weekly sums). Every output says so in its output_space and units attributes.

A runnable version of this spec, scaled down, ships as mapi_plugin_mmm.examples.E33_SPEC_YAML, together with a simulator (e33_dataset) whose true parameters are known.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
For geo g, channel c and week t (model units: the target and spend are mean-scaled):

adstock   a[g,c,t] = sum_l spend[g,c,t,l] * w[c,l]          w = alpha**l (normalised)
saturate  s[g,c,t] = (1 - exp(-lam[c] a)) / (1 + exp(-lam[c] a))
effects   beta[g,c] = beta_channel[c] * exp(beta_sigma[c] * z[g,c])     partial pooling
mean      mu[g,t]  = intercept[g] + sum_c beta[g,c] s[g,c,t] + controls[g,t]
target    y[g,t]  ~ Normal(mu[g,t], sigma)

intercept[g] is a hierarchical effect over geos, and every other numeric variable along time (Fourier terms, holidays, prices…) is a control with one coefficient per feature.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Level Default Meaning pooling basic partial partial shares channel effects across geos; complete uses one effect for all geos; none estimates each geo separately (and then new geos cannot be scored) adstock.kind basic geometric geometric decays from the spend week; delayed peaks after theta weeks saturation.kind basic logistic logistic, hill or none (linear) centred advanced false Centred parameterisation of geo effects; non-centred samples better with few geos adstock.l_max advanced from the data Must equal the lag_tensor l_max adstock.normalize advanced true Lag weights sum to one, so a constant spend has steady-state adstock equal to the spend priors advanced see below Prior overrides by parameter controls advanced auto Control variables (default: every other numeric variable along time) grid advanced 0–2× in 21 steps The spend-multiplier grid of the response curves

Guided mode shows the basic settings only; every field carries x-ui-level in the manifest's JSON Schema.

docs.title: Priors
docs.text:
Priors use pymc-marketing's dict form: a distribution, numeric parameters and the canonical dims the parameter varies over.

Parameter Support Default Meaning intercept real Normal(0.5, 0.5) Population mean of the geo intercepts intercept_sigma positive HalfNormal(0.25) Spread of the geo intercepts beta_channel positive HalfNormal(1) per channel Typical channel effect at full saturation beta_sigma positive HalfNormal(0.3) per channel How much a channel's effect varies across geos alpha unit interval Beta(1, 3) per channel Weekly adstock decay theta positive HalfNormal(2) per channel Delayed adstock: weeks to the peak lam positive Gamma(3, 1) per channel Logistic saturation rate slope, half positive Gamma(3, 2), Gamma(2, 2) Hill curve gamma_control real Normal(0, 0.5) Each control feature's coefficient sigma positive HalfNormal(0.5) Observation noise

The allow-list covers Normal, StudentT, Laplace, HalfNormal, HalfStudentT, HalfCauchy, Exponential, Gamma, InverseGamma, LogNormal, Weibull, Beta, Uniform and TruncatedNormal. A prior whose support does not fit its parameter (a Normal media effect, a HalfNormal adstock decay) is rejected when the spec is validated, before anything runs. A list-valued parameter gives one value per label:

priors:
  lam: {distribution: Gamma, alpha: [3, 2, 2], beta: 1, dims: [channel]}

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Score requests work like for every other model; these are the ones MMM users need most.

ForecastA new marketA weekly EUR planWhat if 
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://growth/eu-geo-mmm-prod
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
side_tables: {fx: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest}    # fx is `supplied` at score time
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90], draws: 200}

Send daily spend in local currency for the next 8 weeks; get weekly EUR revenue.

Add a market the model has never seen (FR). Its intercept and channel effects are drawn from the fitted hyperpriors for every posterior draw, so its forecast is honest about what the model does not know: wider than a fitted market's. The response carries an UNSEEN_LEVELS notice.

mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
inputs_stage: weekly          # enter after fx conversion and resampling

Planners and optimisers send weekly EUR budgets (spend_local(market, channel, date) on W-SUN weeks) instead of inventing daily local-currency spend. No FX table is needed: the steps that use it are skipped. The forecast equals the raw-data path for the same spend.

mode: counterfactual
interventions: [{var: spend_local, sel: {channel: tv}, multiply: 1.2}]
output: {kind: predictive, draws: 200}

The scenario and the baseline share their noise (common random numbers), so the delta group shows the effect of the change, not sampling noise. Only the treated channel's contribution moves.

Every score returns y_hat and contributions(component, geo, time): one component per channel, baseline and one per control. They add up to y_hat.

docs.title: Derived quantities: what a Guided report reads
docs.text:
Ask for them in outputs.derived; they are computed once, at fit, over the first outputs.ui_draws posterior draws, and stored in the bundle in original units:

  • contributions: channel_contribution(sample, channel, geo, time), baseline and one variable per control, over the fit window. mmm.decomposition plots them.
  • response_curves: contribution(sample, channel, multiplier, geo), the total contribution over the fit window when a channel's spend is scaled by the multiplier, plus the EUR spend on every grid point. mmm.response_curves and mmm.marginal_cost plot them, and Guided-mode what-if sliders interpolate them per draw: instant, and the uncertainty bands stay joint.
  • marginal_cost: the extra EUR of spend needed for one extra EUR of revenue at current spend (and its inverse, marginal ROI), per geo and per channel.

response_curves also carries the baseline (intercepts and controls, per draw and per geo), so the what-if grid view closes the expected KPI. Business priors (ROI or share ranges) and lift tests calibrate this model through the spec's calibration block: see Guided modelling.

docs.title: Optimising budgets
docs.text:
mmm.hierarchical_geo declares decision: true. Its objective scores a budget per posterior draw:

import xarray as xr
from mapi_plugin_mmm import HierarchicalGeoMMM
from mapi_sdk.models import ScoreContext

budget = xr.Dataset(
    {"spend": ("channel", [40_000.0, 25_000.0, 10_000.0])},
    coords={"channel": ["tv", "search", "social"]},
    attrs={"periods": 13},                       # EUR per week, for a quarter
)
value = HierarchicalGeoMMM().objective(bundle.model, budget, ScoreContext())
value.dims   # ('chain', 'draw'): expected revenue of the plan, per draw

Budgets are in original units (EUR per week here) and so is the result; this uses the unit conversions cached with response_curves, so request that derived quantity (or pass attrs={"units": "model"} to work in model units). A channel budget is split across geos by each geo's share of that channel's spend; pass spend(geo, channel) to set it yourself. The value assumes the spend is sustained long enough for carry-over to settle (steady state).

docs.title: The pymc-marketing adapter
docs.text:
mmm.pymc_marketing runs pymc_marketing.mmm.MMM (version 1.2, on PyMC 6). pymc-marketing scales the data, carries spend over and reports original units itself, so the adapter declares owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units] and the platform steps aside:

  • keep scaling and lag steps out of the pipeline (currency conversion, resampling and holidays are fine);
  • scoring prepends the last l_max fit weeks before any window, so a four-week window scores exactly like the same weeks of the full series;
  • outputs are labelled model-owned; holdout metrics are not inverted a second time.
model:
  use: mmm.pymc_marketing@^1
  settings:
    dims: [geo]                    # panel dims besides time and channel
    adstock: {l_max: 4}
    saturation: {kind: logistic}
    controls: [holiday]
    yearly_seasonality: 2
  fit: {engine: nutpie, tune: 1000, draws: 1000, chains: 4}

Bundles never contain pickle: the adapter stores the posterior, pymc-marketing's fit_data and its JSON model description, and rebuilds the model through pymc-marketing's own loading path when it scores. Markets are a fixed dim for this adapter: pymc-marketing cannot score a market it has not seen.

settings.priors overrides pymc-marketing's priors (saturation_beta, intercept, gamma_control, gamma_fourier, in its scaled units). Business priors and lift tests in the spec's calibration block calibrate the adapter as they do the geo MMM; the business priors are translated on pymc-marketing's own model (see Guided modelling).

docs.title: BayesInsight models
docs.text: mmm.bayesinsight fits a BayesInsight model_def.json as BayesInsight defines it - likelihoods, priors in KPI units, curves, carry-over, signs, effects per row id, seasons and local trends. Import a BayesInsight project with "target": "mmm.bayesinsight" (see the import); the models reference documents every feature.

docs.title: Trust, but verify
docs.text: Both plugins pass the SDK contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model): bundle round trips, shuffled and subset markets, typed errors, the holdout scored through the same path as a forecast, additive contributions. The conformance corpus runs both through the whole spec → fit → score path, and a parameter-recovery test fits simulated data with known adstock, saturation and channel effects and checks they come back (adstock decay within 0.1, EUR contributions within 20%).

docs.title: Plots: recipes, templates and safe sharing
docs.text:
Every model you fit gets a set of standard plots for free: data overview, convergence, posterior predictive checks, a fit-and-forecast fan, decomposition, scenario comparisons and more. Plots are Vega-Lite (or Plotly for 3D, maps and animation) wrapped in a small envelope called a PlotSpec. The data travels next to the spec as named Arrow tables — never as a URL — and every plot passes a sanitizer before anyone sees it.

uv add "mapi-plots[recipes]"   # recipes + Altair/Plotly helpers (runner images, notebooks)
uv add mapi-plots              # sanitizer and templates only (JSON in, JSON out)

`core.ppc_fan`: model estimate, 50% and 90% bands, actual values and the end of the training data, one panel per market.

docs.title: Render a recipe in a notebook
docs.text:
A recipe is a function from a fitted bundle or a score output to a PlotSpec:

from mapi_plots.examples import example_inputs
from mapi_plots.recipes import get_recipe

inputs = example_inputs()  # synthetic bundle/score trees for every recipe (xarray only)
data, options = inputs["core.ppc_fan"]
plot = get_recipe("core.ppc_fan").render(data, **options)

print(plot.kind, plot.persona)  # vega-lite both
print(sorted(plot.datasets))  # named Arrow tables travel next to the spec, never as URLs
print(plot.caption_plain[:60], "...")

Inputs are flexible: an xr.DataTree (bundle or score output), an xr.Dataset, or a plain {"group": Dataset} mapping. Recipes find their groups at the root, under model/ (bundles) or anywhere in the tree. Options are validated; an unknown option or a missing group raises a typed RecipeDataError (SCHEMA_INVALID) that says what was expected.

Every plot carries:

  • persona — guided (analysts), expert (data scientists) or both;
  • caption_plain — a plain-language reading of the chart with the actual numbers ("The scenario changes total revenue by 184 (90% interval 139 to 251) compared with the baseline. Probability of an increase: 100%.");
  • provenance — the recipe and version, the bundle id and a timestamp.

Try every recipe without a model

mapi_plots.examples.example_inputs() returns synthetic bundle and score trees for every recipe, built with xarray only:

for recipe_id, (data, options) in example_inputs().items():
    rendered = get_recipe(recipe_id).render(data, **options)
    print(f"{recipe_id:28} {rendered.kind:10} {rendered.persona}")

docs.title: The standard catalog
docs.text:
Recipe What it shows Reads core.data_overview Each variable over time per group, a missingness heatmap, group sizes raw data / observed_data core.prior_predictive Datasets the model generates before seeing data vs your data, plus a prior fan prior_predictive, observed_data core.convergence R-hat and ESS per parameter, a table of the worst, trace and rank plots, divergences posterior, sample_stats core.posterior_forest Median, 50% and 94% HDI per parameter, one panel per variable posterior core.ppc Predictive densities vs observed, PIT histogram, interval coverage posterior_predictive, observed_data core.ppc_fan Fit + forecast fan with the train/forecast split line draws or summary, observed core.fit_vs_actual Predicted against actual with R² and MAPE predictions + observed core.residuals_over_time Actual minus predicted over time predictions + observed core.decomposition Stacked contributions over time and each component's total share contributions core.model_comparison elpd per model and the difference to the best (PSIS-LOO table or WAIC) comparison, or one child per model with log_likelihood core.counterfactual Scenario vs baseline over time and the distribution of the total change draws/summary, baseline/…, delta/… core.decision_distribution Distribution of a decision objective per option and P(best) decision/objective

The marketing-mix pack (mmm.*) adds response curves with current spend marked, marginal cost (or marginal ROI) per channel, a budget-plan comparison and a channel decomposition. The tabular pack (ml.*) adds ml.feature_importance: ranked tree importances, or signed coefficients for linear estimators, read from the groups the scikit-learn and xgboost plugins store in their bundles.

Recipes respect each output's representation: they sum joint draws when a dim has to go, but never add up quantiles or intervals — a summary with an extra dim asks you to request an aggregated output instead (summed means are shown without a band). Predicted-vs-actual and residual plots never need a total, so they compare such summaries cell by cell (one dot or line per store × sku, coloured by the facet dim).

docs.title: Bring your own chart
docs.text:
Build with Altair or Plotly as usual, then wrap it:

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
from mapi_plots import from_altair

frame = pd.DataFrame({"week": pd.date_range("2026-01-04", periods=6, freq="W-SUN"),
                      "revenue": [10.0, 12.5, 11.0, 14.2, 15.1, 13.8]})
chart = alt.Chart(frame).mark_line().encode(x="week:T", y="revenue:Q")
mine = from_altair(chart, id="acme.revenue", caption_plain="Weekly revenue.")
print(list(mine.datasets))  # the inline data became a named dataset

import plotly.express as px
from mapi_plots import from_plotly

fig = px.scatter(frame, x="week", y="revenue")
theirs = from_plotly(fig, id="acme.scatter")  # typed arrays -> named Arrow datasets
print(list(theirs.datasets))  # one dataset per trace, referenced as {"$ref": "trace0.y"}
  • from_altair moves Altair's inline data (and any data.values) into named Arrow datasets and rewrites the references; named data (alt.Data(name="pts")) is filled from datasets={"pts": frame}.
  • from_plotly decodes plotly.py 6 typed arrays ({"dtype": "f8", "bdata": ...}) into Arrow datasets, one per trace, and binds them with {"$ref": "trace0.y"}. The default plotly.py template is dropped (the renderer themes plots) unless keep_template=True.

Both run the sanitizer and raise a SanitizeError if the chart breaks a rule. from_plotly also strips HTML from the strings it moves into datasets (see below).

Colours and dark mode. An explicit mark colour wins over any theme, so the platform recipes draw only with mapi_plots.palette (for example OBSERVED, ESTIMATE, BAND, ALERT). In dark mode the plot sandbox swaps each palette colour for its dark variant; every stroke, dot and text colour keeps at least 3:1 contrast on both card backgrounds. Use the palette in your own charts to get the same behaviour. Any other colour is drawn as written in both themes.

docs.title: Role- and dim-bound templates
docs.text:
A template binds channels to roles and dims instead of one model's variable names, so a "target over time, one line per geo" plot applies to every model of a family:

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from mapi_plots.recipes import builtin_templates, render_template

weekly = xr.Dataset(
    {"revenue": (("geo", "time"), np.random.default_rng(0).gamma(20.0, 50.0, (3, 12)),
                 {"role": "target", "units": "EUR"})},
    coords={"geo": ["DE", "FR", "UK"], "time": pd.date_range("2026-01-04", periods=12, freq="W-SUN")},
)
tmpl = builtin_templates()["tmpl.target_over_time"]
print(tmpl.bindings)  # x="dim:time", y="role:target", color="dim:geo" - no variable names
chart = render_template(tmpl, weekly)  # the schema is inferred; roles come from attrs
one_market = render_template(tmpl, weekly.sel(geo="DE", drop=True), optional=["color"])

Inside a template spec, {"$bind": "y"} becomes a Vega-Lite field definition and "{{y}}" (also {{y.field}}, {{y.type}}, {{y.title}}) is replaced by the bound name. Binding kinds are dim:, role:, var:, coord: and stat: (a summary statistic such as stat:hdi_90_lower). The JSON-only half, mapi_plots.templates.apply_template, runs in the API to check that a saved template applies to a model before anything is rendered.

docs.title: What the sanitizer allows
docs.text:
Plots run in an isolated iframe on a separate origin, but the server checks every plot first:

Rejected Why url data (anywhere, including lookups and topojson) data must be referenced by name; no fetching href encodings and mark properties no navigation out of the plot image marks, url channels, layout.images / image traces with non-data: sources no external fetches (only base64 PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) Tile-map traces and subplots (scattermap, choroplethmap, densitymap, layout.map) tiles come from third-party servers; use scattergeo/choropleth __proto__, constructor, prototype keys or field paths prototype pollution javascript:, data:text/html, SVG data URIs, CSS url() in any string script and fetch vectors Vega expressions outside a small allow-list of functions, method calls, window/document/fetch, computed member names expression sandbox escapes Custom format types, Plotly network options (topojsonURL, showLink, ...) code and network hooks Anything that does not match the pinned Vega-Lite v6.4.1 / plotly.js 4.1.1 schemas unknown keys are where exploits hide

Plotly text keeps only <b>, <i>, <br>, <sub> and <sup> (plus <extra> in hover templates); everything else is stripped and reported as a change. The server never decodes Arrow, so text that from_plotly moves into a dataset (text, hovertext, category labels) is stripped and scanned on the sandbox side during conversion; the plot iframe must still treat dataset strings as untrusted and re-strip them before handing them to plotly.js. Vega renders dataset strings as text (and the iframe's tooltip handler escapes them). Method args of Plotly buttons and sliders are checked in both the {attr: value} and positional [attr, value] forms, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected in Vega-Lite specs. Specs are capped in size, depth, node count and string length. See the plots reference for the full rule list and error codes.

from mapi_plots import check_plot, sanitize_plot
from mapi_plots.sanitize import SanitizeError

hostile = {
    "id": "evil.chart",
    "title": "Totally normal chart",
    "kind": "vega-lite",
    "spec": {
        "data": {"url": "https://attacker.example/steal.json"},  # fetches are not allowed
        "mark": "point",
        "encoding": {"href": {"field": "link"}},  # neither is navigation
    },
}
try:
    sanitize_plot(hostile)
except SanitizeError as err:
    print(err.code, sorted(rule.value for rule in err.rules))  # PLOT_UNSAFE ['href', 'url_data']

for issue in check_plot(hostile):  # editor-friendly: every problem, never raises
    print(issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# /spec/data/url - data must be referenced by dataset name, never by URL
# /spec/encoding/href - href links are not allowed in plots
# /spec/$schema - added $schema

docs.title: Write a step or a model plugin
docs.text: A plugin author writes very little: a step implements fit/transform (and inverse when it can); a model implements fit/score. The platform owns everything around them — binding, splits, context tails, coordinates, inverse transforms, summaries and bundles. The contract kit tells you, before anyone else runs your code, whether you followed the rules.

docs.title: A preprocessing step
docs.text:
from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sdk import Step, StepContext, StepSettings, StepState
from mapi_spec import StepKind
from pydantic import Field, JsonValue


class ScaleSettings(StepSettings):
    vars: list[str]
    over: list[str] = Field(default=[])  # plain defaults: the exported JSON Schema keeps them
    unseen_levels: str = "error"  # error | pooled | fill: what a new level's scale becomes
    fill_value: float = 1.0  # the scale used by 'fill'


class ScaleStep(Step[ScaleSettings, StepState]):
    """Divide each variable by its mean absolute value over `over` (learned on train)."""

    id = "acme.scale"
    version = "1.0.0"
    kind = StepKind.VALUE
    Settings = ScaleSettings
    State = StepState  # stateful: fitted on the training data only
    invertible = True
    var_params = ("vars",)  # settings that name variables ...
    dim_params = ("over",)  # ... and dims, so the control plane can check them
    unseen_levels_param = "unseen_levels"
    effect_template: ClassVar[dict[str, JsonValue]] = {  # static: how the schema changes
        "template_params": ["vars"],
        "updates": {"{*vars as v}": {"units": "1"}},
    }
    summary = "Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims"  # catalog and UI text
    summary_plain = "Puts each series on a comparable scale"

    def fit(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, ctx: StepContext) -> StepState:
        return StepState(arrays=xr.Dataset({f"scale__{v}": abs(ds[v]).mean(s.over) for v in s.vars}))

    def _scale(self, v: str, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, st: StepState, ctx: StepContext):
        state = st.array(f"scale__{v}")
        return ctx.align_state(state, ds, s.unseen_levels, fill_value=s.fill_value)

    def transform(self, ds, s, st, ctx):  # never learns; skips absent vars (the target at score)
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] / self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

    def inverse(self, ds, s, st, ctx):
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] * self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

The rules:

  • transform never learns. transform(train, fit(train)) must equal the fit-time output, and a subset of the data must transform to the same subset of the output.
  • Reductions name the dims they reduce over; state stays labelled by the rest.
  • Steps that look back (lags, rolling windows) declare context_template ({"along": "{along}", "n": "{max:lags}", "within": "{within}"}). The platform stores the last n rows per group at the step's input and prepends them at score time.
  • Unseen levels go through ctx.align_state(state, ds, policy).
  • effect_template must describe the real output schema — the control plane validates specs with it and never imports your code.

docs.title: A model
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import PREDICTIONS, CustomModel, FitOutput, ModelSettings, new_level_mask
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, DataSchema, Representation


class BaselineSettings(ModelSettings):
    ridge: float = 1e-6


class GeoBaseline(CustomModel[BaselineSettings]):
    """y = intercept[geo] + beta * spend, by least squares (point predictions)."""

    id = "acme.geo_baseline"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = BaselineSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="point",
        representation=Representation.POINT,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "forecast", "evaluate"}),
    )
    # the data contract the model needs, in canonical names (a DataSchema, or a
    # DataSchemaTemplate whose names come from settings)
    schema_template = DataSchema.model_validate(
        {
            "dims": {
                "geo": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
                "time": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend"},
            },
            "vars": {
                "y": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
                "spend": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "covariate"},
            },
        }
    )
    outputs: ClassVar[dict] = {"y_hat": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "units_of": "y"}}
    pad_extend = False  # time is not indexed by position

    def fit(self, ds, s, cfg, ctx):
        g, t = ds.sizes["geo"], ds.sizes["time"]
        x = np.concatenate(
            [np.repeat(np.eye(g), t, axis=0), ds["spend"].values.reshape(-1, 1)], axis=1
        )
        coef = np.linalg.solve(x.T @ x + s.ridge * np.eye(g + 1), x.T @ ds["y"].values.ravel())
        params = xr.Dataset(
            {"intercept": ("geo", coef[:g]), "beta": coef[g]}, coords={"geo": ds["geo"].values}
        )
        return FitOutput(groups={"params": params})

    def score(self, fitted, ds, req, ctx):
        # `ds` arrives canonicalised: fit order, unseen geos appended and flagged
        p = fitted.group("params")
        new = new_level_mask(ds, "geo")
        known = p["intercept"].reindex(geo=ds["geo"].values)
        pooled = 0.0 if ctx.strategy("geo") == "zero" else float(p["intercept"].mean())
        intercept = xr.where(new, pooled, known.fillna(pooled))
        y_hat = (intercept + p["beta"] * ds["spend"]).transpose("geo", "time")
        return xr.DataTree.from_dict({PREDICTIONS: xr.Dataset({"y_hat": y_hat})})

outputs lists every variable score returns with its dims (representation dims such as chain/draw or quantile may be left out). When the data dims depend on settings, add "dims_of": "y": the output then also carries every dim of that input variable in the resolved schema (for example the sklearn models' settings.rows).

FitOutput.native is for safe native formats only (skops, xgboost JSON, safetensors). Pickle is rejected when a bundle is written and when it is read.

docs.title: Run the contract kit
docs.text:
mapi-sdk installs a pytest plugin, so the fixtures are available in any test suite:

import pytest
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, toy  # toy: small reference steps and models


@pytest.mark.mapi_contract
def test_step_follows_the_contract(mapi_check_step, mapi_panel):
    data, _fx = mapi_panel  # a daily market x channel panel and its FX side table
    report = mapi_check_step(
        toy.ScaleStep, data, {"vars": ["spend_local"], "over": ["date"], "unseen_levels": "pooled"}
    )
    assert report.ok, report.summary()


SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: toy, project: demo}
data:
  dataset: dataset://demo/panel@latest
  bind: {dims: {geo: market, time: date}, vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 14}
model: {use: toy.linear@^1, fit: {seed: 1}}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse]}
"""


@pytest.mark.mapi_contract
def test_model_follows_the_contract(mapi_check_model, mapi_panel, mapi_toy_registry):
    data, _fx = mapi_panel
    fixture = ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=data, registry=mapi_toy_registry)
    report = mapi_check_model(toy.LinearModel, fixture)  # raises ContractViolation on failure
    assert report.ok

check_step checks the exported catalog entry, deterministic fitting, a pure and deterministic transform, that transform never learns, the state's bundle round trip, that the declared schema effect matches the real output, that a missing target is tolerated, the inverse round trip, context-window equivalence and every unseen-level policy.

check_model fits the fixture and checks the bundle round trip (and that it has no pickle), shuffled and subset scoring, new-level policies, the typed errors of every dim policy (gaps and out-of-range coordinates on datetime and integer extend dims, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT past max_extension, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE for a forecast without a future-required variable, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED for a horizon longer than a target lag), unsupported modes, context-window equivalence, that the evaluation metrics are reproduced by the score path, output units (including outputs that inherit the target's units), that every returned prediction is declared in outputs with matching dims, legal aggregation, additive contributions, seed determinism, that the manifest's plots render and pass the sanitizer, and — when the manifest declares fast_score — that fast scoring matches exact scoring within MCSE. That last check calls the plugin's check_fast_score(fitted, ds, *, seed) hook; PyMCModel provides it.

A failed check raises ContractViolation with a readable report:

contract kit: step acme.scale@1.0.0
  [PASS] catalog_entry: exported acme.scale@1.0.0
  [FAIL] transform_never_learns: AssertionError: ...

mapi_sdk.testing.toy holds small, real reference implementations (scale, log1p, lag, resample, Fourier, FX steps; point, draws and quantile models) to copy from.

docs.title: Port a model in 15 minutes
docs.text:
You have a model that works in a notebook. This guide turns it into a plugin that the platform can fit, score on new data, forecast, version and plot, and proves it with the contract kit. You write the statistics; the platform writes everything around them.

flowchart LR
    A["0–3 min<br/><b>Pick a base class</b>"] --> B["3–6 min<br/><b>Declare the data contract</b>"]
    B --> C["6–11 min<br/><b>Write build / estimator / fit+score</b>"]
    C --> D["11–13 min<br/><b>Write a tiny spec</b>"]
    D --> E["13–15 min<br/><b>Run the contract kit</b>"]

docs.title: What you write, what you get
docs.text:
You write The platform does PyMCModel build(ds, settings, ctx) -> pm.Model Engines (nutpie, PyMC with resumable segments, MAP, ADVI), convergence diagnostics, rebuild-and-predict scoring, new levels from the hyperprior, common-random-number counterfactuals, fast scoring SklearnModel estimator(settings) Stacking labelled dims into rows and features, coordinate features, safe persistence (skops / xgboost JSON), quantile / bootstrap / conformal uncertainty, pooled new levels, contributions CustomModel fit(...) and score(...) Binding, preprocessing, splits, context tails, coordinate canonicalisation, inverse transforms, summaries, bundles

All three get, for free: validated settings with JSON Schemas, static spec validation, evaluate-then-refit, CoordPlan checks, representation-aware summaries, plots and bundles.

docs.title: 1. Pick a base class (0–3 min)
docs.text:
• Your model is a PyMC model → mapi_pymc.PyMCModel.
  • Your model is an sklearn or xgboost estimator on a design matrix → mapi_sklearn.SklearnModel (or the quantile, bootstrap, conformal or classifier variants).
  • Anything else (statsmodels, JAX, a Kalman filter, closed-form maths) → mapi_sdk.CustomModel.

docs.title: 2. Declare the data contract (3–6 min)
docs.text:
Write down, in canonical names, the dims and variables your model needs and what may happen to each dim at score time. This is the model's schema_template. Users bind their own dataset names onto it in the spec.

Three questions per dim

Can a score request bring a new level (a new county, store, market)? Then new_levels, with a strategy. Does it grow at forecast time (time, observations)? Then extend. Otherwise fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the model (6–11 min)
docs.text:
PyMCscikit-learn / xgboostCustom 
from typing import Any, ClassVar

import pymc as pm
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc import BuildContext, PyMCModel
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA  # dims obs (extend) + county (new_levels)
from mapi_sdk import ModelSettings
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, Representation
from pydantic import Field


class RadonSettings(ModelSettings):
    beta_sigma: float = Field(1.0, gt=0)


class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    """log radon ~ Normal(a[county] + b * floor, sigma), with partially pooled a."""

    id = "acme.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="mcmc",
        representation=Representation.DRAWS,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "counterfactual", "evaluate"}),
    )
    schema_template = RADON_SCHEMA
    outputs: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {"y": "mu"}  # output -> Deterministic for E[y]
    pad_extend = False  # long layout: no positional time axis

    def build(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: RadonSettings, ctx: BuildContext) -> pm.Model:
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as model:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")  # new counties come from the hyperprior
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0.0, s.beta_sigma)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            sigma = pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1.0)
            pm.Normal("y", mu, sigma, observed=ctx.observed("y"), dims="obs")
        return model

The ctx helpers are what make scoring work without you thinking about it:

Helper Why you use it ctx.coords() The model's coords; at score time includes new levels ctx.data(name) A pm.Data over the training values at fit and the score values at score time (the model is rebuilt) ctx.observed(name) The target at fit; a placeholder at score time (never imputed) ctx.hier_effect(name, dim) A partially pooled effect whose new levels are drawn from the hyperprior per posterior draw ctx.position(dim) 0, 1, 2, … along an extend dim, continued into the forecast horizon

expected names the Deterministic that is the expected value of each output, so output.kind: expected returns it without observation noise.

from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sklearn import PointSettings, SklearnModel, capabilities_for
from mapi_spec import Capabilities
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge


class LinearDemand(SklearnModel[PointSettings]):
    id = "t.acme.linear_demand"
    version = "1.0.0"
    capabilities: ClassVar[Capabilities] = capabilities_for("none").model_copy(
        update={"contribution_scale": "additive"}  # a linear model decomposes exactly
    )

    def estimator(self, s: PointSettings) -> Ridge:
        return Ridge(alpha=0.5)  # must be exactly an allow-listed class

estimator() returns an allow-listed estimator instance (or a {kind, params} mapping). Subclasses and parameters outside the estimator's params model are rejected, so the bundle can always be loaded safely. Rows, columns and coordinate features are settings, not code: see Tabular models.

from mapi_sdk import PREDICTIONS, CustomModel, FitOutput, ModelSettings, new_level_mask
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, DataSchema, Representation


class BaselineSettings(ModelSettings):
    ridge: float = 1e-6


class GeoBaseline(CustomModel[BaselineSettings]):
    """y = intercept[geo] + beta * spend, by least squares (point predictions)."""

    id = "acme.geo_baseline"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = BaselineSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="point",
        representation=Representation.POINT,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "forecast", "evaluate"}),
    )
    # the data contract the model needs, in canonical names (a DataSchema, or a
    # DataSchemaTemplate whose names come from settings)
    schema_template = DataSchema.model_validate(
        {
            "dims": {
                "geo": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
                "time": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend"},
            },
            "vars": {
                "y": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
                "spend": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "covariate"},
            },
        }
    )
    outputs: ClassVar[dict] = {"y_hat": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "units_of": "y"}}
    pad_extend = False  # time is not indexed by position

    def fit(self, ds, s, cfg, ctx):
        g, t = ds.sizes["geo"], ds.sizes["time"]
        x = np.concatenate(
            [np.repeat(np.eye(g), t, axis=0), ds["spend"].values.reshape(-1, 1)], axis=1
        )
        coef = np.linalg.solve(x.T @ x + s.ridge * np.eye(g + 1), x.T @ ds["y"].values.ravel())
        params = xr.Dataset(
            {"intercept": ("geo", coef[:g]), "beta": coef[g]}, coords={"geo": ds["geo"].values}
        )
        return FitOutput(groups={"params": params})

    def score(self, fitted, ds, req, ctx):
        # `ds` arrives canonicalised: fit order, unseen geos appended and flagged
        p = fitted.group("params")
        new = new_level_mask(ds, "geo")
        known = p["intercept"].reindex(geo=ds["geo"].values)
        pooled = 0.0 if ctx.strategy("geo") == "zero" else float(p["intercept"].mean())
        intercept = xr.where(new, pooled, known.fillna(pooled))
        y_hat = (intercept + p["beta"] * ds["spend"]).transpose("geo", "time")
        return xr.DataTree.from_dict({PREDICTIONS: xr.Dataset({"y_hat": y_hat})})

The rules for score:

  • the dataset arrives canonicalised: fit order, new levels appended and flagged by <dim>__is_new (new_level_mask(ds, dim)), so position-indexed parameters line up;
  • return an xr.DataTree with a predictions group in your declared representation;
  • never look at targets in the payload (evaluate mode passes them for metrics, not for you).

FitOutput.groups uses ArviZ group names (posterior, sample_stats, …), learned holds small JSON, and native holds bytes in a safe format only (skops, xgboost JSON, safetensors). Pickle is rejected.

docs.title: 4. Write a tiny spec (11–13 min)
docs.text:
The spec the contract kit fits. Keep it small and fast: few draws, few trees.

PyMCCustom (with a step) 
from mapi_pymc.examples import radon_dataset
from mapi_sdk import Registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: radon, project: demo}
data: {dataset: dataset://demo/radon@latest}
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit: {mode: train_only, engine: pymc, tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, seed: 3}
"""
report = check_model(
    Radon, ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=radon_dataset(), raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA, registry=Registry())
)
print(report.summary())

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

registry = default_registry().copy()
registry.register(ScaleStep)  # the model is registered by check_model itself

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: acme-baseline, project: demo}
data:
  dataset: dataset://demo/sales@latest
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 6}
pipeline:
  - {id: scale, use: acme.scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
model:
  use: acme.geo_baseline@^1
  fit: {seed: 1}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape]}
"""
raw_schema = infer_schema(data, targets=["y"], policies={"geo": "new_levels"})
report = check_model(
    GeoBaseline,
    ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=data, raw_schema=raw_schema, registry=registry),
)
print(report.summary())
# contract kit: model acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0
#   [PASS] fit: ...
#   [PASS] bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle: ...
#   [PASS] shuffled_scoring: ...
#   ...

docs.title: 5. Run the contract kit (13–15 min)
docs.text:
check_model fits your fixture and then tries to break your plugin the way real users will:

contract kit: model acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0
  [PASS] manifest: acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0 (point)
  [PASS] fit: bundle ef4100375dbb, metrics ['mape', 'rmse']
  [PASS] bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle: scores match after write/read
  [PASS] shuffled_scoring: shuffled ['geo']
  [PASS] subset_scoring: subset of 'geo'
  [PASS] new_level_policies: geo: new level scored (pooled)
  [PASS] extend_typed_errors: raised NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION; raised COORD_NOT_ALLOWED
  [PASS] unsupported_mode: raised MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED
  [PASS] context_window_equivalence: holdout via stored context == in-sample full series
  [PASS] evaluate_path_equals_score_path: metrics ['rmse', 'mape'] reproduced through the score path
  [PASS] output_space_and_units: y_hat in raw (None)
  [PASS] representation_aggregation: point aggregation over 'geo' allowed
  [SKIP] additive_contributions: contribution_scale is not additive
  [PASS] seed_determinism: same seed, same fit and scores
Check What it proves bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle Scores are identical after writing and reading the bundle, and nothing in it is pickle shuffled_scoring, subset_scoring Reordered labels and subsets give the same answers for the same cells new_level_policies Every strategy your dims declare works (or raises UNSEEN_LEVELS when it should) extend_typed_errors Gaps and out-of-range time labels raise typed errors unsupported_mode Undeclared modes are refused context_window_equivalence Scoring the last training periods as a forecast equals the in-sample result evaluate_path_equals_score_path The holdout metrics are reproduced through the normal score path output_space_and_units Outputs are inverted and labelled with units and output space representation_aggregation Aggregations are allowed or refused according to the representation additive_contributions Declared-additive contributions sum to the prediction seed_determinism The same seed gives the same fit and scores, when the plugin claims it

A failed check raises ContractViolation with the report (pass raise_on_failure=False to get the report instead).
