handled: set[str] = set()  # use your database: deliveries are at least once


@app.post("/mapi/webhook")
def mapi_webhook() -> dict[str, str]:
    try:  # request.get_data(): the raw body, before anything reads request.json
        event = verify(request.headers, request.get_data(), SECRET)
    except MapiError:
        abort(401)
    if event.id in handled:
        return {"status": "duplicate"}
    handled.add(event.id)
    if event.type == "model.version.ready":
        print("model ready:", event.data["ref"], "scorecard:", event.data["scorecard_overall"])
    return {"status": "ok"}

Both receivers are run by the test suite (docs/snippets/webhook_receiver.py and webhook_receiver_flask.py), which posts deliveries signed exactly as the platform signs them, then a replay, a tampered body and a stale timestamp.

docs.title: 4. Try it on your laptop
docs.text:
A make dev stack already trusts a receiver on your own machine: the dev profile writes a throwaway CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to .local/dev/webhook-tls/, trusts that CA and allow-lists both hosts (configuration). Save the FastAPI receiver as receiver.py, create a webhook for it and serve it with that certificate, from the repository (the workspace already has FastAPI and uvicorn):

uv run mapi webhooks create https://localhost:8443/mapi/webhook \
  -e endpoint.promoted -e run.failed               # prints the secret once
export MAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_…                 # that secret
uv run uvicorn receiver:app --port 8443 \
  --ssl-certfile .local/dev/webhook-tls/cert.pem --ssl-keyfile .local/dev/webhook-tls/key.pem

Promote a fitted model to an endpoint (the Quickstart fits one; promote it in the Integrations hub): the receiver prints now serving endpoint://<project>/<alias> revision 1. In the web app, the webhook's Delivery log shows the try with your receiver's response code and time; Send test replays the newest delivery, so you can check a receiver you just changed (mapi webhooks replay <webhook_id> <delivery_id> does the same). The M3 end-to-end suite receives every event type this way.

You can also post a correctly signed delivery to your receiver yourself, without a stack: mapi_spec.webhooks.signature_header(body, [secret]) builds the header exactly as the platform does.

docs.title: Good receivers
docs.text:
• Answer fast with a 2xx, then do the work in the background: the platform gives up on a delivery after 5 seconds and retries it (after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h).
  • Expect duplicates. Retries and replays send the same event again; keep the event.ids you handled.
  • Answer 410 Gone to stop deliveries for good: the webhook is disabled at once. After 20 consecutive failed events it is disabled anyway (mapi webhooks ls shows why; re-enable it with api.webhooks.update(id, active=True)).
  • Keep the secret secret. It is shown once; store it in your secret manager. Rotate it with mapi webhooks rotate <id> and give the receiver both secrets until the old one expires.
  • Serve HTTPS on port 443 or 8443 under a public host name in production: the platform refuses to deliver to private, loopback or link-local addresses (see SSRF protection).

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• React to endpoint.promoted by refreshing a Google Sheet or a cache.
  • Chain a pipeline: on model.version.ready with scorecard_overall: pass, promote it with a token scoped endpoints:promote (Endpoints and webhooks).

docs.title: Deployment v0.3
docs.text:
The whole platform runs on one machine in two ways that start the same services on the same ports, so URLs, the CLI, the Python client and the tests work with either. v0.3 adds Google Cloud: Terraform for every project and scripts that deploy, migrate and roll back. All three run the same multi-tenant code; only the executor, the store and the identity provider change.

Local, without Docker Docker Compose Google Cloud (v0.3) Command make dev make docker-build && make compose-up deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env ENV PostgreSQL embedded (pgserver) or your DATABASE_URL the official postgres:16 image Cloud SQL Object storage the GCS shim, in .local/gcs the GCS shim image, in a volume Cloud Storage Runs execute as mapi-runner subprocesses of the worker subprocesses of the worker container, or one container per run Cloud Run Jobs, one fresh sandbox per run Code your working tree, with hot reload the container images the same images Sign-in the development IdP the development IdP Google or another OpenID provider Use it for development, demos, the end-to-end tests checking the production images end to end a multi-tenant private beta: start with the [verify M0] checklist 
flowchart LR
    browser(("browser")) -->|":5173"| web["web app"]
    browser -->|":5174"| plots["plot sandbox<br/>(separate origin)"]
    browser -->|":8000 /v1"| api
    browser -->|":4443 signed URLs"| shim
    cli["mapi CLI ·<br/>Python client"] -->|"/v1"| api
    api["api<br/>(mapi-server api)"] --> pg[("PostgreSQL")]
    api --> shim["GCS shim"]
    worker["worker<br/>(dispatcher · reconciler ·<br/>finalizer · events)"] --> pg
    worker --> shim
    worker -->|"starts"| runner["mapi-runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    runner -->|"signed URLs only"| shim

Whichever you choose:

  • Sign-in is for development only. Both run the servers in the dev profile: anyone who can reach the API can sign in as one of the seeded accounts through the built-in identity provider (MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant turns sign-in off). The API listens on 127.0.0.1, and compose publishes every port on 127.0.0.1 only. Do not expose a local stack to untrusted networks; see the security model.
  • State is the database plus the object store. Back up both (.local/pg and .local/gcs locally; the pgdata and gcsdata volumes under compose), and the bundle signing key (.local/keys/) if you want existing model versions to stay downloadable.
  • Migrations run first. make dev and compose both run mapi-server migrate before the API and the worker start, and stop if it fails.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
• Local, without Docker: what make dev starts, everyday commands, working on one component, where state lives.
  • Docker Compose: the compose stack, its network layout and the executor choice.
  • Container images: the six images, how they are built and the guards that keep them honest.
  • Deploying to Google Cloud: the [verify M0] checklist, then the Terraform and deploy scripts, step by step, to the first tenant.
  • Security hardening on Google Cloud: what each control does, and the M0 verification checklist.
  • Authentication and isolation: sign-in, API tokens, operators, row-level security and Pub/Sub push.
  • Cloud Run Jobs executor: the v0.3 execution backend.
  • Observability: metrics, logs, traces, and the dashboards, alerts and runbooks in ops/.
  • Security suite: the sandbox-escape probes and what each isolation level must block.
  • M2 verification: what was verified of the M2 exit criteria without a cloud project, the measured numbers, and the steps left for a real one.
  • M3 verification: the Guided journey and the integrations through the live stack, the unaided-tester timings and fixes, and the protocol for the five testers.
  • Configuration reference: every environment variable.
  • Troubleshooting: port conflicts and everything else.

docs.title: Authentication and tenant isolation v0.3
docs.text: This page is for whoever runs mapi-server. The concepts (roles, scopes, project selection) are in Tenancy and authentication; every variable named here is in the configuration reference.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
MAPI_PROFILE Who may call the API Sign-in single-tenant (default) Anyone who can reach it (it listens on loopback): credential-less requests act as the local administrator of the default tenant. Sessions and API tokens work too Optional multi-tenant Only callers with a browser session or an API token; everything else is 401 MAPI_OIDC_* dev As multi-tenant The built-in development IdP (below)

In every profile, each request is checked against the operation's rule in mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS (a route without one cannot start), the caller's roles are read from memberships at that moment, and every database query of a request runs in a transaction pinned to the request's tenant (row-level security, below).

docs.title: Browser sign-in (BFF)
docs.text:
The web app never sees an OAuth token. The API does the OpenID Connect work:

  1. GET /auth/login?return_to=/runs stores a login transaction (state, nonce and PKCE verifier) server-side, sets a 10-minute __Host-mapi_login cookie and redirects to the provider (Authorization Code flow, PKCE S256, nonce).
  2. GET /auth/callback consumes the transaction exactly once, compares state in constant time, exchanges the code with the verifier and verifies the ID token against the provider's JWKS: signature (asymmetric algorithms only; alg must match the key), issuer, audience (and azp), expiry, issued-at and nonce. Keys are cached for an hour and refetched when a token names an unknown key id (rotation).
  3. It finds the user by (issuer, subject). A first sign-in with a verified e-mail claims pending invitations for that address; an unverified e-mail claims nothing.

  4. It starts a server-side session and sets two cookies:

    Cookie Attributes Purpose __Host-mapi_session HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ The session (the server stores only its SHA-256). 2 h idle, 12 h absolute __Host-mapi_csrf Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ (readable by the app) The CSRF token

Without TLS (MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE=false, the default for http:// API URLs) the cookies are mapi_session and mapi_csrf without Secure. Use that for local development only.

CSRF. Every cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (logout included) must send the session's token in X-CSRF-Token (the mapi_csrf cookie, or the X-CSRF-Token response header of GET /auth/session). Requests whose Origin is not the web app or the API, or with Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, are refused too. API-token requests are not cookie-authenticated and need no CSRF token.

GET /auth/session answers whether the browser is signed in; POST /auth/logout ends the session. Failed sign-ins answer 401 with a generic message; the reason is in the audit log (auth.login_failed).

docs.title: Google sign-in
docs.text:
1. In the Google Cloud console, create an OAuth client ID of type Web application with the authorized redirect URI https://<api host>/auth/callback.

  2. Configure the API:

    MAPI_PROFILE=multi-tenant
MAPI_API_URL=https://api.mapi.example
MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com
MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=...            # from Secret Manager, never in images
MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS=oncall@mapi.example

    Google's ID tokens use the issuer https://accounts.google.com (older ones accounts.google.com); both are accepted. MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS='{"hd": "acme.com"}' pre-selects a Workspace domain in the account chooser. It is only a hint: who may do what is decided by memberships.

Other providers (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0, an Identity Platform tenant fronted by an OIDC-compliant provider): set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER to the issuer whose /.well-known/openid-configuration lists an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint and a JWKS. Identity Platform's own client-SDK tokens (issuer securetoken.google.com/<project>, obtained without an authorization-code endpoint) are not accepted by the BFF yet.

docs.title: The development IdP (offline)
docs.text:
MAPI_PROFILE=dev mounts a small OpenID provider in the API at /dev/idp, so sign-in works without a network:

  • /auth/login redirects to /dev/idp/authorize, a page listing the accounts in MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS (default admin@dev.local, analyst@dev.local, viewer@dev.local);
  • at start-up these accounts are invited: the first as admin of the default tenant and platform operator, the second as runner and the others as viewer of the default project;
  • its ID tokens are RS256-signed with a key generated at start-up and go through exactly the same verification as a real provider's; PKCE is enforced and codes are single-use.

There are no passwords: anyone who can reach a dev API can sign in as any listed account. The IdP refuses to mount in any other profile.

The CLI can use it too (see The CLI). Its issuer is the identifier https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost, and the API serves its discovery document:

mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost \
           --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
mapi login signs in with the identity provider directly, using the authorization code flow with PKCE and a one-off listener on 127.0.0.1. It then sends the ID token as Authorization: Bearer. The API accepts such a bearer when all of these hold:

  • it is a JWT, not a mapi_ API token;
  • it is signed by the configured issuer (checked against its JWKS), and has not expired;
  • its audience is one of MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS (default mapi-cli). The BFF's own client id is not accepted.

The caller is then the same user as in a browser session. The first use claims a pending invitation, exactly like /auth/callback. No cookie is involved, so no CSRF token is needed, and GET /v1/me reports auth: session. Set MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS= (empty) to accept API tokens only. Register the CLI as a public "installed app" client with your provider; it needs a loopback redirect URI, PKCE and the openid email scopes.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs send Authorization: Bearer mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>. A token is minted for its caller in the selected project (POST /v1/tokens, shown once), acts as its owner narrowed by its scopes, and is bound to that project:

  • the server stores only HMAC-SHA256 of the token under a pepper derived from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET and compares in constant time; a typo is caught by the checksum before any database lookup, and no error ever echoes the presented value;
  • expired, revoked or orphaned tokens (owner disabled) answer 401; a wrong secret for a known prefix, expiry and revocation are audited as token.auth_failed, at most five times per token prefix and minute (anyone who knows a prefix can cause them). An unknown prefix and a wrong secret get the same answer, the API token is invalid;
  • a disabled account stays disabled: signing in again is refused (a generic 401, audited as auth.login_failed), and only an invitation becomes active at its first sign-in;
  • a token never carries operator powers, even if its owner is an operator;
  • a token cannot mint tokens, whatever its scopes (admin included): a child would escape its parent's expiry, budget, rate limit and revocation, so POST /v1/tokens needs a signed-in session (mapi login or the browser);
  • per-token rate_limit_per_minute (RATE_LIMITED, Retry-After) and a vCPU-second budget per UTC day or month apply in addition to the tenant's quotas.

Rotate the root secret only together with every token: all existing tokens stop working.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Users whose verified e-mail is in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS are platform operators. The server decides this on every request from the current configuration, so removing an address takes effect at once for browser sessions and mapi login ID tokens alike; nobody needs to sign in again. With a browser session they may use /v1/admin/* (tenants, quota policies, kill switches, executor health, the platform audit log) and read metadata of every tenant: tenants, members, token listings, runs and usage. No role, flag or token lets them read datasets, specs, models or plots. Every change and every refused attempt at an operator endpoint is audited.

docs.title: Row-level security
docs.text:
mapi-server migrate creates three cluster-wide roles and turns on FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY for every table that holds tenant data, with a fail-closed policy on current_setting('app.tenant_id', false):

Role Used by Row-level security mapi_app Request handlers (one transaction per request, pinned with set_config('app.tenant_id', <tenant>, true)) Applies: it sees and writes only that tenant's rows. Owns no table mapi_gateway What the API and the events service look up before a tenant is known: authentication (which token is this, which tenants does this user belong to), tenant and member administration, operator endpoints, and routing a pushed event to its run's tenant Applies, with explicit policies: tenants, projects, memberships, API tokens (read, and touch last_used_at) and audit events (read, append), plus a few metadata columns of runs and cost_ledger (state, estimate, attempt, executor, amounts) for global quotas, the spend cap and executor health. No access at all to datasets, uploads, specs, models, plots, attempts, events or logs mapi_system The orchestrator only: dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer, housekeeper (plan §9) BYPASSRLS where the migrating login is a superuser, plus an explicit policy, so it also works on managed Postgres and for logins that are members of it

Every API request runs its platform sessions as mapi_gateway, whatever the handler does, and in a cloud deployment the API and events services cannot even read the URL of the orchestrator's login. An authorization slip in a handler that runs before the tenant is known is therefore still contained by row-level security.

A transaction that forgot to pin a tenant fails closed: on a fresh connection every query errors, on a pooled connection the setting is empty and matches no row. The test suite runs deliberately unscoped queries for two tenants over one pooled connection to prove it.

The audit log (audit_events) and the cost ledger (cost_ledger) are append-only. Neither runtime role may UPDATE or DELETE them, and a trigger refuses any change to an existing row whoever asks, so a bug or an injection cannot rewrite a tenant's audit trail or billing history. Purging them (tenant deletion, retention) is a deliberate act of the table owner, who must drop the *_append_only trigger first.

With a single DATABASE_URL (local development, the default Compose file) both pools log in as the migrating user and select their role with the start-up option role=... (RESET ROLE returns to that role). In production give each its own login:

CREATE ROLE mapi_api LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_app;
CREATE ROLE mapi_api_gateway LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_gateway;
CREATE ROLE mapi_orchestrator LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_system;

and set MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL (API and worker), MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL (API) and MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL (worker only). DATABASE_URL (the owner) is then needed by mapi-server migrate and procrastinate only.

docs.title: Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
In the cloud, run events reach POST /internal/events from a Pub/Sub push subscription with OIDC authentication. Configure the subscription with a dedicated service account and the audience https://<api host>/internal/events, then set

MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE=https://api.mapi.example/internal/events
MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=pubsub-push@mapi-prod-control.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# optional: only accept pushes from these subscriptions
MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS=projects/mapi-prod-control/subscriptions/mapi-run-events-push

Each push must carry a Google-signed ID token (RS256, checked against MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL) whose issuer is Google, audience the configured one, email the service account with email_verified: true, and which has not expired (a valid Google token for another audience or account gets 403). With MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS set, the envelope must also come from one of those subscriptions. Without these settings MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN is required when set, and a multi-tenant deployment with neither refuses every push. Refused pushes are audited as event.rejected.

docs.title: Cloud Run Jobs executor
docs.text:
The cloudrun-jobs executor runs every attempt as a fresh Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) execution: a microVM per run, created from a small, fixed set of Jobs. It is the primary backend of the hosted platform (v0.3).

Tested against fakes only

The executor, the Pub/Sub push endpoint, the KMS signer and the Cloud Storage driver are built on the real Google client libraries but have only been exercised against test doubles: an in-memory Cloud Run API (FakeCloudRun), locally generated OIDC keys, a KMS double backed by local keys and a fake storage client. Items marked [verify M0] depend on Cloud Run behaviour that still has to be confirmed in a real project.

docs.title: Install and select it
docs.text:
pip install 'mapi-server[gcp]'      # google-cloud-run, -storage, -pubsub, -kms
export MAPI_EXECUTOR=cloudrun-jobs
export MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT=mapi-prod-exec-paid
export MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION=europe-west1

The orchestrator (mapi-server worker) authenticates with Application Default Credentials: on Cloud Run, its own service account, which needs run.jobs.run, run.executions.get, run.executions.list, run.executions.cancel and run.tasks.list on the exec project (roles/run.developer, or a custom role with just these).

docs.title: The Job inventory
docs.text:
Execution overrides can change only environment variables, the task count and the timeout — never the image, CPU or memory. The platform therefore deploys one Job per base image and resource class, and picks one per attempt:

S (2 vCPU, 8 GiB) M (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) L (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) base-bayes (mmm.*, tabular.*, ingest, describe) mapi-prod-base-bayes-s mapi-prod-base-bayes-m mapi-prod-base-bayes-l base-ml (sklearn.*) mapi-prod-base-ml-s mapi-prod-base-ml-m mapi-prod-base-ml-l base-forecast (ts.*) mapi-prod-base-forecast-s mapi-prod-base-forecast-m mapi-prod-base-forecast-l

The names follow MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE (default mapi-{env}-{base}-{class}); the infrastructure must create exactly these Jobs, each with:

  • max-retries = 0 (the platform decides about retries);
  • the execution service account (get and delete on the bootstrap bucket, nothing else);
  • the static environment MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL=gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce};
  • the deny-all network and the restricted Google APIs VIP.

XL runs belong to the GKE executor (M6); the dispatcher refuses them for cloudrun-jobs.

docs.title: What one attempt looks like
docs.text:
1. The dispatcher writes the intent row (run, attempt, nonce) and the bootstrap object bootstrap/<nonce> (the RunSpec with signed URLs and the HMAC key).
  2. jobs.run on the chosen Job with only these overrides: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE, taskCount and the task timeout (the run's timeout plus MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S, so the supervisor can flush checkpoints before the backstop). Nothing goes in args.
  3. The operation's metadata names the execution; the execution name is stored as the attempt's handle and the operation name is logged.
  4. The supervisor reads and deletes its bootstrap object, runs the worker and prints HMAC-signed events, which travel Cloud Logging → Pub/Sub → POST /internal/events.
  5. The reconciler polls executions.get (and tasks.list once the execution finished, for the exit codes). Event silence only marks a run stalled; the executor's status decides whether it is alive.
Execution outcome Reported as Run outcome All tasks succeeded succeeded, exit 0 finalized after the complete event Supervisor exit 16 (checkpoints flushed) failed or cancelled, exit 16 finalized as partial Exit 137, or "memory limit exceeded" failed, exit 137 failed (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), retry one class up Task timeout failed, exit 143 failed (TIMEOUT) Cancelled through executions.cancel cancelled cancelled, or partial if it flushed Execution not found unknown cancelled and confirmed gone, then retried as an infrastructure failure

docs.title: Orphans and duplicates
docs.text:
Cloud Run chooses execution names, so an execution is identified by its nonce. If the dispatcher dies after jobs.run but before storing the handle, the reconciler calls adopt(nonce): it lists the recent executions of every Job in the inventory and matches the MAPI_NONCE override in the execution template [verify M0]. If two executions carry the same nonce, the oldest is kept and the others are cancelled; a duplicate that starts anyway finds no bootstrap object (the first one deleted it) and exits without doing any work.

A jobs.run call that fails ambiguously (a timeout or a 5xx after the request was sent) is never retried blindly: the next submit of that nonce adopts first.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: jobs.run is limited per project and region (180 calls a minute [verify M0]). Each orchestrator keeps a token bucket at MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE (default 150 — split the quota between orchestrator replicas). A 429 answer means nothing was created: the executor puts every submitter into a shared cool-down (exponential back-off from MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, at least the server's Retry-After but never more than MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S), counts the answer as an alarm (ALARM cloudrun-jobs: jobs.run answered 429 in the log, throttled_last_hour in the executor health, mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total{executor} at /metrics, which the MapiJobsRun429 alert watches) and retries the same nonce. When MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES answers in a row are exhausted the run goes back to the queue for a new attempt, without using up one of its MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES: a throttling storm delays runs, it never fails them. While a dispatcher works through a batch it keeps extending the leases of the runs it has not submitted yet, so the reconciler never takes over a run whose submit is only slow. A single submit that hangs for more than ten lease lengths stops the renewals: the leases lapse and the reconciler adopts what jobs.run created (by nonce) or retries the attempt.

docs.title: Fan-out with taskCount
docs.text: Homogeneous children of a fan-out parent (same kind, class, base and timeout) can run as the tasks of one execution (RunSubmit.task_count). Task i reads its own bootstrap object at a nonce derived from the execution nonce and CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX (mapi_server.executors.tasks.task_nonce), numbers its events from task_seq(i, 0) so the event dedupe keeps every task's events, and writes its outputs under .../a{n}/tasks/{i}/. The execution succeeds only when every task does; a cancel stops all of them. Fan-out parents (Sweep, SBC, Backtest) arrive in v0.5; the executor side is ready.

docs.title: Events: authenticated Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
A Cloud Logging sink with the filter jsonPayload.mapi_event:* publishes the supervisors' event lines to a topic; a push subscription with OIDC authentication delivers them to POST /internal/events. Configure the expected token:

export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE=https://api.example.com/internal/events
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=mapi-events-push@mapi-prod-control.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS=projects/mapi-prod-control/subscriptions/mapi-run-events-push

Every push is then checked in this order, before anything in the body is read:

  1. the bearer token's RS256 signature against Google's JWKS (cached per Cache-Control; an unknown key id triggers at most one refetch every 30 s; cached keys ride out a short JWKS outage);
  2. its claims: issuer Google, our audience, the push service account with a verified e-mail, not expired (60 s leeway);
  3. the subscription name against MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS.

Failures answer 401/403 and are retried by Pub/Sub (configure a dead-letter topic). The message is then decoded — base64 Cloud Logging entry, jsonPayload.mapi_event, the run.googleapis.com/execution_name label — and the event is HMAC-verified with its attempt key, deduplicated on (run, attempt, seq) and coalesced into the run's progress row. A forged or replayed event is acknowledged (200, counted as a sandbox violation) and changes nothing.

In the multi-tenant profile the endpoint refuses every request until push authentication is configured (or, for a local setup, MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN is set).

docs.title: Bundle signatures with Cloud KMS
docs.text:
export MAPI_SIGNER=kms
export MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION=projects/mapi-prod-control/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/mapi/cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/2
export MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS=projects/.../cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/1

Only the SHA-256 digest of a manifest is sent to asymmetricSign (EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256 or RSA_SIGN_PSS_*_SHA256). The response is checked for verified_digest_crc32c, the key version name and signature_crc32c, and the signature is verified locally before it is stored. The public keys of the active and trusted versions are loaded at startup, so verifying a manifest before minting URLs is local and never waits on KMS. To rotate, create a new version, point MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION at it and keep the old one in MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS until no model version signed with it is in use. With Terraform these are control.kms_key_version and control.kms_trusted_key_versions (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md).

docs.title: Cloud Storage
docs.text: GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run(...) signs V4 URLs and POST policies through the IAM Credentials signBlob API with a refreshing token (the control-plane service account), and create-only POST policies as an uploader account that can create but not delete objects — GCS POST forms take no generation precondition, so an account that cannot delete cannot overwrite. The URLs are byte-identical to google-cloud-storage's own V4 signer. Every write is checked against the CRC32C and MD5 that Cloud Storage computed, and copies pin the source generation and compare the result. See GCS shim.

docs.title: Executor conformance and load
docs.text:
An executor takes shared tiers only after it passes the executor conformance suite (mapi_spec.conformance_executor) and the security suite: submit, orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash, duplicate submit, cancel mid-run, timeout, stalled-not-lost, confirmed cancel before retry, checkpoint resume, OOM classification, fan-out, generation verification and 429 back-off.

uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py      # fake-cloudrun, local-process
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py -m docker   # needs a daemon
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_load_cloudrun.py -s           # 100 fits; prints metrics

Each case runs the real dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and finalizer and checks the exact sequence of run states (recorded by a database trigger). The load test pushes 100 concurrent fits through cloudrun-jobs over the fake backend, with outputs on the GCS shim, events as lagging, duplicated Pub/Sub pushes, three 429s and two lost jobs.run responses. At the default 150 submits a minute it measures a p95 time-to-running of about 46 s with no lost run and exactly one execution per run. Real Cloud Run cold starts come on top.

docs.title: The shared-tier gate
docs.text:
The gate is enforced in code. verified and public tenants are placed on an executor only when both hold:

  1. its caps allow it: isolation of at least gVisor, with egress and DNS enforced;
  2. a passing executor-conformance report and a passing security-suite report were recorded for exactly the caps it currently reports, and neither is older than MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S (3 days by default, so the nightly suites keep it open).

A security-suite report only counts as evidence of enforced egress and DNS when the http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes ran and were blocked (skipped is not evidence). Record results with PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence (operators only, audited), with the target the suites ran against:

curl -X PUT "$API/v1/admin/executors/cloudrun-jobs/evidence" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"target": {"executor": "cloudrun-jobs", "caps": <caps from GET /v1/admin/executors>,
                  "remote_control_api": true, "enforces_memory_limit": true},
       "conformance": <ConformanceReport>, "security": <mapi-security --json output>}'

Until then the dispatcher leaves verified and public runs queued (it never fails them for missing evidence), and GET /v1/admin/executors shows shared_tiers_enabled: false with the reason in message, plus conformance_passed and security_passed. The executor itself stays enabled for the trusted tiers: enabled and the disabled status are the operators' switch (PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}, incident containment), never the evidence gate's. Evidence recorded for other caps (a changed region list, a flipped MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED) no longer counts. internal and self_hosted_trusted tenants are not gated.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT — Exec project holding the Job inventory (required) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 Region of the inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} Job id convention MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to base (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes Base for runs without a plugin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 Token bucket in front of jobs.run (at most 180) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 429 answers in a row before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 Exponential back-off after a 429 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + margin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false The DNS response policy is verified for Jobs [verify M0]; verified and public tenants need both, plus recorded evidence MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption looks MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT — Expected push token (set both) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any Accepted subscriptions (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL Google's Where the OIDC signing keys come from MAPI_SIGNER local local (PEM key file) or kms MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION, MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS — Active and still-trusted key versions

docs.title: Configuration reference v0.3
docs.text:
Every component is configured through environment variables; no component reads a config file except the CLI and the Python client (~/.config/mapi/config.toml) and Docker Compose (.env). This page lists every MAPI_* variable in the code base, grouped by who reads it. A test (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py) scans the source tree and fails when a variable is missing here. Two tables are generated from the code at every docs build: the server settings (every mapi-server field with its type and default) and the index of environment variables (every MAPI_* name in the code, the images, the Terraform and the deploy scripts, with who mentions it and the section below that explains it).

New in v0.3

Sign-in and tenancy (MAPI_PROFILE, MAPI_OIDC_*, MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, MAPI_SERVER_SECRET, the two database roles), quotas and cost (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH, MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED), the Cloud Run Jobs executor (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_*), Cloud Storage and KMS (MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs, MAPI_SIGNER=kms), Pub/Sub push authentication and observability (MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN, MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT). On Google Cloud, Terraform sets them (the deployment contract).

The short version

For a local stack you only ever need the four addresses, and only when a port is taken: MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN. Export the same values in every shell that runs make dev, make seed, make e2e, mapi or the Python client. Troubleshooting has an example.

docs.title: Topology (every component)
docs.text:
These come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev, the one contract the API, worker, runner, GCS shim, make dev, make seed, the end-to-end tests and (through VITE_*) the web app share, so they cannot disagree about where things are.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_ENV local Environment name; buckets are mapi-{env}-quarantine, -bootstrap, -runs, -bundles, -data DATABASE_URL (or MAPI_DATABASE_URL) unset A postgresql:// URL. Unset: make dev and mapi serve start an embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver) in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/pg MAPI_API_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 Where the API listens and is reached. make dev derives the API's host and port from it MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT http://127.0.0.1:4443 The object store (the GCS shim). Signed URLs point here MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5173 The web app's origin. The API and the shim allow it for CORS MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox's origin. Must differ from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN: every component refuses a configuration where they are equal MAPI_DATA_DIR .local Local state: pg/, gcs/ (objects and the shim's keys), keys/ (the bundle-signing key), executions/, dev/

docs.title: mapi-server (API and worker)
docs.text:
mapi-server api, worker, migrate and dev read mapi_server.settings.Settings: each field is the variable MAPI_<FIELD>. Besides the topology above:

Identity and API

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev (multi-tenant with the built-in development identity provider). The local-process executor refuses multi-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID, MAPI_PROJECT_ID default The platform's own tenant and project (the only ones of a single-tenant install; platform runs such as describe live there) MAPI_API_HOST, MAPI_API_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8000 Bind address of mapi-server api when started without --host/--port MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS 127.0.0.1,localhost,api Host header values the API answers (comma-separated; the host of MAPI_API_URL is always allowed; * turns the check off). The DNS-rebinding guard of the unauthenticated M1 API MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES unset Addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of the API (load balancer, Cloud Run front end, the web container's /v1/ proxy), comma-separated. A request from one of them takes the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy as the client address, which the per-address limits (sign-up, verification, embed views), the Sybil same_ip check and audit fingerprints use. none: clients connect directly and X-Forwarded-For is ignored. Required in the multi-tenant profile; make dev sets none for its multi-tenant stack MAPI_DEBUG false Put tracebacks into problem documents' untrusted_text. Never in production MAPI_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warning or error MAPI_LOG_JSON true One JSON object per log line (structlog, with trace_id/span_id and the request, run and tenant context); false gives a human console format MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics (see Observability) MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset Bearer a scraper must present on GET /metrics. Required in the multi-tenant profile, which refuses scrapes without it (the series carry tenant ids and spend) MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 Serve the worker's own GET /metrics (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer series) on this address; same bearer rule as the API MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Create OpenTelemetry spans for requests, outgoing HTTP calls and runs MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset OTLP/HTTP collector to export spans to (also read from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT); unset creates spans without exporting them MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN unset If set (and Pub/Sub push authentication is not), POST /internal/events requires this bearer token. A multi-tenant profile with neither refuses every push MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset Set both to require a Google-signed OIDC token from the push subscription's service account on POST /internal/events (see Authentication and the Cloud Run settings below) MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S 15 Seconds between : keepalive comments on event streams MAPI_SSE_POLL_S 5 Fallback poll of an event stream when no PostgreSQL NOTIFY arrives MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S 60 How often an open event stream re-checks its caller's credential (revoked tokens, ended sessions and lost access close it) MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES 8 MiB Largest JSON sidecar (plots.json, diagnostics.json, …) the control plane will parse

MAPI_PROFILE means two things

The CLI and the Python client read MAPI_PROFILE as the name of a config-file profile; the server reads it as the deployment profile. Do not export a client profile name in a shell that starts make dev or mapi-server: the server refuses any value other than single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev.

Database

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE 10 Request-path connections per process (plus as many overflow connections) MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_POOL_SIZE 5 Platform-role connections per process (the orchestrator) MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_POOL_SIZE 5 Gateway-role connections per process (the API and events service) MAPI_DB_ECHO false Log every SQL statement MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL unset Dedicated login of the request-path role (row-level security applies). Unset: DATABASE_URL with the start-up option role=$MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL unset Dedicated login of the platform role, the only one that bypasses row-level security: the orchestrator's dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and housekeeper. The API never needs it. Unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL unset Dedicated login of the gateway role: what the API and events service look up before a tenant is known (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, pushed events), with row-level security applying. Unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE, MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE mapi_app, mapi_system, mapi_gateway The three runtime roles mapi-server migrate creates and grants (see Authentication)

Authentication (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_AUTH_REQUIRED on, except single-tenant Require a session or API token on every non-public route. Cannot be turned off in a multi-tenant profile MAPI_SERVER_SECRET from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH Root secret of the API-token pepper, the audit fingerprints and the key that seals webhook secrets. Every API and worker instance must share it; changing it invalidates every token and webhook secret MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH server-secret next to the bundle-signing key File holding the root secret (0600, created by mapi-server migrate; Compose keeps it on the keys volume) MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE on when MAPI_API_URL is https __Host- prefixed, Secure session cookies. Off: mapi_session/mapi_csrf for plain-HTTP development MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER unset The OpenID provider (for example https://accounts.google.com). Unset outside the dev profile: browser sign-in is off, tokens still work MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration Where the provider's metadata is MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET unset The OAuth client registered for the BFF (the secret is optional for public clients; PKCE is always used) MAPI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI $MAPI_API_URL/auth/callback The registered redirect URI MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS RS256,ES256 Accepted ID-token algorithms (asymmetric only) MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS mapi-cli Public OIDC clients of the same issuer whose ID tokens the API accepts as Authorization: Bearer (what mapi login sends). Comma-separated; empty accepts API tokens only. In the dev profile these clients may also use the built-in IdP with a loopback redirect MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS {} Extra authorization parameters as JSON, for example {"hd": "acme.com"} MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS unset Verified e-mails that sign in as platform operators (comma-separated) MAPI_DEFAULT_TENANT_ADMINS unset E-mails invited as admins of the default tenant at start-up (claimed at first sign-in with that verified e-mail) MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS admin@dev.local,analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local The dev profile's accounts: the first is an operator and tenant admin, the second a runner, the rest viewers

Quotas and cost (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH unset A JSON PriceTable; unset: Cloud Run-like list prices (mapi_spec.cost.DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE) MAPI_ESTIMATE_WALL_S fit 300, score 30, ingest 60, … Per run kind, the wall time (seconds, capped at the run's timeout) a run is charged against vCPU-second quotas until it is metered (JSON) MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED true Enforce requests_per_minute at token, tenant and global level MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES 500 Queued runs the dispatcher's fair-share planner considers per pass (runs held by a suspended tenant, the kill switches or the spend cap are not among them) MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT 50 At most this many of them per tenant, so one tenant's held runs cannot crowd out the others MAPI_EXECUTOR_REPORT_INTERVAL_S 10 How often each dispatcher reports executor health for /v1/admin/executors MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S 259200 (3 days) How long a recorded conformance or security-suite report lets an executor take verified and public tenants (the shared-tier gate)

Plot rendering and embed links (v0.4)

See Sharing plots.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S 300 Wall-clock limit of a POST /v1/plots:render run; the sandbox stops it after this MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED false Accept Plotly plots for static rendering. This needs kaleido and a Chrome or Chromium in the runner image, which the base images do not ship. While it is off, Plotly renders are refused with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE 300 Public views per minute of one embed link (429 RATE_LIMITED beyond) MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE 120 Public embed requests per minute from one client address, valid or not (slows down token guessing) MAPI_EMBED_CACHE_S 60 How long an API instance reuses an embed's resolved plot. Expiry and revocation are still checked on every request, and responses are Cache-Control: private, no-cache, so a revoked link stops rendering on the next load MAPI_EMBED_IMAGE_URL_TTL_S 900 Lifetime of the signed URL of an embed's PNG fallback

Object storage

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim shim (the GCS shim at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT), gcs (real Cloud Storage; needs the gcp extra, MAPI_URL_SIGNER and MAPI_URL_UPLOADER) or memory (tests only) MAPI_GCP_PROJECT unset With gcs: the project of the Cloud Storage client (default: the environment's) MAPI_URL_SIGNER unset With gcs: the service account that signs URLs through IAM signBlob, so no key file exists anywhere MAPI_URL_UPLOADER unset With gcs (required): the account that signs create-only upload policies, which every run uses for its outputs. It must differ from MAPI_URL_SIGNER and may create objects but never delete them: a GCS POST form has no generation precondition, so only a signer without storage.objects.delete makes it create-only. The server refuses to start without it MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT The base URL put into signed URLs, when browsers or containers reach the shim under another host name MAPI_GCS_ROOT $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs The shim's state directory; the server reads the principals' key files under _shim/keys/ MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE $MAPI_GCS_ROOT/_shim/keys/control.json Key file of the control plane's principal MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN from exec.json Bearer token of the shim's exec principal, handed to local runs (local executors only, never in the cloud)

Executors

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process local-process, docker, docker-gvisor or cloudrun-jobs (Cloud Run Jobs executor, with its own settings) MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND mapi-runner next to the interpreter The supervisor's command line (shell-quoted) for local-process MAPI_EXECUTOR_WORKDIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/executions Per-run scratch of the local executor MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE mapi/base-bayes:<version> Runner image of the docker executors for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to runner image (JSON), tagged with the workspace version MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK none The run containers' network: container:<gcs-shim container> or an internal network that contains only the shim. none is refused while the bootstrap URL is HTTP MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED false Declare MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK an internal network holding only the shim, so docker-gvisor reports enforced egress and DNS. verified and public tenants still need a recorded security-suite run with the network probes blocked (docker) MAPI_DOCKER_RUNTIME_GVISOR runsc The OCI runtime of docker-gvisor MAPI_CANCEL_GRACE_S 10 Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when a run is cancelled

Dispatcher and reconciler

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DISPATCH_RATE_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_DISPATCH_BURST 180, 10 Token bucket in front of the executor (Cloud Run's jobs.run quota) MAPI_DISPATCH_BATCH, MAPI_DISPATCH_POLL_S 10, 1 Queued runs leased per pass, and the pause between passes MAPI_DISPATCH_LEASE_S 120 How long a dispatcher's lease on a run lasts; a live dispatcher extends it every third of that while the run waits to be submitted (for at most ten lease lengths per submit) MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS all Trust tiers whose runs this orchestrator leases (comma-separated). Several orchestrators that serve different exec pools need disjoint lists, or any of them leases any tenant's runs MAPI_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S 10 The reconciler's level-triggered loop MAPI_STALL_INTERVALS 15 A run is stalled (a warning) after this many progress intervals of silence MAPI_COMPLETE_EVENT_GRACE_S 60 How long to wait for a run's complete event after the executor reports an exit MAPI_LOST_EXECUTION_GRACE_S 60 How long an execution may be missing from the executor before the attempt is lost MAPI_DEADLINE_GRACE_S 60 Slack after a run's timeout before the reconciler stops it MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES 2 Automatic retries after infrastructure failures MAPI_HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_S 300 Sweep of expired upload intents (their quarantine objects are deleted), expired browser sessions and abandoned sign-ins MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_WINDOW_S 1800 No automatic retry of a run that has been going for longer than this MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR 2 No automatic retry once a run has cost this multiple of its estimate MAPI_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 Attempts of the finalizer job before a run fails

Catalog and signing

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CATALOG_PATH unset A catalog JSON exported at image build; unset: the worker queues a sandboxed describe run MAPI_IMAGE_DIGEST sha256 of uv.lock The runner image digest the catalog is cached under MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH found above the working directory The uv.lock whose hash is the local image digest MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH $MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem The EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests (standing in for Cloud KMS). The worker signs and the API verifies, so both must load the same file. mapi-server migrate creates it MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS none Retired bundle-signing keys (PEM files, public or private; comma-separated) whose signatures still verify, so a key rotation does not break the models the old key signed (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md) MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE true Create the key on first use when it is missing. Compose turns it off for api and worker, so a missing key fails start-up instead of a new key being minted MAPI_SIGNER local local: the key file above. kms: a Cloud KMS asymmetric key version signs (gcp extra) MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION unset With MAPI_SIGNER=kms: the projects/…/cryptoKeyVersions/N that signs new manifests MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS none Older key versions whose signatures still verify (comma-separated; rotation)

Cloud Run Jobs (MAPI_EXECUTOR=cloudrun-jobs; see Cloud Run Jobs executor)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT unset (required) The exec project holding the Job inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 Region of the inventory MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY derived Data residency of the platform tenant, of tenants the migrations adopt and of tenants created without one. Default: the multi-region of MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION with cloudrun-jobs (eu for europe-west1), else us MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} Job id convention; it must match the Jobs the infrastructure creates MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to base image family (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes Base for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 Token bucket in front of jobs.run per orchestrator (at most 180, the regional quota) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 429 answers in a row before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 Exponential back-off after a 429 (never shorter than Retry-After) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + this margin (the reconciler stops runs at their deadline; this is the backstop) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress except the restricted Google APIs VIP MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false The DNS response policy is verified to apply to Jobs (the M0 DNS red-team gate). verified and public tenants (verified is the default tier) are placed only when both are true and passing suite evidence is recorded (the shared-tier gate); until then their runs are refused at submission MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption lists executions

Webhooks (v0.4) (see Endpoints and webhooks)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S 2 How often the worker's relay looks for due deliveries and hands them to the webhooks procrastinate queue MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 Tries per delivery (1 to 8; retries wait 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h, plus up to 10% jitter) MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER 20 Disable a webhook after this many consecutive events could not be delivered (a 410 Gone disables at once); audited as webhook.disabled MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_PER_PROJECT 25 Webhooks one project may have (409 beyond) MAPI_WEBHOOK_RETENTION_DAYS 30 Days events and their delivery logs are kept MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE unset An extra PEM CA bundle trusted for receivers (a private CA); the system trust store is always used MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP false Development only: accept http:// URLs for the hosts in MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST. Refused in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST none Development only: host names (comma-separated, optionally host:port) exempt from the SSRF address and port checks, such as a receiver on localhost. Refused in the multi-tenant profile

Webhook signing secrets are sealed with a key derived from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET: changing the server secret makes every webhook secret unusable (rotate them afterwards).

Pub/Sub push events (POST /internal/events)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE unset Expected audience of the push subscription's OIDC token. When set, every push needs a Google-signed token MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset The service account the subscription signs as (set together with the audience) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any Accepted subscription names (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs Google's OIDC signing keys

Sign-up, e-mail and abuse controls (v0.4) (see Sign-up and abuse controls)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED on in dev and multi-tenant when a mailer works, off single-tenant Self-service sign-up at POST /auth/signup. Setting it on without a usable mailer refuses to start MAPI_MAILER outbox in dev, smtp in multi-tenant, console otherwise console (log the message), outbox (JSON files, read at GET /dev/outbox in dev), smtp or none. multi-tenant refuses console and outbox while sign-up is on: whoever reads the logs or the disk could verify any address MAPI_MAIL_FROM modeling-api <no-reply@mapi.localhost> The From: header MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/outbox Where the outbox mailer writes (mode 0600, newest 200 kept) MAPI_SMTP_HOST, MAPI_SMTP_PORT unset, 587 The SMTP server. Without a host the smtp mailer is off (and so is sign-up) MAPI_SMTP_TLS starttls starttls (required, not opportunistic: a server without it is refused) or ssl (implicit TLS, port 465). The certificate is verified against the system trust store MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME, MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD unset SMTP authentication (keep the password in a secret store) MAPI_SMTP_TIMEOUT_S 10 Connection and command timeout MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN/verify-email?token={token} The link e-mailed to a sign-up; {token} is replaced MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS none E-mail domains refused besides the built-in disposable list (comma-separated; subdomains included) MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH unset A file of disposable domains, one per line (# comments), for example a maintained public list MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR 5 Sign-ups accepted per client address and hour MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY 25 Verified sign-ups per e-mail domain and day (unverified ones do not count; the shared free-mail domains are exempt) MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR 500 Verified sign-ups per hour on the whole platform (unverified ones do not count) MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS built-in list (gmail.com, outlook.com, ...) Free-mail domains shared by unrelated people (comma-separated; replaces the built-in list): no per-domain cap and no domain_burst flag MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE 20 E-mail verification attempts per client address and minute MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS 30 Look-back of the Sybil heuristics MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD 3 Workspaces from one client address, browser or e-mail within the window before the next one is flagged for review (a domain is flagged at twice as many within an hour) MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND false Suspend a flagged sign-up's workspace until an operator approves it (default: it works and waits in the review queue) MAPI_SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS 30 Unverified sign-ups, with their e-mail, are deleted after this MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED false Cut line B (M5): let identity-verified public tenants run uploaded code. Off: public tenants run built-in models and declarative specs only

Tenant deletion and GDPR export (v0.4) (see Deleting data)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S 604800 (7 days) Grace period of a deletion: the tenant is suspended and may cancel MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S unset Also require a sign-in at most this many seconds old to request a deletion; unset: the confirmation phrase alone MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S 3600 How long a purge waits for the tenant's cancelled runs to stop before it goes ahead MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 Automatic retries (with back-off from 5 minutes to 6 hours) of a failed purge; then an operator retries MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The bundles bucket's retention period (Terraform bundle_retention_days): when a purge retries the objects a retention lock kept MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S 15 Cadence of the orchestrator's deletion and export scheduler MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES 256 MiB Dataset bytes an export archive includes; the rest is listed in its manifest MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S 604800 (7 days) How long an export archive is kept MAPI_EXPORT_LINK_TTL_S 900 Lifetime of an export's signed download link (a fresh one on every GET) MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY 3 Exports a tenant may request per day (one at a time) MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES 256 MiB Metadata rows an export archive includes; tables cut short are listed in its manifest MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S 3600 How long an export build may take; a build still running five minutes later (its process died) is built again once, then failed

docs.title: The runner (per run)
docs.text:
Executors start mapi-runner with exactly these variables, and nothing secret in its arguments. Never set them by hand.

Variable Meaning MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE The run, and the 256-bit nonce of its one-time bootstrap object MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL A template with {nonce}: where the supervisor reads (and deletes) the bootstrap object MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN Local executors only: the shim's exec principal, which may only get and delete bootstrap objects MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The worker's interpreter (default: the supervisor's) MAPI_BASE_IMAGE The base image recorded in the run's lineage MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION Set to 1 by the docker executor: the supervisor fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION instead of running the worker in dev mode MAPI_TRACEPARENT The W3C traceparent of the dispatching span, so the supervisor's stderr diagnostics carry the run's trace id (nothing is exported from the sandbox) MAPI_LOG_JSON 1 (the default) makes the supervisor's stderr diagnostics JSON lines; 0 plain text

The supervisor passes the untrusted worker only an allow-list of variables (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale and thread-count variables, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, XLA_FLAGS, …). Every MAPI_* is scrubbed.

Inside the runner images, MAPI_CACHE_SEED (/opt/mapi/cache) is the baked, read-only PyTensor and Numba cache and MAPI_CACHE_DIR (/tmp/mapi-cache) the writable symlink farm the entry point builds over it (Container images).

docs.title: The GCS shim
docs.text: mapi-gcs-shim serve takes its defaults from the topology: MAPI_DATA_DIR (state in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs), MAPI_ENV (bucket names), MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT (host and port) and MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN (the CORS origin). Each has a command-line flag; see the GCS shim reference. MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS, when set, is also the bundles bucket's locked retention in days when the shim creates its state (0: none; unset: write-once, about 100 years).

docs.title: The CLI and the Python client
docs.text:
Variable Meaning MAPI_URL The API (falls back to MAPI_API_URL, then the profile, then http://127.0.0.1:8000) MAPI_TOKEN An API token (mapi_…), sent as Authorization: Bearer. It wins over a stored mapi login sign-in, and is never sent over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host MAPI_PROJECT The project to act in, <tenant>/<project> (v0.3), sent as X-Mapi-Project on project-scoped requests. Wins over mapi use MAPI_PROFILE The profile of the config file to use (see the warning above) MAPI_CONFIG The config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml, else ~/.config/mapi/config.toml) MAPI_CREDENTIALS Where mapi login keeps sign-ins (default credentials.json next to the config file; mode 0600) MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER The identity provider for mapi login (https, or plain http on a loopback address for a local development provider) MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID The OIDC client id of the CLI (default mapi-cli) MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL Where the issuer's discovery document is, when not under the issuer. The dev profile's built-in IdP has the issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost and serves its document at <api>/dev/idp MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Only for identity providers that require one from installed apps (for example Google "desktop" clients); never printed

Arguments (--url, --token, --project, --profile, or Client(base_url=…, token=…, project=…)) win over the environment, which wins over the file. mapi config show prints the result and where each value came from. mapi login, mapi use and mapi config set rewrite the config file atomically with mode 0600.

docs.title: make dev
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py reads the topology variables and:

Variable Meaning MAPI_STACK_PROFILE The servers' MAPI_PROFILE: dev (the default: sign-in through the built-in development IdP, the default tenant and project, the seeded accounts of MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS with admin@dev.local as tenant admin and platform operator), single-tenant (the credential-less M1 API) or multi-tenant. A separate name so that a CLI MAPI_PROFILE in your shell never reaches the servers MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN Outside the single-tenant profile, a random bearer for POST /internal/events is created in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/internal-token and given to the servers (the end-to-end suite reads it there) MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE, MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST Unless you set them, the dev profile writes a throwaway CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/ (ca.pem, cert.pem, key.pem), trusts the CA and allow-lists both hosts, so webhooks reach an HTTPS receiver on your machine (the M3 end-to-end suite's) MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD Replace one service's command (shell-quoted). <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS, e.g. MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --port 8000" NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR Disable or force coloured service prefixes

make dev ONLY=api and make dev WITHOUT=web,plots choose services; make seed SIZE=full loads the large demo. These are make arguments, not environment variables.

make seed, make e2e and python -m mapi_conformance run --stack sign in to a stack that requires it: with MAPI_TOKEN when set, otherwise through the development IdP as MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT (default admin@dev.local), acting in MAPI_PROJECT (default default/default).

docs.title: The web app and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
Vite build-time variables. make dev sets them from the topology; set them yourself for a production build.

Variable Default Meaning VITE_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:8000 The API the app calls (it must allow the app's origin) VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox; must differ from the app origin VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS http://127.0.0.1:4443 Origins of signed storage URLs, allowed by the app's CSP connect-src VITE_APP_ORIGINS (sandbox) http://127.0.0.1:5173,http://localhost:5173 Origins allowed to frame the sandbox and talk to it VITE_AUTH_BASE VITE_API_BASE Where the sign-in routes (/auth/*) live, when they are not on the API base VITE_TERMS_URL /terms The terms of service sign-up links to (an http(s) URL or a path on the app's origin); the default is the plain-language summary the app ships VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL /acceptable-use The acceptable-use policy sign-up links to, likewise. A public installation should publish its own versions of both

The web app's Playwright smoke suite serves the app on 5173 and the sandbox on 5174. When those ports are taken, set MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT and MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT; the suite then builds the app for that sandbox origin and exports it to the specs as MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_ORIGIN.

The sandbox's index.html carries a %MAPI_CSP% placeholder that its Vite build replaces with the Content-Security-Policy; it is not a variable you set.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example).

Variable Default Meaning POSTGRES_PASSWORD required The database password; compose refuses to start without it MAPI_VERSION the workspace version The mapi/* image tag (make compose-up sets it) MAPI_ENV local As above MAPI_STACK_PROFILE dev The servers' MAPI_PROFILE, as for make dev MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process The worker's executor MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY, MAPI_WORKER_CPUS 4g, 12g, 4 The worker's /tmp (the scratch of every local-process run), memory limit and CPUs DOCKER_GID 0 With the docker executor override: the group that owns the Docker socket

docs.title: The mapi/web image (nginx)
docs.text:
Rendered into the nginx configuration when the container starts (only MAPI_* variables are substituted).

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT the local defaults Origins written into the CSP and frame-ancestors headers MAPI_API_UPSTREAM http://api:8000 Where /v1/ is proxied (a URL without a path) MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES 127.0.0.1 localhost Host names the app server answers (space-separated); any other Host gets no response. Keep in step with MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA empty Extra script-src sources for the app. Widening the CSP needs a review NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR /etc/nginx/templates/all …/web or …/plots serves only one of the two apps

docs.title: Image build arguments
docs.text:
docker build --build-arg NAME=value (the Makefile passes VERSION, VCS_REF and BUILD_DATE). The defaults define what each image is; change them only to build a variant.

Argument Meaning MAPI_PACKAGES The workspace packages installed into the image (mapi-runner mapi-steps mapi-pymc …) MAPI_WORKER_PACKAGES What the worker target adds to base-bayes (mapi-plugin-ts mapi-server[docker]) MAPI_NO_INSTALL Distributions never installed (the 300 MB nvidia-nccl-cu13) MAPI_APT_PACKAGES System packages of the runtime stage (tini, and g++ for PyTensor) MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT, MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT Distributions that must, and must not, be installed; the build fails otherwise MAPI_IMAGE_NAME, MAPI_DESCRIPTION OCI labels, and the name the catalog export records PYTHON_IMAGE (and the other base images) Base images, pinned by tag and digest (make docker-pin)

docs.title: Deploying to Google Cloud
docs.text:
The deploy scripts under deploy/gcp/ take their settings as flags (--help on each). One variable changes where they keep local files:

Variable Meaning MAPI_DEPLOY_OUT Local scratch of deploy/gcp/*.sh: images files, saved plans, Terraform outputs (default deploy/gcp/.out, one directory per environment; never committed) MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL Repository secret of the nightly workflow: the Pushgateway the security jobs push mapi_security_probe_unexpected to (unset: no push; ops/README.md)

The variables Terraform sets on the Cloud Run services (the deployment contract with mapi-server) are listed in Deploy to Google Cloud.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_E2E Set by pnpm --filter @mapi/web e2e: run the Playwright @e2e suite against a running stack MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT The development-IdP account make seed and the end-to-end suites sign in as (default admin@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_ACCOUNTS The two development-IdP accounts the M2 tenancy suite makes tenant admins (default analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_UI_ACCOUNT The tenant admin of the M2 browser flow and the fit burst (default analyst@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS Opt-in: how many concurrent real fits tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py submits (M2 verification) MAPI_E2E_SIGNUP_ACCOUNT The address the M3 trust-lifecycle suite (tests/e2e/test_m3_trust_stack.py) signs up with; it must be a development-IdP account so it can sign in (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_GUIDED_ACCOUNT The address the M3 journey (tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py) signs up with; a development-IdP account (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_WEBHOOK_TLS_DIR Where the M3 journey's webhook receiver finds cert.pem and key.pem (default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls) MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS 1 regenerates the contract snapshot of mapi_spec and the Guided catalog fixture of the server tests (make snapshots) MAPI_HYPOTHESIS_EXAMPLES Examples per property in the wire-format round-trip tests (default 60)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_DOCS_SPEC The spec scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs (make docs-screenshots) opens and fits, default eu-geo-mmm. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN MAPI_DOCS_PROJECT The project scripts/docs_screenshots_admin.mjs (make docs-screenshots-admin) selects after capturing the project switcher, default Default project. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL and MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT MAPI_GUIDED_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/guided-screenshots.spec.ts, which captures the Guided tutorial's screenshots from the mock-mode app (make docs-screenshots-guided sets it, with MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT/MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT defaulting to 15173/15174); the smoke suite skips it otherwise MAPI_EMBED_VIEW The EmbedView JSON that scripts/docs_screenshots_tutorials.mjs (make docs-screenshots-tutorials) serves to the plot sandbox's embed page, written by scripts/docs_embed_view.py (default .local/embed-view.json). The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (default ports 15173/15174) MAPI_EMBED_API The API origin the embed page asks for the view in that script, answered by Playwright (default http://127.0.0.1:8000, the sandbox dev server's VITE_API_URL; nothing needs to listen there)

docs.title: Docker Compose v0.2
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml runs the platform's container images as a local stack on one machine, in the dev profile like make dev (sign in as admin@dev.local; see signing in): the same services as make dev, on the same ports, but from the exact images that production uses. You do not need Docker for development (see Local, without Docker); use compose to check the images end to end or to run a self-contained demo. What is inside each image, how it is built and the build-time guards are on Container images.

cp .env.example .env               # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD
make docker-build                  # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make compose-up                    # docker compose up -d --wait
make seed                          # load the E33 demo through the API
open http://127.0.0.1:5173
make compose-logs SERVICE=api      # follow one service
make compose-down                  # VOLUMES=1 also deletes the database and objects

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph ns["shared network namespace (gcs-shim)"]
        shim["gcs-shim :4443"]
        api["api :8000"]
        worker["worker<br/>(local-process runs)"]
    end
    pg[("postgres :5432")]
    web["web :8080"]
    plots["plot-sandbox :8081"]
    browser(("browser")) -->|127.0.0.1:5173| web
    browser -->|127.0.0.1:5174| plots
    browser -->|"127.0.0.1:4443 (signed URLs)"| shim
    web -->|/v1/ proxy| api
    api --> pg
    worker --> pg
    migrate["migrate (one-shot)"] --> pg
Service Image Published on the host postgres postgres:16 (pinned by digest) not published; see the override example gcs-shim mapi/gcs-shim 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 (the API, which shares this namespace) migrate mapi/server, migrate; compose waits for it to exit with status 0 — api mapi/server, api via gcs-shim worker mapi/worker, mapi-server worker, MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process — web mapi/web with only the app server block 127.0.0.1:5173 plot-sandbox mapi/web with only the sandbox server block 127.0.0.1:5174

Why api, worker and gcs-shim share one network namespace. Signed URLs embed the object store's address, and the bootstrap URL template embeds it for runner processes. If the API reached the shim as gcs-shim:4443 while the browser needed 127.0.0.1:4443, every URL would need a public form and an internal form. With a shared namespace, 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 mean the same thing to the browser, the API, the orchestrator and every runner subprocess. That is exactly the make dev topology, and it matches the LocalDev defaults. The web container reaches the API as api:8000, which is a network alias of the shim's container.

Durable state. Three named volumes outlive the containers: pgdata (the database), gcsdata (the shim's objects and principal key files) and keys (the bundle-signing key). The worker's finalizer signs every bundle manifest, and the API verifies that signature before it hands out an artifact link, a ui/ view or a plot, and before it accepts a score request. Both must therefore load the same key, and the key must survive restarts. migrate creates it once at /var/lib/mapi/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH). api and worker mount the volume read-only, with MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false, so a missing key fails start-up loudly instead of a new key being minted silently. MAPI_DATA_DIR (/tmp/mapi-data) is per-container scratch. make compose-down VOLUMES=1 deletes the key along with the data. A new key cannot verify old bundles, so delete it only together with the database and the objects.

Hardening. Every mapi/* service runs as a non-root user, with a read-only root filesystem, a tmpfs on /tmp, all Linux capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges. Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only. The PostgreSQL password comes from .env, and compose refuses to start without it. The official postgres image is the one exception: it starts as root to fix data directory ownership, then drops to the postgres user.

Host names. The M1 API has no authentication, and a web page whose host name is re-pointed at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding) is same-origin to itself, so CORS does not stop it. The API therefore answers only the Host names in MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (default 127.0.0.1, localhost, api, plus the host of MAPI_API_URL) and returns 400 for anything else. The app's nginx server answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (default 127.0.0.1 localhost) and closes the connection for any other host. The GCS shim does the same, for loopback names and the hosts of its endpoints (--allowed-host adds more). If you reach the stack under another name, such as a LAN host name, add it to both variables.

docs.title: Executor choice: local-process vs docker
docs.text:
The compose worker runs the local-process executor inside a runner-capable image: each run is a mapi-runner subprocess of the worker container. That is the default because it needs no Docker socket and is daemon-agnostic. Its trade-offs:

local-process in mapi/worker (default) docker executor (compose.override.example.yml) Isolation Process only: runs share the worker's uid, filesystem (including its keys, see below), /tmp and memory limit One container per run, from the exact runner image, with its own limits and a network that reaches only the shim Images One large image holding every plugin plus the control plane mapi/worker for the orchestrator, and per run the mapi/base-* image that ships the run's plugin (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES) Privileges None beyond the worker's own The worker mounts /var/run/docker.sock, which is root-equivalent on the host Networking Runs reach 127.0.0.1:4443 directly Run containers join the gcs-shim network namespace (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=container:mapi-gcs-shim) Use it for Day-to-day development, demos, CI Checking production images end to end, and self-hosted setups (gVisor runsc in v0.3)

Docker executor settings. MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES maps a plugin namespace to its runner image: mmm.* and tabular.* run in mapi/base-bayes, sklearn.* in mapi/base-ml and ts.* in mapi/base-forecast. Runs without a model plugin (ingest, describe) use MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE. The defaults are the tags make docker-build produces for the current version. MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK must give the run a way to reach the object store, because the bootstrap object and every signed URL point at it. In compose that means joining the shim's network namespace (container:mapi-gcs-shim). An internal Docker network that holds only the shim also works, provided MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT names the shim on that network. none would leave the runner with nothing to fetch its bootstrap object from, so the worker refuses to start with it.

docker-gvisor for verified and public tenants. Shared tiers need an executor with egress and DNS enforced. Since none is not usable, put the run containers on an internal network that holds nothing but the shim (docker network create --internal mapi-sandbox, the shim attached to it and to nothing that routes out), set MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=mapi-sandbox and declare it with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED=true (host, bridge and default are refused). The executor then reports enforced egress and DNS, but the dispatcher places verified and public tenants on it only once the security suite ran against it with the http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes blocked, and that result and a passing conformance run are recorded (the shared-tier gate).

Worker isolation in run containers. A run container starts its supervisor as root, with every Linux capability dropped except the few the uid split needs, and with no-new-privileges. The supervisor then starts the untrusted worker as uid 10001, which has no capabilities at all. So the worker cannot signal the supervisor, read its or the init process's environment, or write to its event pipe.
