docs.title: Known gaps (not cloud-specific)
docs.text:
• Executor evidence is recorded by hand. Shared tiers are gated on stored conformance and security-suite reports (the shared-tier gate), but no job posts the nightly results to PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence yet: an operator records them.
  • The nightly workflow has not run yet. .github/workflows/nightly.yml has no remote to run on here, and its gVisor job (installing runsc on the runner) is untested.

docs.title: What remains for real GCP
docs.text:
Everything below needs a Google Cloud project. Use a throw-away dev environment, built as described in Google Cloud deployment. The values below are placeholders taken from infra/terraform/envs/dev/terraform.tfvars.example:

export ENV=dev REGION=europe-west4
export CONTROL=acme-mapi-dev-control EXEC=acme-mapi-dev-exec DATA=acme-mapi-dev-data
export EXEC_SA=mapi-$ENV-exec@$EXEC.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export NET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid SUBNET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid-jobs

docs.title: 1. Stand the environment up
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh --env $ENV --region $REGION --control-project $CONTROL \
  --data-project $DATA --build-project acme-mapi-dev-build --exec-project paid=$EXEC \
  --state-project acme-mapi-dev-build
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV --foundation
deploy/gcp/build-push.sh --env $ENV
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV            # migrations, apply, smoke test

docs.title: 2. Work through the M0 checklist
docs.text:
Every [verify M0] item is listed, with its pass condition, in the M0 verification checklist. The checklist covers four areas:

  • DNS response policy: honoured by the Direct VPC resolver, with root wildcard and bypass rules.
  • Network: egress really denied, VPC-SC on Jobs.
  • Sandbox: gen2 uid split with seccomp, no_new_privs and ptrace denial; env-only overrides; ephemeral disk and the in-memory filesystem limits; bootstrap read-then-delete.
  • Platform:
    • quotas: 1,000 Jobs and 1,000 running executions per region, 180 jobs.run a minute;
    • the Logging → Pub/Sub path and its labels;
    • push to an internal service;
    • pooled connections;
    • BYPASSRLS on Cloud SQL;
    • runWithOverrides without actAs;
    • image indexes.

docs.title: 3. Cold start and p95 time-to-RUNNING
docs.text:
Measure one cold execution per base image. Overrides only change env, so this measures exactly what the dispatcher does:

for base in base-bayes base-ml base-forecast; do
  gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-$base-s --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
    --update-env-vars MAPI_RUN_ID=coldstart,MAPI_NONCE=none --wait --format='value(name)'
done
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name:mapi-$ENV-" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='table(timestamp,resource.labels.job_name,textPayload)'

The supervisor exits at once (it finds no bootstrap object); the time from the execution's createTime to its first log line is the cold start. Then run the burst through the deployed API with a token that has the admin scope:

MAPI_API_URL=https://api.$ENV.example.com MAPI_TOKEN=<token> MAPI_PROJECT=<tenant>/<project> \
MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS=100 uv run pytest -q -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py

It asserts no loss or duplication (through the API) and p95 time-to-RUNNING under 90 s, and prints the percentiles.

docs.title: 4. Security suite inside a Cloud Run Jobs execution
docs.text:
--executor cloud only runs inside a Job execution. The runner images do not ship the suite, so build a probe image on top of the deployed base and run it as its own Job, with the same network and identity as the inventory Jobs:

REPO=$(terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/envs/$ENV output -raw image_repository)   # …/mapi-$ENV-images
IMAGE=$REPO/base-bayes@sha256:<digest from deploy/gcp/.out/$ENV/images.tfvars.json>
PROBE=$REPO/security-probe:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
printf 'FROM %s\nCOPY security/src /opt/mapi-security\nENV PYTHONPATH=/opt/mapi-security\n' "$IMAGE" \
  | docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$PROBE" -f - . && docker push "$PROBE"
gcloud run jobs create mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
  --image "$PROBE" --command python --args=-m,mapi_security,run,--executor,cloud \
  --service-account $EXEC_SA --network $NET --subnet $SUBNET --network-tags mapi-exec \
  --vpc-egress all-traffic --execution-environment gen2 --max-retries 0 --task-timeout 15m
gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION --wait
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name=mapi-$ENV-security-probe" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='value(textPayload)'

Pass: PASS: all 17 probe outcomes acceptable for this executor. On MICROVM, every isolation probe must be BLOCKED or SKIPPED. The DNS probe passes only if the zone's authoritative query log also never sees the probe's name (checklist, network section). Delete the probe Job afterwards. Making this nightly means adding the probe image to build-push.sh and the Job to infra/terraform/modules/exec. That is not done yet.

docs.title: 5. Executor conformance against the real Admin API
docs.text:
There is no live conformance target yet. packages/server/tests/mapi_server_testkit/conformance.py drives fake-cloudrun, local-process and docker only. A cloudrun-live target needs a harness that:

  • builds CloudRunJobsExecutor from settings (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT=$EXEC, the dev inventory);
  • injects the faults through real means: kill an execution with gcloud run jobs executions cancel; an OOM with a run that exceeds class S; a 429 by lowering MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE above the quota;
  • marks itself cloud.

Until then, run the chaos cases by hand against the deployed stack:

# orphan adoption: scale the orchestrator worker pool (manual scaling) to 0 right after a
# submit, then back (`gcloud beta run worker-pools update --help` names the flag of your gcloud)
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 0
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 1
# Cloud SQL failover (regional/HA instance)
gcloud sql instances failover mapi-$ENV-pg --project $CONTROL

After each one, every affected run must reach a terminal state with exactly one attempt per execution.

docs.title: 6. Cost
docs.text: Compare a day's cost_ledger with the billing export for the exec project. Then adjust the price table (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH) if list prices or discounts differ.

docs.title: M3 verification v0.4
docs.text:
Milestone M3 (Guided mode and integrations) has three exit criteria:

  1. five non-technical testers complete upload → report → scenario unaided in under 30 minutes;
  2. Atlas optimises against an endpoint;
  3. cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins (untrusted data, trusted code).

This page records how far each was verified locally, the numbers measured, what the runs found and fixed, and what remains. Real testers cannot be simulated, so the first criterion was prepared, not met: an automated "unaided tester" script measures the floor of the time budget and the screens were reviewed as a first-time analyst would read them; the protocol for the five testers below is what remains to run.

Verified on 2026-10-16 on branch feat/m3-e2e (v0.4 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS), against a live make dev stack:

  • the API, worker, web app and plot sandbox on non-default ports (API 18000, GCS shim 14443, web 15173, plot sandbox 15174);
  • the dev profile: the development identity provider and the outbox mailer;
  • the GCS shim instead of Cloud Storage and the embedded pgserver Postgres;
  • every run on the local-process executor (no Docker daemon, no cloud project);
  • MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S=0 and MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0, so a deletion can be watched to the end; higher MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR and MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY, since every run signs up new workspaces from one address.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Exit criterion Verified locally Result Still needs 5 non-technical testers: upload → report → scenario unaided in < 30 min The browser script apps/web/e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts clicks the whole Guided flow on a realistic spreadsheet, timing each step; every screen was reviewed for plain language, next steps and dead ends 135 s of automated wall time, nearly all of it the system working (the beliefs preview, the fit, the exact runs). Six usability defects found and fixed, among them two dead ends Five real testers (protocol) Atlas optimises against an endpoint mapi_client.atlas.RemoteModel against the live endpoint, with Atlas installed (atlas.core.interfaces), an optimiser written against Atlas's OptimizerProtocol The chosen allocation beats the current one under the model: +0.22 % revenue for next quarter at the same budget, from 25 candidate allocations (22 score requests) in 220 s The in-sandbox optimize job (M4) Cut line A A self-service sign-up creates a public workspace: e-mail verified, uploaded code refused (uploaded_code_allowed: false); built-ins and declarative specs run (here on an operator-promoted internal workspace, because the local executor admits only trusted tiers) Pass Public workspaces running on docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs, the only executors shared tiers may use

Everything M3 added was also exercised end to end through the API by tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py (15 tests, 7 minutes): 15 passed.

docs.title: The API journey
docs.text:
make dev        # with the variables above
make e2e        # or: uv run --with-editable ../optimizer-framework python -m pytest -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py

One analyst's workspace, from outside the processes. Each row is one test, in order; the times are wall-clock seconds of the last run.

Step What is checked Time Sign-up POST /auth/signup → the verification e-mail read from GET /dev/outbox → POST /auth/verify-email creates a public workspace whose signer is admin; the operator promotes it to internal (the local executor runs trusted tiers only) 0.03 Guided data All four templates listed; the analyst's CSV (5 regions × 3 channels × 104 weeks, columns Week, Region, Revenue, TV Spend, Search Spend, Social Spend, Avg Price) profiled locally like the browser does; role detection fills every question correctly, each with a plain reason; the draft validates; the upload ingests with the draft's mapping; detection on the stored version (columns.json) gives the same answers 13.3 MFF The same data as a BayesInsight MFF long table (Period, Geography, VariableName, VariableValue) ingests to the same variables and roles 8.3 Business priors ROI and share ranges and a baseline share (true to the simulation) plus a lift test, translated by a sandboxed translate_priors run: the translated priors hold 81 %, 76 % and 80 % of their mass inside the stated 80 % ranges; written into the spec with the run's id 13.3 Tiny fit 150 tuning steps and draws × 2 chains: every check of the template's scorecard is measured, in plain words with a docs anchor and an action; its gate (blocked: chains disagree) is exactly what mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate derives, and the server refuses the promotion with that gate's checks 30.9 Endpoint fit 1000 × 4 chains, target_accept 0.95: convergence passes or warns, holdout error under 1 %, coverage passes, every plausibility check passes 61.0 What-if vs Run exact The per-draw response grid answers a slider at once; "Run exact" (compiled by the server) scores the fit window: tv × 0.5 → grid −454,590 vs exact −454,241 (sd 14,003); search × 1.5 and tv × 0.8 → −4,762 vs −4,255 (sd 14,980). Out-of-grid multipliers are refused 10–13 per exact run Forecast, channel off An 8-week forecast fan with history and the split line; tv off over the fit window −1,046,519, against −1,046,414 from the grid's multiplier 0 10 each Promotion 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED naming the warned checks, then an audited admin override with a reason; history, schema with an example call, snippets (none carries a secret) 0.01 Score token A score:<alias> token scores the endpoint's example (8-week forecast) as an xarray tree, and gets 403 on datasets, specs, webhooks and models 10.0 Webhooks An HTTPS receiver on 127.0.0.1 (the dev profile's certificate) receives run.succeeded, model.version.ready, endpoint.promoted and score.completed, each verified with mapi_client.webhooks.verify; no body carries a data value, link or secret; the delivery log shows them; a replay arrives as the same event with a new delivery id; another secret fails verification 0.3 Embed A saved platform-recipe plot as an embed link: the public view needs no credentials, every write method answers 405, the sandbox page carries its CSP; after revocation 410 LINK_EXPIRED < 1 Atlas See Atlas 219.6 GDPR export A 49-file zip downloads; it holds the workspace's records and objects, and none of the webhook secret, the score token or the ID token 16.4 Deletion 645 tenant rows and 285 objects before. After the purge: no row in any table with a tenant_id except the retained audit_events (53), cost_ledger (33) and the deletion record; no object under t/<tenant>/ in any of the five buckets; a signed tenant.deletion.completed reaches the receiver; the admin and the score token are refused 13.4

docs.title: Atlas against the live endpoint
docs.text:
Atlas (../optimizer-framework) ships the model and optimiser interfaces. The test registers RemoteModel as an atlas.core.interfaces.AbstractModel and runs an optimiser written against OptimizerProtocol that returns Atlas's own OptimizationResult: it moves a step of budget between two channels while that raises the endpoint's predicted revenue, halving the step when no move does. Every candidate is one score request against the live endpoint (inline XrJSON, score:<alias> token).

Search Social TV Predicted revenue (13 weeks) Current plan 16,136 9,737 37,890 929,612 Chosen 19,324 9,737 34,702 931,620 (+0.22 %)

25 candidates cost 22 requests (the cache answered the rest); 220 s in all. Each request is a sandboxed score run, so the wall time is run start-up; a geo MMM's markets cannot be batched into one request (new markets are pooled), which is why the in-sandbox optimize job (M4) is the path for longer optimisations.

docs.title: The unaided-tester script
docs.text:
MAPI_E2E=1 pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec playwright test e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts

tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py creates a fresh project and writes the analyst's spreadsheet; the script then does what the five testers will be asked to do, with no hesitation, as the default tenant's admin. Screenshots land in apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m3-*.png (git-ignored); timings in m3-timings.json.

The timings below are from the release check of v0.4.0 on the integrated develop branch (2026-10-16, same laptop and settings); the first run on feat/m3-e2e took 137 s.

Step What the script does Wall time (s) 1. Template Starts where sign-in lands (/), finds Guided; "What do you want to learn?" → Geo marketing mix 0.7 2. Your data Names the analysis, chooses the CSV; checks that every question is pre-filled correctly; Upload and continue (upload, sandboxed check) 4.7 3. What you believe Ticks tv, states an ROI of 1.5 to 4, previews what it means (a sandboxed run) and continues 20.7 4. Fit the model Fit the model; plain-language phases and progress; See the results 78.5 5. Results Headline numbers, ROI and share per channel, two charts, the sanity scorecard 0.4 6. What if… Search spend +20 % on the slider (instant), Run exact, Turn off tv, a 13-week forecast 29.6 Upload → report → scenario 134.6 7. Share The gate explained; an admin's reason; Approve and go live; an embed link 0.4

Nearly all of the 135 s is the system working: the beliefs preview, the fit (79 s), the exact run, the channel-off run and the forecast; clicks, typing and page loads take a few seconds. A person reads, hesitates and explores, so the 30-minute budget is about how long the testers take to understand each screen: the script shows that the system's share is about two and a half minutes on this laptop.

The second test walks the Integrations hub: the overview cards, the endpoint page, Try it (validate, then score: 8.6 s), the curl snippet copied, a score:<alias> token from the snippet's shortcut, a webhook with its one-time secret, and the embed link: it renders read-only in a new page (no button to press) and, once revoked in the hub, the page says "This link has expired or was revoked".

docs.title: What the review found and fixed
docs.text:
Every screenshot was read as a first-time analyst would: is it plain language, is the next step obvious, is there a dead end, is an error explained? Fixed on this branch, each with a test:

Finding Where Fix "Run exact" always failed on the live stack ("User or plugin code failed"): the compiled counterfactual named no data What if… POST /v1/guided/requests:compile names the fit dataset in data for what-ifs and presets over the fit window; a score request without data is refused with 422 before a run starts "Forecast error on held-back weeks: 83 %" for a 0.8 % error (mapi_sdk reports MAPE in percent) Results The headline reads the scorecard's measured fraction Dead end: the template's fit failed the convergence checks on two years of weekly data, the checks' advice ("raise target_accept") names settings Guided screens hide, and Share said "cannot go live" Results, Share The geo_mmm template (1.1.0) samples longer and more carefully; a warned or failed convergence check offers Fit again, more carefully; a blocked Share step links to it Beliefs the analyst never stated: every channel started ticked with a 0.5–4 ROI range (search's true ROI was 6.3) although the page says "leave a channel unticked if you have no view" What you believe Channels start unticked; ticking one starts from the sensible range "Results without any media: between −164 % and 271 %" Beliefs preview Without a stated baseline: "anything from none to all of your results - the model has no view yet" A revoked embed link kept rendering for a minute (Cache-Control: public, max-age=60) Embed page private, no-cache: revocation applies on the next load Jargon: "y_hat" on the fit chart's axis and caption; "evenly spaced (W-SUN)"; "the host did not resolve (gaierror)"; "Sampler convergence" offered first under Share a chart Report, data step, webhook dialog, Share The dataset's name ("revenue"); "weekly, on Sundays"; "no such name"; result charts first

Also fixed: mapi_client refused to upload an MFF table (a CSV file) with a Guided MFF draft's mapping.

Seen and left for later (not blocking the flow, noted for the testers' sessions):

  • the fit chart facets markets under the dim name geo, and the forecast chart's y axis starts at zero, which flattens the fan (both fixed in the M3 review: panels take the dataset's own name and the axis fits the band);
  • the endpoint page showed who promoted a version as a user id, not a name (fixed in the M3 review: names come from the project's members);
  • the header showed Expert mode on the Integrations hub: that test runs in a new browser context, and the default tenant (not a self-service one) started in Expert mode there. The choice is remembered per browser; since then a self-service workspace starts in Guided mode, and Expert navigation and Home link to Guided;
  • the fit takes about 80 s with the sturdier settings (30 s before), still well within the budget.

docs.title: Protocol for the five non-technical testers
docs.text: The exit criterion needs people. Run this protocol with five testers, one at a time, against a stack like the one above (or staging), and record the results on the observation sheet.

docs.title: Who
docs.text:
• Five people who analyse marketing or sales results in spreadsheets (marketing analysts, media planners, finance business partners), with no statistics or programming training beyond spreadsheet formulas. Screen them with two questions: "Have you fitted a regression or written Python or R?" (no) and "Do you work with weekly spend and sales by market?" (yes).
  • None of them has seen modeling-api before. Nobody from the team that built it.

docs.title: Setup (before each session)
docs.text:
1. A fresh workspace for the tester: sign up at /signup with their work address, in a fresh browser profile. Signing in after the e-mail link opens an empty Guided page, and a self-service workspace starts in Guided mode on any browser. With an operator-created internal tenant instead (a stack without a sandboxed executor), the session starts on Expert Home: finding Guided in the sidebar is then part of T1.
  2. The spreadsheet on their desktop: uv run python tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py seed --run <id> writes weekly_media_by_region.csv (two years, five regions, three channels), or the tester's own anonymised data in the same shape.
  3. A screen recorder, a stopwatch, and the observation sheet. The facilitator sits beside or behind the tester and does not touch the keyboard.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Read this aloud, word for word:

"Thank you for helping. We are testing the software, not you; anything that is hard is our fault. Please think aloud: say what you are looking for and what you expect to happen. I cannot help you during the tasks - if you would give up in real life, tell me and we move on. You have up to 30 minutes in all."

Then give one task card at a time.

Task Card Success means T1 Upload "Here is last two years' media spend and revenue by region. Load it into the tool so it can explain what each channel brings in." The analysis reaches "What you believe" with Revenue, Week, Region, the three spend columns and Avg Price answered correctly T2 Report "Get the tool to tell you which channel returns the most per euro, and whether you can trust the numbers." The fit finishes; the tester names the best channel and its range, and says what the scorecard concluded, in their own words T3 Scenario "Next quarter you could move 20 % more into search. What would it do to revenue? How sure is the tool?" The tester gives the change in revenue with its range (instant or exact), from the What if… step

The optional "What you believe" step counts as part of T1 to T2: testers may skip it.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Unaided: the facilitator answers no question about the product. Allowed: repeating the task card, "what would you do if I were not here?", "please keep thinking aloud". Any other help is an assist and is recorded; a task with an assist does not count as unaided.
  • Give-up: the tester says so, or 12 minutes pass on one task. Record it, give the next card; if a later task needs the earlier one's result, the facilitator performs that step silently and the later task's time starts afterwards.
  • Waiting for the fit counts towards the 30 minutes (about 1.5 minutes on a laptop).

docs.title: Metrics and pass mark
docs.text:
Per tester and task: completion (unaided, assisted or failed), time on task, the number of errors (a wrong turn the tester had to undo), and the Single Ease Question (1 = very difficult to 7 = very easy) after each task. After the session: the System Usability Scale (10 items) and two open questions: "What was most confusing?" and "What would you trust least?".

The criterion is met when all five testers complete T1, T2 and T3 unaided with a total under 30 minutes. Also report the median and maximum total time, the mean SEQ per task and the mean SUS (aim: above 68). Every assist, give-up or recurring error is a defect to fix before the public launch, even when the five pass.

docs.title: Observation sheet
docs.text:
Copy one per tester.

Field T1 Upload T2 Report T3 Scenario Start / end (mm:ss) Completed (unaided / assisted / failed) Errors (wrong turns, with the screen) Assists (what was said) Words or screens the tester did not understand Answer given (T2: best channel, trust; T3: change and range) SEQ (1-7) Session Tester (role, years of experience; no name) Total time SUS score Most confusing Would trust least Facilitator notes (quotes, hesitations, where the cursor went first)

docs.title: What remains unverified
docs.text:
• The five testers. Only the automated floor and an expert review were done (above).
  • Real Google Cloud. Cloud Storage (the GCS shim stood in), Cloud Run Jobs (the local-process executor ran every run), Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, Identity Platform, Cloud Armor (the policy is Terraform, validated and never applied) and Cloud Logging retention. The cold start of the base images adds to every fit, exact run and Atlas evaluation.
  • Docker. No daemon here: the images, the docker and docker-gvisor executors and the compose stack were not run, so public (shared-tier) workspaces never ran a fit; cut line A's admission rule was checked, its sandbox was not.
  • Plotly rendering. Static renders and embeds were Vega-Lite only; Plotly needs kaleido and a Chrome in the runner image (MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED), which this laptop does not provide.
  • Identity verification by a vendor. Only the fake IdentityVerifier and the operators' manual verification exist; no vendor integration was exercised.
  • Real e-mail. The dev outbox stood in for SMTP: deliverability, SPF/DKIM and bounce handling are untested.
  • Webhooks to the internet. Deliveries went to a receiver on 127.0.0.1 through the dev allow-list; the full SSRF policy for public hosts is covered by unit tests only.
  • Bundle retention. With a retention lock (the default, and 30 days when deployed) a purge stops at the model bundles and resumes when the lock expires; locally this was checked only up to the stop (the journey's deletion test does so on a stack without MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0), not the resumption after 30 days.
  • The Atlas in-sandbox optimize job is M4; here Atlas ran on the client.

docs.title: Observability v0.3
docs.text:
The API and the worker emit three signals:

  • Metrics: Prometheus text at GET /metrics on every API process. The worker records the orchestrator's series (dispatch, reconciliation, finalization, pipe event ingestion) and serves them on MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT when that is set.
  • Logs: one JSON object per line on stderr. Each line carries trace_id and span_id, plus the request, run and tenant it belongs to.
  • Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for every request, every outgoing HTTP call and every run's dispatch and finalization. Spans are exported over OTLP/HTTP only when a collector is configured.

Nothing is exported from inside a sandbox. Each execution gets the dispatching span's traceparent in MAPI_TRACEPARENT, so the supervisor's own stderr diagnostics can be joined to the run's trace without any telemetry leaving the exec project.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Effect MAPI_LOG_JSON true JSON logs. false gives a readable console format for local work MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve GET /metrics MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset Bearer a scraper must present. Required in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 Where the worker serves its own /metrics (same bearer rule) MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Create spans (their ids reach the logs even without a collector) MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset OTLP/HTTP collector (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT also works). Needs the otlp extra of mapi-server

docs.title: Scraping /metrics
docs.text:
The series carry tenant ids and spend, so /metrics is not a public route. It authenticates its own bearer, like the Pub/Sub push endpoint does:

# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: mapi-api
    authorization:
      type: Bearer
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/mapi-metrics-token
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["api.internal:8000", "worker.internal:9464"]

In the multi-tenant profile a server without MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN refuses every scrape (401). The single-tenant and dev profiles serve /metrics openly on their loopback API unless a token is set.

docs.title: The metric set
docs.text:
Generated from mapi_server.observability.metrics.Metrics, the one registry every series is defined in, so this table cannot drift from what /metrics serves. Label cardinality is bounded on purpose: tenant_id is the only unbounded label, on the two counters that are meaningless without it, and HTTP series are labelled by route template, never the raw path.

Metric Type Labels Meaning mapi_runs_total counter kind, state Runs that reached a terminal state, by kind and terminal state. mapi_runs_active gauge state Runs currently in a non-terminal state (sampled each reconcile pass). mapi_run_transitions_total counter state Run state transitions, by target state (every edge, terminal or not). mapi_dispatch_latency_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to the executor accepting its submission. mapi_time_to_running_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to its first event (RUNNING). mapi_event_ingestion_lag_seconds histogram — Seconds between a run event's timestamp and its ingestion. mapi_events_ingested_total counter result Run events seen by the ingestor, by result (accepted, duplicate, bad_hmac, ...). mapi_finalize_outcomes_total counter kind, outcome Finalize attempts, by outcome (succeeded, partial, integrity, infra, retry). mapi_integrity_failures_total counter tenant_id Output-integrity verification failures at FINALIZING (a security signal). mapi_sandbox_violations_total counter reason Sandbox violations observed by the control plane, by reason. mapi_quota_rejections_total counter scope, code Requests denied by a quota or rate limit, by scope and error code. mapi_cost_micros_total counter tenant_id Billed compute cost in currency micros, by tenant (cost ledger). mapi_global_spend_micros gauge — Current spend against the global cap, in currency micros (0 until set). mapi_global_spend_cap_micros gauge — The configured global spend cap, in currency micros (0 = no cap set). mapi_sse_clients gauge — Live Server-Sent-Events subscribers connected to this process. mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total counter executor 429 answers from an executor backend to a submission (Cloud Run jobs.run), each one, retried or not. Not the API's own 429s to tenants. mapi_executor_running_executions gauge executor Runs holding a live execution on this executor (fleet-wide, from the run table; each orchestrator reports the same value, so aggregate with max). mapi_http_requests_total counter method, route, status HTTP requests handled by the API, by method, route template and status. mapi_http_request_duration_seconds histogram method, route HTTP request handling time, by method and route template. mapi_endpoint_promotions_total counter outcome Endpoint promotion and rollback decisions, by outcome (allowed, overridden, needs_override, blocked, forbidden, rollback). mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total counter result, inline POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score calls, by result (accepted, replayed, invalid) and whether the payload was inline XrJSON. mapi_webhook_events_total counter type Webhook events written to the outbox, by event type. mapi_webhook_deliveries_total counter status Webhook delivery tries, by resulting status (succeeded, retrying, failed, blocked). mapi_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds histogram — Time of one webhook delivery try (resolution, connection, answer). mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total counter stage Webhook URLs refused by the SSRF policy, by stage (create, update, replay, delivery). mapi_webhooks_disabled_total counter reason Webhooks the platform disabled, by reason (failures, gone).

What to watch first:

  • mapi_time_to_running_seconds: the M2 target is p95 under 90 s.
  • mapi_integrity_failures_total and mapi_sandbox_violations_total: any increase is a security signal, not a reliability one.
  • mapi_global_spend_micros against mapi_global_spend_cap_micros: the kill switch's window.
  • mapi_runs_active{state="stalled"}: runs whose events went quiet (the executor's status, not the silence, decides what happens to them).

The security suite adds one more series from outside the server, mapi_security_probe_unexpected{executor}, through a textfile collector or a Pushgateway (Security suite).

Every response carries X-Request-Id: the caller's own header when it sent one, otherwise the trace id. Quote it when you report a problem; it finds the log lines and the trace.

docs.title: Dashboards, alerts and runbooks
docs.text: Everything operators need is in ops/ at the root of the repository; ops/README.md explains how to import each one. The tables below are generated from those files.

A Grafana dashboard and a Cloud Monitoring dashboard over the same series:

docs.text:
ops/alerts/prometheus-rules.yml (Prometheus rules, with recording rules such as mapi:global_spend_ratio) and ops/alerts/cloud-monitoring-alerts.yaml (the same policies for Cloud Monitoring). page wakes someone; ticket is for the next working hour. The thresholds are starting points for the private beta.

Alert Severity Fires when Says Runbook MapiIntegrityFailure page increase(mapi_integrity_failures_total[10m]) > 0 Integrity failure finalizing a run (N in 10m) ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiSecurityProbeFailure page max(mapi_security_probe_unexpected) > 0 Security probe had an unexpected outcome on an enforcing executor ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiSandboxViolationSpike ticket mapi:sandbox_violations:rate5m > 0.2 for 10m Sandbox violations () elevated ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiGlobalSpendCap70 ticket mapi:global_spend_ratio >= 0.70 and mapi:global_spend_ratio < 0.90 for 5m Global spend at N % of the cap ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiGlobalSpendCap90 page mapi:global_spend_ratio >= 0.90 for 1m Global spend at N % of the cap ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiJobsRun429 ticket mapi:executor_submit_throttled:rate5m > 0 for 5m 429s on jobs.run from (N/s) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiRunningExecutions70 ticket max by (executor) (mapi_executor_running_executions{executor=~"cloudrun.*"}) > 700 for 10m : N running executions (70 % of the 1,000 quota) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiQuotaRejections ticket sum by (scope) (rate(mapi_quota_rejections_total{code="QUOTA_EXCEEDED"}[15m])) > 0.05 for 15m Quota rejections sustained at the level ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiStalledRateHigh page mapi:runs_stalled / clamp_min(mapi:runs_running + mapi:runs_stalled, 1) > 0.2 for 10m N % of live runs are STALLED ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiTimeToRunningSlow ticket histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(mapi_time_to_running_seconds_bucket[30m])) by (le)) > 90 for 15m p95 time-to-RUNNING Ns (> 90s SLO) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiNoProgressIngested page (sum(rate(mapi_events_ingested_total{result="accepted"}[10m])) or vector(0)) == 0 and sum(mapi_runs_active{state=~"running\|provisioning"}) > 0 for 10m Runs are live but no events are being ingested ops/runbooks/db-failover.md

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
Each alert names the runbook that resolves it:

Runbook For Starts with ops/runbooks/db-failover.md database (Postgres) failover / outage Triggered by MapiNoProgressIngested, /readyz reporting postgres: fail, a Cloud SQL failover event, or widespread 5xx. ops/runbooks/incident-response.md incident response (control plane) The general flow for any control-plane incident. ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md rotating the HMAC / signing keys Two long-lived secrets protect run integrity (plan §8.6, §8.7, §9). ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md suspected or confirmed sandbox escape Triggered by MapiIntegrityFailure, MapiSecurityProbeFailure, a MapiSandboxViolationSpike, or any external report of untrusted code reaching something it should not. ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md stuck runs (STALLED, stuck in a state, jobs.run 429) Triggered by MapiStalledRateHigh, MapiTimeToRunningSlow, MapiJobsRun429, MapiRunningExecutions70, MapiNoProgressIngested, or tenant reports that a run "isn't moving".

The sandbox-escape runbook is the plan's incident response for a confirmed escape: turn off uploaded code with the kill switch, rotate the signing and HMAC keys (which invalidates every outstanding signed URL), quarantine the affected bundles and notify the tenants.

docs.title: Tests that guard the signals
docs.text:
Command What it checks make chaos A worker killed during PROVISIONING and RUNNING, Pub/Sub redelivery and reordering, bad-HMAC redelivery, and a PostgreSQL restart mid-run. Every run converges to one outcome, with one attempt and no duplicate execution make load-test 100 concurrent fits through the real dispatcher, reconciler and finalizer on the fake Cloud Run backend, with injected 429s, lost responses and duplicate pushes. No run is lost, and p95 time-to-RUNNING stays under 90 s make security-suite The sandbox-escape probes (see Security suite)

All three run offline, against the embedded PostgreSQL and the in-memory or shim object store.

docs.title: Security hardening on Google Cloud v0.3
docs.text:
Tenants can submit specs (and, from M4, code) that run on the platform's infrastructure, so the cloud deployment assumes every execution is hostile. This page lists each control of the Google Cloud deployment, the threat it answers (plan §9), where it lives in infra/terraform, and how to check it on a live environment. The application-level model (supervisor and worker, signed events, verified outputs) is on Security model.

The last section is the M0 verification checklist: the cloud behaviours the design depends on that have not yet been confirmed against a real project. Work through it before production.

docs.title: Executions cannot reach the network
docs.text:
Control Threat Where Check Direct VPC egress with egress = ALL_TRAFFIC on every Job Bypassing the VPC's controls modules/exec/jobs.tf gcloud run jobs describe shows the network interface and ALL_TRAFFIC No default route; one route to 199.36.153.4/30 Any path to the internet modules/exec/network.tf gcloud compute routes list --filter=network:mapi-<env>-exec-<pool> lists only restricted-vip (and the subnet routes) Firewall: deny all egress (IPv4 and IPv6) at priority 65534, logged Data exfiltration over IP modules/exec/network.tf Red-team probe: curl https://example.com from a Job fails; the denial appears in the firewall logs Firewall: allow only TCP 443 to the restricted VIP and port 53 to 35.199.192.0/19 The two exceptions executions need modules/exec/network.tf gcloud compute firewall-rules list shows exactly these two allow rules DNS response policy: *. answered locally (sinkhole), bypassed only for googleapis.com, *.googleapis.com and metadata.google.internal DNS exfiltration (queries for <secret>.attacker.example) modules/exec/dns.tf Red-team gate below: a unique subdomain of a zone you control is never seen by its authoritative servers Private zone googleapis.com → restricted.googleapis.com (199.36.153.4–7) Reaching Google APIs through non-VPC-SC endpoints modules/exec/dns.tf From a Job, storage.googleapis.com resolves to 199.36.153.4–7 VPC-SC perimeter around exec and data projects; every data-moving API restricted; VPC-accessible services = Cloud Storage only Exfiltration through the VIP to an attacker-owned bucket, topic or dataset (with any credential) modules/perimeter Red-team probe: a signed PUT URL for a bucket outside the perimeter fails from a Job with a VPC-SC violation in the audit logs

Cloud DNS response policies can answer with local data or bypass the policy; they cannot return NXDOMAIN. The plan's "*. → NXDOMAIN" is therefore a local sinkhole answer (192.0.2.1 / 100::1, both non-routable and denied by the firewall). What matters for exfiltration is that the query is answered locally and never forwarded.

docs.title: Identities hold only what they use
docs.text:
Identity Can Cannot Execution SA (one per exec project) storage.objects.get + delete on the bootstrap bucket (custom role, no list) Anything else: no project roles, no secrets, no access to bundles or data Orchestrator Run, list, inspect and cancel executions of existing Jobs (custom role); write bootstrap objects; verify, copy and sign outputs (KMS signer) Create or change a Job (image, class, identity); delete bundles API Read bucket metadata; mint signed URLs (signBlob on the URL signer only); read the signing key's public key Sign manifests; run Jobs; read secrets other than its own Events Database (through db-url-app) Everything else URL signer The bucket permissions signed URLs carry (custom reader/writer roles) Nothing else; no key file exists, and nobody can impersonate it (only signBlob) Pub/Sub push SA Invoke the events service Anything else CI: ci-push / planner / deployer Push images / read-only plan / apply; each bound to one GitHub environment of one repository Use a long-lived key (none exist)

Where: modules/control/iam.tf, modules/exec/iam.tf, modules/data/iam.tf, modules/build/wif.tf. Check with gcloud projects get-iam-policy <project> --flatten=bindings --format='table(bindings.role,bindings.members)' and gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://mapi-<env>-<bucket>.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Control Threat Where Public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access on every bucket; no ACL resources anywhere Public or ACL-granted objects modules/data/buckets.tf Bootstrap: 1-day lifecycle, soft delete off The RunSpec (signed URLs, per-run HMAC key) surviving its read-then-delete modules/data/buckets.tf Bundles: retention policy (locked in prod), no delete role for anyone, never force_destroy Artifact swap or replay after verification modules/data/ Quarantine and runs expire (7 and 30 days), soft delete off Tenant data outliving its purpose modules/data/buckets.tf Optional CMEK (data.kms_key_name) Crypto-shredding for enterprise tenants modules/data/buckets.tf CORS only for the app origin and only the methods each bucket needs Cross-origin abuse of signed URLs modules/data/buckets.tf

docs.title: Secrets and signing
docs.text:
• No secret in Terraform state or plans. Database passwords, the server's root secret (the API-token pepper and audit key derive from it) and the metrics scrape token come from ephemeral resources; the OAuth client secret is an ephemeral variable; all are written with write-only arguments (password_wo, secret_data_wo). Cloud Run revisions reference secrets by name, never by value.
  • Secrets replicated in one region (the control region), for data residency.
  • Bundle manifests are signed by KMS (EC P-256 / SHA-256, HSM in prod); only the orchestrator may sign, and the API verifies with the public key before minting any URL for a bundle (plan §8.6). Key versions are destroyed only after a 30-day schedule.
  • Database: private IP only, TLS required, password policy enforced. Four roles: the migrations own the schema; mapi_app and mapi_gateway (API, events) are not the table owner, so FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY binds them (the gateway sees identity tables and a few metadata columns only); mapi_orchestrator alone gets BYPASSRLS from the migrations, and only the orchestrator can read its URL. The managed pooler runs in transaction mode, which is safe because the tenant is set with SET LOCAL per transaction.

docs.title: Event path and control-plane ingress
docs.text:
• The Logging sink of each exec project routes only jsonPayload.mapi_event:* lines of this environment's Jobs, and writes as its own identity, which may only publish to the events topic.
  • User output is excluded at the exec project's _Default sink (plan §8.7, modules/exec/logging.tf): log and progress events of the runner Jobs still reach the events service through the routing sink, but are not ingested (and billed) in the exec project. State changes, warnings, errors, completions and Cloud Run's system logs stay.
  • The events service is internal-only and IAM-protected: only the push identity may invoke it, and Cloud Run checks the push token's signature and audience before the request reaches the container. The server additionally checks the claims (mapi_spec.auth.check_push_claims) and the per-line HMAC.
  • Undeliverable events are dead-lettered after 10 attempts instead of being dropped.
  • Behind the load balancer the API accepts traffic only from it; TLS 1.2+ (MODERN profile); the plot sandbox has its own host (use a different registrable domain in prod), as plan §10.3 requires. Every backend carries the Cloud Armor policy below.

docs.title: Cloud Armor
docs.text:
modules/control/armor.tf creates a Cloud Armor policy with the load balancer (var.domains) and attaches it to the api, web and plots backends (lb.tf). Supply your own with security_policy instead, or turn it off with cloud_armor.enabled = false.

Rule Priority Threat Setting Trusted ranges (CI, office) 100 Being banned by your own load tests cloud_armor.trusted_ip_ranges (at most 10 CIDRs, never *) OWASP CRS: sqli, xss, lfi, rce, scannerdetection (v3.3 stable) 1000–1004 Injection probes and scanners against the API and the SPA cloud_armor.waf_mode (preview by default), cloud_armor.waf_sensitivity (paranoia level 1–4, default 1) Per-IP rate ban on /auth/signup (and /v1/signup) 2000 Sign-up floods, Sybil farms rate_limits.signup_per_minute (10) Per-IP rate ban on /auth/* 2001 Credential stuffing on sign-in, callback and e-mail verification rate_limits.auth_per_minute (120) Per-IP rate ban on /v1/embeds/* 2002 Scraping of public embed links rate_limits.embed_per_minute (600) Per-IP rate ban on /v1/endpoints/<alias>/score 2003 Denial of wallet through scoring rate_limits.score_per_minute (600) Default last allow
  • Preview, then enforce. The OWASP rules start in preview: matches are logged (jsonPayload.previewSecurityPolicy on the load balancer's request logs), nothing is blocked. Watch a week of real traffic, add exclusions or lower the sensitivity where a rule matches legitimate requests (spec YAML and plot JSON are the likely ones), then set waf_mode = "enforce" (in prod: cloud_armor_waf_mode). Enforced matches answer 403.
  • Rate bans are enforced from the start (rate_limit_mode = "enforce"): over the per-minute threshold a client gets 429; three times the threshold within five minutes bans the address for ban_duration_sec (600 s). The API's own limits (sign-up per address, domain and platform; token and tenant request rates) apply behind them.
  • Adaptive Protection (Layer 7 DDoS defense) is on: it learns each backend's normal traffic and alerts with a suggested rule; it never blocks by itself.
  • Request bodies. JSON bodies are parsed (json_parsing = STANDARD), so the rules see field values instead of raw text. Cloud Armor inspects only the first request_body_inspection_size bytes of a body (8 KB by default, at most 64 KB): larger bodies (spec documents, inline XrJSON score payloads up to 5 MB) are inspected partially, not blocked. The API enforces its own body limits; signed-URL uploads go to Cloud Storage directly and never pass the load balancer.

Check on a live environment:

gcloud compute backend-services describe mapi-prod-api --global --format='value(securityPolicy)'
gcloud compute security-policies describe mapi-prod-edge --format='yaml(rules,adaptiveProtectionConfig)'
# a burst against sign-up is banned (expect 429s after the threshold)
for i in $(seq 1 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://app.example.com/auth/signup; done | sort | uniq -c

Logs and tenant deletion. The load balancer logs every request (log_config.sample_rate = 1) into the control project's _Default bucket, whose retention Terraform sets explicitly (log_retention_days, 30 days, modules/control/logging.tf). Tenant deletion does not purge logs; they hold ids, not content, and expire with that retention (Deleting data).

docs.title: Supply chain
docs.text:
• Images are deployed by digest only; Terraform rejects tags. The registry's tags are immutable and nothing is garbage-collected automatically (digests referenced by live model versions must survive, plan §12).
  • Builds attach SBOM and provenance attestations (build-push.sh, --no-attestations to skip).
  • A Binary Authorization attestor, note and signing key exist (modules/build/binauthz.tf); enforcement on the Jobs (binary_authorization = true) is switched on in M5, once CI attests every base digest.
  • CI authenticates with Workload Identity Federation; no service-account key is ever created.

docs.title: M0 verification checklist
docs.text: Plan items marked [verify M0] and the assumptions this Terraform adds. Each needs a throw-away environment (dev, perimeter enforced) and a probe Job built from a base image. Record the date, the result and the evidence (log query, screenshot) for each.

docs.title: Network and DNS
docs.text:
• The Direct VPC egress resolver honours response policies. From a Job, resolve <random>.probe.<zone you control> (A, AAAA and TXT). Pass: the answer is the sinkhole (or NODATA) and the zone's authoritative query logs never see the name. Plan §9's red-team gate; if it fails, Cloud Run Jobs cannot host untrusted code (fallback: GKE Sandbox). Until this passes, verified and public tenants stay off: only then set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED=true on the orchestrator and record the security-suite and conformance evidence (the shared-tier gate). New tenants default to verified, so the private beta needs this item.
  • A wildcard rule for the root (*.) is accepted by Cloud DNS, and local data for A/AAAA does not leak TXT or other record types upstream (same probe, other types).
  • The bypass rules work: storage.googleapis.com resolves to 199.36.153.4–7 and metadata.google.internal still serves the execution's token.
  • Egress is really denied: curl to a public IP and to a public name, a raw TCP connect to 8.8.8.8:53 and an ICMP ping all fail; the firewall logs show the denials.
  • VPC-SC applies to Cloud Run Jobs: a signed PUT URL for a bucket outside the perimeter fails from a Job, and a VPC-SC violation appears in the audit logs.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
• The supervisor/worker uid split works on gen2: the supervisor can start the worker under uid 10001 with no_new_privs and a seccomp filter; the worker cannot ptrace the supervisor or read /proc/1/environ. Note that Cloud Run runs the image's USER; the runner images must start the supervisor as root (or with the capabilities to switch users) for this to work.
  • Execution overrides are env-only: jobs.run with overrides cannot change the image, resources, service account or network (try each; all must be refused or impossible).
  • Ephemeral disk: whether Jobs offer any disk beyond the in-memory filesystem, and what happens at the memory limit (exit 137 → RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, class+1 offered).
  • In-memory filesystem limits: writing the class's scratch budget (3/6/12 GiB for S/M/L) succeeds; going beyond it gets the execution killed rather than the host degraded.
  • Bootstrap read-then-delete: after the supervisor deletes the RunSpec, the object is gone (no soft-deleted copy can be restored) and the nonce in the audit log points at nothing.

docs.title: Quotas and rates (plan §8.8)
docs.text:
• Jobs per region: 1,000 (the inventory uses 9 per exec project).
  • Running executions: 1,000 per project and region; an alert fires at 70 %.
  • jobs.run rate: 180 per minute per region; the dispatcher's token bucket stays below it, and a 429 raises an alarm and backs off (mapi_spec.quotas.backoff_seconds).
  • Regional CPU and memory for the expected fan-out (sweeps, SBC).
  • Cold start of a ~2.5 GB base image: p50 measured; time-to-RUNNING p95 under 90 s.

docs.title: Control plane
docs.text:
• Logging → Pub/Sub path: an event line reaches the events service with the execution's labels (job, execution) in the push payload, within seconds.
  • Pub/Sub push to an internal-only service works (same-project subscription).
  • Managed connection pooling: the pooler port (6432 by default here) and transaction mode work with the server's driver; LISTEN goes over the direct URL.
  • BYPASSRLS can be granted to mapi_orchestrator by the migrate role on Cloud SQL.
  • run.jobs.runWithOverrides without iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the execution service account is enough for the orchestrator (otherwise grant actAs on that account only).
  • Image indexes: Cloud Run runs the images build-push.sh pushes with attestations (an OCI index); otherwise build with --no-attestations.

docs.title: Red-team probes (security suite, plan §13)
docs.text: Run nightly once the platform is up, and keep them green for two weeks before cut line B: metadata-token use beyond the bootstrap object, HTTP and DNS egress, writes outside signed objects, reuse of another tenant's URL, reading /proc/1, overlay .pth injection, fork, memory and disk bombs, log flood (SANDBOX_VIOLATION), forged events (bad HMAC, replayed sequence numbers), a tampered manifest (INTEGRITY_FAILURE), ReDoS schemas, plot XSS and postMessage abuse.

docs.title: Security suite v0.3
docs.text:
The security suite is a set of deliberately hostile probes. For each executor, it reports which attacks were BLOCKED and which were ALLOWED, and compares the result with what that executor's isolation level must guarantee. It runs nightly in the cloud. It has to stay green for two weeks before public code upload (cut line B) can open.

The suite lives in security/ at the root of the repository and is never installed: security/ is not a uv workspace member, so uv sync --all-packages leaves it out. Its malicious plugin is not registered as a mapi.models entry point either, so the platform can never discover it. The suite runs on the installed environment with security/src on PYTHONPATH, which is what the Make targets do.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
make security-list                              # the probe corpus
make security-suite                             # EXECUTOR=local-process (always runnable)
make security-suite EXECUTOR=docker-gvisor      # sandbox probes inside a gVisor container

make security-suite exits non-zero when any outcome is unacceptable for the executor's isolation level. It also writes .local/security-<executor>.prom, which exports mapi_security_probe_unexpected{executor} for a textfile collector or a Pushgateway. The MapiSecurityProbeFailure alert in ops/alerts/ watches that series. The nightly workflow pushes the file to the Pushgateway named by the MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL repository secret; without that secret the alert has no data and the failing nightly job is the signal.

docs.title: The probes
docs.text:
Isolation probes test operating-system and sandbox controls. Each one tries a hostile action, safely and with bounds, and reports ALLOWED or BLOCKED:

Probe Attempts metadata_token Fetch an instance token from the metadata server http_egress, dns_egress Open an outbound connection; resolve a unique subdomain (DNS exfiltration) write_outside_scratch Write outside the run's output area reuse_foreign_url Reach an object-store endpoint, the first step to reusing another run's signed URL read_proc1_environ, read_supervisor_mem Read the supervisor's environment or memory pth_injection Drop a .pth or sitecustomize file into site-packages fork_bomb, memory_bomb, disk_bomb Exceed the process, memory or scratch limits (all capped) log_flood Write past the per-run log cap

Platform probes call the real control-plane defences in mapi_spec and mapi_plots. They must be BLOCKED on every executor:

Probe Attempts forged_stdout_event A run event with the wrong HMAC tampered_manifest An output object the signed manifest never listed redos_schema A catastrophic-backtracking regex in a plot spec plot_xss_exfil A plot with an external image URL or a <script> caption reuse_foreign_manifest One run's signed manifest presented under another run's key

docs.title: What each isolation level must block
docs.text:
Isolation Executors Isolation probes Platform probes PROCESS local-process, docker (runc) Either outcome is accepted: these are not security boundaries BLOCKED GVISOR docker-gvisor (shared tiers only on a network declared with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED) BLOCKED BLOCKED MICROVM cloud (the cloudrun-jobs executor) BLOCKED BLOCKED

SKIPPED is always acceptable, for example when there is no procfs or no Docker daemon. ERROR never is. A passing run of this matrix, recorded for the executor's current caps, is one half of what lets an executor take verified and public tenants; a passing run of the 12-case executor conformance suite (packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py) is the other. Record both with PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence: see the shared-tier gate. For that gate, the network probes (http_egress, dns_egress, metadata_token) must have run and been blocked.

docs.title: Where the probes run
docs.text:
• local-process: the suite process is the execution environment, so the probes run in process. On a developer machine most isolation probes are ALLOWED. That is expected and documented.
  • docker, docker-gvisor: the isolation probes run in a locked-down container (--network none, read-only root, non-root user, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, and --runtime runsc for gVisor). Without a Docker daemon they report SKIPPED, and the platform probes still run.
  • cloud: the probes must run inside a Cloud Run Jobs execution of a base image, judged against the MICROVM row. --executor cloud therefore refuses to run (exit status 2) anywhere CLOUD_RUN_JOB and CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION are not set, because a report made on a laptop or a CI runner would describe the wrong sandbox. The base images do not ship the suite yet and Terraform defines no probe Job, so the nightly cloud run is still to be wired up: see M2 verification. The authoritative DNS-exfiltration check reads the query logs of a zone we control (security hardening).

security/THREAT-MODEL.md maps each probe to its threat and to the control expected to stop it.

docs.title: Sign-up and abuse controls v0.4
docs.text: Self-service sign-up lets anyone with an e-mail address create a public workspace. Public workspaces run untrusted data through trusted code: built-in models and declarative specs only (cut line A). This page is for whoever runs the platform: how sign-up works, what stops abuse, and what operators review. Every variable named here is in the configuration reference; the HTTP operations are in the HTTP API reference.

docs.title: How sign-up works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant API as API (/auth)
    participant M as Mailer
    B->>API: POST /auth/signup {email, name, organisation, accepted_terms}
    API->>API: terms, blocklist, bot check, rate limits
    API->>M: verification link (single use, 24 h)
    API-->>B: 202 {"status": "check_email"}
    B->>API: POST /auth/verify-email {token}
    API->>API: create tenant (public), project "default", admin grant; Sybil checks
    API-->>B: 200 {tenant_id, login_url}
    B->>API: GET /auth/login (OpenID sign-in with that address)
  1. POST /auth/signup refuses early what can never sign up: terms not accepted (TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED), a malformed or disposable address (EMAIL_NOT_ALLOWED), a failed bot check. Then it applies the rate limits below (RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After).
  2. It stores the sign-up with an HMAC of a fresh 200-bit token (never the token itself) and e-mails the link MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL. Only the newest link of an address works.
  3. The answer is the same for every address, new or already registered, so sign-up cannot be used to find out who has an account. An existing account that verifies a new sign-up gets one more workspace.
  4. POST /auth/verify-email consumes the token and, in one transaction, creates the tenant (tier public, id from the organisation name), its default project, the person as tenant admin (an invitation claimed at their first sign-in with that verified address) and the tenant's verification record. An expired, superseded or used link answers 410 LINK_EXPIRED.

Everything is audited: auth.signup, auth.signup_rejected (bounded per client and minute, since anyone can cause them), auth.email_verified, tenant.create and auth.signup_flagged.

docs.title: Mailers
docs.text:
MAPI_MAILER Use Notes smtp Production smtplib with STARTTLS (required, never opportunistic) or implicit TLS (MAPI_SMTP_TLS=ssl, port 465); certificates are verified. Needs MAPI_SMTP_HOST; credentials in MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME/MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD. No third-party mail API outbox dev profile, end-to-end tests One JSON file per message (mode 0600) under MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR. The dev profile serves the newest at GET /dev/outbox?to=<address>, with the token in tags.token console Single-user installs Logs the message, link included none Sign-up is off

The multi-tenant profile refuses console and outbox while sign-up is on: whoever can read the logs or the disk could verify any address. Without an SMTP host sign-up is simply off (POST /auth/signup answers 403). Messages are plain text; header values with line breaks are refused (no header injection through a sign-up's name).

# dev: follow a verification link without a mail server
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/auth/signup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ana@acme.example","name":"Ana","accepted_terms":true,"terms_version":"2026-10"}'
TOKEN=$(curl -s 'localhost:8000/dev/outbox?to=ana@acme.example' | jq -r '.items[0].tags.token')
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/auth/verify-email -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"token\":\"$TOKEN\"}"

docs.title: Disposable addresses
docs.text: The built-in list (mapi_spec.trust.DEFAULT_DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS) is deliberately small. Add domains with MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS (comma-separated) or point MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH at a file (one domain per line, # comments), for example a maintained public disposable-domain list refreshed by your deployment. A listed domain also blocks its subdomains. Deployments that want a vendor check plug a mapi_spec.trust.DisposableEmailPolicy into TrustServices.email_policy.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Limit Default Variable Sign-ups per client address and hour 5 MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR Verified sign-ups per e-mail domain and day 25 MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY Verified sign-ups on the whole platform per hour 500 MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR Verification attempts per client address and minute 20 MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE

They are counted in Postgres from the sign-ups themselves, so they hold across API instances. Every request counts toward the per-address limit, which is what holds back unverified floods. The domain and platform caps count only sign-ups whose link was opened: otherwise anyone could send 25 made-up @gmail.com (or @your-customer.com) addresses and lock that domain out of sign-up for a day. Large free-mail domains (MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, by default gmail.com, outlook.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, proton.me and similar) have no per-domain cap at all. Behind the Google Cloud load balancer, Cloud Armor adds per-IP rate bans in front of /auth/signup and /auth/* before a request reaches the API. Client addresses are stored only as keyed digests.

The client address is the connecting peer unless that peer is a trusted proxy (MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES): then it is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy, so callers behind one load balancer keep separate limits and a caller cannot forge its address by sending the header itself. The multi-tenant profile refuses to start without the setting (none when clients reach the API directly).

docs.title: Sybil heuristics and the review queue
docs.text:
When a sign-up is verified, the platform looks back MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS (30) days for workspaces created from the same signals:

Flag Signal same_ip the same client address (keyed digest) same_device the same browser: a random, HttpOnly mapi_device cookie set at sign-up same_email the same e-mail address domain_burst many verified sign-ups from one domain within an hour (twice the threshold); never for the shared free-mail domains

At MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD (3) earlier workspaces the new sign-up is flagged: the workspace works, and it waits in the review queue (auth.signup_flagged in the audit log). With MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND=true a flagged workspace is suspended (read-only) until an operator approves it.

Operators review flagged sign-ups:

# the queue, newest first
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/admin/signups?review=flagged"
# reject: the workspace is suspended (audited, with the reason)
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/admin/signups/$ID/review" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"decision":"reject","reason":"device farm"}'
# approve: the flag is cleared, and a suspension the review caused is lifted

An approval only lifts suspensions the review itself caused (never an operator's own suspension). Rejecting a sign-up that was never verified kills its link.

docs.title: Identity verification and cut line A
docs.text:
Every tenant has a verification record: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification answers email_verified, identity_verified, the method and uploaded_code_allowed with a reason in plain words. The rule (mapi_spec.trust.uploaded_code_allowed):

Trust tier Uploaded code (plugins with an overlay) internal, self-hosted-trusted allowed verified only once identity is verified public never before cut line B (MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED, M5); then only with identity verification

The rule is enforced at run admission: a run of uploaded code for a tenant that may not run it is refused with 403 IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED (audited as a denied run.create). Built-in models and declarative specs are always admitted. The plugin upload of M4 calls the same check (mapi_server.services.verification.require_uploaded_code_allowed).

Operators record identity verification after an out-of-band check (a contract, an invoice):

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X PUT \
  "$API/v1/admin/tenants/acme/verification" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"identity_verified":true,"method":"manual","reason":"signed enterprise contract"}'

The request-path database role may only read verification records, so no tenant session can mark its own tenant verified. A card or document provider plugs in as a mapi_server.services.trust.IdentityVerifier (a deterministic FakeIdentityVerifier exists for tests and drills); no vendor is integrated yet.

docs.title: Bot checks
docs.text: SignupRequest.challenge carries a bot-check token (for example Cloudflare Turnstile). The server consults TrustServices.challenge (mapi_server.services.trust.SignupChallenge); the default accepts every sign-up, leaving the rate limits, Cloud Armor and the Sybil review to do the work. A deployment that adds a vendor check implements the protocol.

docs.title: Runbook: a sign-up wave
docs.text:
1. Look at the queue (GET /v1/admin/signups?review=flagged) and the audit log (auth.signup_rejected, auth.signup_flagged).
  2. Lower the limits (MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR, MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR) or set MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND=true, and redeploy the API.
  3. Block the domains (MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS) and, at the edge, lower cloud_armor.rate_limits.signup_per_minute in Terraform.
  4. Reject the flagged sign-ups; suspend any other workspace with PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{id}. Public workspaces never ran uploaded code, so their runs used built-in models only; the kill switches and the spend cap still bound what they can spend.
  5. To close sign-up entirely: MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED=false.

docs.title: Troubleshooting v0.2
docs.text: Start with make status: it shows which services of a make dev stack are up and whether the embedded PostgreSQL is running. The web app's Settings page shows the API's readiness checks, and curl -s $MAPI_API_URL/readyz shows the same from a shell.

docs.title: Port conflicts
docs.text:
make dev refuses to start when a port it needs is taken:

cannot start - fix these first
  - 127.0.0.1:8000 is already in use

Another make dev (in another terminal or worktree), a compose stack, or an unrelated program owns the port. Find it, and either stop it or move the platform:

lsof -iTCP:8000 -sTCP:LISTEN          # who has it?
make stop                              # if it is another make dev of this checkout

To move the platform, export the addresses in every shell that talks to it, then start again. Every component (make dev, make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client, the web app's build) reads the same variables:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174
make dev
Port Variable Service 8000 MAPI_API_URL API 4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT GCS shim (signed URLs point here) 5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Web app 5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Plot sandbox

A state directory belongs to one stack at a time; to run two stacks side by side, also give each its own MAPI_DATA_DIR. The Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on 5173 and 5174, so run it while make dev is stopped. Docker Compose publishes the same four ports as make dev, on purpose: run one or the other.

docs.title: The local stack
docs.text:
cannot start - fix these first

The supervisor checks every requirement before starting anything. Besides ports:

  • module 'mapi_server.__main__' not found: your environment is stale. Run uv sync --all-packages (or make install).
  • exe 'pnpm' not found or run pnpm install first: install pnpm (corepack enable) and the JavaScript dependencies (pnpm install), or skip the front end with make dev WITHOUT=web,plots.
already running (supervisor pid N) A previous make dev is still alive, perhaps in another terminal. Run make stop. If that process is gone but its state file stayed behind (after kill -9, for example), the next start detects the dead pid and ignores the file. plots exited unexpectedly with status 143; stopping the stack Something outside the stack sent the service SIGTERM (a pkill vite, for example). The supervisor never restarts services silently: it stops everything and exits. Start it again; runs that were in flight are recovered by the reconciler as a new attempt. postgres | failed to start Read .local/pg/log. If the data directory came from a different PostgreSQL major version, or is corrupt, run make clean-local; this deletes the local database. An orphaned server from an earlier crash is stopped by make stop. migrate exited with status 1 The migration's own output is printed just above this line. Fix the migration, or reset the database with make stop && make clean-local, then run make dev again. api not ready after 60s The API process is running but GET /healthz never succeeded. Look at the api | lines. A wrong DATABASE_URL, or a GCS shim that is not reachable, are the usual causes. Validation says the catalog is unavailable On the first start against a new environment (and after every change to uv.lock) the worker queues a sandboxed describe run to export the catalog: no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. It takes a few seconds. If it fails, its run page under Runs shows why. The server refuses MAPI_PROFILE MAPI_PROFILE is also the CLI's config-profile variable. If you exported a client profile name, unset it in the shell that runs make dev (the server accepts only single-tenant or multi-tenant). Leftover processes after a crash Each service runs in its own process group, which you can find with ps -o pid,pgid,command. make stop also kills the process groups recorded in .local/dev/supervisor.json when the supervisor itself does not respond within 30 s.

docs.title: The web app and plots
docs.text: API unreachable in the header, or the app cannot load anything The app calls the API at the VITE_API_BASE it was started with. make dev sets it from MAPI_API_URL; if you start Vite yourself, set it too. The API must also allow the app's origin: it allows MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, so both must agree. Plots stay blank MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN must be different origins, the plot sandbox must be running (make status), and the sandbox must allow the app's origin (VITE_APP_ORIGINS, set by make dev). The browser console names the blocked origin. Uploads fail in the browser The browser PUTs files straight to MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. The shim must allow the app's origin (--cors-origin, set by make dev from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN), and the app's CSP must allow the storage origin (VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS).

docs.title: Runs and scoring
docs.text: A run is stalled No progress arrived for a while. It is a warning, not a failure: the executor's own status decides whether the run is alive. A long PyTensor compile on the first fit of a new machine can cause it. DEV_MODE_ISOLATION on every run Expected on a laptop: the local executor runs the model code as your own user, without a separate uid or no_new_privs. See the security model. SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE when scoring A side table with score_policy: supplied (in the demo, fx) must be given in the score request (side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}) and cover the scored dates. Enter the pipeline after the step that uses it (inputs_stage: weekly) to skip it. MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, … Typed errors from the static checks: the request asks for something the model cannot answer honestly. The problem's detail and JSON pointer say what; the codes are listed in Error codes. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED The run ran out of memory or scratch space. Retry on the run page suggests the next resource class. Under compose, raise MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS. INTEGRITY_FAILURE when downloading The bundle's signed manifest no longer verifies, so the API refuses to mint download links. Locally this happens when .local/keys/ was deleted: the old model versions cannot be trusted any more. Fit again.

docs.title: Docker and compose
docs.text: error: the Docker daemon is not reachable make docker-build and make compose-up check docker info first. Start Docker Desktop, Colima or dockerd, or use make dev, which needs no Docker. required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value Copy .env.example to .env and set POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Compose reads .env from the repository root. image check failed: forbidden distribution 'numpy' is installed (server build) A control-plane dependency started pulling in a science package. Run uv run python scripts/lock_closure.py "mapi-server[docker]" --lacks numpy to see the closure, then find which dependency brings numpy in. Contracts: 1 broken in the contracts stage Server code imports a forbidden module. make lint (lint-imports) shows the same failure locally, with the import chain. PyTensor found no C++ compiler (base-bayes / base-forecast build) g++ is missing from MAPI_APT_PACKAGES. The PyMC images need it at run time too. The api container is unhealthy make compose-logs SERVICE=api. Typical causes are that migrate failed (look at its logs), or that the DATABASE_URL password does not match the database volume, which happens after you change POSTGRES_PASSWORD. In that case reset with make compose-down VOLUMES=1; this deletes the data. no bundle-signing key at /var/lib/mapi/keys/... and MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE is off api or worker started before migrate created the key, or without the keys volume. Check make compose-logs SERVICE=migrate. Never point the two at different keys: the API would reject every bundle the worker signs with INTEGRITY_FAILURE. 400 Invalid host header from the API, or nginx closes the connection The stack answers only known host names (a DNS-rebinding guard). If you reach it under a name other than 127.0.0.1, localhost or api, add that name to MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (the API) and MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (the web image's nginx). mapi-entrypoint: /tmp/mapi-cache is not writable The container runs with a read-only root filesystem but without a writable /tmp. Add --tmpfs /tmp (compose already does). Port already allocated on docker compose up A make dev stack, or another process, holds 4443, 8000, 5173 or 5174. Stop it with make stop. Both stacks use the same ports on purpose, so the same URLs work with either. nginx exits with host not found or invalid number of arguments in "set" MAPI_API_UPSTREAM is empty or malformed. It must be a URL without a path, for example http://api:8000.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes are documented here. The project follows Semantic Versioning; milestone releases are tagged on main.

docs.title: [0.4.0] — M3: Guided mode and integrations — 2026-10-16
docs.text:
Analysts who do not write code can now build a model from a spreadsheet, read it and try scenarios on it, and teams can wire a model they trust into the tools they already use. Everything was verified on a laptop against a live local stack (the GCS shim, embedded Postgres, the local-process executor). The real Google Cloud, Docker and the five non-technical testers are still to come (see Known gaps). In summary:

  • Guided mode: a task flow for non-technical analysts. Pick a template (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice), upload a CSV, Parquet, MFF or Meridian table, confirm the detected column roles, state business beliefs (ROI or contribution-share ranges, a baseline) and lift tests, fit, and read a plain-language report with a scorecard. What-if sliders answer at once from a per-draw response grid (a TypeScript port of the model's own maths), and "Run exact" checks a scenario, a forecast or a counterfactual with a real score run.
  • modelling: business priors translated into model priors (translate_priors runs and a preview chart) and lift tests as calibration in mmm.hierarchical_geo and mmm.pymc_marketing; the mmm.bayesinsight built-in and a BayesInsight importer; a scorecard per version and a promotion gate that needs an audited admin override for a failing or unevaluated version.
  • endpoints and integrations: endpoints with aliases, promotion, history and rollback; generated snippets (Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, notebook, Atlas); score answers with the summary inline; webhooks signed with HMAC, behind an SSRF guard, with an outbox, a delivery log and replays; saved plots, static PNG/SVG/PDF rendering with vl-convert and expiring embed links served by the plot sandbox; the Integrations hub in the web app.
  • trust and data lifecycle: self-service sign-up with e-mail verification, identity verification and Sybil flags with a review queue, trusted-proxy client addresses, per-tier draw and egress caps, GDPR export and tenant deletion with a grace period, and a Cloud Armor policy in Terraform.
  • client and CLI: the v0.4 Python client (endpoints, webhooks, plots, Guided, tenants) and Atlas RemoteModel, which lets Atlas optimise a budget against an endpoint; mapi endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors, signup and tenant.
  • docs: a new landing page, Why modeling-api, use cases, a Tutorials section (Google Sheets, embeds, BayesInsight, webhook receivers, a first Guided analysis, Atlas), Guided and Integrations guides, the security model for v0.4, and the M3 verification report.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.4.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes. Upgrading from 0.3 runs migrations 0007 to 0010 (Guided drafts, endpoints and webhooks, saved plots and embeds, the trust lifecycle). Multi-tenant deployments must now set MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES (none when clients connect directly), or the server refuses to start.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• web: the Integrations hub (/integrations).
