Guided cards for Google Sheets (the endpoint's Apps Script and a score:<alias> token), a BI embed link and a webhook; endpoints and aliases with the promotion dialog (the version's scorecard, the expected gate, the server's reasons on 409 and the audited admin override), history and rollback, the frozen input contract with Try it (validate or score the example call), snippets for Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script and Atlas plus an Open-in-notebook cell; webhooks with an event picker, the secret shown once, rotation, Resend newest (a replay of the newest delivered event; there is no synthetic test event), the delivery log (status, attempts, response code) with replays and the auto-disabled notice; saved plots with PNG/SVG/PDF downloads (Plotly disabled with the server's reason on MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED) and expiring embed links with allowed sites and revocation; a Share button in the plot gallery; /tokens?preset=score:<alias>.
  • web: the trust pages. Public /signup (disposable-address and terms errors at their fields, the "check your inbox" state, the development outbox link) and /verify-email; Settings > Data for organisation admins (GDPR export and download, tenant deletion with the typed confirmation, grace period, cancel and per-store progress); a banner for scheduled deletions; in the admin console, the sign-up review queue and per-tenant identity verification and deletion status with a retry.
  • docs: The Integrations hub guide (with screenshots) and the Integrations section of the web app guide; make docs-screenshots-integrations.
  • spec: the M3 contracts for Guided mode and integrations, shared by the server, runner, web app and client components (contract v0.1, additive only).
  • mapi_spec.guided: four guided templates (geo_mmm, weekly_forecast, store_demand, customer_choice - the last needs a built-in choice model that is not shipped yet), plain-language questions, role detection from column profiles, drafts (ingest mapping + ModelSpec + YAML) and the BayesInsight model_def.json import.
  • mapi_spec.ingest: ingest presets (mff, meridian, bayesinsight), wide variables and the mff format; IngestMapping moves here (still exported by mapi_spec.api).
  • mapi_spec.calibration: business priors (ROI or share ranges with a credibility), lift tests, the ModelSpec.calibration block and the sandboxed translate_priors run kind.
  • mapi_spec.scorecard: the check catalog, items with check ids, categories and docs anchors, and the promotion gate (pass → allowed, warn → admin override with a reason, fail → blocked); Scorecard moves here (still exported by mapi_spec.api).
  • mapi_spec.whatif and ResponseGridView: per-draw response grids, the slider interpolation contract, "Run exact" and forecast/counterfactual presets; ScoreRequest.future_covariates.
  • mapi_spec.endpoints, mapi_spec.xrjson, mapi_spec.snippets: endpoints and aliases, score calls with inline XrJSON, input-schema compatibility, example payloads and pure snippet generators (Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, Atlas).
  • mapi_spec.webhooks: events, envelope, Mapi-Signature signing and verification, retries and the SSRF policy; mapi_spec.sharing: saved plots, renders (PNG, SVG, PDF) and embed links for platform recipes; mapi_spec.trust: sign-up, e-mail and identity verification, tenant deletion and GDPR export.
  • mapi_spec.api.M3_ENDPOINTS (45 operations) with their access rules; new permissions (webhook, embed, tenant_deletion, tenant_export, plot delete, endpoint manage for gate overrides), scopes (endpoints:promote, webhooks:manage), audit actions, problem codes and Project.guided_locked.
  • docs: Guided mode and Integrations concept pages; the v0.4 section of the HTTP API reference.
  • server: the Guided data path. GET /v1/guided/templates (paged) and /{template_id}; POST /v1/guided/detect-roles from browser profiles or a stored dataset version; POST /v1/guided/drafts and POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight, validated statically against the catalog with the schema the draft's mapping promises. Every operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in the OpenAPI document.
  • Migration 0007_guided: projects.guided_locked and dataset_versions.columns.
  • The persona lock is persisted, audited (project.guided_lock) and enforced: in a locked project, members below admin store Guided specs only, and only their basic fields may change (403 FORBIDDEN with the pointers otherwise).
  • The finalizer validates and stores an ingest's columns.json, which detection reads and …/artifacts/columns.json serves.
  • runner: sandboxed ingest for Guided mode: wide variables (one column per channel or product), the Meridian preset, MFF tables mapped like a CSV after the pivot, MffOptions.combine, and the BayesInsight preset (allowed_* values, period range, necessary variables). Caps on rows, columns, cell and name length, and decompression (gzip CSV streamed under a budget, Parquet, zip and netCDF by their declared sizes) are checked before a parser allocates; every refusal is a plain message with a suggested action. Ingest writes columns.json, the profile of every uploaded column.
  • plugins: choice.multinomial_logit in mapi-plugin-tabular, a conditional logit with household product effects and Bayesian-bootstrap draws, so the customer_choice template is real. The e84_lite conformance fixture replaces the corpus deferral.
  • spec: mapi_spec.bayesinsight.import_bayesinsight maps model_def.json onto mmm.hierarchical_geo - adstock, Hill saturation and pooling with BayesInsight's own priors where they have equivalents, controls, seasonality, trends - and reports every feature without one as an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning (BayesInsightImport.target keeps the mmm.bayesinsight draft). Role detection gains ColumnProfile.monotonic and origin, profiles_from_dataset, draft_schema and guided_lock_issues; GuidedAnswers.format accepts mff; IngestJob gains the ingest caps.

  • docs: the "From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft" guide; the Guided mode concept page, the built-in models and the conformance guide describe the served parts.

  • mmm: mmm.hierarchical_geo declares business_priors and lift_tests calibration.

  • Business priors (ROI or contribution-share ranges at a credibility, a baseline share) become per-channel LogNormal beta_channel priors (and an intercept prior) through a vectorised location/scale bisection over Monte Carlo draws of the other priors, with a prior-predictive preview in business units and the prior mass inside each stated range (mapi_plugin_mmm.calibration; property tests check the round trip).
  • Lift tests add kpi_delta ~ Normal(implied lift, se) over the test window; the extra spend is carried over through the lag tensor and the implied lift is kept as lift_tests__model.
  • response_curves carries the baseline (intercepts and controls), closing the expected KPI.
  • mmm.pymc_marketing takes lift tests through pymc-marketing's add_lift_test_measurements.
  • runner: translate_priors runs (priors.json and the mmm.prior_beliefs / core.prior_predictive plots); every fit writes scorecard.json (the whole check catalog, or the guided template's, each measured or skipped with a reason) and the what-if grid view ui/grids/response_curves.json; forecast and counterfactual score runs write ui/guided/forecast.json and ui/guided/counterfactual.json, and a forecast's fan chart shows the fitted history with the split line. Lift tests are checked against the raw data before a fit.
  • server: POST /v1/guided/prior-translations and GET …/{run_id} (static checks of the beliefs and lift tests against the dataset summary, a pinned translate_priors run, its verified priors.json). The finalizer stores the runner's scorecard on the model version and validates priors.json; spec validation checks a spec's lift tests against the dataset.
  • sdk: FitContext.calibration and FitContext.to_original (the fitted scales); prepare_model_stage for runs that build but do not fit a model; the optional translate_priors plugin hook. sdk-pymc: PyMCModel.prior_overlap_vars keeps cheap prior draws for the scorecard's new plausibility.prior_overlap check.
  • sdk/runner/server: forecasts extend the covariates their payload lacks (ScoreRequest.future_covariates: carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero) from the fitted history (mapi_sdk.future); the server passes the fit dataset as the score run's history input. mapi_server.services.scorecards.promotion_decision derives the promotion gate from a stored model version.
  • plots: mmm.prior_beliefs (each channel's prior ROI or share against the stated range).
  • docs: Guided modelling (the translation math, the lift-test likelihood, how each scorecard check is measured, the what-if, forecast and counterfactual views).
  • server: endpoints and aliases (/v1/endpoints, migration 0008_endpoints_webhooks).
  • PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} promotes a model version through the promotion gate: the sanity scorecard, the endpoint's evaluation policy (evaluate_then_refit by default, so endpoints serve versions refitted on all data after their holdout evaluation) and input-schema breaks. A warn needs a signed-in project admin's override with a reason (audited endpoint.promote_override; no API token can override); a fail blocks. expected_revision guards concurrent promotions.
  • History, rollback (audited with its reason) and delete; GET …/schema with an example payload, POST …/validate, and GET …/snippets rendered with the server's base URL.
  • POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score: inline XrJSON payloads are checked against the endpoint's input contract and the CoordPlan rules, stored as run inputs and decoded only in the sandbox; Prefer: wait, Idempotency-Key (repeat the call to collect a result), score:<alias> tokens, and the per-token rate limit and vCPU budget. Bodies are capped (413) and depth-checked before parsing.
  • server: webhooks (/v1/webhooks).
  • CRUD with the signing secret shown once and stored sealed (AES-GCM under a key derived from the server secret); rotation keeps the old secret signing for 24 hours.
  • A transactional outbox: run.succeeded, run.failed, model.version.ready, score.completed and endpoint.promoted are written in the transaction of the change; emit_tenant_event serves tenant.deletion.completed.
  • Deliveries from the worker on a webhooks procrastinate queue: signed (Mapi-Signature), retried with exponential backoff and jitter, auto-disabled after MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER consecutive failed events or a 410 (audited), with a delivery log and replays.
  • The SSRF guard: static URL checks, one resolution with every address checked, a pinned connection with the original name as SNI and Host, no redirects, time and size caps; MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP and MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST for development only.
  • Metrics for promotions, endpoint calls, events, delivery tries, SSRF refusals and disabled webhooks; every new operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in OpenAPI.
  • docs: the Endpoints and webhooks guide and the webhook settings.
  • server: saved plots, static rendering and embed links (plan §10.3 items 4-5).
  • POST/GET/DELETE /v1/plots[/{plot_id}]: a model version's plot (after its signed manifest verifies) or a user-authored PlotSpec, sanitized on save and on every read. User-authored plots are recorded with author provenance whatever they claim.
  • POST /v1/plots:render (Prefer: wait, Idempotency-Key) and GET /v1/plots/renders/{run_id}: a render run of one sanitized plot. The API writes its plots.json input and pins each bundle dataset as a plotdata.<n> input. Plotly is refused with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED unless MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED.
  • POST/GET/DELETE /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds[/{embed_id}]: tokenised links for platform recipes only (EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED otherwise), stored as keyed hashes, with expiry, revocation, view counts and audit events. A PNG fallback is rendered when the caller may start render runs, and copied write-once into the bundles bucket on first use.
  • The public GET /v1/embeds/{token}: no credential is read (cookies and Authorization are dropped), CORS for the plot-sandbox origin only, rate limits per link and per address, every dataset inlined from the verified bundle without decoding it.
  • Migration 0009_plots_embeds: saved_plots and plot_embeds with forced row-level security; the gateway role may read only the embed lookup columns.
  • Every new operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in the OpenAPI document.
  • runner: render runs draw PNG, SVG and PDF with vl-convert (pinned in the new mapi-plots[render] extra) with network access off, refuse anything that could fetch a resource, read plotdata.<n> inputs, apply width/height and cap images at 32 MiB. Plotly needs kaleido and a system Chrome (MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise; no browser is ever downloaded).
  • plot-sandbox: the embed page /embed/<token>. It fetches the embed view with no credentials under its own CSP (connect-src adds only the API's /v1/embeds/ path), validates and decodes it, honours the link's allowed origins and offers the PNG fallback. The mapi/web image serves it with the API origin filled in at start-up.
  • docs: the "Sharing plots" guide and the new settings in the configuration reference.
  • spec: the sign-up review queue (SignupReview, SignupReviewDecision, the SYBIL_FLAGS catalog), GET /v1/admin/signups, POST /v1/admin/signups/{signup_id}/review and POST /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion/retry; the auth.signup_flagged, auth.signup_review and tenant.deletion_retry audit actions; the deletion record and platform logs in RETAINED_RECORDS.
  • server: the trust lifecycle (migration 0010_trust_lifecycle).
  • Self-service sign-up (POST /auth/signup, POST /auth/verify-email): single-use e-mail tokens stored as HMACs (24 h), the same answer for new and known addresses, a mailer protocol (SMTP with required TLS, a file outbox read at GET /dev/outbox in the dev profile, console), the disposable-domain blocklist plus configured domains and files, per-address, per-domain and platform-wide sign-up limits, and Sybil heuristics (same address, browser cookie, e-mail, domain burst) that flag sign-ups for the operators' review queue. Verification creates a public tenant, its default project and the admin grant.
  • Identity verification (GET /v1/tenants/{id}/verification, operators' PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/verification, an IdentityVerifier provider protocol with a fake) and cut line A at run admission: uploaded code needs a trusted tier or identity verification (IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED); public tenants run built-ins and declarative specs only.
  • Tenant deletion: a confirmed request suspends the tenant and cancels its runs; after the grace period the orchestrator makes it deleting (tokens revoked, sessions ended, revoker hooks) and a procrastinate job purges the queue, every tenant table, every t/{tenant}/ object prefix (resuming after retention locks), then notifies and writes the tenant.purged tombstone; progress per store; automatic and operator retries.
  • GDPR export: a zip of every tenant record (credentials redacted), dataset objects and bundle manifests, with a short-lived signed link.
  • infra: a Cloud Armor policy on every load-balancer backend (OWASP CRS sqli, xss, lfi, rce and scanner rules in preview-then-enforce, per-IP rate bans on sign-up, /auth/*, embeds and endpoint scoring, Adaptive Protection), and an explicit retention for the control project's _Default log bucket (tenant deletion does not purge logs).
  • docs: Sign-up and abuse controls, Deleting and exporting data, and a Cloud Armor section in Security hardening.
  • integration: the M3 parts work together.
  • Tenant deletion revokes the tenant's embed links and disables its webhooks when it starts, purges every M3 table (endpoints and their history, webhooks, events and deliveries, saved plots, embeds, column profiles) and then delivers a signed tenant.deletion.completed to the webhooks that subscribed to it, through the same SSRF-guarded sender as every delivery (mapi_server.services.tenant_hooks).
  • Webhook events come from the finalizer's terminal transitions (run.*, model.version.ready with the runner's scorecard), promotions and rollbacks (endpoint.promoted), score runs (score.completed) and deletions.
  • Endpoint promotion gates on the scorecard the runner measured at fit (services.scorecards.promotion_decision, the single gate derivation).
  • Sign-up workspaces are public tier: built-ins and declarative specs only, on executors with enforced egress and DNS (cut line A).
  • server: POST /v1/guided/requests:compile turns a what-if scenario, a forecast or an intervention preset into its ScoreRequest, checked against the model version's score metadata ("Run exact").
  • runner: score runs read an endpoint call's inline XrJSON payloads (inline.data, inline.scenario) with the wire-format caps and the model's dim types.
  • mmm: mmm.bayesinsight, a BayesInsight model_def.json as a built-in model (Q8): Normal, log-normal, Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated likelihoods; coefficient and intercept priors in the KPI's own units; Hill, linear and S-shaped curves before delayed, geometric, Weibull or no carry-over; enforced sign constraints; fixed and partially pooled effects per row id (new levels pooled); Fourier seasons and local spline trends. Contributions sum to the expected KPI (a log-mean Divisia split for log links); lift tests observe the incremental KPI under the model's own likelihood. It passes the contract kit; mapi_plugin_mmm.bayesinsight_examples simulates a project with known parameters.
  • spec: mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model types model_def.json as the plugin runs it (the mmm.bayesinsight settings); import_bayesinsight(target="mmm.bayesinsight") now drafts a runnable spec - every row id a panel dim, the KPI bound to y, lagged media - falling back to BayesInsight's defaults with IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warnings (and info issues for faithful but surprising behaviour).
  • mmm: business-prior translation for mmm.pymc_marketing (1.1.0): ROI and share ranges become per-channel log-normal saturation_beta priors and a baseline share an intercept prior (narrowing the control and seasonality priors when needed), solved on prior draws of pymc-marketing's own model; settings.priors hands them to pymc-marketing's model_config; a translate_priors hook previews them and a fit without a translation run translates them itself.
  • sdk: categorical holdout metrics - accuracy, accuracy_naive, accuracy_lift, log_score and brier - for a text target scored as one probability per category.
  • spec/runner: the holdout.hit_rate scorecard check (the holdout hit rate against always guessing the most popular product, in plain words) for the customer_choice template.
  • conformance: the guided_mmm fixture (the geo_mmm Guided draft with business priors and a lift test, true to its simulation); e84_lite evaluates the categorical metrics; the dedicated BayesInsight import ingests, validates and fits end to end.
  • docs: the built-in models reference covers mmm.bayesinsight and every plugin's calibration; Guided modelling covers business priors for the pymc-marketing adapter and the BayesInsight lift likelihood.
  • docs: the v0.4 site. A new landing page (both personas, how it works, the Guided quick path, the v0.4 feature grid and the numbers measured in the M3 verification), "Why modeling-api?" (compared with notebooks and ad-hoc apps, MMM vendors and libraries, and generic model serving, with when to use something else) and "Use cases"; a Tutorials section with new tutorials "Connect Google Sheets" (an Apps Script that writes an endpoint's forecast into a sheet, run in the tests against stand-ins for Apps Script), "Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI" and "Import a BayesInsight model" (import, check and a local fit that recovers the simulated parameters), and "Receive webhooks" as a tutorial with a tested Flask receiver; the roadmap with v0.4 released and v0.5 (expert plugins, MCP, optimise jobs) next; the security model and architecture pages for v0.4; make docs-screenshots-tutorials.
  • cli: mapi tokens create --scope lists the endpoint, endpoints:promote and webhooks:manage scopes.
  • dev: make outbox (dev.py outbox) prints the dev mailer's newest e-mails and verification links; make dev sets MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR and the plot sandbox's VITE_API_URL; compose keeps the outbox on a volume. make api-types and make snapshots regenerate the web API types and the snapshots.
  • web: Guided mode, the task flow for non-technical analysts (plan §11 Guided 1-7), replacing the placeholder page.
  • "What do you want to learn?": the templates as cards, and the analyses in progress. A session is a stored spec (metadata.labels.guided); every step has its own URL (/guided/<spec>/<step>) and is rebuilt from server state, so it can be resumed or shared.
  • Your data: the upload (CSV, Parquet, MFF; Google Meridian tables recognised) is profiled in the browser and only the column profiles go to role detection; questions with suggested answers, confidence and reasons; a live preview with a sparkline per chosen series; plain validation messages; then the dataset, the signed upload, the sandboxed ingest with the draft's mapping and the spec.
  • What you believe: ROI or contribution-share ranges per channel with a confidence, the baseline share and lift tests, a translate_priors preview (prior ROI/share distributions and a KPI fan in the plot sandbox) and the translated priors applied when they match the beliefs saved.
  • Fit the model: plain-language phases, progress, time left and cancel, live over SSE.
  • Results: headline numbers, ROI and share per channel with 90% ranges, the fit and response-curve plots, and the sanity scorecard grouped by question with what to do.
  • What if…: per-channel spend sliders answered instantly from the per-draw response grid (a TypeScript port of mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario, checked against golden cases the spec tests export), "Run exact" next to the instant answer, scenario presets (channel off, budget × k) and a forecast fan chart with its split line.
  • Share: promotion to an endpoint with the gate explained (a warning needs a project admin's reason), an embed link for a platform chart, and the way to the Integrations hub.
  • "View as YAML" on every step (read-only Monaco) and "Edit in Expert" with "Back to Guided mode"; settings Expert mode changed are kept and marked "advanced settings applied". The Guided/Expert choice is remembered per user, and in a project locked to Guided mode members below admin see Guided screens only.
  • Mock-mode handlers for every Guided call (src/mocks/guided.ts), Vitest unit and route tests and the Playwright smoke spec e2e/guided.spec.ts (the whole flow, the lock, the persona and a 375 px phone).
  • spec: tests/snapshots/whatif_golden.json, golden what-if cases shared with the web app (make snapshots regenerates it).
  • docs: "Your first analysis in Guided mode", a step-by-step tutorial with screenshots (make docs-screenshots-guided recaptures them from mock mode).
  • client: the v0.4 Python client. Every operation of ENDPOINTS has a request builder (the coverage test now checks the whole v0.4 table), sync and async.
  • api.guided (templates, role detection, drafts, the BayesInsight import, "Run exact" compilation, preview_priors), api.endpoints (promote, history, rollback, schema, validate, keyed Prefer: wait scoring, snippets), api.webhooks (secrets returned once; deliveries, replay, rotation), saved plots, renders (waited for, CRC32C-checked download) and embeds on api.plots, api.signup/api.verify_email (sent without credentials), verification, deletion and the GDPR export (size-checked atomic download) on api.tenants, and the sign-up review queue on api.admin.
  • Client().endpoint(alias) (RemoteEndpoint): schema(), validate(ds) and score(ds) -> xr.Dataset with inline XrJSON (mapi_client.xrjson, the SDK wire format); the generated Python snippet runs as-is.
  • mapi_client.webhooks.verify(headers, body, secret) for receivers.
  • mapi_client.atlas.RemoteModel: Atlas's model interface, structurally (Atlas is never imported at import time): KPI at the mean or as draws, batching along an independent dim into one score request, an LRU cache, backoff on RATE_LIMITED; register_with_atlas(); the atlas extra; make test-atlas runs the tests with Atlas installed in a throwaway overlay.
  • cli: mapi endpoints ls|get|history|promote|rollback|schema|score|snippets, mapi webhooks ls|get|create|update|rotate|deliveries|replay|rm, mapi plots render|embed|embeds|revoke, mapi guided templates|detect|draft (CSV files are profiled locally), mapi priors preview, mapi tenant status|export|delete, mapi signup and mapi verify-email. Promotions, rollbacks, rotations, deletions and revocations ask first; webhook secrets and embed links are printed once, alone on stdout.

  • docs: the v0.4 sections of the Python client and command-line guides, "Optimise a budget with Atlas" and "Receiving webhooks" (FastAPI and Flask), with offline, tested snippets.

  • integration (web): Guided mode and the Integrations hub work as one.

  • The Share step links into the hub: the promoted endpoint's snippets, a score:<alias> token, the chart link under Plots and links, and the hub itself (typed routes). A project locked to Guided mode keeps Integrations in the navigation.
  • Both use the same endpoint and saved-plot queries and the same promotion-gate preview (the port of promotion_gate), so a promotion or link made in one shows in the other at once; in mock mode they share one endpoint, history, plot and embed state.
  • Every snippet the app shows and copies is the server's (mapi_spec.snippets), the notebook cell included; the mock's fixture endpoint, example call and snippets are generated from mapi_spec (apps/web/scripts/gen_integration_fixtures.py, checked by make web-check and CI, rewritten by make snapshots), and a test checks each tab against them.

  • spec: a notebook snippet language: a Jupyter or marimo cell that scores the endpoint with Client().endpoint(alias).score(...) and shows an xarray.Dataset; the client's tests run it as generated.

  • e2e: the M3 exit criteria through the running stack. tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py (in make e2e) follows one analyst from sign-up and e-mail verification through the geo_mmm Guided flow (CSV and MFF), business priors and a lift test, the scorecard and its gate, what-if vs "Run exact", forecast and channel-off, an endpoint scored with a score:<alias> token, signed webhooks to a local HTTPS receiver with a replay, an embed link and its revocation, Atlas optimising a budget through RemoteModel against the live endpoint, the GDPR export and a tenant purge checked in Postgres and the GCS shim. apps/web/e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts is the timed "unaided tester" script (upload → report → scenario) and the Integrations hub flow. make e2e overlays Atlas from ATLAS_DIR when it is there.

  • dev: the dev profile trusts a local webhook receiver: a throwaway CA and certificate for 127.0.0.1/localhost in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/, with MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE and MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST set unless given.
  • gcs-shim: --bundle-retention-days (default $MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS) chooses the bundles bucket's locked retention when a root is created (0: none), so a test stack's tenant deletions can finish.
  • web: "Fit again, more carefully" on the Guided report when a convergence check warns or fails (twice the tuning and draws and a higher target_accept, up to a ceiling); a blocked Share step links to it.
  • spec: mapi_spec.guided.freq_plain: role detection explains a detected date frequency in words ("weekly, on Sundays").
  • docs: M3 verification: what was verified of the M3 exit criteria, the timings, the defects found, and the protocol and observation sheet for the five non-technical testers.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• spec: the geo_mmm template (1.1.0) fits with 1000 tuning steps and draws and target_accept 0.95: the 500-draw fit failed the scorecard's convergence checks on two years of weekly data, which Guided users cannot act on, so the analysis could never go live.
  • web: in What you believe, channels start without a belief (unticked); ticking one starts from the sensible range. Untouched channels no longer become ROI beliefs.
  • server: GET /v1/embeds/{token} answers Cache-Control: private, no-cache (was public, max-age=60), so a revoked link stops rendering on the next load.
  • spec: mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the v0.4 surface (M1 + M2 + M3, every row served); V03_ENDPOINTS keeps the v0.3 table and ALL_ENDPOINTS is an alias of ENDPOINTS.
  • server: the M3 migrations run in one chain after 0006_executor_disable: 0007_guided, 0008_endpoints_webhooks, 0009_plots_embeds, 0010_trust_lifecycle.
  • spec: the customer_choice template (1.1.0) targets the built-in choice.multinomial_logit; wide column labels drop the question's keywords (price_cola → cola); a draft refuses answers that would give two columns the same dataset name.
  • spec: the customer_choice template (1.2.0) evaluates the categorical metrics and runs holdout.hit_rate; BayesInsightImport(target="mmm.bayesinsight") drafts the shipped plugin's settings (variables maps analytic names to variables; the KPI is y) instead of keeping model_def verbatim.
  • server: POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight validates mmm.bayesinsight drafts against the catalog too.
  • conformance: the corpus runner compares fit-time and evaluate-run metrics only when it rebuilt the holdout (a last_per_group split is scored in sample).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• cli: mapi webhooks update ID [--enable|--disable] [-e EVENT ...] [--url URL] [--description TEXT]. A webhook created with --inactive, or disabled automatically after repeated failures, could only be switched back on in the browser; --enable does it from the command line and resets the failure count.
  • docs: the Guided tutorial's report and scorecard screenshots contradicted each other (media drove 23% of results, yet "about 80%" would happen without media). The mock-mode scorecard now reads its baseline, largest-channel and best-return checks from the same response grid as the report, and the screenshots were recaptured.
  • server: "Run exact" failed on every live stack: POST /v1/guided/requests:compile left what-ifs and presets over the fit window without data. The compiled request now names the fit dataset version, and a score request without data, scenario or horizon is refused with 422 SCHEMA_INVALID before a run starts.
  • web: the Guided report showed MAPE in percent as a fraction ("83 %" for 0.83 %); it reads the scorecard's measured value. The beliefs preview no longer prints impossible baseline shares ("between -164 % and 271 %"); Share a chart offers result charts before the sampler's diagnostics.
  • plots: prediction plots name the predicted quantity as the dataset does (revenue, not y_hat).
  • client: datasets.upload accepts an mff mapping for a .csv MFF table.
  • server: an unresolvable webhook host is explained in plain words (no gaierror).
  • web: the New token dialog's budget period showed "pe" instead of "per day"/"per month": native selects no longer shrink below their width in a flex row (filters, the cap window, the intervention editor and the upload mapper had the same risk).
  • spec: index dims extend contiguously (their coordinates have ordinals), so scoring an index dim with an extend policy no longer fails with NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION.
  • sdk: cell-level splits treat an empty text target as missing and hold text targets out with '', so a choice panel's chosen product can be held out.
  • runner: the holdout.mape scorecard check read mapi_sdk's MAPE, which is in percent, against thresholds in fractions, so a 1.4% holdout error showed as 140% and blocked the promotion of almost every model; percent metrics are now divided by 100 first.
  • runner: inline endpoint payloads named like the endpoint's input contract (canonical names such as time) failed to score when the dataset's own name differed (week); the score run renames them to the dataset's names before typing coordinates. The snapshot's documentation says which names a payload uses.
  • spec: an endpoint's example call (GET …/schema, the snippets, mapi endpoints score --example) asked quantile models for a mean they cannot serve; it now asks for the representation's default summary.

docs.title: Fixed (M3 review: Guided modeling)
docs.text:
• spec/server/web: the promotion gate let through an evaluate_then_refit version that was never evaluated on a holdout (a spec without data.split skips every holdout check and its scorecard can still pass). Such a version now needs an administrator override with the new gate reason NOT_EVALUATED, as does a guided version whose template's scorecard checks did not all run (Q13). The web app's gate preview follows.
  • mmm: a contribution-share belief for a channel with no spend in the fit window translated to an absurd prior (LogNormal(mu≈692), so any new spend on the channel predicted ~1e300) with no issue. Both translators (mmm.hierarchical_geo, mmm.pymc_marketing) now refuse it with an error, as they do for an ROI belief, and refuse any solved prior that is not finite or has |mu| > 50, keeping the channel's default.
  • mmm/runner: a response grid whose spacing skipped multiplier 1 (grid.max_multiplier: 3, grid.points: 20, or a maximum below 1) lost its what-if sliders, and the scorecard's ROI, share and baseline checks were read at the nearest point (1.05x or 0.5x spend). The grid now always holds 1 (inserted when the spacing skips it; max_multiplier must be at least 1), the curves are read at exactly 1, and a what-if grid the view contract refuses is reported as VIEW_INVALID instead of VIEW_TOO_LARGE.
  • runner: a model with more than 256 geos lost its whole what-if grid (the per-geo view failed its geo cap and the national grid was dropped with it); it now gets the national grid (mapi_spec.views.MAX_GRID_GEOS).
  • server: POST /v1/guided/requests:compile answered 404 for an endpoint:// model target, and POST /v1/specs:validate reported a score request aimed at an endpoint as REF_UNRESOLVED ("endpoint aliases arrive in v0.4"). An endpoint ref now resolves to the version the endpoint serves.
  • runner: a dense ingest (and the MFF pivot) built every combination of the dim labels with no cap, so a 2 MB CSV whose keys rarely repeat asked for ~80 GB and the run was OOM-killed. The cube is now checked before it is built (at most 250 million values, and within the class's scratch budget) and refused as PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE with a hint.
  • spec/server/runner: static renders had no pixel cap, so scale: 8 with a 4096 x 4096 size (or a plot that sets its own huge size) asked vl-convert for a ~4 GiB raster and the run was OOM-killed. A PNG or PDF now holds at most 50 megapixels (mapi_spec.sharing.MAX_RENDER_PIXELS): POST /v1/plots:render refuses a bigger request with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, and the runner checks the laid-out size (composite views included) before it rasterises.
  • spec/runner: the data.history check counted periods (warn below 104, fail below 52) whatever the data's frequency, so 105 days of daily data passed as "enough to learn seasonality". It now measures years (history_years: periods over the periods in a year at the time dim's frequency, or the one its dates follow; warn below 2 years, fail below 1; the weekly_forecast template fails below 0.5).
  • mmm: a lift test cut by the fit window (one that straddles the end of an evaluate_then_refit evaluation fit's training periods, or starts before the data) put all of its spend into the periods left and compared them with the whole test's KPI change, biasing the evaluation fit and the holdout scorecard. Such a test is now skipped and logged, in mmm.hierarchical_geo, mmm.bayesinsight and mmm.pymc_marketing.
  • runner: dates with a UTC offset (2024-01-07T00:00:00+01:00, common in BI exports) or a tz-aware Parquet timestamp became time zone-aware labels that the ingest then refused as "not dates" (and offsets that change with daylight saving time failed outright). They are now read as the local date and time they name, with an info issue saying the offsets were dropped.
  • sdk: future_covariates: seasonal_naive aligned the last season by position, so a horizon that started after a gap (or a payload of later periods only) shifted the seasonal pattern, and a missing value in the last season was copied forward as NaN. It now takes the value whole seasons before each horizon date, stepping back past missing values, and carries the last value forward (with a warning) only where no season has one.
  • plots/runner: a Guided geo MMM's fit chart titled its panels with the spec's internal dim name (geo) instead of the analyst's column (market), and faceted response curves said channel whatever the column was called. Recipes now title facets with the dataset's name for the dim (RecipeInput.dim_label, from the bundle's /binding), and the fit's holdout prediction tree carries the binding.

docs.title: Fixed (M3 review: integrations and trust)
docs.text:
• server: every per-address control saw the proxy's address, not the caller's, so the sign-up, verification and embed-view limits and the Sybil same_ip check applied to the whole platform behind a load balancer. New MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES (addresses or CIDR ranges): a request from a trusted proxy takes the right-most untrusted X-Forwarded-For hop as the client; any other peer's header is ignored. The multi-tenant profile refuses to start without it (none when clients connect directly); Terraform sets Cloud Run's and the load balancer's hops and make dev sets none for its multi-tenant stack.
  • server: a promoter, an endpoints:promote token included, could switch off the schema-change and train-only gates by sending a laxer evaluation_policy with the promotion. Relaxing the policy (schema_change toward allow, fit_mode to train_only) now needs a signed-in endpoint admin, like an override (403 FORBIDDEN otherwise, audited as a denial), and the promotion's audit event records the policy before and after (mapi_spec.endpoints.policy_relaxations).
  • server: the per-domain (25 a day) and platform (500 an hour) sign-up caps counted unverified sign-ups, so made-up addresses could lock a whole e-mail domain, or everyone, out of sign-up. They now count verified sign-ups only (the per-address limit still counts every request), and large free-mail domains (MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, default mapi_spec.trust.SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS) have no per-domain cap and never trip the domain_burst Sybil flag.
  • server: the plan's draw cap (Q2: 300, 500 on paid tiers) was enforced only by the Python client, so any caller could ask a model or endpoint for 10,000 draws. Score requests asking for more than the tenant tier's MAX_SCORE_DRAWS (public 300, other tiers 500) are refused with QUOTA_EXCEEDED at /output/draws, and the score job carries the cap (ScoreJob.max_draws: score runs now store a {request, max_draws} payload) so the runner enforces it too.
  • server: a score:<alias> token could score any dataset of the project by dataset:// reference (and probe which exist through …/validate) without dataset read access. Callers without it now send inline data or name the endpoint's own fit dataset; any other reference, existing or not, gets the same 403 FORBIDDEN.
  • server: a GDPR export whose build process died stayed running forever and blocked every later export of the tenant. A build now holds a lease (MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S, after which it fails, plus five minutes); a running export past its lease is built once more, then failed, and only the build holding the lease may mark it ready. Metadata rows are capped at MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES (tables cut short are listed under skipped), so the in-memory archive stays bounded.
  • server: an export still building when a tenant purge started wrote the whole archive after the purge, where nothing would ever delete it. The deletion's start cancels the tenant's queued and running exports (revoked.exports in the audit event), the queue store waits for a cancelled build to end (or its lease to pass), and a build that lost its lease never uploads and deletes an archive it uploaded after losing it.
  • server: a purge went on after MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S while cancelled runs that never stopped still held signed upload policies under t/{tenant}/, so they could write objects after the object store was purged. The queue store now also waits until those runs' signed links have expired (attempt start + run timeout + 30 minutes) and says until when.
  • server, web, client: GDPR exports could not be listed, and Settings > Data found the last export only through the browser's localStorage, so another admin or browser could neither see nor download an export that was running or finished (and could not start another one while it ran). New GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports (newest first, paged, tenant admins); Settings > Data shows the newest export from it, and the Python client has tenants.exports(tenant_id).
  • server: the storage_bytes quota left out model bundles although the docs count them; a tenant's storage now adds the size of every model version's stored objects.
  • server: the per-tier egress cap (egress_bytes_per_month, 5 GiB on the free tier) was defined but never measured. Every signed download link the API mints (dataset and model artifacts, ui/ views, score and render outputs) and every public embed view (its inline data and PNG link) is now charged to the tenant's monthly egress, which GET /v1/usage reports; past the cap the link is refused with 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED (with Retry-After until the month resets). GDPR exports are never charged; a purge deletes the counter.
  • server: the embeds' "platform recipes only" rule trusted the provenance in plots.json, which the worker writes while it runs plugin code, so uploaded code could label any spec core.* and get it onto public embed links. Plots of model versions fitted with uploaded code (an overlay in their lineage) are saved with plugin provenance, are never embeddable, and existing links stop serving them.
  • server, runner, spec: endpoint and model scores answered only with signed links to zarr and Arrow files, so the Google Sheets card wrote the word "done" into A1 and the curl, R and TypeScript snippets printed links nobody could open without those libraries. Score runs now write summary.json (the requested summary - mean and 90% HDI by default - as plain tables: coordinate columns, then one column per statistic, at most 100,000 cells), and ScoreCallResult.summary carries it inline once the run succeeded. The Apps Script builds its payload from an Input sheet (long format) when there is one and writes the summary tables to a Result sheet; the other snippets print the tables.
  • web, plot-sandbox, docs: embed links were advertised for Slack, but Slack does not frame pages and the embed page had no unfurl tags, so a pasted link showed a bare "Shared plot". The page now carries static Open Graph tags (a "Shared chart" card, never the plot's name or the token), and the UI and guides recommend posting the rendered PNG to Slack instead of promising a live chart there.
  • docs: webhooks do not attach rendered plots, a deliberate deviation from the plan (bodies carry ids and states only, so no chart or signed link reaches a third-party receiver); the webhooks guide says so and shows how a receiver renders a chart with POST /v1/plots:render when model.version.ready arrives.

docs.title: Fixed (M3 review: web)
docs.text:
• web: a new self-service sign-up landed in Expert mode, with no way into Guided mode but the header's Mode switch. Until a user chooses, a public tier workspace now starts in Guided mode (other workspaces and platform operators in Expert; the browser's stored v2 default is forgotten, per-user choices are kept), "Sign in" after the e-mail link opens /guided, / opens the Guided start page in Guided mode, and Expert navigation (g g) and Home (Start a guided analysis) lead to Guided.
  • web: the admin console's Promotions tab was a placeholder. It lists the endpoint promotions that needed attention across tenants (gate overrides with their reason and failing checks, blocked promotions and those refused for want of an override), from the audit log. There is still no queue: the gate decides each promotion at once.
  • web: a project could be locked to Guided mode only through the API. Project admins now have Lock … to Guided mode under Settings > Mode (PATCH …/projects/{project_id}, audited as before).
  • web: a webhook's Send test button only replayed the newest delivery (and was disabled until one existed). It is now Resend newest, and the empty delivery log says how a new webhook gets its first delivery.
  • web: the beliefs preview charted every channel, the unticked ones at the model's wide default prior, so they looked like the analyst's beliefs (ROI near 100, media shares adding up past 100 %) and squashed the ranges actually stated. The charts show the ticked channels only and name the others ("No view on …: … learns them from the data"). The mock engine previews every channel, as the server does.
  • spec, web: a "Results without any media" belief stated without any channel belief was silently dropped (BusinessPriors.channels needed at least one entry, and the page then saved "no business priors"). BusinessPriors now needs at least one belief of either kind (channels defaults to {}; a baseline-only block validates, and the "largest shares" warning no longer fires without channel shares), both MMM plugins translate a baseline alone, and the Guided page previews and saves it.
  • plot-sandbox: in dark mode, rule and text marks without a colour of their own were drawn black on the dark card (Vega-Lite's default): the beliefs preview's 90% line, the forecast's split line and its "Forecast starts" label. The theme colours rules in muted ink and text and ticks in body ink, so a median tick also stands apart from its bar.
  • web: the Guided forecast panel always said "weeks" (daily data too) and accepted horizons up to the template's limit (520), past the horizon a weekly forecast was fitted for, which then failed. It names the data's period (days, weeks, months) and stops at the fitted horizon (max_extension), saying a longer one needs a new fit.
  • web: Guided fan charts (forecast, prior predictive) started their y axis at zero, which squeezed the bands into slivers; the axis now fits the data (zero: false).
  • web: the endpoint page said "Promoted by usr_01…" and its history listed user ids, and saved plots said "of mdl_01…". People are named from the project's members (the id stays in the tooltip, and an unknown id is shown as is), and saved plots name their model.
  • web: sign-up asked people to accept the terms of service and the acceptable-use policy without a way to read them. Both are links (new tab) to VITE_TERMS_URL and VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL, by default the plain-language summaries the app now publishes at /terms and /acceptable-use.
  • web: the Guided upload box described weekly marketing data by market (and the MFF and Meridian presets) for every template, Customer choice and Demand by store included. It describes the rows each template needs and names the presets for the marketing mix only.
  • web: adding an experiment showed a red error under every field at once, its example values ("-120000") read as prefilled data, and nothing said why Preview and Save were disabled. A field's message now waits until the field is left, the examples read "e.g. -120,000", and a summary beside the actions says what each unfinished experiment still needs.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• docs: the Google Sheets tutorial showed the Apps Script from before score answers carried their summary (it wrote done into A1). Its snippet is the server's current script again (the summary tables in a Result sheet, an optional Input sheet), the tutorial says what the sheet shows, and the Node test checks the Result sheet.
  • spec: the example of PlotEmbedCreated (in the OpenAPI document) used an /e/<token> link; the server answers with /embed/<token>.
  • docs: M3 verification and the landing page give the unaided-tester timing measured on the integrated branch, with the script starting at / (135 s, was 137 s from /guided).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The M3 exit criterion is not met yet. Five non-technical testers must go from upload to report to scenario unaided in under 30 minutes. The protocol and observation sheet are written (the M3 verification page in the operations docs), and a script clicks through the same flow in 135 s of system time, but no tester session has run.
  • Nothing has run against real Google Cloud or a Docker daemon. The Cloud Armor policy, the trusted-proxy ranges Terraform sets for Cloud Run behind the load balancer, the Cloud Run executor, the docker and docker-gvisor executors and the compose stack are checked with fakes, mocked providers and terraform validate only. After the first deploy, check that sign-ups from two networks get different fingerprints.
  • Static rendering covers Vega-Lite only out of the box. Plotly needs kaleido and a system Chrome, so POST /v1/plots:render refuses it with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED unless MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED, and that path has not run in an image. Webhook bodies never carry charts (a deliberate deviation), and Slack shows one generic card for every embed link.
  • Webhooks have no synthetic test event: Resend newest replays the newest delivery, and a new webhook gets its first delivery from a real event.
  • The Google Sheets Apps Scripts and the embed page inside Notion, Looker Studio and Power BI are tested only against stand-ins, never in the real tools.
  • Egress is estimated from object size when a link is minted, not measured as bytes served; a caller that polls a score result is charged again on each poll. The GDPR export archive is still built in memory (bounded by two settings) because the object store has no streaming upload.
  • There is no combined cap across all free-tier tenants beyond the global quota scope; the Python client's Atlas RemoteModel caps draws at 300 on every tier (the server allows 500 on paid tiers).
  • The Guided/Expert choice is stored per browser, not per user on the server; there is no mapi command to lock a project to Guided mode (the web switch and the API do it).
  • In the geo_mmm template, the default priors of channels without a stated belief can still imply media shares above 100% in total; the beliefs preview no longer presents them as the analyst's beliefs.
  • The /terms and /acceptable-use pages are plain-language drafts, not reviewed legal text. A public installation should publish its own and set VITE_TERMS_URL and VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL.
  • Some screenshots predate the M3 review's wording (the Guided beliefs page, the Integrations hub pages including the Sheets card, Settings).
  • A few tests are timing-sensitive under a fully loaded laptop (the 100-fit Cloud Run load test, the Postgres-restart chaos test, Terraform's provider plugin start-up); each passes when run again.

docs.title: [0.3.0] — M2: cloud & multi-tenant core — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
The platform is now multi-tenant and ready for Google Cloud. Many teams can share one deployment: each tenant has its own projects, members, API tokens, quotas, cost and audit trail, and PostgreSQL row-level security keeps their data apart. Runs can execute as Cloud Run Jobs, and Terraform describes every Google Cloud project. Nothing has been applied to real Google Cloud yet: cloud code is tested against fakes, and the Terraform is validated and tested against mocked providers. In summary:

  • tenancy and auth: tenants with trust tiers and data residency, projects with ordered roles (viewer < editor < runner < admin), browser sign-in through a backend-for-frontend OIDC flow (with a dev identity provider for local work), mapi login for the CLI, and checksummed, scoped, project-bound API tokens.
  • isolation: forced row-level security on every tenant table. The API runs as roles without the bypass (mapi_app for tenant data, mapi_gateway for sign-in and operator lookups); only the orchestrator holds the platform role. The audit log and the cost ledger are append-only.
  • quotas and cost: token, tenant and global quotas with weighted fair-share leasing and 429 back-off; an integer-micros cost ledger with per-run cost, usage reports and cost by tenant for operators; a global spend cap.
  • operations: kill switches (pause or cancel uploaded code, the spend cap), executors that operators can disable, a shared-tier gate that needs recorded conformance and security-suite evidence, audit events for every change, Prometheus metrics, dashboards, alerts and runbooks, plus a security probe suite and chaos tests.
  • cloud: a Cloud Run Jobs executor (orphan adoption, fan-out, 429 handling), Pub/Sub push events, a Cloud KMS bundle signer, Terraform for the control, data and exec projects, and deploy and rollback scripts.
  • web, CLI and client: tenant switcher, members, tokens, usage and an operator console (tenants, quotas, cost, kill switches, executors, audit); mapi admin, mapi tokens and mapi usage; client methods for every new endpoint.
  • docs: Administration and Authentication guides with tested walkthroughs, a security model, deployment to Google Cloud with the [verify M0] checklist, and reference tables generated from the code.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.3.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes. Upgrading from 0.2 runs migrations 0003 to 0006, which adopt existing rows into a platform tenant.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• spec: the M2 contracts. They cover tenants, trust tiers and placement, ordered project roles (viewer < editor < runner < admin) with one permission matrix, and AuthContext as the single authorization decision. They also add checksummed API tokens stored as HMACs, scopes, BFF OIDC helpers (PKCE, cookies, safe return_to) and Pub/Sub push claims; token/tenant/global quotas with fair-share leasing and 429 back-off; integer-micros cost pricing and the ledger (RunCost moves to mapi_spec.cost); audit events; kill switches and executor health; and the 12-case executor conformance suite as data. mapi_spec.api gains the 40 M2 endpoints and ROUTE_ACCESS, the scope and permission of every operation (all 44 M1 ones included). Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes.
  • server: authentication on every route.
  • Bearer API tokens, browser sessions through an OIDC backend-for-frontend (authorization code + PKCE, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, CSRF token), and ID tokens of the mapi CLI (MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS).
  • A credential-less local administrator in the single-tenant profile, and a dev profile with a built-in identity provider and seeded accounts.
  • Tenants, projects, members and invitations.
  • Row-level security: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every tenant table, set_config(…, true) per transaction, failing closed, with separate app and platform roles.
  • Quotas and rate limits at admission and at dispatch.
  • A cost ledger written whenever an attempt ends, for every executor.
  • The audit log, the operator endpoints (tenants, quota policies, kill switches, executor health, audit) and usage reports.
  • server: the cloudrun-jobs executor for a fixed inventory of 3 bases × S/M/L.
  • Env-only overrides, orphan adoption by nonce, and a jobs.run token bucket with a shared 429 cool-down.
  • Exit-code classification (OOM, timeout, partial) and taskCount fan-out plumbing.
  • Tested against a deterministic FakeCloudRun.
  • Pub/Sub push authentication: a Google-signed OIDC token, a JWKS cache, a subscription allow-list and decoding of the log entry.
  • A Cloud KMS manifest signer, alongside the local one.
  • MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs: Cloud Storage with keyless IAM signBlob URLs and integrity checks on every write.
  • server: observability.
  • structlog JSON logs carrying the trace and span ids.
  • OpenTelemetry spans, with an optional OTLP exporter.
  • The Prometheus metric set at GET /metrics, behind a bearer (MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN, which the multi-tenant profile requires), plus the worker's own endpoint (MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT).
  • Request ids on every response.
  • tests: the executor conformance suite, run against fake Cloud Run and local-process. It also checks that every attempt that ran is in the cost ledger.
  • A 100-fit load test on the fake backend (make load-test).
  • Chaos tests (make chaos).
  • A route-table test that every non-public route needs credentials and that no M1 or M2 route serves another tenant's project.
  • End-to-end M2 suites against a running dev stack, run by make e2e. Two tenants are created through the dev IdP. The suites cover sign-in, cross-tenant refusal at the API and by row-level security in Postgres, token scopes, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, the spend-cap kill switch held at dispatch, per-run cost and the audit trail (tests/e2e/test_m2_tenancy_stack.py). They also include a browser flow: sign-in, tenant switch, fit with metered cost, tokens, and the admin kill switch (apps/web/e2e/m2-flow.e2e.spec.ts).
  • An opt-in burst of concurrent real fits, against the dev stack or a deployment (MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS).
  • A nightly workflow: chaos, executor conformance, both load-test modes, and the security suite on local-process and inside gVisor.
  • infra: Terraform modules control, exec, data, build, perimeter and stack, plus the dev, staging and prod environments.
  • The exec projects get zero egress, a restricted VIP, a DNS response policy and VPC-SC.
  • Cloud SQL with three login roles, generated secrets written only through write-only arguments, a Pub/Sub push to an internal-only events service, and KMS.
  • Deploy scripts (deploy/gcp) and a manual Deploy workflow.
  • make tf-validate runs fmt, validate and the mocked-provider module tests; nothing is ever applied.
  • ops and security: Grafana and Cloud Monitoring dashboards, alert rules and runbooks (ops/). A sandbox-escape probe suite with an expected-outcome matrix per isolation level, and a deliberately malicious plugin that is never installed (security/, run with make security-suite).
  • web: sign-in, a tenant and project switcher, and pages for API tokens, members, and usage and cost. Per-run cost, and plain-language quota and permission errors with a Retry-After countdown. An operator console for tenants, quota policies, kill switches, executor health and the audit log.
  • client and cli:
  • mapi login (browser or device code, refreshed and stored with mode 0600, or --with-token), logout, whoami and use, plus X-Mapi-Project selection.
  • Token, usage and admin commands and resources.
  • 429 handling with RateLimited/QuotaExceeded and Retry-After.
  • --discovery-url for providers whose discovery document lives elsewhere (the dev IdP).
  • mapi_client.oidc.dev_idp_login for scripts.
  • docs: tenancy and auth, and quotas and cost concepts; the v0.3 HTTP API; the authentication, Cloud Run, Google Cloud deployment, security hardening, observability and security-suite operations pages; and every new variable in the configuration reference.
  • The M2 verification record (docs/operations/m2-verification.md): what was proven locally, the measured numbers, and the exact steps left for a real Google Cloud project.
  • server: GET /v1/admin/usage (operators) returns cost by tenant for a UTC day or month, summed from the cost ledger with the biggest spender first. It also returns the current spend against the global spend cap (AdminUsageReport, TenantCost and GlobalSpend in mapi_spec.api). The Python client exposes it as admin.usage().
  • web: the admin console has a Cost tab with cost by tenant per period and each tenant's share of spend. The global spend-cap card shows current spend against the cap on a meter that warns at 70% and 90%.
  • docs: the v0.3 site.
  • New Administration and Authentication guides, each driven by a walkthrough that make e2e runs against a dev stack (docs/snippets/admin_tour.sh, auth_tour.sh).
  • Generated from the code at every build (scripts/gen_docs_platform.py): the roles, token-scope and trust-tier matrices (mapi_spec.tenancy.PERMISSIONS), the metric set, the alerts, dashboards and runbooks of ops/, and an index of every MAPI_* variable. Pages embed generated tables with <!-- generated: NAME -->.
  • The landing page tells the multi-tenant story, with screenshots of the new screens (make docs-screenshots-admin); the security model shows what each executor enforces and the threat model in plain terms; Deploying to Google Cloud starts with the [verify M0] checklist and ends at the first tenant; the roadmap moves to M3.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• devops: make dev and compose run the servers in the dev profile by default (MAPI_STACK_PROFILE): sign in as admin@dev.local (tenant admin and operator) or one of the other seeded accounts. make seed, make e2e and mapi_conformance run --stack sign in by themselves. MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant restores the credential-less API.
  • server: every v0.2 route is project-scoped. Callers name the project with X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project>, a token's binding, or the single-tenant default.
  • web: mutations send the session's CSRF token (X-CSRF-Token). openapi.json and the TypeScript types are generated from the server alone.
  • client: QUOTA_EXCEEDED is no longer retried by default (RetryPolicy.max_quota_wait). RATE_LIMITED has its own retry budget and is retried for every method.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• server: the start-up check that every route has an access rule now covers routes of included routers (FastAPI 0.143 keeps them as branches).
  • server: two finalizations of the same model at once no longer deadlock, and a retried finalization reuses its stored signed manifest.
  • server: /auth/callback sends the browser back to the web origin, and a single-tenant server answers /auth/session as the local administrator.
  • web: costs below $0.0001 keep two significant digits instead of showing $0.00.
  • Usage lists session runs as "Signed-in users" (the server's group key is -).
  • Memory under an hour is shown in GiB-seconds.
  • A finished run without output no longer says "yet".
  • The project switcher no longer truncates names on wide screens.
  • web: a live log tail no longer trips the tenant's rate limit. Before, it sent up to 10 requests every 500 ms while catching up. It now fetches one page per poll, at least 2 s apart (5 s once caught up), and waits out Retry-After on 429.
  • security: the docker and gVisor probe container gets the suite through a read-only mount; before, every isolation probe ended in ERROR on a host with Docker.
  • --executor cloud refuses to run outside a Cloud Run Jobs execution.

docs.title: Fixed (M2 review: spec, server and auth)
docs.text:
• server: an API token can no longer administer its tenant. Tokens are bound to one project, so tenant members, project create and delete, the tenant audit log and tenant usage now need a signed-in session (403 for any token). A token may still read its own tenant and list its own project (mapi_spec.api.TOKEN_TENANT_ROUTES).
  • server: signing in again no longer re-activates a disabled account. /auth/callback refuses it with the generic 401 and audits auth.login_failed; only an invitation becomes active at its first sign-in.
  • server: operator status is decided on every request from MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS (and the dev profile's first account). Before, a demoted operator kept operator powers through mapi login ID tokens indefinitely and through browser sessions until they expired.
  • spec/server: an API token can no longer mint tokens, whatever its scopes (mapi_spec.tokens.TOKEN_NEVER). A child token dropped its parent's expiry, vCPU budget and rate limit, and outlived its revocation. POST /v1/tokens needs a signed-in session.
  • spec/server: score:<target> tokens can score. They authorized nothing, because :score checks run on the model and the scope covered only endpoints, so integrations fell back to broader runs:create tokens. score:<model id> now covers :score on that model and score:* on every model of the project (RouteAccess.name_param). The web tokens page, the CLI help and the docs say so.
  • server: concurrent uploads can no longer overrun the storage quota. Storage admission now locks the tenant row like run admission does, so six concurrent 800-byte intents against a 1000-byte quota admit exactly one.
  • server: abandoned upload intents no longer hold storage quota forever. Usage counts a pending intent only while its signed PUT is valid, and a new housekeeper loop in the worker (MAPI_HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_S, default 300 s) marks expired intents expired and deletes whatever reached quarantine.
  • server: expired browser sessions are deleted. The delete in load_session was rolled back with the request's 401, and nothing else removed web_sessions rows. The row is now deleted in its own transaction after the 401, and the housekeeper sweeps expired sessions and abandoned sign-ins.
  • server: a FINALIZING run no longer counts its vCPU estimate on top of its metered attempt. Quota usage counts an active run's estimate only while its current attempt has no actual ledger entry, so runs near a daily or monthly limit are not refused by mistake.
  • server: concurrent submissions from different tenants can no longer exceed a global concurrent_runs or vCPU limit. Run admission takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock after the tenant row when the global policy sets such a limit.
  • server: the global spend cap counts work in flight. The ledger only grows when runs finish, so every queued run used to be admitted and dispatched against the same figure. Admission now adds the estimates of admitted, unmetered runs, and the dispatcher adds the estimates of started runs and of each run it leases in the same pass.
  • server: held runs can no longer fill the dispatcher's window of queued runs and stall fair share for every tenant. Runs of suspended tenants, uploaded code paused by the kill switch and non-internal work past the spend cap are left out in SQL, and each tenant takes at most MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT (50) of the window.
  • server: a retry resumes from the newest checkpoints of any earlier attempt. Before, it only looked at the attempt just before it, so an attempt that died before its first segment threw away all earlier progress. Automatic infra retries are also capped by cost (MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR, default 2× the estimate), as plan §8.3 asks, and no longer by count alone.
  • server: an unknown token prefix and a wrong secret for a known prefix get the same answer (the API token is invalid), so the API no longer tells which prefixes exist. Unauthenticated failures that anyone can cause (token.auth_failed, auth.login_failed) are audited at most five times per token prefix or client and minute, so they can no longer flood a tenant's audit log. The housekeeper sweeps old rate counters.
  • server/web: run event streams re-check the caller's credential every MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S (60 s). A revoked token, an ended session or a lost membership no longer keeps receiving a 24-hour run's progress and logs: the stream closes and the reconnect is refused. The web client stops on 401 (and raises the session-expired prompt) or 403, where it used to retry forever.
  • server: the audit log and the cost ledger are append-only (migration 0004_append_only_records). Both runtime roles lose UPDATE and DELETE on them, and a trigger refuses any change to an existing row, so a request-path bug or injection can no longer rewrite a tenant's audit trail or billing history.
  • server/infra: the default data residency follows the deployment. It used to be us everywhere, so on the documented EU deployment every run of the platform tenant and of tenants created with defaults failed as INFRA_ERROR. MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY defaults to the multi-region of the Cloud Run region, and Terraform sets it from the dispatch pool's region (default_residency overrides it). It applies to the platform tenant, to rows the tenancy migration adopts and to POST /v1/admin/tenants without data_residency. Submissions that no reporting executor can place are refused at admission with a clear 403 instead of being queued, and the worker warns at start-up about such tenants.
  • server/infra: the API and events services no longer hold the RLS-bypassing database role, which plan §9 reserves for the dispatcher, reconciler and finalizer. Their platform lookups (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, routing pushed events) now run as a new mapi_gateway role (migration 0005_gateway_role, MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE). It has no BYPASSRLS, gets explicit policies on identity tables and column privileges on a few run and ledger metadata columns, and cannot read datasets, specs, models, plots, attempts, events or logs. Every API request uses it automatically. Pushed events are written through tenant sessions. Terraform adds the mapi_gateway login and its db-url-gateway secret, and only the orchestrator can read db-url-orchestrator.

docs.title: Fixed (M2 review: executors, cloud and infrastructure)
docs.text:
• infra: the deployed stack can run work at all. Terraform creates a create-only url-uploader account (MAPI_URL_UPLOADER), without which every run failed at dispatch; the server refuses MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs without a distinct uploader.
  • infra: checkpoint policies may overwrite their own checkpoints (conditional storage.objects.delete under .../checkpoints/ only), so PARTIAL bundles and resume see every segment on real GCS.
  • server: verified and public tenants are placed only on an executor with passing, unexpired conformance and security-suite reports for its current caps (PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence, MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S); the admin console, CLI and web show the real state. Runs that no executor can place are refused at submission (503) instead of failing at lease, and the docs say that verified tenants need DNS enforcement verified first.
  • server: docker-gvisor can qualify for shared tiers on a network declared isolated (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED).
  • server: Cloud Run 429s requeue a run without using up an infrastructure retry, leases are renewed while a batch is submitted (for at most ten lease lengths per submit), and Retry-After is capped. The executor's per-process bookkeeping is bounded.
  • sdk: zip artifacts (skops) are no longer rejected as pickles depending on the second they were written.
  • infra: user log and progress events are excluded from the exec projects' _Default log bucket; the API identity only reads the quarantine bucket.
  • deploy: the deploy workflow is valid (no runner context in job env; CI runs actionlint); rollback.sh --previous picks the release before the deployed one (records are named after their images, rollbacks are marked); dry runs no longer claim what they did not do.

docs.title: Fixed (M2 review: CLI, operations and docs)
docs.text:
• server: incident containment can now stop running tenant code. PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name} (audited executor.update, reason required; mapi admin executors disable|enable, a Disable button in Admin → Executors) disables an executor: orchestrators lease nothing onto it and their periodic reports no longer reset enabled to true. The kill-switch update takes cancel_untrusted_runs (with untrusted_execution_enabled=false; mapi admin kill-switches set --cancel-untrusted-runs, "Cancel running uploaded code" in the web app), which moves every unfinished run of uploaded code to cancelling. The sandbox-escape and incident-response runbooks use both.
  • ops: the jobs.run 429 alarm (plan §8.3) watches Cloud Run's 429s. The orchestrator exports mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total{executor} (every 429, retried ones included), and MapiJobsRun429 and the dashboard use it instead of the API's own 429s to tenants on POST /v1/runs. The Cloud Monitoring policy uses serviceruntime.googleapis.com/api/request_count (RunJob, response_code=429). Its old filter named a metric that Cloud Run jobs do not export, and it counted every 4xx.
  • ops: the plan's alert on running executions at 70 % of Cloud Run's 1,000 (§8.8) exists. The orchestrator's report exports mapi_executor_running_executions{executor} from the run table; MapiRunningExecutions70 and a Cloud Monitoring policy on run.googleapis.com/job/running_executions fire above 700.
  • infra: on GCP the mapi_* series reach Cloud Monitoring.
  • The orchestrator serves its own /metrics on 127.0.0.1:9464. Before, the dispatch, reconcile and finalize series had no endpoint in the cloud.
  • api, events and the orchestrator run a collector sidecar (metrics_collector_image, an OpenTelemetry Collector pinned by digest). It scrapes /metrics over loopback with the metrics bearer and writes to Managed Service for Prometheus.
  • Without an image Terraform warns that the alerts and dashboard stay empty.
  • The nightly security jobs push mapi_security_probe_unexpected to the Pushgateway at MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL.
  • gcp-deployment.md has a Metrics section.
  • server: rotating the local bundle-signing key no longer breaks every existing model. MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS lists retired keys (public or private PEM) that still verify. Terraform gains control.kms_trusted_key_versions (MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS on every server workload). The key-rotation runbook now gives the real local and Cloud KMS procedures and the compromise path. It no longer tells GCP operators to rotate a Pub/Sub "internal token": pushes there are OIDC-authenticated.
  • docs: data residency is enforced only on executors that declare regions (Cloud Run Jobs). The self-hosted executors are not checked, and the tenancy page now says so instead of promising a region match everywhere.
  • server: MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS restricts an orchestrator to some trust tiers. Two orchestrators serving different exec pools can no longer lease each other's runs (leasing was not pool-aware, so public-tier code could land in the paid pool). gcp-deployment.md no longer suggests a second orchestrator without it, and says that one environment deploys one pool until M5.
  • ops: three Prometheus rule fixes.
  • MapiQuota70 is now MapiQuotaRejections. It fires on rejections, not at 70 %, and it aggregates by (scope), so its summary names the scope.
  • MapiNoProgressIngested also fires when no event was ever accepted (or vector(0)).
  • Clearing the spend cap now resets mapi_global_spend_micros and mapi_global_spend_cap_micros to 0, both at once and at every admission. The spend ratio ignores a cap of 0, so MapiGlobalSpendCap90 stops firing.
  • cli: mapi logout --revoke revokes the token in the project it is bound to (it was refused with 403 when another project was selected) and forgets the local credentials even when the revocation fails, then exits 1.
  • security: the report writers create their directory, so make security-suite (and both nightly security jobs) no longer fail on a fresh checkout without .local/.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• server: two review branches each added a database role for the API without the row-level-security bypass. One is kept (0005_gateway_role, column-level grants, used for every API request); MAPI_DB_PLATFORM from the other is gone. The executor-disable migration is renumbered 0006_executor_disable and lets the gateway change an executor's enabled and disabled_reason.
  • server: an executor's enabled flag belongs to operators. Missing shared-tier evidence no longer turns it off; it shows in shared_tiers_enabled and the executor's message.
  • server: a submission that no executor can place gets one answer per cause. A residency or resource class no executor serves is refused with 403. A trust tier that no executor can take yet (enforcement not verified, no suite evidence) gets 503.
  • server: as the gateway role, the kill switch's cancel_untrusted_runs cancels each tenant's runs in a session of that tenant. The operators' usage report can read the ledger columns it sums.
  • tests: the end-to-end spend-cap drills use a self-hosted-trusted tenant, which the local executor can still place.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• Nothing has run against real Google Cloud. The Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, KMS and Cloud SQL code paths, the IAM conditions, the logging exclusion, the metrics collector sidecar and the Cloud Monitoring filters are checked with fakes and mocked providers only.
  • No job posts the nightly conformance and security-suite results to the evidence endpoint yet. Until an operator records them (and the M0 DNS check passes), verified and public tenants cannot run on any executor.
  • There is no endpoint to disable a user account. disabled is set in the database, and sign-in keeps it.
  • The gateway role still reads some tables across tenants for the operator console, quota counters and sign-in.
  • A live log tail polls the logs endpoint instead of using the run's event stream.
  • The API's built-in /docs and /redoc pages load assets from a public CDN.

docs.title: [0.2.0] — M1: local vertical slice — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
The platform now runs end to end on one machine. From the Expert web app (or the CLI, the Python client or plain HTTP) you can upload data, write and validate a spec, fit an E33-style hierarchical geo MMM, inspect it, and score it: an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals. Real Cloud Run and multi-tenancy come in M2 (v0.3.0). In summary:

  • server (mapi-server): a single-tenant FastAPI control plane on PostgreSQL with procrastinate. It includes a dispatcher, a level-triggered reconciler, a metadata-only finalizer with signed bundle manifests, HMAC-verified run events, SSE with resume, and local-process and docker executors. It never imports plugin code or array libraries.
  • runner (mapi-runner): a trusted supervisor and an untrusted worker harness for ingest, describe, validate, fit, score, evaluate, derive and render runs. It produces signed events, checkpoints, partial manifests and the ui/ views the web app reads.
  • gcs-shim (mapi-gcs-shim): a local Cloud Storage emulator. It provides generations, server-side CRC32C/MD5, V4 signed URLs and POST policies, per-principal permissions and a write-once bundles bucket.
  • web and plot-sandbox: the Expert web app (YAML editor with live validation, runs with live progress and logs, model inspection, scoring) and a separate-origin, CSP-locked plot renderer.
  • client and cli: a typed sync/async Python client for every v1 endpoint, and mapi for local and remote work.
  • devops: make dev (the whole stack without Docker), digest-pinned images, docker compose, make seed, make e2e and make release-check.
  • conformance: the corpus also runs through the live stack (run --stack URL), and a sklearn conformal fixture is added (7 fixtures in all).
  • docs: a 10-minute quickstart, guides to the web app, CLI, client and HTTP API, a deployment section, an architecture overview and a security model.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.2.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• spec: the M1 shared contracts, so the API, runner, executors, GCS shim, web app and plot sandbox can be built in parallel against one source of truth:
