  • mapi_spec.run: the run state machine (RunState, RunTrigger, a pure transition() with owners, failure classes and attempt bumps), the RunSpec bootstrap object, typed event payloads, canonical HMAC-SHA256 event signing, the {"mapi_event": …} stdout format, OutputManifest with metadata-only verification, the signed BundleManifest, RunnerEnv and exit codes.
  • mapi_spec.storage: ObjectMeta, the async ObjectStore protocol, signed GET/PUT and POST policy shapes, GCS-style CRC32C/MD5 helpers, storage errors and the bucket/key naming scheme.
  • mapi_spec.api: REST DTOs for the v1 surface (each with examples), SSE/Prefer/idempotency helpers and M1_ENDPOINTS, the machine-readable endpoint table.
  • mapi_spec.localdev: local ports, origins and environment variable names.
  • spec (additive, contract v0.1): RunKind gains the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign); RunEventType gains checkpoint and metric; RunEvent.ts must be timezone-aware and is normalised to UTC; PlotSpec carries a schema example. The new schemas join export_schemas() and the contract snapshot.
  • docs: the "HTTP API (v1)" and "Run protocol" reference pages (docs/reference/http-api.md, docs/reference/run-protocol.md).
  • gcs-shim: mapi-gcs-shim, a local Cloud Storage emulator. It serves the GCS JSON-API subset the platform uses, with generation and metageneration preconditions, plus V4 signed GET (with Range) and PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix and size range). It adds IAM-lite principals (control, and exec with bootstrap get and delete only), a write-once bundles bucket, lifecycle sweeps, and server-computed CRC32C and MD5 on a crash-safe filesystem backend. ShimObjectStore and the import-guarded GcsObjectStore implement mapi_spec.storage.ObjectStore, and a pytest11 plugin provides the gcs_shim fixture. See docs/reference/gcs-shim.md.
  • runner: mapi-runner, the sandboxed run harness. A trusted supervisor reads and deletes the bootstrap object, starts the untrusted worker with a scrubbed environment (uid 10001 and no-new-privs as root, dev mode otherwise), signs every stdout event, caps logs, events, scratch and outputs, handles SIGTERM/deadline with partial manifests from checkpoints, and uploads outputs plus a signed OutputManifest. The worker runs ingest (CSV/Parquet with a column mapping or the MFF preset, zarr zip, netCDF), describe, validate (dry run), fit (bundle, sidecars, plots, ui/ views, checkpoints), score, evaluate, derive and render through the SDK harness. See docs/reference/runner.md.
  • server: the M1 control plane (mapi-server api|worker|migrate|dev): FastAPI /v1 API covering every M1_ENDPOINTS row plus /v1/me, spec diff, ui/ redirects and :evaluate; SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic schema (every row carries tenant_id/project_id) with procrastinate on the same Postgres; dispatcher (token bucket, intent row before submit), level-triggered reconciler (executor status is the liveness source of truth, STALLED is a warning, orphan adoption by nonce), metadata-only finalizer with server-side copy and EC P-256 signed bundle manifests verified at URL minting; HMAC-verified event ingestion from the executor pipe and POST /internal/events; SSE with Last-Event-ID resume over one LISTEN connection per process; local-process and docker/docker-gvisor executors; OpenAPI 3.1 export (python -m mapi_server.openapi).
  • web: apps/web, the Expert-mode web app (React 19, TanStack Router/Query/Table, Tailwind + shadcn/ui, Monaco + monaco-yaml with live :validate diagnostics, SSE run progress per chain, dataset upload via signed URLs, model inspection, scoring) and the Guided-mode shell; a pnpm workspace at the repo root.
  • plot-sandbox: apps/plot-sandbox, the separate-origin Vega-Lite/Plotly renderer with a strict CSP and a validated postMessage protocol.
  • devops: containers, local orchestration and developer tooling for M1:
  • images/: base-bayes (with a worker target), base-ml (no PyMC), base-forecast, server (control plane only, checked with import-linter and package assertions at build time), gcs-shim and web (nginx serving the app and the plot sandbox on separate origins with strict CSPs). All are digest-pinned, run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, and have health checks. The runner images bake the catalog JSON and a warmed PyTensor/Numba cache.
  • docker-compose.yml (postgres 16, gcs-shim, migrate, api, worker with the local-process executor, web, plot-sandbox), compose.override.example.yml and .env.example, which documents every MAPI_* variable.
  • scripts/dev.py (make dev): runs the whole stack without Docker (pgserver PostgreSQL, GCS shim, migrations, api, worker and both Vite servers) with readiness probes, prefixed logs and clean process-group shutdown. Also stop, status, migrate, db-shell and clean.
  • New make targets: dev/run, stop, status, migrate, db-shell, seed (the E33 demo through the API), clean-local, docker-build, docker-pin, compose-up/down/logs, web-build, web-test, test-all, e2e and release-check.
  • CI: a web job, a build-only docker job for every image, and digest-pin and compose checks.
  • Docs: "Local development" and "Containers and docker compose" (Operations), and deploy/README.md.
  • client: mapi-client, the typed Python client (Client, AsyncClient) for every M1_ENDPOINTS row: DTO-typed resources, RFC 7807 errors as MapiError subclasses, idempotency keys and safe retries, lazy pagination, SSE with Last-Event-ID resume, dataset upload through signed URLs, Prefer: wait scoring, CRC32C-checked transfers without the API token. See docs/reference/cli.md.
  • cli: mapi (new, check, fit, score locally or --remote, runs, datasets, catalog, plugin init|test, spec upgrade, serve, config), with --json output and ANSI-stripped untrusted text.
  • spec: mapi_spec.jobs, the run job contract shared by the dispatcher and the runner (IngestJob, DescribeJob, ScoreJob, EvaluateJob, DeriveJob, RenderJob, input and output object names, MetricsSidecar, DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR), and mapi_spec.views, the UI views the web app reads (mapi.preview/v1, mapi.profile/v1, mapi.tree-index/v1).
  • gcs-shim: CORS for the web origin (--cors-origin, default $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) so browsers can use signed URLs, and a wrap hook on ShimServer.
  • server: mapi-server dev (and so mapi serve) starts an embedded GCS shim when nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; the OpenAPI document publishes the run-event payload schemas.
  • docs: "CLI and Python client" and "Web app and plot sandbox" reference pages; the run protocol documents job payloads, object names and UI views.
  • server: GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots (list_run_plots) returns the plots a succeeded run rendered, sanitized on every read; the client has runs.plots().
  • web: the score form takes the input dataset and the spec's side tables (defaulting to the versions the fit used), shows the score run's own plots and pivots the summary by statistic.
  • devops: scripts/seed.py --export DIR writes the E33 demo tables, score payloads and spec as files for the web app.
  • tests: the M1 exit criterion end to end against the running stack: tests/e2e (Python client: fit, SSE, signed manifest and bundle generations, the bundle read back with the corpus' checks, five E33 score requests, bootstrap deletion, forged events) and apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts (the same flow in the browser, plots in the sandbox iframe); a server test proves the finalizer refuses tampered output of the real runner.
  • docs: "Your first model in the web app" guide; the local-development page covers the first start, make e2e and the state under .local/.
  • docs: the M1 documentation set. A landing page with screenshots of the running platform (docs/assets/screenshots/, captured by scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs and shrunk by scripts/optimise_screenshots.py, make docs-screenshots); a validated "zero to first model in 10 minutes" quickstart; guides to every page of the Expert web app, the CLI, the Python client and the HTTP API; an OpenAPI explorer page (a vendored, hash-pinned Redoc bundle over the committed openapi.json, scripts/vendor_redoc.py); a Deployment section (local, Docker Compose, container images, a configuration reference naming every MAPI_* variable, troubleshooting); an architecture overview and a security model; an updated roadmap (M2 cloud and multi-tenant, M3 Guided mode). scripts/gen_docs_reference.py (run by make docs-build and the MkDocs hook) generates the CLI reference from the Typer app, the server settings table from Settings, and copies the OpenAPI document. conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py runs the CLI walkthrough, checks the generated pages, the configuration reference, the Redoc pin and the screenshots, and (under make e2e) runs the client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs against the live stack.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• docs: anchors are validated in strict builds; mermaid is pinned to 11.17.2 instead of Material's moving mermaid@11.
  • server: the object store is ShimObjectStore built from the shim's control key file (MAPI_GCS_ROOT, default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs, or MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE); local executions get the exec token from the same directory unless MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN is set. RunSpec payloads and input names follow mapi_spec.jobs (score data under dataset, side tables under side.<name>, bundle.manifest passed to score runs); evaluate/derive default to the fit dataset and render gets the bundle's plots.json. metrics.json is read as MetricsSidecar.
  • runner: fit writes coords.json and ingest writes summary.json (the control plane's CoordPlan metadata); preview.json, profile.json and ui/tree_index.json follow mapi_spec.views. The runner tests run against the real GCS shim.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are generated from the real server (apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py, checked in CI); the @e2e specs can reuse a running stack on any ports.
  • devops: make dev starts mapi-gcs-shim serve --root … with CORS and passes the resolved URLs to the Vite servers; compose mounts the shim volume read-only into api and worker (MAPI_GCS_ROOT) so they can load the principal keys.
  • sdk: zarr zips record their data-variable order (group attribute _mapi_var_order, removed again on read).
  • devops: make e2e runs the browser @e2e suite (it ran the mocked smoke suite).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• spec: static score validation binds dataset names to canonical names at every inputs_stage, as the runtime does (a weekly EUR plan entering at weekly was refused).
  • server: the dry-run and evaluate endpoints declare their Run response in OpenAPI.
  • seed: make seed ships E33's raw schema with the data, so the fit keeps market: new_levels and new-market scoring works.
  • client: the run event stream decodes the live progress and log frames (sent without an id) as RunLiveFrame; it aborted on the first progress frame of a real fit.
  • server: model lineage records the side-table versions a fit read (it was always empty).
  • sdk: variables come back from a zarr zip in their written order; plot recipes that default to the first variable chose a random one on a bundle read back from storage (mmm.response_curves failed). The response-curve recipe also prefers variables with a channel dim.
  • plot-sandbox: composite Vega-Lite specs (concat, facet) rendered at zero width; they now keep their own size and scroll when wider than the frame.
  • plots: the convergence table's columns no longer overlap; the fan chart draws and captions only the intervals a summary holds.
  • web: a spec opened right after "Save spec" no longer shows unsaved changes (the editor used CRLF for models created empty on Windows user agents), so Fit is enabled; the run page's result column no longer overflows; result tables show dates as dates.
  • devops: make seed ignores a SIZE exported by other toolchains (conda).
  • devops: the compose api and worker containers start. The mapi/server and mapi/worker images bake uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH, so both resolve the same image digest. Before, neither could resolve one and both failed at start-up.
  • devops: compose keeps the bundle-signing key on a keys volume that migrate writes and api/worker mount read-only (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false). Each container used to mint its own key on its tmpfs, so the API rejected every bundle the worker signed, and a restart orphaned every model. mapi-server migrate now creates the key, and concurrent first starts converge on one key.
  • server: mapi-server api|worker|dev make themselves non-dumpable on Linux, so local-process runs (same uid) cannot read their environment or memory. The worker's start-up warning and the operations docs state what such runs can still read.
  • server: a Prefer: wait long-poll stops waiting when its client disconnects.
  • client: models.score() extends the read timeout of each long-poll by its wait and treats a read timeout as "still running", so scores slower than about 90 s no longer raise TransportError. stream_events() counts only connections that deliver nothing towards max_reconnects, so it follows long fits behind proxies that cut connections.
  • cli: run progress and state messages are never parsed as rich markup (no terminal hyperlink injection, no MarkupError aborting mapi fit).
  • devops: .env.example documents every mapi-server setting, and the devops test now derives the list from Settings.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: spec, runner, shim and plots)
docs.text:
• runner: fit runs write ui/preprocess.json (mapi_spec.views.PreprocessView, mapi.preprocess/v1): each step's resolved plugin, learned JSON and small numeric state arrays, so the web app's Preprocessing tab is no longer empty.
  • runner: an INFRA_ERROR reported by the worker fails the run as a user error. Only failures the supervisor sees itself are retried automatically as infrastructure failures.
  • runner: every string the worker sends has ANSI, control and bidi characters stripped. The CLI's strip_control also removes the bidi ranges.
  • server, gcs-shim: the artifacts upload policy is create-only (post_policy(create_only=True) signs x-goog-if-generation-match: 0, and the shim answers 412 for an existing key).
  • plots: recipes draw from mapi_plots.palette, whose dark variants keep at least 3:1 contrast, and the plot sandbox swaps them in dark mode. The decomposition legend is titled "component" when baseline or controls join the channels. Faceted fans and MMM curves give each panel its own axes, in coordinate order.
  • conformance: new sklearn_store_demand fixture. Fixtures not yet ported are listed in DEFERRED with reasons (list --deferred). run --stack URL drives fixtures through the API.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: server)
docs.text:
• GET /v1/runs/{id}/plots and score results are scoped to the caller's tenant and project.
  • Runner JSON is parsed with a nesting limit, and deep nesting is reported as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Bundle inputs are verified again at dispatch and on :retry.
  • The API refuses unexpected Host headers (MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS), nginx answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES and the GCS shim checks hosts too, which guards against DNS rebinding.
  • Ingest and spec validation enforce the per-resource-class data caps (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE).
  • An omitted fit seed is pinned to 0 at submission, so lineage records the seed actually used.
  • Run lifecycle:
  • A cancelled checkpointed fit ends PARTIAL and can be resumed (new CANCELLING --complete--> FINALIZING edge).
  • :cancel on a finalizing run is a no-op.
  • A run stopped at its deadline fails as TIMEOUT or finalizes as PARTIAL.
  • An exit counts only after its event backlog is ingested.
  • A restarted reconciler re-adopts live executions.
  • Stalled finalize jobs are re-queued.
  • Executor cancels no longer block the reconcile pass.
  • SSE reads the run state before its events, and a run never shows another attempt's progress.
  • Docker executor:
  • Each plugin namespace gets its own versioned mapi/base-* image (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES).
  • Run containers join the shim's network namespace; none is refused.
  • The supervisor and the worker run under separate uids (10001 for the worker), and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1 fails a run closed rather than falling back to dev mode.
  • The import-linter contract also forbids plugin packages, plot recipes and columnar libraries in mapi_server.
  • Docs: invalid submissions are refused without a run, and REJECTED is reserved.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: web)
docs.text:
• Plots:
  • The plot host accepts a sandbox exported reply only for an export the app requested.
  • Downloading a score output saves a checksum-verified file instead of leaving the app.
  • Run pages:
  • Live progress and log SSE frames, which the server sends without an id, are delivered.
  • The live log view follows the tail.
  • Performance: Monaco and Arrow are no longer in first paint, and routes are lazy-loaded. A build-time budget keeps first-paint JavaScript under 640 KiB (it was 4.26 MB; now about 515 KB).
  • Spec editor:
  • It never replaces unsaved edits when a newer revision appears.
  • Save sends the revision the text came from as parent_revision.
  • Accessibility:
  • No sideways scroll at phone width, and the compact nav shows every page.
  • Status colours and form borders meet WCAG AA.
  • Score form errors are marked on their fields and announced.
  • The Score page resets its form and results when the version changes, and shows a loading state while the version loads.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• tests: a devops docstring no longer names a fake MAPI_ variable that the configuration reference test picked up.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are regenerated (the cancel endpoint documents the finalizing no-op).
  • docs: pages written before the review fixes landed now describe the shared compose signing key, ui/preprocess.json, the docker executor's network and images, and the new MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS, MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES, MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION settings.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The docker executor, the compose stack and the new compose smoke test have not run against a real Docker daemon yet.
  • Under the local-process executor, run code shares the orchestrator's uid and can read its key files. The uid split is M2.
  • MAPI_PROFILE means a config profile to the CLI and client, but the deployment profile to the server.
  • The API's built-in /docs and /redoc pages load assets from a public CDN.
  • Conformance fixtures E13, E84-lite, E82-slim and E45 are deferred: they need new plugins or run kinds.

docs.title: [0.1.0] — M0: contract layer — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
First milestone release: the typed contract layer and the in-process xarray runtime, with no platform services yet. In summary:

  • spec (mapi-spec): pure-Pydantic contracts (DataSchema, SchemaEffect, ModelSpec, ScoreRequest, capabilities, representations, PlotSpec envelope, error codes) with static validation and JSON Schema export, frozen as contract v0.1.
  • sdk (mapi-sdk): wire formats, the stage/split/context/replay/inverse pipeline engine, CoordPlan, bundles without pickle, the fit_spec/score_bundle harness, the in-process executor and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit.
  • steps (mapi-steps): 28 built-in core.* preprocessing steps and five split kinds, each with exported static effects.
  • pymc (mapi-pymc) and sklearn (mapi-sklearn): model adapters where an author writes only build() or estimator().
  • plots (mapi-plots): JSON-only Vega-Lite/Plotly sanitizer and the core, mmm and ml recipe catalogs.
  • plugins: mmm.hierarchical_geo, mmm.pymc_marketing, ts.hsgp_trend, ts.gaussian_hmm, tabular.hierarchical_glm and tabular.regressor.
  • conformance (mapi-conformance): the corpus runner and six fixtures (E02, C08, E24, store demand, E33, pymc-marketing), all passing at --size tiny.
  • docs: the MkDocs Material site with tested snippets and generated catalogs.

Every workspace package is versioned 0.1.0. The server, runner, CLI, client and GCS shim packages are still skeletons.

  • Repository scaffold: uv workspace, package skeletons, split Apache-2.0 / AGPLv3+commercial licensing.

docs.title: Contract v0.1 (frozen)
docs.text:
• mapi_spec.CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.1" names the contract the exported JSON Schemas describe; every exported schema carries it as x-mapi-contract-version.
  • The contract is frozen for the v0.1.x line: packages/spec/tests/snapshots/contract.json pins a digest of every exported schema and the drift test fails on any change. Additive changes (new optional fields, new error codes) regenerate the snapshot (MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1); breaking changes bump CONTRACT_VERSION first.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mapi-spec: the pure-Pydantic contract layer.
  • DataSchema, DimSpec and VarSpec, with schema templates.
  • SchemaEffect propagation; ModelSpec, ScoreRequest and the Sweep, Backtest, SBC and Campaign wrappers.
  • A strict YAML 1.2 loader, canonical JSON and spec hashes.
  • Static validation: split stage, LEAKAGE_RISK, dim policies, recursion and the CoordPlan checks.
  • Capabilities, representation rules, the PlotSpec envelope, stable RFC 7807 error codes, the Executor protocol shapes, JSON Schema export and the mapi-spec CLI.
  • mapi-sdk: the xarray runtime.
  • Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips and Arrow IPC.
  • Array-level schema validation; the step contract, pipeline engine and stages.
  • Split and per-group context replay; inverse chains with output-space labels.
  • CoordPlan and coordinate canonicalisation, the representation-aware summariser and metrics.
  • Bundle IO with integrity sidecars and no pickle; the fit_spec/score_bundle harness with evaluate_then_refit.
  • The entry-point registry, the in-process executor, and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit (check_step, check_model, pytest plugin).
  • mapi-steps: 28 built-in core.* steps (reshape, value, feature, formula, adstock and saturation).
  • Each exports a templated SchemaEffect and a shipped catalog JSON.
  • Catalog entries for the five split kinds.
  • mapi-pymc: PyMCModel, where an author writes only build().
  • BuildContext with hier_effect new levels.
  • Engines: nutpie, pymc, MAP and ADVI, plus guarded numpyro, blackjax and pathfinder.
  • Segmented, resumable sampling with checkpoints; CRN counterfactuals.
  • Convergence diagnostics, FrozenPredictor fast scoring and check_fast_score.
  • mapi-sklearn: SklearnModel with an allow-listed estimator registry (sklearn and xgboost).
  • skops and xgboost-JSON persistence.
  • Point, quantile, bootstrap, conformal and classifier plugins (sklearn.tabular_*).
  • Pooled new levels; exact or zeroing contributions.
  • mapi-plots: a JSON-only PlotSpec sanitizer (pinned Vega-Lite 6.4.1 and plotly.js 4.1.1 schemas, an expression allow-list, HTML stripping) and role-bound templates.
  • The standard core.* recipe catalog, plus the mmm.* and ml.* domain packs.
  • Altair and Plotly converters with named Arrow datasets, and the render_plots batch entry point.
  • mapi-plugin-mmm: marketing-mix model plugins (entry point mapi.models: mmm).
  • mmm.hierarchical_geo 1.3.0, the E33 hierarchical geo MMM: adstock over core.lag_tensor features, logistic/Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, new geos from the hyperprior, additive contributions.
  • Fit-cached derived quantities in original units: contributions, per-draw response-curve grids for Guided sliders, marginal cost/ROI; a decision objective for budgets; fast scoring.
  • mmm.pymc_marketing 1.0.0, an adapter around pymc-marketing 1.2's MMM (verified on PyMC 6.3) that owns scaling, carry-over and units and never pickles.
  • Declarative priors in pymc-marketing's dict form, typed per parameter so wrong priors fail static validation; a synthetic E33 simulator with known parameters and a parameter-recovery test.
  • mapi-sdk: outputs.derived with cache: fit is computed on the production fit through the plugin's derive hook; ScoreContext.to_original maps model-stage arrays to the output space.
  • Cross-package conformance suites:
  • the plan's xgboost spec through real steps, models and plots;
  • an E33-shaped core.* pipeline in front of a PyMC model.
  • mapi-plugin-ts: ts.hsgp_trend (C08: HSGP trend + seasonality whose domain comes from the anticipated coords; HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT past max_extension; sentinel months left out of the likelihood) and ts.gaussian_hmm (E24: forward-algorithm HMM over padded tracks with a terminal_state group, forecast and filter modes, relabelling postprocess, LOO declared invalid).
  • mapi-plugin-tabular: tabular.hierarchical_glm (E02: partially pooled GLM in long layout, hyperprior new groups, group-level covariates, four families) and tabular.regressor (plan §6.2 store demand: quantile regression restricted to the registry's quantile-capable estimators).
  • mapi-conformance: the corpus runner python -m mapi_conformance run [--size tiny|full] [--fixture id] (validate, fit, score requests, evaluate, contract kit, plots, expectations; summary table and JSON) with the e02, c08, e24, xgb_store_demand, e33 and pymc_marketing fixtures; pytest -m conformance, make conformance (tiny) and make conformance-full.
  • Score cases can opt out of side tables (side_tables: false, e.g. a weekly EUR plan entering after the FX step).
  • Expectation hooks that declare ctx receive a FixtureContext (seed, size, registry, side tables and earlier score results).
  • Docs: spec format, SDK, built-in steps and plots references; guides for plugins, PyMC, tabular models and plots.
  • Docs: built-in models reference, marketing-mix models guide, forecasting and sequential models guide, conformance corpus guide.
  • Docs: the MkDocs Material site.
  • A landing page, getting started (install, first model, runs and executors), concepts (labelled data, pipelines and stages, representations, bundles, coord plans, capabilities), the "port a model in 15 minutes" guide, licensing, contributing and roadmap pages for v0.2–v0.4.
  • Generated reference pages: steps, models and plot-recipe catalogs, the ModelSpec/ScoreRequest schema and error codes (scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py, run by an MkDocs hook and make docs-catalog); API reference via mkdocstrings.
  • Every Python example lives in docs/snippets/ and is executed by conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py (make docs-test).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The workspace runs numpy 2.4 (pymc-marketing 1.2 requires numpy < 2.5).
  • make typecheck also covers plugins/mmm, plugins/ts, plugins/tabular and conformance.
  • Score requests that name a pinned side table now fail validation. Score outputs along time and extend dims come back sorted. validate_spec emits an INFO issue when the model's target role overrides a declared role.
  • Plugin-raised error text now appears in untrusted_text, not in detail.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• The plan's xgboost example names the real quantile plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles). A new ml.feature_importance recipe covers its plot list.
  • core.fit_vs_actual and core.residuals_over_time compare quantile and interval summaries cell by cell instead of refusing them.
  • The contract kit flags step settings whose defaults are missing from the exported JSON Schema (default_factory), and finds reverse-bound outputs when checking units.
  • Holdout metrics no longer invert the predictions of models that own inverse_units a second time.
  • Score outputs that declare their own units (e.g. state probabilities) no longer go through the target's inverse transforms.
  • The contract kit runs its shuffled, subset and new-level checks on long layouts (index variables are remapped) and shifts calendar-frequency time coords by whole periods.
  • The in-process executor no longer resolves a score request's side-table refs when the run payload already supplies those tables.
  • The contract kit's score requests name the spec's score_policy: supplied side tables, so models with supplied tables (E33's FX) pass the scoring checks.
  • The E33 and pymc-marketing fixtures use the corpus runner's fixture layout and run in python -m mapi_conformance run.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: spec and SDK)
docs.text:
• Counterfactuals: score_bundle takes a baseline data payload and a separate scenario payload, and scores the scenario's interventions against the baseline. A scenario without baseline data, or a named scenario that was not supplied, is SCHEMA_INVALID.
  • owns is enforced: catalog steps declare provides (scaling, carryover), and validate_spec rejects such a step on the target, media or spend variables of a model that owns that preprocessing (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • Target dependence follows the model template's target roles, even with an inferred raw schema, so RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED fires reliably. The recursion and future-covariate checks measure how far the payload extends past the fit, not only horizon.
  • No target leakage into evaluation lags for dynamic or cell-level splits. as_of gap periods stay in the holdout with masked targets and are excluded from metrics.
  • Pinned side tables always replay the fit-time version; a request that names one fails with SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE.
  • Score payloads are sorted along ordered/extend dims before the pipeline; duplicate labels are COORD_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • Chained look-back steps (adstock then lag) replay with fit-time history. A score window that starts inside the fitted range and loses look-back history gets a WARNING.
  • Long-layout per-group context works end to end.
  • Inverses: steps declare additive inverses, and decompositions along component only go through additive steps (otherwise they stay at the blocking stage, with a WARNING). Smearing residuals come only from target-shaped outputs. The moments sd uses the delta method.
  • Model-owned outputs are labelled per variable with their units and output_space.
  • Derived quantities named in output.vars come back from the fit cache. An uncached one is refused.
  • PyMC CRN counterfactuals give identical draws in untouched cells for Poisson, negative binomial and binomial likelihoods (crn_ppf).
  • Wire and bundle hardening: XrJSON budgets decoded bytes (max_decoded_bytes), caps declared dim sizes and accepts only ISO-8601 dates. Zarr-zip decoding is bounded by declared shapes, string lengths and an expansion ratio. Pickle is detected by opcode stream, in object .npy and inside archives. The evaluation sub-bundle is verified and never kept stale. Entry points can no longer replace registered or built-in plugin ids.
  • Spec parsing rejects non-finite floats and reports oversized JSON integers as SpecParseError.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: models and steps)
docs.text:
• core.formula: scalar ~ is logical not; overflow and division by zero give inf/nan, and other arithmetic errors are reported as SCHEMA_INVALID rather than escaping.
  • PyMC checkpoints: the codec rebuilds only classes defined in PyMC step-method modules (plus pymc.util and mapi_pymc), at exactly the encoded module:qualname.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: plots, conformance and tooling)
docs.text:
• Plot sanitizer (Plotly): updatemenus/sliders method args are checked in the positional [attr, value] form and inside nested frame/trace objects, so external image sources, href/url paths, tile-map subplots and tile-map trace types can no longer hide there.
  • Plot sanitizer (Vega-Lite): select.toggle strings and bind.legend event filters are checked as expressions, event['view'] is rejected like event.view, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected.
  • from_plotly strips HTML from (and scans) the strings it moves into Arrow datasets, which the JSON sanitizer never decodes.
  • Plugin-originated error text stays out of trusted fields: render_plots and the step/model wrappers (Pipeline, harness fit/score/derive) move a plugin MapiError's detail into untrusted_text and keep its code only when plugin code may raise it (mapi_spec.errors.from_plugin_error, PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES).
  • Contract kit, check_step: effect_matches_output also compares each dim's kind and frequency and each variable's units; the toy FX and scale steps now set the units they declare.
  • Contract kit, check_model: new horizon_exceeds_fit, missing_future_covariate, recursive_unsupported, fast_score_matches_exact (plugin check_fast_score hook, provided by PyMCModel), plots_sanitize and outputs_match_manifest checks; extend_typed_errors covers integer extend dims; output_space_and_units covers outputs that inherit the target implicitly.
  • OutputDecl.dims_of (additive) lets a manifest declare settings-dependent data dims; the sklearn models (and so tabular.regressor) and mmm.pymc_marketing use it, so their static output dims match what score returns.

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
We use git flow with two long-lived branches, main and develop.

gitGraph
    commit id: "v0.1.0" tag: "v0.1.0"
    branch develop
    checkout develop
    commit id: "integration"
    branch feat/m1-runner
    checkout feat/m1-runner
    commit id: "feat(runner): …"
    commit id: "test(runner): …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-runner
    branch feat/m1-docs
    checkout feat/m1-docs
    commit id: "docs: …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-docs
    checkout main
    merge develop tag: "v0.2.0"
Branch Purpose main Releases only. Each milestone is merged from develop and tagged vX.Y.Z. Nobody commits to main directly. develop Integration. Feature branches are merged here with --no-ff. feat/<milestone>-<topic> One unit of work, branched from the latest develop. 
git checkout -B feat/m1-my-change develop
# ... small, logical commits ...
make fmt lint typecheck test

Never rebase or rewrite develop or main. Keep changes to shared files (the root pyproject.toml, the Makefile, uv.lock, CI) minimal and additive, and mention them in your pull request.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Conventional commits, scoped by package:

feat(sdk): replay context tails at each step's input stage
fix(server): reject score requests whose horizon exceeds the fit
docs: add the porting guide
test(conformance): add the e24 filter fixture
chore: bump ruff

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Python 3.12, ruff (line length 100), type hints everywhere; mypy strict for the core packages.
  • Tests live next to each package in tests/. PyMC fits in tests use tiny settings (tune: 50–150, draws: 50–150, chains: 2) and are marked slow when they take more than about ten seconds.
  • Docstrings are concise (Google style). The contract tests are the executable documentation.
  • mapi_spec must not import numpy, xarray or pandas; the server must not import plugin or array code. make lint enforces both.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is MkDocs Material (mkdocs.yml at the repository root, pages in docs/).

  • Every Python example is executed. Examples live in docs/snippets/*.py, are included in pages with --8<-- "file.py:section", and conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py runs each
  • Platform examples run against a live stack. The client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs (docs/snippets/client_tour.py, http_tour.sh, cli_remote.sh) run under make e2e; the local CLI walkthrough (cli_local.sh) runs in the default suite (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py). Shell snippets use the same section markers.
  • Reference pages are generated. scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py writes the steps, models, plot recipes, spec schema and error-code pages, and scripts/gen_docs_reference.py the CLI reference, the server settings and a copy of apps/web/openapi.json, into docs/reference/generated/ (git-ignored); an MkDocs hook runs both before every build.
  • New MAPI_* variables go into the configuration reference (docs/operations/configuration.md); a test scans the source tree for them.
  • Screenshots live in docs/assets/screenshots/ (at most 300 KB each, each used by a page). make docs-screenshots recaptures them from a running, seeded stack.
  • make docs-build must pass (mkdocs build --strict, with anchor validation).
  • Write for two readers: an analyst who wants to know what a feature does for them, and a data scientist who wants to know exactly how it works.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
modeling-api uses a split licence. People who write models and integrations are never pulled into copyleft; the hosted platform itself is protected.

Component Where Licence SDK and contracts: mapi-spec, mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc, mapi-sklearn packages/spec, packages/sdk, packages/sdk-pymc, packages/sdk-sklearn Apache-2.0 Built-ins: steps, plots, model plugins, conformance corpus packages/steps-core, packages/plots-core, plugins/*, conformance/ Apache-2.0 Tools: CLI, Python client, GCS emulator packages/cli, packages/client, packages/gcs-shim Apache-2.0 Platform: API server, run harness, web apps, images, infrastructure packages/server, packages/runner, apps/*, images/, infra/, ops/, security/ AGPLv3 or a commercial licence Documentation docs/ CC BY 4.0

Each package declares its SPDX expression in its pyproject.toml (Apache-2.0, or AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-mapi-commercial) and carries its own LICENSE file. The full texts are in the repository root: LICENSE.md, LICENSE-APACHE.txt, LICENSE-AGPL.txt and COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md.

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text:
Plugins you write are yours

A step, model or plot recipe written against mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc or mapi-sklearn uses Apache-2.0 libraries. License it however you like, including proprietary.

Applications that call the platform are not derivative works

Calling the platform over HTTP, with the Python or TypeScript client, through webhooks or MCP, does not make your application subject to the AGPL.

Modifying and hosting the platform

If you modify the platform components (server, runner, apps) and offer them as a network service, the AGPLv3 requires you to publish your modifications, unless you hold a commercial licence. Contact mattreda@mattreda.pro for commercial terms.

docs.title: Third-party libraries
docs.text: The SDK builds on xarray, numpy, pandas, zarr and Pydantic; the model packages on PyMC, ArviZ, scikit-learn, xgboost and skops; the marketing-mix adapter on pymc-marketing; the plot recipes on Altair and Plotly. Each keeps its own licence.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Contributions are accepted under the Contributor Licence Agreement (CONTRIBUTOR-LICENSE.md), which lets the project keep offering the platform under both licences. See Contributing.

docs.title: CLI and Python client v0.4
docs.text:
Two Apache-2.0 packages talk to the /v1 HTTP API:

  • mapi-client (mapi_client): a typed Python client, sync and async, built on httpx;
  • mapi-cli (mapi): the command line, built on the client and on the SDK for local runs.

Both use the Pydantic DTOs from mapi_spec.api for every request and response, and raise mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses rebuilt from RFC 7807 problem documents.

This page is a compact summary. The guides walk through each with tested examples (command line, Python client), and the CLI reference lists every command's --help, generated from the installed CLI.

docs.title: Python client
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

with Client() as api:  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_TOKEN / ~/.config/mapi/config.toml / 127.0.0.1:8000
    version = api.datasets.upload("eu_media.zarr.zip", dataset="eu_media_daily")
    rev = api.specs.upsert(open("spec.yaml").read())
    run = api.runs.fit(rev.spec_id, rev.revision)
    for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE, resumes with Last-Event-ID
        print(item)
    run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
    result = api.models.score(
        model_id,
        1,
        {
            "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
            "mode": "forecast",
            "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        },
    )
    result.tree  # xr.DataTree with the `xarray` extra
Resource Calls projects list, get catalog get, models, model, steps, plots, schema datasets create, list, get, find, ensure, create_upload, create_version, versions, version, wait_version, upload, artifact, download specs validate, create, list, get, find, revise, upsert, revisions, revision, dry_run runs create, fit, get, list, wait, stream_events, events, logs, plots, cancel, resume, retry models list, get, versions, version, artifact, download, score plots list, get, validate tenants (v0.3) list, get, rename, projects, create_project, update_project, delete_project, members, add_member, set_role, remove_member, usage, audit tokens (v0.3) list, create, get, revoke usage (v0.3) get (the project), tenant admin (v0.3, operators) tenants, tenant, create_tenant, update_tenant, quotas, set_quota, delete_quota, kill_switches, set_kill_switches, executors, executor, audit; v0.4: signups, review_signup, set_verification, retry_deletion guided (v0.4) templates, template, detect_roles, draft, import_bayesinsight, compile, translate_priors, prior_translation, wait_prior_translation, preview_priors endpoints (v0.4) list, get, promote, delete, history, rollback, schema, validate, submit, score, snippets webhooks (v0.4) list, create, get, update, delete, rotate_secret, deliveries, replay plots sharing (v0.4) save, saved, get_saved, delete_saved, render, render_status, render_output, download_render, create_embed, embeds, revoke_embed, embed tenants trust (v0.4) verification, request_deletion, deletion, cancel_deletion, export, export_status, wait_export, download_export

v0.4. api.endpoint(alias) is a RemoteEndpoint (schema(), validate(ds), score(ds) -> xr.Dataset with inline XrJSON); api.signup() and api.verify_email() are public calls sent without credentials. mapi_client.webhooks.verify(headers, body, secret) checks a delivery's Mapi-Signature (Receiving webhooks); mapi_client.atlas.RemoteModel is an Atlas model backed by an endpoint (Atlas); mapi_client.xrjson encodes and decodes inline payloads. Every operation of the v0.4 endpoint table has a request builder, checked against the contract by the client's tests.

  • AsyncClient has the same resources with await and async for.
  • List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor.
  • Calls that accept an Idempotency-Key get a fresh UUID unless you pass one. Idempotent calls are retried on 502, 503, 504 and connection errors, honouring Retry-After.
  • 429 RATE_LIMITED is waited out (Retry-After, then exponential back-off) and resent for every method, because the server refused it before acting; RateLimited is raised after RetryPolicy.rate_limit_retries attempts. 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED raises QuotaExceeded at once, and retry_after_of(exc) gives the seconds until the quota resets (v0.3).
  • api.tokens.create returns the token's secret once (TokenCreated.secret, kept out of repr) and is never resent after a lost response, so it cannot mint two tokens.
  • datasets.upload accepts a path, bytes or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). It creates the dataset if needed, PUTs the file to the signed URL, starts the ingest run and waits for the version to be ready. A dataset that carries its raw schema in the mapi_schema attribute keeps its dim policies and roles.
  • runs.stream_events yields RunSnapshot, RunEventFrame (persisted events, with an id), RunLiveFrame (live progress and log frames, without an id) and finally RunEnd.
  • models.score sends Prefer: wait=N. While the run is still going it repeats the same request with the same Idempotency-Key; the server's idempotent replay returns the finished ScoreCallResult with fresh output links.
  • Signed storage URLs are fetched without the API's Authorization header, and every transfer is checked against the storage-computed CRC32C and size.

Configuration. Arguments beat MAPI_URL (fallback MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN, MAPI_PROJECT and MAPI_PROFILE, which beat a profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME), which beats http://127.0.0.1:8000. A token is never sent over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host. v0.2 has no authentication.

Credentials and project (v0.3). The client authenticates with an API token (argument, MAPI_TOKEN or the profile's token) or, when none is set, with the OpenID Connect sign-in mapi login stored for the profile in credentials.json (mode 0600, next to the config file, or $MAPI_CREDENTIALS). A stored sign-in is used only for the API URL it was made for; its ID token is renewed with the refresh token shortly before it expires and after a 401. project (Client(project=…), MAPI_PROJECT, the profile's project) is sent as X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project> on project-scoped requests only: not on identity, tenant and operator routes, nor where the path already names the project.

File Mode Holds ~/.config/mapi/config.toml 0600 when written by mapi Profiles: url, project, token, timeout, max_retries, verify, oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id, oidc_client_secret ~/.config/mapi/credentials.json 0600 Per profile: the API URL, issuer, client id, ID token, refresh token and expiry of a mapi login sign-in

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
mapi new geo-mmm -o spec.yaml --with-data   # template + tiny sample data (needs mapi-conformance)
mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip   # full static validation against installed plugins
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip \
    --side-table fx=fx.zarr.zip --side-table holidays=holidays.zarr.zip   # in-process fit
mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/geo-mmm --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip

mapi serve                                  # the local stack in one process (see below)
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --remote @   # upload, create/revise spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --state running | get RUN | logs RUN | watch RUN | cancel RUN | retry RUN
mapi datasets ls | upload file.csv --name sales --mapping mapping.yaml
mapi score request.yaml --remote @ --model MODEL_ID --version 1 -o result.zarr.zip
mapi catalog [models|steps|plots] [--remote @]

mapi plugin init acme-demand && mapi plugin test acme-demand   # scaffold + contract kit
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check
mapi config show | path | set KEY VALUE | unset KEY

Multi-tenant commands (v0.3; walked through in Authentication and Administration, both run by the test suite):

mapi login [--device | --no-browser | --with-token] [--issuer URL --client-id ID]
mapi whoami
mapi use [TENANT/PROJECT | --unset]          # --project / MAPI_PROJECT for one command
mapi logout [--revoke]
mapi tokens ls [--all] | get TOKEN | create NAME -s SCOPE... [--save] | revoke TOKEN

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev: database migrations, then the API and the orchestrator (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and event pump) in one process. Postgres is the embedded pgserver unless DATABASE_URL is set, and the GCS shim is started in-process when nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. Runs execute through the local-process executor with the real mapi-runner. For the web app as well, use make dev (Local development).

docs.title: GCS shim (local Cloud Storage)
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim is a local emulator of the parts of Google Cloud Storage the platform relies on. The local stack, the test suites and the runner use it in place of real GCS. It implements:

  • object generations and metagenerations, with generation preconditions;
  • server-computed CRC32C and MD5, in the GCS wire forms (base64);
  • V4 signed URLs: GET with HTTP Range, and PUT;
  • V4 POST policies that limit uploads to a key prefix and a content-length-range;
  • IAM-lite: per-principal tokens and keys, with per-bucket role bindings;
  • a retention lock (write-once buckets) and lifecycle (age-based delete).

The control plane talks to it through ShimObjectStore, which implements the ObjectStore protocol from mapi_spec.storage. GcsObjectStore implements the same protocol on real GCS.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim                                   # serve .local/gcs on 127.0.0.1:4443
python -m mapi_gcs_shim --root .local/gcs --port 4443
mapi-gcs-shim init --root .local/gcs            # write config + key files, then exit
mapi-gcs-shim key exec --field token            # print the exec principal's bearer token

The defaults come from the local-dev variables:

  • MAPI_DATA_DIR: the root is $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs;
  • MAPI_ENV: bucket names are mapi-{env}-*;
  • MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT: the host and port.

--port 0 picks a free port. The server stops gracefully on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Only one server may serve a root at a time, which is enforced by a lock file.

docs.title: State on disk
docs.text:
Path Content _shim/config.json Buckets and principals, including secrets. Mode 0600. _shim/keys/{principal}.json One key file per principal: email, bearer token, HMAC secret and endpoint. Mode 0600. buckets/{bucket}/bucket.json The bucket's retention and lifecycle policies. buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.json The live generation's metadata, where h = sha256(object name). buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.{generation}.bin The object's bytes. tmp/ The staging area for uploads.

No object name ever becomes a filesystem path. Names are hashed, and bucket names must match the GCS bucket grammar. Names with empty, . or .. segments, a leading / or control characters are rejected with 400, whether they arrive in the JSON API, the XML API or a POST-policy key.

Writes are crash-safe:

  1. bytes are streamed into tmp/ while the CRC32C and MD5 are computed;
  2. the data file is renamed into place;
  3. the metadata sidecar is atomically replaced, which is the commit point.

On startup, the shim deletes leftover staging files and any data files that never committed. Only the live generation is kept, as in a bucket without object versioning. Reading a superseded generation therefore returns 404.

docs.title: Buckets and principals
docs.text:
By default init creates the five buckets from the plan's storage layout:

Bucket Policy mapi-{env}-quarantine Lifecycle: objects are deleted after 7 days. mapi-{env}-bootstrap Lifecycle: objects are deleted after 1 day. mapi-{env}-runs No policy. mapi-{env}-bundles Locked retention of about 100 years. Objects cannot be overwritten or deleted, even by an admin. --bundle-retention-days N (default $MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS) locks it for N days instead, like the deployed bucket (30); 0 sets no retention, so a test stack's tenant deletions finish at once. The choice applies when the root is created; an existing root keeps its policy. mapi-{env}-data No policy.

It also creates two principals:

Principal Bindings control (control@mapi-{env}.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/storage.admin on every bucket. Used by the control plane and the finalizer. exec (exec@…) storage.objects.get and storage.objects.delete on the bootstrap bucket only. It cannot list that bucket and has no access to the bundles bucket. Its token is the local executor's MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN.

You can add principals and bindings to config.json. The predefined roles are:

  • roles/storage.admin
  • roles/storage.objectAdmin
  • roles/storage.objectUser
  • roles/storage.objectViewer
  • roles/storage.objectCreator
  • roles/storage.legacyBucketReader

A binding targets one bucket, or "*" for every bucket.

Permissions are checked as follows:

  • JSON-API calls are checked against the caller's bearer token. A missing or unknown token returns 401, and a missing permission returns 403.
  • Signed URLs and POST policies carry the signer's authority, which is checked when the URL is used. A URL signed by exec for the runs bucket is refused.
  • Overwriting an existing object also requires storage.objects.delete, as in GCS.

docs.title: JSON API
docs.text:
Every JSON-API request needs Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Method and path Operation GET /storage/v1/b List buckets. Needs storage.buckets.list. POST /storage/v1/b Create a bucket. The body may set retentionPolicy and lifecycle (Delete with an age condition). GET or DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket} Get a bucket, or delete it if it is empty. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o List objects. Accepts prefix, delimiter, pageToken, maxResults, startOffset and endOffset. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Get metadata. With alt=media it returns the content, and Range gives 206. PATCH /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Update contentType or metadata, which increments metageneration. DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Delete an object. Accepts generation. POST /storage/v1/b/{b}/o/{o}/rewriteTo/b/{b2}/o/{o2} Server-side copy. Also available as copyTo. Accepts sourceGeneration. POST /upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o Upload with uploadType=media or multipart. Resumable uploads return 501. GET /download/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Download the content.

Every object operation accepts the ifGenerationMatch, ifGenerationNotMatch, ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch preconditions. A rewrite also accepts the ifSource… forms.

  • On writes, a failed precondition returns 412.
  • On reads, a failed …NotMatch returns 304.
  • ifGenerationMatch=0 means "the object must not exist yet".

Errors use the GCS JSON shape: {"error": {"code", "message", "errors": [{"reason"}]}}.

docs.title: Signed URLs (XML style)
docs.text:
Method and path Operation GET /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Download. With Range it returns 206, with Content-Range. An unsatisfiable range returns 416. PUT /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Upload. POST /{bucket} (multipart/form-data) Upload through a V4 POST policy. The file field must be last.

Signing follows GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 with per-principal HMAC keys:

  • Canonical request: method, path, every query parameter except X-Goog-Signature, the signed headers (always including host) and UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD.
  • Signed values: X-Goog-Expires (at most 7 days) and X-Goog-Date are signed. Expiry is strict, but X-Goog-Date may be up to 5 minutes in the future to allow for clock skew.
  • Bound to the signature: the method, path, host, query (for example generation) and signed header values. Changing any of them returns 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.
  • Unsigned headers: any x-goog-* header that was not signed returns 400, except x-goog-hash.
  • Expiry: an expired URL returns 400 ExpiredToken.

Signed GET URLs from sign_get are pinned to a generation. If the object is overwritten, the URL returns 404; it never silently serves the new bytes.

Signed PUT URLs from sign_put sign these headers, which the uploader must send verbatim:

  • content-type;
  • x-goog-if-generation-match: 0, so the object is write-once by default;
  • x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max>.

The uploader may also send Content-MD5 or x-goog-hash: crc32c=…,md5=…. A mismatch returns 400 BadDigest, and nothing is stored.

POST policies from post_policy are a base64 JSON document of conditions, with an HMAC signature over the document. The conditions are:

  • {"bucket": …};
  • ["starts-with", "$key", prefix];
  • ["starts-with", "$content-type", ""];
  • ["content-length-range", min, max];
  • the x-goog-* credential fields;
  • with create_only=True, {"x-goog-if-generation-match": "0"} (also sent as a form field).

When the policy is used, the shim enforces:

  • the signature and the expiration;
  • every condition;
  • that every form field is covered by a condition, except x-goog-signature, policy, file and x-ignore-*;
  • the size range. A body that is too large is rejected while it streams;
  • an x-goog-if-generation-match form field as a precondition, so a create-only policy returns 412 for a key that already exists, whatever the signer may delete.

Real GCS takes no generation precondition in a POST form. GcsObjectStore signs create-only policies with uploader_credentials instead: a principal without storage.objects.delete, which GCS requires to overwrite.

success_action_status (200, 201 with an XML PostResponse, or 204 by default) and ${filename} in key behave as in GCS.

docs.title: Shim-only endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /_shim/healthz: no authentication.
  • POST /_shim/v1/lifecycle:sweep?now=<iso>: needs shim.admin. It runs the lifecycle rules now; objects under retention are never swept.

The server also sweeps every --sweep-interval seconds. The default is 300.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta
from mapi_gcs_shim import ShimObjectStore

async with ShimObjectStore.from_root(".local/gcs", "control") as store:
    meta = await store.put("mapi-local-runs", "t/default/runs/r1/a1/x.json", b"{}",
                           content_type="application/json", if_generation_match=0)
    url = await store.sign_get("mapi-local-runs", meta.name, expires_in=timedelta(minutes=15))

ShimObjectStore has three constructors:

  • ShimObjectStore(endpoint, credentials, public_endpoint=None). public_endpoint is the host written into signed URLs, so a sandbox can reach the shim under another name. The host is signed.
  • .from_root(root, principal).
  • .from_local_dev(LocalDev).

Besides the protocol methods, it offers create_bucket, get_bucket and sweep_lifecycle. Errors map to NotFound, PreconditionFailed, AccessDenied, InvalidRange and StorageError:

  • get(max_bytes=…) raises PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE before it reads the body;
  • a full read whose CRC32C does not match raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

mapi_gcs_shim.transfer has helpers for whoever holds a URL:

  • download_signed;
  • upload_signed_put;
  • upload_post_policy.

They speak plain GCS XML semantics, so they also work against real GCS.

docs.title: Real Cloud Storage
docs.text:
GcsObjectStore (install mapi-gcs-shim[gcp]) implements the same protocol with google-cloud-storage. It has been tested only with a fake client, never against live GCP.

  • Signing. With a BlobSigner (blob_signer=), signed GET/PUT URLs and POST policies are built by mapi_gcs_shim.gcs_signing (GOOG4-RSA-SHA256, byte-identical to the library's V4 signer) and only the string to sign goes to the signer. IamSignBlobSigner signs with the IAM Credentials signBlob API and a token provider that refreshes (google_token_provider()), retrying 429/5xx. GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run( service_account_email=..., uploader_service_account_email=...) wires both: the control account for URLs, the uploader account (create but no delete) for create-only POST policies.
  • Integrity. A write whose server-computed CRC32C, MD5 or size differs from the bytes sent is deleted (that generation only) and raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE. A copy pins the source generation (ifSourceGenerationMatch) and compares the destination's size and CRC32C with the source.
  • Preconditions. Signed GETs are pinned to a generation; signed PUTs carry a signed x-goog-if-generation-match (0, write-once, by default); put, copy and delete pass if_generation_match through.

docs.title: pytest fixtures
docs.text:
The package registers a pytest11 plugin, so every workspace test can use these fixtures:

async def test_something(gcs_shim):            # a fresh shim per test, on a free port
    async with gcs_shim.store() as store:       # the control principal; store("exec") also works
        await store.put(gcs_shim.buckets.runs, "t/default/x", b"...")
    headers = gcs_shim.auth_headers("exec")     # for raw httpx calls

gcs_shim_session gives one shim for the whole session. For use outside pytest, ShimServer(root) is a context manager that runs the shim on a background thread.

docs.title: Differences from real GCS
docs.text:
• There is no object versioning: only the live generation is kept.
  • Resumable uploads (uploadType=resumable) are not implemented. Use media or multipart uploads, or a signed PUT.
  • Signing uses HMAC keys (GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256) instead of service-account RSA keys (GOOG4-RSA-SHA256). GcsObjectStore signs RSA URLs itself through a BlobSigner (IAM signBlob on Cloud Run), or falls back to the library's signing.
  • There are no ACLs, CMEK, storage classes, notifications or bucket PATCH. Bucket policies are set when the bucket is created or in config.json.
  • A signed URL is valid only for the method it was signed for. A HEAD request needs its own signature, as in GCS.

docs.title: HTTP API (v1) v0.2
docs.text:
The platform API that ships with v0.2 (milestone M1, the local vertical slice). Every request and response body is a Pydantic model in mapi_spec.api. The server serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from those models, and each model carries examples. The endpoint table on this page matches mapi_spec.api.M1_ENDPOINTS, and a test fails if the two drift apart.

See also OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, browsable, with every schema and example (full screen) HTTP API guide The main flow with curl and jq: upload, validate, fit, follow, score Python client The same flow with mapi_client

M1 is single-tenant

A local install has one tenant and one project, both called default. Every resource still carries tenant_id and project_id, and every storage key starts with t/{tenant}/, so multi-tenancy in v0.3 adds row-level security without changing the schema. There is no authentication in M1. The API listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The tenants, sign-in, tokens and quotas that v0.3 adds are described in Multi-tenant API.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Topic Rule Base URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 locally. Resource paths start with /v1. Bodies application/json (UTF-8). Spec text travels as a string field (yaml) inside JSON. Unknown fields Request bodies reject unknown fields (SCHEMA_INVALID). Clients ignore unknown response fields, so the server can add fields without a new version. Timestamps RFC 3339, timezone-aware, UTC (2026-10-15T09:30:00Z). Ids <prefix>_<26 lowercase Crockford base32>, ULID layout, sortable by creation time (run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0). Prefixes: ds, upl, spc, run, mdl, mv. Projects and tenants use slugs (default). Durations "45m", "1h30m", "90s". Actions Non-CRUD actions use a colon suffix: POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel. Untrusted text Log lines, tracebacks and plugin messages only ever appear in untrusted_text or LogLine.line. Render them as text, never as HTML or markdown.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json, model mapi_spec.Problem) with a stable code:

{
  "type": "urn:mapi:error:LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "title": "A stateful step runs before the split",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "detail": "validation failed with 1 error; first at /pipeline/2: …",
  "errors": [
    {"code": "LEAKAGE_RISK", "severity": "error", "pointer": "/pipeline/2",
     "message": "stateful step 'scale_y' runs before the split"}
  ]
}
  • Malformed request bodies, path parameters and query parameters return 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. Each problem goes in errors[] with an RFC 6901 pointer into the request (/body/kind, /query/limit).
  • Every endpoint can also return RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500) and INFRA_ERROR (503). These are not repeated in the table.
  • The full list of codes and their HTTP statuses is in Error codes.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
List endpoints return Page[T]:

{"items": [ … ], "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6InJ1bl8wMWphZiJ9"}
  • Pass ?limit= (default 50, maximum 200) and ?cursor=<next_cursor> to fetch the next page. A null cursor means the current page is the last one.
  • Cursors are opaque and only valid for the same list and filters.
  • Items are ordered newest first by id.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
POST /v1/runs, …:score, …:retry, …:dry-run and POST …/versions (ingest) accept an Idempotency-Key header (1–255 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the project and kept for 24 hours):

Situation Response First request with the key The normal response, for example 201 Created with the Run Same key, same body (byte-equal after canonical JSON) 200 OK with the originally created resource. No second run is created. Same key, different body 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT Same key while the first request is still in flight 409 CONFLICT. Retry later.

Clients should generate one key per user intent, for example a UUIDv4 when the user clicks Fit, and reuse it on every network retry.

docs.title: Long-running work and Prefer: wait
docs.text:
Runs are asynchronous. Creating one returns the Run at once in state created or queued. POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score also honours RFC 7240 Prefer: wait=N, with N capped at 60 seconds:

  • If the score run reaches a terminal state within N seconds, the response is 200 with ScoreCallResult{done: true, run, outputs: [ArtifactLink…]}.
  • Otherwise the response is 202 with done: false and the run. Follow the run with GET /v1/runs/{run_id} or its event stream.
  • The Preference-Applied: wait=N response header echoes the wait the server actually used.

docs.title: Run events (server-sent events)
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events has two representations:

  • Accept: text/event-stream: a live SSE stream.
  • Any other Accept: a JSON Page[RunEventView] of persisted events. Pass ?after=<id> to read events after a given id.

The stream sends these frames, in this order:

  1. event: snapshot with the full Run JSON. It is the first frame on every connection and has no id:.
  2. A replay of the persisted events whose id is greater than the Last-Event-ID request header. Without the header the replay starts from the beginning. Every replayed frame carries id: <RunEventView.id>. The ids increase per run, so a reconnecting client resumes exactly where it stopped, including across the 60-minute request cut on Cloud Run.
  3. Live frames as events arrive: state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete and error. The data: of each frame is one line of compact JSON (RunEventView).
  4. event: end once the run is terminal (data: the final Run). The server then closes the stream. A client that sees end must not reconnect.

The server also sends a fresh event: snapshot (no id:) whenever the run's state changes, so a client can re-render from the latest Run without reassembling it from events. progress and log frames are not persisted: they are sent live without an id: (data: {run_id, attempt, seq, ts, type, payload}) and are never replayed; Last-Event-ID only covers persisted events.

Between events the server writes a heartbeat comment (: keepalive) every 15 seconds. The first frame also carries retry: 3000.

An open stream checks its caller's credential again every minute (MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S). Once the token is revoked or expired, the session has ended, or the caller has lost access to the project, the server closes the stream without end. The reconnect then answers 401 or 403, and clients should stop there rather than retry.

Progress frames are coalesced to at most one every 2–5 seconds. Only state changes, warnings, diagnostics, checkpoints, metrics and terminal events are persisted and replayable. A reconnecting client gets the latest progress from the snapshot frame. Log lines are paged from GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs.

retry: 3000
event: snapshot
data: {"id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"running", …}

id: 17
event: state
data: {"id":17,"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","attempt":1,"seq":3,"type":"state", …}

: keepalive

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Columns: Request and Response are DTO names in mapi_spec.api, unless they are catalog or plot models from mapi_spec. Errors lists the endpoint-specific codes. The common ones from the Errors section are not repeated.

docs.title: Health
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /healthz Process liveness — Health 200 — GET /readyz Postgres and the object store are reachable (503 with the same body if not) — Health 200 —

docs.title: Projects and catalog
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/projects List projects — Page[Project] 200 — GET /v1/projects/{project_id} Get a project — Project 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/catalog The whole catalog with its digest — CatalogResponse 200 — GET /v1/catalog/models Model plugins — Page[ModelCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/catalog/models/{model_id}/{version} One plugin version (manifest, sanitized schemas, schema template) — ModelCatalogEntry 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/catalog/steps Steps — Page[StepCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/catalog/plots Plot recipes — Page[PlotCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/schemas/{name} An exported JSON Schema, for example modelspec.json (drives Monaco and JSON Forms) — JSON Schema 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Data reaches the platform in three steps:

  1. Create the dataset.
  2. PUT the file to the signed URL from an upload session. The URL points into the quarantine bucket and the API never sees the bytes.
  3. Create a version. A sandboxed ingest run parses the upload, validates it, and writes the content-addressed data.zarr.zip with its schema, profile and preview.
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/datasets Create a dataset DatasetCreate Dataset 201 CONFLICT (name taken) GET /v1/datasets List datasets — Page[Dataset] 200 — GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id} Get a dataset — Dataset 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads Signed PUT URL into quarantine UploadCreate UploadSession 201 NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions Ingest an upload as a new version; starts an ingest run. Accepts Idempotency-Key. DatasetVersionCreate DatasetVersion (status ingesting) 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (upload not finished or already consumed) GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions List versions — Page[DatasetVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version} Schema, summary, profile and preview refs — DatasetVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for data.zarr.zip, schema.json, profile.json or preview.json — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Specs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/specs:validate Synchronous static validation. Returns every issue at once with JSON pointers, plus the schema at each pipeline stage. ValidateRequest ValidateResponse 200 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID POST /v1/specs Create a spec and its revision 1 SpecCreate SpecDoc 201 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT GET /v1/specs List specs — Page[SpecDoc] 200 — GET /v1/specs/{spec_id} Get a spec with its latest revision — SpecDoc 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions Add an immutable revision SpecRevisionCreate SpecRevision 201 NOT_FOUND, SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (stale parent_revision) GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions List revisions — Page[SpecRevision] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision} Get one revision — SpecRevision 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision}:dry-run Explicit sandboxed dry-run, the same as POST /v1/runs with kind: validate. Accepts Idempotency-Key. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, QUOTA_EXCEEDED

How validation reports results:

  • POST /v1/specs:validate returns 200 even when the document is invalid. The verdict is in ValidateResponse.valid and issues.
  • The non-2xx statuses are kept for requests that cannot be validated at all: unparseable YAML, an oversized document, or a malformed request body.
  • Creating a spec or a revision stores invalid revisions too, with valid: false and their issues, so the editor can save work in progress.
  • POST /v1/runs refuses invalid revisions with the first error's code. Examples: LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/runs Submit a run (200 on an idempotent replay). Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunCreate Run 201 NOT_FOUND, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED GET /v1/runs List runs (filters: kind, state, spec_id) — Page[Run] 200 — GET /v1/runs/{run_id} Get a run (state, failure class and problem, attempt, progress snapshot, cost: placeholders in v0.2, metered from v0.3) — Run 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events SSE stream or JSON page of persisted events (see Run events). Accepts Last-Event-ID. — Page[RunEventView] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs Captured log lines; filters attempt, stream — Page[LogLine] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots Plots a succeeded run rendered (plots.json: forecast fans, counterfactual bands), passed through the plot sanitizer on every read; rejected plots are left out. Empty until the run succeeds. — Page[PlotSpec] 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel Request cancellation. Idempotent: it returns the run in cancelling, or in its terminal state if the run had already finished. A finalizing run is left alone and returned as it is: its execution is already over. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:resume Resume a partial run from its checkpoints (new attempt) — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (not partial) POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:retry Start a new run from a failed one, for example one resource class up after RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunRetry Run 201 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (not failed)

What RunCreate needs depends on kind:

kind Required Not allowed fit, validate (sandboxed dry-run) spec_id, revision model_version_id, request score model_version_id, request (a ScoreRequest document) spec_id, revision evaluate, derive, render model_version_id (optional params) spec_id, revision, request

ingest runs are created by POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions. describe, optimize and the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign) cannot be created in v0.2. Run states and the transitions between them are listed in Run protocol.

docs.title: Models and scoring
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/models List models — Page[Model] 200 — GET /v1/models/{model_id} Get a model — Model 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions List versions — Page[ModelVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version} Signed bundle manifest, diagnostics, scorecard, lineage, metrics — ModelVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for a bundle object or a ui/… view; name may contain / — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score Score with replayed preprocessing. Accepts Prefer: wait=N (200 if done, else 202) and Idempotency-Key. ScoreCall ScoreCallResult 200 NOT_FOUND, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED

Artifact links are minted only after two checks pass:

  1. The authorization check.
  2. Verification of the model version's signed bundle manifest: tenant, model version, digests and object generations must all match.

If the second check fails, the response is INTEGRITY_FAILURE and no URL is issued. Each link is pinned to an object generation, expires after 15 minutes, and supports HTTP Range requests.
