docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/plots Plots of a model version — Page[PlotListItem] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/plots/{plot_id} A sanitized PlotSpec. Render it only inside the plot-sandbox iframe, which has its own origin. — PlotSpec 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/plots:validate Run the server-side plot sanitizer on a user-authored spec PlotSpec PlotValidateResponse 200 SCHEMA_INVALID

docs.title: Multi-tenant API v0.3
docs.text: v0.3 (milestone M2) adds tenants, projects, members, API tokens, quotas, cost and an operator console. The models are in mapi_spec.api, mapi_spec.tenancy, mapi_spec.tokens, mapi_spec.quotas, mapi_spec.cost, mapi_spec.audit, mapi_spec.admin and mapi_spec.auth. The endpoint table below matches mapi_spec.api.M2_ENDPOINTS, and mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives every operation (v0.2 ones included) its scope and the permission it checks. Tests fail if the code, this page and the server drift apart. Roles, tokens and scopes are explained in Tenancy and authentication, limits and prices in Quotas and cost.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Caller Credential Notes Browser (the web app) Session cookie __Host-mapi_session (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/), set by GET /auth/callback OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce, run by the API as a backend-for-frontend. The browser never holds an OAuth token. Programs, SDKs, CLI, Atlas Authorization: Bearer mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum> An API token. It acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes, in the one project it is bound to. Google Pub/Sub A Google-signed OIDC ID token on POST /internal/events Audience, issuer and the push service account are checked. Nothing in the body authenticates.

Responses for authentication and authorization:

Situation Response No credential, or an expired session, on a non-public route 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A malformed token, or one whose checksum fails 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. The presented value is never echoed. A revoked or expired token 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A resource in a project or tenant the caller cannot see 404 NOT_FOUND, the same as a missing one, so ids cannot be probed A visible resource, but the role or the token's scopes do not allow the action 403 FORBIDDEN A token used outside the project it is bound to 403 FORBIDDEN The tenant is suspended Reads work. Everything else returns 403 FORBIDDEN.

docs.title: Selecting the project
docs.text:
Every v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) belongs to a project. From v0.3 a request names its project in one of these ways, in this order of precedence:

  1. Path parameters, on routes under /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}.
  2. The X-Mapi-Project header: X-Mapi-Project: <tenant_id>/<project_id>, for example X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth. A bare X-Mapi-Project: growth is accepted when the tenant is unambiguous: the caller belongs to one tenant, or uses a token.
  3. The token's binding. A token always acts in its own project, so token clients may omit the header. A header that names another project returns 403 FORBIDDEN.
  4. The deployment default, in the single-tenant local profile only (default/default, as in v0.2).

If none applies, or path and header disagree, the request fails with 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope implements these rules.

The scope of each v0.2 endpoint (by operation id) and the permission checked:

Scope Operations Permission Public health, ready, get_schema None Authenticated list_projects, get_catalog, list_catalog_models, get_catalog_model, list_catalog_steps, list_catalog_plots Any signed-in caller. Lists are filtered to what the caller can see. Project get_project read project Project create_dataset / create_upload, create_dataset_version create / update dataset (editor) Project list_datasets, get_dataset, list_dataset_versions, get_dataset_version, get_dataset_artifact read dataset Project validate_spec, list_specs, get_spec, list_spec_revisions, get_spec_revision read spec Project create_spec / create_spec_revision create / update spec (editor) Project create_run, dry_run_spec, resume_run, retry_run create run (runner). Runs on a model version also need run model. Project cancel_run cancel run (runner) Project list_runs, get_run, run_events, run_logs, list_run_plots read run Project list_models, get_model, list_model_versions, get_model_version, get_model_artifact read model Project score_model run model (runner) Project list_plots, get_plot, validate_plot read plot

Storage keys and rows were already tenant- and project-qualified in v0.2 (t/{tenant}/…), so the switch needs no data migration. Postgres enforces the boundary with row-level security on tenant_id in every table.

docs.title: Identity, tenants and projects
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/me The caller (Principal), their tenants, projects and roles; for a token, the token too — Me 200 UNAUTHENTICATED GET /v1/tenants Tenants the caller belongs to — Page[Tenant] 200 — GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Get a tenant — Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Rename a tenant (tenant admin) TenantUpdate Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects Projects of the tenant that the caller can see — Page[Project] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects Create a project (tenant admin) ProjectCreate Project 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (id taken) PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Rename or describe a project (project admin) ProjectUpdate Project 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Delete an empty project (tenant admin) — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (it still holds data)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
A membership grants one role. A tenant-wide membership grants it on the tenant and on every project in it; a project membership grants it on that project only. The effective role in a project is the higher of the two. Add a member by principal_id, or by email to invite someone who has not signed in yet (the invitation is claimed at first sign-in with that verified e-mail). Removing or demoting the last admin returns 409 CONFLICT.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members Tenant-wide members — Page[Membership] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members Grant a tenant-wide role (tenant admin) MembershipCreate Membership 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members/{principal_id} Change a tenant-wide role MembershipUpdate Membership 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members/{principal_id} Remove a tenant-wide role — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members Project members, tenant-wide grants included — Page[Membership] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members Grant a project role (project admin) MembershipCreate Membership 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members/{principal_id} Change a project role MembershipUpdate Membership 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members/{principal_id} Remove a project role — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Tokens belong to the project selected by X-Mapi-Project. POST /v1/tokens returns the full token once, in TokenCreated.secret; it cannot be shown again. Listings show the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_…. Any member may mint, list and revoke their own tokens; listing everyone's tokens (?all=true) or revoking someone else's needs manage on token (project admin).

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/tokens The caller's tokens; filters all, status — Page[ApiToken] 200 — POST /v1/tokens Mint a token with scopes, an expiry, and an optional rate limit and vCPU-second budget TokenCreate TokenCreated 201 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tokens/{token_id} Get a token (never its secret) — ApiToken 200 NOT_FOUND DELETE /v1/tokens/{token_id} Revoke a token. Idempotent. — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/usage Cost and quota of the selected project for a UTC period (day or month), optionally grouped (group_by: resource_class, project, day, token, run) — UsageReport 200 — GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/usage The same for the whole tenant (tenant admin) — UsageReport 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/audit The tenant's audit log (tenant admin); filters project_id, actor_id, action, outcome, since, until — Page[AuditEvent] 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN

Every Run now carries a filled-in cost (RunCost): estimated is true until the run's first attempt has been metered, amount_micros is in currency (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros) and price_version names the price table used. The v0.2 fields vcpu_seconds, gib_seconds and usd keep their meaning.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator endpoints need a platform operator. Tenant admins get 403 FORBIDDEN. Operators see tenant metadata, usage and audit logs, but no tenant content (datasets, specs, models, plots). Every change is written to the audit log.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/admin/tenants All tenants; filters status, trust_tier — Page[Tenant] 200 FORBIDDEN POST /v1/admin/tenants Create a tenant, optionally inviting its first admin TenantCreate Tenant 201 FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id} Get any tenant — Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id} Change trust tier, status (suspended and deleting need a reason) or data residency TenantAdminUpdate Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/quotas Quota policies; filters scope, subject_id — Page[QuotaPolicy] 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/quotas Create or replace the policy for one (scope, subject_id) QuotaPolicyUpsert QuotaPolicy 200 FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/admin/quotas/{scope}/{subject_id} Remove a policy; the tier default applies again (subject_id is * for the global policy) — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/kill-switches The kill switches — KillSwitches 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/kill-switches Change them; omitted fields keep their value, reason is required. cancel_untrusted_runs (with untrusted_execution_enabled=false) also cancels every unfinished run of uploaded code; without it in-flight runs continue KillSwitchUpdate KillSwitches 200 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors Every executor: caps, health, submit rate, 429s, conformance report — Page[ExecutorHealth] 200 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors/{name} One executor — ExecutorHealth 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence The conformance and security-suite reports recorded for an executor — ExecutorEvidence 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence Record suite results (audited); shared tiers need both, passing, for the current caps ExecutorEvidenceUpdate ExecutorEvidence 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/usage Cost by tenant for a UTC period (day or month, start inside it), biggest spender first, and the current spend against the global spend cap (spend_cap: always the cap's current window, with fraction = spent / cap) — AdminUsageReport 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name} Enable or disable an executor (audited, reason required). Nothing new is leased onto a disabled one; orchestrator reports never re-enable it ExecutorUpdate ExecutorHealth 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/audit The platform audit log; filters tenant_id, project_id, actor_id, action, outcome, since, until — Page[AuditEvent] 200 FORBIDDEN

docs.title: Browser session (backend-for-frontend)
docs.text:
These routes are not versioned and live at the root, next to the web app.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /auth/login Start sign-in. Redirects to the identity provider with response_type=code, a PKCE code_challenge (S256), state and nonce. ?return_to= must be a same-origin path; anything else becomes /. — — 302 — GET /auth/callback Check state, exchange the code with the PKCE verifier, verify the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry), set the session cookie and redirect to return_to — — 302 UNAUTHENTICATED POST /auth/logout End the session and clear the cookies. Works without a valid session; with one it needs X-CSRF-Token. — — 204 — GET /auth/session Whether the browser is signed in, as whom and until when. authenticated: false is a 200, not a 401. — SessionInfo 200 —

The login transaction (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) is held by the server for 10 minutes and referenced by a __Host-mapi_login cookie with SameSite=Lax, because the identity provider's redirect back is a cross-site navigation that would drop a Strict cookie. Sessions expire after 2 hours idle or 12 hours in total. Every state-changing API route takes JSON, which a cross-site form cannot send without a CORS preflight, and the session cookie is SameSite=Strict, so cross-site requests never carry it.

On top of that, every cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (including POST /auth/logout when a session is live) must echo the session's CSRF token in an X-CSRF-Token header, and is refused (403 FORBIDDEN) when its Origin is neither the web app nor the API or it says Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site. The web app reads the token from the __Host-mapi_csrf cookie (readable, SameSite=Strict) or from the X-CSRF-Token header of GET /auth/session. Requests with an API token need no CSRF token.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /internal/events Pub/Sub push of run events from the Cloud Logging sink PubSubPushEnvelope Ingest result 200 UNAUTHENTICATED, SCHEMA_INVALID

The push envelope is {message: {data, attributes, messageId, publishTime}, subscription, deliveryAttempt}. message.data is a base64 Cloud Logging entry whose jsonPayload.mapi_event is one HMAC-signed run event (see Run protocol). The request must carry Authorization: Bearer <Google-signed ID token>; after verifying the signature, the server checks the claims with mapi_spec.auth.check_push_claims: issuer https://accounts.google.com, the configured audience, the push service account's verified e-mail, and expiry. Events that fail their HMAC are acknowledged with 200 (redelivery would not help) and audited as event.rejected.

docs.title: Quotas and rate limits on every endpoint
docs.text:
Requests and submissions are checked against three levels of quota: token, tenant and global (see Quotas and cost).

  • A request over a requests-per-minute limit returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header. Retry after that many seconds.
  • A submission that would exceed a compute, concurrency, fan-out, resource-class, storage or egress limit returns 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Retry-After is set when the limit resets with a window (the UTC day or month). The problem's detail names the level and the limit.
  • The platform kill switches (uploaded code paused, global spend cap reached) also return QUOTA_EXCEEDED, at the global level.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
v0.4 (milestone M3) adds the contracts for Guided mode and for connecting other applications: guided templates and drafts, business priors and lift tests, what-if scenarios, endpoints and aliases, code snippets, webhooks, saved and rendered plots with embed links, and the trust lifecycle (sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and export). The endpoint table matches mapi_spec.api.M3_ENDPOINTS; mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives each operation its scope and permission, and mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the whole v0.4 surface (M1, M2 and M3; the server's route-table test checks that it serves every row). The ideas behind them are explained in Guided mode and Integrations.

Project-scoped M3 routes take the project from X-Mapi-Project, like every v0.3 route.

docs.title: Guided mode
docs.text:
GET /v1/guided/templates lists the built-in templates (GuidedTemplate): plain-language questions, the built-in plugin they target, a ModelSpec template with {{placeholder}} strings, default settings, the scorecard checks that apply and x-ui-level hints. Role detection (POST /v1/guided/detect-roles) ranks the columns of an upload for every question from ColumnProfiles computed in the browser (or from a stored dataset version: its ingest's columns.json, else its schema and summary) and returns RoleSuggestions, each candidate with a confidence and a reason_plain. A draft (POST /v1/guided/drafts) turns GuidedAnswers into an IngestMapping for the upload, a ModelSpec document and its YAML ("View as YAML") without storing anything, with the static validator's findings in issues; save it with POST /v1/specs. POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight does the same for a BayesInsight model_def.json and metadata.json (BayesInsightImport), for the built-in geo MMM unless target says mmm.bayesinsight (the dedicated BayesInsight model). Business priors become model-space priors in a sandboxed translate_priors run (PriorTranslationRequest → PriorTranslation, whose result is a PriorTranslationResult with a prior-predictive preview in business units). POST /v1/guided/requests:compile turns a what-if scenario, a forecast or an intervention preset (GuidedCompile) into the ScoreRequest it stands for, so "Run exact" submits a real score run. The persona lock is Project.guided_locked, changed with PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} (ProjectUpdate.guided_locked); in a locked project, POST /v1/specs and POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions by members below admin answer 403 FORBIDDEN for anything but Guided specs that keep their template's advanced and hidden fields. Served in this release: the templates, role detection, drafts, the BayesInsight import and the lock (see From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft).

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/guided/templates Guided templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, choice) — Page[GuidedTemplate] 200 — GET /v1/guided/templates/{template_id} One template: questions, spec template, scorecard checks, UI levels — GuidedTemplate 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/guided/detect-roles Suggest a column for every question from column profiles DetectRolesRequest RoleSuggestions 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND POST /v1/guided/drafts Answers → ingest mapping + ModelSpec draft (+ YAML); stores nothing GuidedAnswers GuidedDraft 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight BayesInsight model_def.json + metadata.json → draft for the geo MMM BayesInsightImport GuidedDraft 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED POST /v1/guided/requests:compile What-if scenario, forecast or preset → the ScoreRequest it stands for ('Run exact') GuidedCompile ScoreRequest 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE POST /v1/guided/prior-translations Business priors → model-space priors + prior predictive (a translate_priors run) PriorTranslationRequest PriorTranslation 202 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID, CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED GET /v1/guided/prior-translations/{run_id} The translation run and, once done, its priors and preview — PriorTranslation 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text:
An endpoint is a stable alias (endpoint://<project>/<alias>) for one model version. PUT promotes a version: the promotion gate (PromotionGateDecision) allows a passing scorecard, asks for override: true with a reason from a signed-in project admin when it warns (409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED; the override is audited as endpoint.promote_override), and blocks a failing one (409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED). The endpoint's EvaluationPolicy requires evaluate_then_refit fits by default and blocks input-schema changes that would break callers. POST …/score takes an EndpointScoreCall (a score request without model, whose data and scenario may be inline XrJSON datasets up to 5 MB) and answers like …:score on a model version: Prefer: wait=60 gives 200 with the result when it is done in time, otherwise 202 with the run. A score:<alias> token may read the endpoint, its schema, history and snippets, and score it; endpoints:promote tokens may promote and roll back but never override the gate.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/endpoints Endpoints of the project — Page[Endpoint] 200 — GET /v1/endpoints/{alias} An endpoint and the version it serves — Endpoint 200 NOT_FOUND PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} Create or promote (gated on the scorecard; override = admin + reason, audited) EndpointPromote Endpoint 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT, PROMOTION_BLOCKED, OVERRIDE_REQUIRED DELETE /v1/endpoints/{alias} Delete the alias (model versions stay) — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/history Promotions and rollbacks, newest first — Page[EndpointRevision] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score Score the current version (Prefer: wait=N → 200 if done, else 202 with the run) EndpointScoreCall ScoreCallResult 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/schema Input schema of the current version and an example payload — EndpointSchema 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/validate Static checks of a score call without running it EndpointScoreCall EndpointValidation 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/rollback Point the alias back at an earlier revision's version (audited) EndpointRollback Endpoint 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, Atlas and notebook code for the endpoint — SnippetSet 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
POST /v1/webhooks returns the signing secret once (WebhookCreated). Deliveries carry a WebhookEnvelope and the header Mapi-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>; see Integrations for verification and the SSRF policy. Managing webhooks needs a project admin or a webhooks:manage token.

docs.title: Saved plots, rendering and embeds
docs.text:
A SavedPlot keeps a model version's plot or a user-authored PlotSpec. Rendering (PlotRenderRequest → PlotRender) produces PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox. Embed links (PlotEmbedCreate → PlotEmbedCreated, listed as PlotEmbed) are tokenised, read-only and expire; only plots of platform recipes can be embedded (422 EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED). The public GET /v1/embeds/{embed_token} returns an EmbedView with every dataset inline, or 410 LINK_EXPIRED; it reads no credential and answers cross-origin reads from the plot sandbox origin only. See Sharing plots.

docs.title: Sign-up, verification, deletion and export
docs.text:
Self-service sign-up (SignupRequest → SignupAccepted) answers the same for new and known addresses. Verifying the e-mail (EmailVerify → VerificationResult) creates a public-tier tenant. VerificationStatus says whether the tenant may upload code: never for public tenants before cut line B, and only after identity verification (operators record it with VerificationUpdate). Deletion is scheduled with a grace period during which the tenant is suspended and can cancel (TenantDeletionRequest → TenantDeletion, with progress per store); a GDPR export (GdprExportRequest → GdprExport) packages everything the tenant stored.

creates a public-tier tenant EmailVerify VerificationResult 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, LINK_EXPIRED, RATE_LIMITED GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification E-mail and identity verification, and whether code upload is allowed — VerificationStatus 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification Record identity verification (operators; audited) VerificationUpdate VerificationStatus 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Schedule deletion of the whole tenant (grace period, then purge) TenantDeletionRequest TenantDeletion 202 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Deletion state and progress per store — TenantDeletion 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Cancel a scheduled deletion (within the grace period) — TenantDeletion 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports GDPR export of everything the tenant stored GdprExportRequest GdprExport 202 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, QUOTA_EXCEEDED GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports The tenant's GDPR exports, newest first (GET one for its download link) — Page[GdprExport] 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports/{export_id} An export and, once ready, its download link — GdprExport 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/signups Sign-ups, newest first; filter by review state (the Sybil review queue) or tenant_id — Page[SignupReview] 200 FORBIDDEN POST /v1/admin/signups/{signup_id}/review Approve or reject a sign-up (a rejection suspends its tenant; audited) SignupReviewDecision SignupReview 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT POST /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion/retry Restart a failed tenant purge (operators; audited) — TenantDeletion 202 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT

docs.title: Built-in models
docs.text:
These model plugins ship with the platform (tier T0). They register through the mapi.models entry point, so default_registry() and the control-plane catalog list them without any configuration. Every one passes the contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model) and all but mmm.bayesinsight have a conformance fixture (see Conformance corpus); the BayesInsight model is exercised end to end by the import test of the Guided data path instead.

Calibration (M3, the spec's calibration block, Guided task 3) is declared per plugin in Capabilities.calibration; a spec with calibration data for a plugin that does not declare it fails static validation with CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED:

Plugin Business priors Lift tests mmm.hierarchical_geo yes - beta_channel and intercept priors yes - with carry-over inside the test window mmm.pymc_marketing yes - saturation_beta, intercept (and narrowed gamma_control/gamma_fourier) priors yes - pymc-marketing's add_lift_test_measurements mmm.bayesinsight no - its priors are already in KPI units: state them in model_def.json yes - the incremental KPI under the model's own likelihood

The math of the translation and of each lift likelihood is in Guided modelling.

Plugin Package Representation Score modes Corpus fixture mmm.hierarchical_geo@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, simulate, evaluate e33 mmm.pymc_marketing@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate pymc_marketing mmm.bayesinsight@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, simulate, evaluate – (contract kit and the BayesInsight import test) ts.hsgp_trend@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, evaluate c08 ts.gaussian_hmm@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, filter, evaluate e24 tabular.hierarchical_glm@1 mapi-plugin-tabular draws predict, counterfactual, evaluate e02 tabular.regressor@1 mapi-plugin-tabular quantiles predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate xgb_store_demand choice.multinomial_logit@1 mapi-plugin-tabular draws (Bayesian bootstrap) predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate e84_lite

Plugins use canonical names for their inputs; bind your dataset's names onto them in the spec's data.bind block. Outputs come back under your names (reverse binding) unless they are new variables such as y_hat.

The mapi-sklearn package also registers five general-purpose tabular plugins, sklearn.tabular_regressor, sklearn.tabular_quantiles, sklearn.tabular_bootstrap, sklearn.tabular_conformal and sklearn.tabular_classifier; see Tabular models.

Every setting, generated

The models catalog is generated from the installed manifests: capabilities, outputs, derived quantities, every setting with its default and Guided-mode level, and the input data contract.

docs.title: mmm.hierarchical_geo: geo marketing mix
docs.text:
A hierarchical marketing-mix model: adstock over a core.lag_tensor spend tensor, logistic or Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, a hierarchical intercept and controls. New geos are drawn from the fitted hyperprior. Contributions are additive and, with outputs.derived, the fit caches contributions, per-draw response curves and marginal costs in original units. It declares a decision objective for budget optimisation.

Inputs. y(geo, time), spend(geo, channel, time, lag) from core.lag_tensor (the adstock.l_max setting must equal the step's l_max), and any other numeric variable along time as a control. geo is new_levels (hyperprior), channel is fixed, time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(geo, time) and contributions(component, geo, time) (one component per channel, baseline and one per control; they sum to y_hat).

Read the marketing-mix guide for the model, its priors and a complete spec.

docs.title: mmm.pymc_marketing: the pymc-marketing adapter
docs.text:
Runs pymc_marketing.mmm.MMM behind the platform. The model scales data, carries spend over and reports original units itself, so the plugin declares owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units] and the platform skips its own versions of those. Bundles store the posterior, pymc-marketing's fit_data and its JSON model description, never a pickle. Markets are a fixed dim: pymc-marketing cannot score a market it has not seen. See the adapter section.

Priors and calibration. settings.priors hands prior overrides to pymc-marketing's model_config, in its scaled units (the KPI divided by its maximum): saturation_beta (the channel effect, one parameter per channel; saturation_b for saturation: none), intercept, gamma_control and gamma_fourier. Business priors are translated into them on prior draws of pymc-marketing's own model, so its scaling, adstock and curves are exactly the fit's: a log-normal saturation_beta per channel matches each ROI or contribution-share range at its credibility, a Normal intercept the baseline share, and the control and seasonality priors are narrowed when they alone spread the baseline share wider than the range (an info issue says by how much). A translate_priors run previews them; a fit without one translates them itself (learned.calibration.translated_priors). Lift tests go through pymc-marketing's add_lift_test_measurements (the saturation curve, no carry-over).

docs.title: mmm.bayesinsight: a BayesInsight model_def.json
docs.text:
Fits a BayesInsight model exactly as its model_def.json defines it - the dedicated target of the BayesInsight import (POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight with "target": "mmm.bayesinsight"; see Guided mode). The settings carry model_def (typed by mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model), map every analytic variable name to its model-stage variable and list the panel dims (the model's row ids besides Period).

Inputs. The KPI y(*panel, time) as stored (BayesInsight does not rescale it; priors are in its units), every media variable as a core.lag_tensor with pad: nan (the history before a series starts carries no media, BayesInsight's zero-padded convolution) and the controls along (*panel, time). Panel dims are new_levels (pooled); time extends.

Model. eta = intercept + Σ media + Σ controls + Σ seasons + Σ trends:

Feature model_def.json Semantics Likelihood exog.likelihood.type Normal, LogNormal (on eta), Poisson, NegativeBinomial, ZeroInflatedPoisson, ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial (log link, exp(clip(eta, -20, 20))); none given means Poisson, as in BayesInsight. likelihood_params parametrise the dispersion prior, dispersion_dims vary it by row id Coefficients coeff_prior, intercept_prior Any of Normal, Laplace, StudentT, Uniform, HalfNormal, HalfCauchy, Exponential, LogNormal, Gamma, Beta with its parameters, in KPI units; defaults are BayesInsight's (LogNormal(log 0.05, log 1.3) for media, Normal(0, 3) otherwise) Effects per row id fixed_ind_coeff_dims, random_coeff_dims One coefficient per level combination of the fixed row ids, plus sigma * z per level combination of the random ones with sigma ~ HalfNormal(partial_pooling_sigma) (0, BayesInsight's default, pools nothing). New levels at score time get the pooled value; a coefficient estimated per level of a dim has none for a new level (UNSEEN_LEVELS) Signs sign Enforced (BayesInsight declares but does not enforce them): real priors are truncated at 0, positive priors negated for negative, random effects multiplicative so no level crosses zero. Media are always positive Media curve media_transform, media_transform_prior First the curve on transform(x) / index (index: each series' non-zero median or mean, index_to): hill (K ~ LogNormal, n = 1 + Exponential), linear, or the S-shaped curve of an SShaped prior, anchored so no spend has no effect Carry-over adstock, adstock_prior Then delayed (alpha^((l - theta)^2)), geometric (alpha^l), weibull (pymc-marketing's PDF or CDF weights, a Weibull prior) or none, over l_max lags, normalised to sum to one Controls deterministic_transform, normalization linear, log, exp, indexp, power; Global Standardize over the fit window (or the stored mean/std) Seasons season n_fourier cos/sin pairs of period, one coefficient each, on BayesInsight's time grid Local trends localtrend A B-spline basis (num_knots, order) with Gaussian-random-walk coefficients, per level of random_coeff_dims or grouped by grouping_map; forecasts hold the last fitted level

Where BayesInsight's own code cannot run a feature it defines (geometric and Weibull carry-over, the S-shaped curve, linear media, the zero-inflated negative binomial's psi), the plugin's choice is documented on mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model and the import reports it as an info issue. MvNormal likelihoods, time transforms (moving averages) and event priors are not supported: the import falls back to BayesInsight's defaults with an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning.

Outputs. y_hat(*panel, time) - the expected KPI (eta for a Normal likelihood, exp(eta + sigma^2 / 2) for a log-normal, the count mean times the zero-inflation share) or, predictive, a draw of the likelihood with common random numbers where the family allows - and contributions(component, *panel, time): each media variable, baseline (the intercepts), each control, season and trend. They sum to y_hat: additive terms for a Normal likelihood, a log-mean Divisia split of E[y] - baseline for the others, exact for terms of either sign.

Calibration. Lift tests (channel: a media variable's analytic or model-stage name, geo: a label of the first panel dim) observe the incremental KPI Σ E[y | x + dx] - E[y | x] over the test window under the model's own likelihood, with the extra spend spread in proportion to the actual spend and carried over. Business priors are not supported: BayesInsight's coefficient priors are already statements in KPI units.

Response curves, marginal costs and the decision objective are not offered yet, so the Guided what-if sliders and the scorecard's ROI checks skip this model (they say so).

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend — smooth trend with seasonality
docs.text:
A Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) trend plus an optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality, for one regularly spaced series (Mauna-Loa style CO2, sales, traffic).

Inputs. t (time, policy extend) and the target y(t). Missing months are allowed: replace sentinel codes with core.replace_sentinel and they are left out of the likelihood while the model still interpolates them. Put core.standardize on y; the priors are on the standardised scale and outputs are mapped back to your units.

Forecast horizon. max_extension (default 24 periods) is part of the model's input schema. The HSGP domain is sized at fit time from the anticipated coordinates (the fitted range plus max_extension periods), so every forecast up to that horizon evaluates exactly the fitted functions. A longer horizon is rejected before any compute with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (HTTP 409): refit with a larger max_extension.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 24 Periods a forecast may reach past the fit without a refit kernel expquad expquad, matern52 or matern32 m, c 30, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation lengthscale_mu, lengthscale_sigma 0.4, 0.5 Log-normal lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] eta_sigma 1.0 Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude linear_trend true Add intercept + slope * t season_period, season_order 12, 3 Fourier seasonality (periods of t, order) noise_sigma 0.5 Half-normal scale of the observation noise

Outputs. y_hat(t) (expected value or a predictive draw) and trend(t), the long-term component without seasonality, both in the target's units.

data:
  bind: {dims: {t: date}, vars: {y: co2}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 12}
pipeline:
  - {id: clean, use: core.replace_sentinel@^1, with: {vars: [y], below: 0}}
  - {id: scale, use: core.standardize@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [t]}}
model:
  use: ts.hsgp_trend@^1
  settings: {max_extension: 24, season_order: 2}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: pymc, seed: 11}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm — hidden states with a terminal state
docs.text:
A K-state Gaussian hidden Markov model over many sequences at once (animal tracks, machine regimes, customer phases). Hidden states are summed out with the forward algorithm, so sampling is fast and exact.

Inputs. Padded layout: animal (the sequence dim, new_levels with strategy pooled), step (extend), y(animal, step) with NaN padding and a boolean mask(animal, step).

Terminal state. After the fit the filtered state distribution at the last fitted step is stored as the bundle's terminal_state group, alpha_T(chain, draw, animal, state).

  • predict / evaluate use the one-step-ahead state distribution of the fit inside the fitted range and alpha_T propagated by the transition matrix after it; they never look at targets in the payload.
  • forecast propagates alpha_T over the horizon.
  • filter runs the forward filter over new observations that continue the fitted steps and returns an updated terminal_state group with the filtered state_prob.
  • New animals start from the initial distribution pi at the first fitted step.

Draws are relabelled after sampling so that the state means increase (label switching); identification: ordered uses an ordered prior instead. Pointwise LOO is declared invalid (elpd_loo is rejected at validation): steps within a track are dependent.

Setting Default Meaning n_states 2 Number of hidden states mu_center, mu_sigma 0.0, 2.0 Normal prior of the state means sigma_scale 1.0 Half-normal scale of the per-state sds stickiness 2.0 Extra Dirichlet weight on staying in a state pi_concentration 1.0 Dirichlet weight of the initial distribution identification relabel relabel (sort draws by mean) or ordered

Outputs. y_hat(animal, step) in your units and state_prob(animal, step, state) (units probability, never inverse-transformed).

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm — partial pooling in long layout
docs.text:
Varying intercepts (and optionally slopes) by group with group-level predictors: the radon model and its many relatives (schools, stores, clinics).

Inputs. Long layout: rows along obs (extend), a group dim (group_dim, default county, new_levels with strategy hyperprior), the index <group_dim>_idx(obs), the target y(obs), observation-level covariates and group-level group_covariates. Covariates are part of the input schema, so a spec naming a missing one fails validation.

New groups. A county the model never saw is drawn from the fitted hyperprior for every posterior draw; its group-level covariates shift its prior mean exactly as for fitted counties. Score payloads may list counties in any order: the platform remaps county_idx.

Setting Default Meaning group_dim county The grouping dim family normal normal, student_t, poisson (log link) or bernoulli (logit) covariates [] Predictors over obs varying_slopes [] Covariates whose slope varies by group group_covariates [] Predictors over the group dim centered false Centred group effects

docs.title: tabular.regressor — quantile regression for panels
docs.text:
The plan's store-demand model: rows are stacked from labelled dims (store × sku × week), the coordinates become categorical features, and an allow-listed estimator predicts conditional quantiles. Its estimator setting accepts exactly the quantile-capable estimators of the registry (xgboost, scikit-learn's gradient boosting and histogram boosting, and quantile regression), so other estimators are rejected at validation.

  • Defaults: xgboost (300 trees, depth 5, learning rate 0.05) and quantiles [0.1, 0.5, 0.9].
  • New stores are pooled (new_levels: pooled); forecasting is direct, so future covariates marked future_required must be supplied (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE otherwise).
  • Quantiles are per cell: aggregating them across stores is refused (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • The manifest lists core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time and ml.feature_importance.

All other settings are those of mapi_sklearn (see Tabular models).

docs.title: choice.multinomial_logit — which product customers pick
docs.text:
The built-in model of the Guided customer choice template (E84-style household panels): on every shopping trip a household picks one product, and price and promotions shift the choice.

Inputs. A dense hh × trip panel - hh (categorical, new_levels with strategy hyperprior), trip (index, extend) - with the alternatives along product (categorical, fixed). The target y(hh, trip) is text: the product chosen, empty where a household made no trip (ragged panels are fine). Covariates are alternative-specific variables along product, such as price(hh, trip, product) and promo(hh, trip, product); by default every numeric variable with the product dim is one. A product whose covariates are missing on a trip was not available on that trip (off the shelf).

Model. A conditional logit with household-specific product intercepts: U[h, t, j] = asc[j] + Σ_k beta[k]·x_k[h, t, j] + u[h, j], the choice probabilities a softmax over the available products, u[h, j] ~ Normal(0, effect_sd) (a random-intercept logit). It is fitted by penalised maximum likelihood, the posterior mode of that model. Uncertainty comes from the Bayesian bootstrap: each of fit.draws draws refits with Dirichlet weights on households, so every household keeps its own effect in every draw and the draws are joint (draws representation: shares, counterfactual deltas and sums over trips are valid). There is no pointwise log-likelihood, so LOO is not offered.

Scoring. y_hat(hh, trip, product) is the choice probability (expected) or one sampled choice per draw (predictive, one-hot). A household never seen at fit draws its preferences from Normal(0, sd) per draw, sd being the spread of the fitted effects in that draw. Trips never made have probability 0 for every product, so sums over trips count expected purchases. Price scenarios are interventions, e.g. {var: price, sel: {product: cola}, multiply: 1.1} in a counterfactual request. Choice values match product labels after lower-casing and replacing punctuation with _.

Setting Default Meaning covariates every numeric variable along product Alternative-specific covariates random_effects [hh] Household product intercepts ([]: none) effect_sd 1.0 Prior sd of the household effects (smaller pools more) coef_sd 10.0 Prior sd of the product intercepts and coefficients reference the first product The product whose intercept is fixed at 0 max_iter 500 Iterations of each L-BFGS fit

fit.draws (default 100, at most 2000) sets the bootstrap draws and fit.seed makes them reproducible. The in-sample hit rate is reported as the CHOICE_HIT_RATE diagnostic.

Holdout metrics. A text target scored as one probability per product gets the categorical metrics of evaluate.metrics: accuracy (the hit rate of the most likely product), accuracy_naive (always guessing the holdout's most common product), accuracy_lift (their difference), log_score (mean log probability of the product bought) and brier (multi-class Brier score). The Guided customer_choice template evaluates all five on each household's last trip and its scorecard runs holdout.hit_rate; numeric metrics such as mape are skipped for a text target.

docs.title: OpenAPI explorer v0.2
docs.text:
The /v1 API's OpenAPI 3.1 document, rendered with Redoc. It is the committed apps/web/openapi.json, generated from the server's own FastAPI app and the mapi_spec.api models (uv run python apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py); CI fails when it drifts from the server. A running API serves the same document at /openapi.json.

Open full screen Download openapi.json

The explorer loads nothing from outside this site: the Redoc bundle (version 2.5.4) is vendored by scripts/vendor_redoc.py, which checks the npm tarball's integrity and pins the bundle's SHA-256, and a Content-Security-Policy on the page allows scripts, styles, images and requests from this site only.

For prose (conventions, idempotency, server-sent events, which errors each endpoint returns) read the HTTP API reference; for a worked example, the HTTP API guide.

docs.title: Plots reference (mapi-plots)
docs.text:
mapi-plots has two halves with different dependency footprints:

Install Modules Imports Runs in mapi-plots mapi_plots.sanitize, mapi_plots.templates mapi-spec, jsonschema (JSON only) API server, runner, notebooks mapi-plots[recipes] mapi_plots.convert, mapi_plots.recipes, mapi_plots.packs, mapi_plots.examples + altair, plotly, numpy, pandas, pyarrow, xarray runner images, notebooks

An import-linter contract keeps the sanitizer and templates free of numpy, pandas, xarray, pyarrow, altair, plotly and mapi_sdk, and import mapi_plots loads nothing heavy (exports are lazy).

docs.title: The PlotSpec envelope
docs.text:
Defined in mapi_spec.plots (the contract package):

id: core.ppc_fan                    # [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}
title: Fit and forecast
kind: vega-lite                     # or plotly
spec: {...}                         # Vega-Lite JSON, or Plotly {data, layout, frames, config}
datasets:                           # referenced BY NAME only
  fan: {kind: inline_arrow, data: <base64 Arrow IPC stream>, rows: 84}
  big: {kind: data_ref, path: ui/plotdata/fan.arrow, format: arrow}
bindings: {x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}   # templates only
schema_version: v6.4.1
persona: both                       # guided | expert | both
caption_plain: "The line is the model's median estimate ..."
provenance: {recipe: core.ppc_fan@1.0.0, bundle_id: ..., generated_at: ...}
  • Vega-Lite references data with {"data": {"name": "fan"}}.
  • Plotly references a column with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"} in any data-array attribute (and in arrayOk attributes such as marker.color). The part before the first . is the dataset; the rest is the column (trace0.marker.color → dataset trace0, column marker.color). Its JSON Schema ships as mapi_plots.sanitize.PLOTLY_REF_SCHEMA and as the file mapi_plots/sanitize/schemas/plotly-ref.schema.json:
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "urn:mapi:schema:plotly-dataset-ref:v1",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {"$ref": {"type": "string",
    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{0,63}\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]{0,127}$"}},
  "required": ["$ref"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • Inline Arrow datasets are at most 2 MiB of base64 each. Recipe datasets are written compactly (float32, int32, dictionary-encoded strings); timestamps are UTC milliseconds.

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot, check_plot, sanitize_spec, SanitizeLimits

result = sanitize_plot(doc)            # PlotSpec | dict | JSON str | bytes
result.plot                            # validated, sanitized PlotSpec
result.changes                         # list[Issue] (severity info): HTML stripped, $schema pinned ...

issues = check_plot(doc)               # errors + changes, never raises
spec, changes = sanitize_spec("plotly", figure_dict)   # bare spec, no envelope

SanitizeError is a MapiError; err.issues lists every violation (capped at max_issues), each with an RFC 6901 pointer, a platform-written message, the rule in context["rule"] and any user-supplied text only in untrusted_text. err.rules is the set of rules that fired. The error code is the most severe present:

Code HTTP Rules PLOT_UNSAFE 422 url_data, href, external_image, tile_map, proto_key, script_url, css_url, expression, format_type, config PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 too_large, too_deep, too_many_nodes, string_too_long, array_too_long SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 parse (invalid JSON, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity) SCHEMA_INVALID 422 schema, envelope, dataset_ref, typed_array

Changes (never errors) use the rules html_stripped, schema_url and template_pruned.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: SanitizeLimits field Default max_document_bytes 16 MiB (whole PlotSpec, inline Arrow included) max_spec_bytes 2 MiB (the spec member) max_depth 48 max_nodes 200 000 max_string_bytes 64 KiB (inline Arrow payloads are capped by the envelope instead) max_array_items 100 000 max_expr_chars 2 000 max_typed_array_bytes 8 MiB max_issues 50

docs.title: Vega-Lite rules
docs.text:
1. $schema must be an official Vega-Lite v5 or v6 URL (or absent); it is pinned to v6.4.1.
  2. The spec must validate against the vendored Vega-Lite v6.4.1 JSON Schema (draft-07, local $refs only).
  3. No url key anywhere; no href; no image mark; formatType only number, time or utc; config.customFormatTypes must not be enabled.
  4. Expressions — expr, calculate, filter/test strings (and their and/or/not compositions), any …Expr key such as labelExpr, and bracketed filters inside selection event streams — must use only allow-listed Vega functions. Method calls, this/new, assignment, statements, template and regex literals, \u/\x escapes, non-ASCII outside strings, computed member access with a non-literal key, browser globals (window, document, fetch, globalThis …) and event.view are rejected.

docs.title: Plotly rules
docs.text:
1. Top level has only data, layout, frames and config.
  2. Trace types, attribute names and value types are checked against a table derived from the official plotly.js 4.1.1 plot-schema.json (enumerations, flag lists, subplot ids, colour scales, info arrays; xaxis2-style subplot keys; annotationdefaults-style keys in templates). Unknown attributes are errors — except inside layout.template, where they (and tile-map sections) are pruned and reported.
  3. Data arrays are inline lists, dataset references or plotly.py typed arrays ({dtype: i1|u1|u1c|i2|u2|i4|u4|f4|f8, bdata, shape?}, validated for base64, length and shape).
  4. Tile-map traces/subplots, non-data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64 image sources (also inside updatemenus/sliders relayout arguments), url/href/topojsonURL keys and network config options are rejected.
  5. Strings are stripped to <b> <i> <br> <sub> <sup> (attributes dropped, stray < escaped); <extra> survives in hover templates.

docs.title: Vendored schemas

docs.text:
resolve_bindings(bindings, schema, *, optional=()) -> dict[channel, BoundField | list[BoundField]]
apply_template(plot, schema, *, optional=(), title=None) -> PlotSpec
template_issues(plot, schema, *, optional=()) -> list[Issue]
Binding Resolves to Vega-Lite type dim:<name> a dim of the schema time → temporal, numeric → quantitative, ordered/index → ordinal, else nominal role:<role> the single variable with that role (lists for tooltip) from the dtype var:<name> that variable from the dtype coord:<name> a coordinate (dim or not) from the dim, else nominal stat:<name> a summary statistic column (mean, hdi_90_lower, q5 …) quantitative

docs.title: Recipes (mapi_plots.recipes)
docs.text:
get_recipe(id) -> Recipe                 # bundled recipes (core + packs)
standard_recipes() -> list[Recipe]       # entry point  mapi.plots: core
mapi_plots.packs.mmm.mmm_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: mmm
mapi_plots.packs.ml.ml_recipes()         # entry point  mapi.plots: ml
Recipe.render(data, **settings) -> PlotSpec       # also Recipe(data, **settings)
Recipe.catalog_entry() -> PlotCatalogEntry        # id, version, persona, required groups/representation

# what the runner calls for outputs.plots: never raises for a single bad plot
report = render_plots(tree, ["core.ppc_fan", "mmm.response_curves@^1"],
                      registry=None, options={"core.ppc_fan": {"facet": "market"}})
report.plots          # sanitized PlotSpecs
report.issues         # skipped plots: REF_UNRESOLVED / SCHEMA_INVALID / USER_CODE_ERROR
                      # (warnings) and PLOT_UNSAFE (error)
report.to_json()      # plots.json sidecar body

Write your own with the decorator — the result works with Registry.register and the mapi.plots entry-point group:

import altair as alt
from mapi_plots.recipes import Figure, RecipeSettings, named, recipe


class Settings(RecipeSettings):
    var: str = "y_hat"


@recipe("acme.weekly_total", title="Weekly total", settings=Settings, persona="guided")
def weekly_total(inp, s: Settings) -> Figure:
    ds = inp.require("summary")
    frame = ds[s.var].sel(stat="mean").sum("market").to_dataframe().reset_index()
    chart = alt.Chart(named("weekly")).mark_line().encode(x="date:T", y=f"{s.var}:Q")
    return Figure(chart, {"weekly": frame}, caption=f"Total {s.var} per week.")
