docs.title: Fit and score
docs.text:
The fit/score harness: the platform side of every run (plan §4.2).

:func:fit_spec implements fit.mode:

  • bind the data, validate it, fit the stateless prefix on all data up to the split stage;
  • split; fit the remaining step states and the model on train (the evaluation fit);
  • evaluate the holdout through the score path (context from train) - never a separate code path - and compute the spec's metrics;
  • evaluate_then_refit: refit states and model on train ∪ holdout so the context tails and terminal state come from the full data; the production bundle links the evaluation bundle and its metrics. train_only keeps the train fit as the result.
  • derived quantities the spec requests (outputs.derived) whose manifest declaration says cache: fit are computed on the production fit by the plugin's derive hook, over the first outputs.ui_draws draws of the thinning index, with ScoreContext.to_original mapping them to the output space.

:func:score_bundle implements scoring: CoordPlan checks, binding, interventions, entry at inputs_stage, context replay, canonical coords, model.score, context removal, selection, inverse transforms to the output space, aggregation, summaries, thinned draws and reverse binding. It returns an xr.DataTree.

score_bundle(
    bundle: Bundle,
    request: ScoreRequest | str,

    history: Dataset | None = None,
) -> DataTree

Score a fitted bundle; returns a DataTree.

data is the request's data payload and scenario its scenario payload. Outside counterfactuals a scenario simply is the payload. A counterfactual scores the scenario (or the data, when no scenario is given) with the interventions applied against the baseline data; a scenario without baseline data is rejected.

Groups: summary (stats along a stat dim), draws (when requested; joint, from the bundle thinning index), predictions (full representation, when return_full), and for counterfactuals baseline/... and delta/.... Root attrs carry the representation, output kind, units/output space, retransformation labels, non-error issues and - in evaluate mode - the metrics. observed (evaluation of cell-level splits) gives the observed targets for metrics when data has them masked. history (M3) is the fitted dataset (dataset names): forecasts whose future_covariates policy is carry_last or seasonal_naive extend the covariates the payload lacks from it (:mod:mapi_sdk.future).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
The preprocessing step contract: Step, StepState and StepContext.

A step is a class with static metadata (id, version, kind, a Pydantic Settings model, an optional State model) and four methods::

fit(ds, settings, ctx) -> State           # learn on train data only
transform(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds # never learns; must tolerate an absent target
inverse(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds   # invertible VALUE steps only

Rules the contract kit (:mod:mapi_sdk.testing) enforces:

  • transform(train, fit(train)) equals the fit-time output exactly, and transform is deterministic and does not mutate its input;
  • reductions name the dims they reduce over; the state stays labelled by the rest;
  • group-local operations take along/within and declare a :class:ContextNeed;
  • unseen levels go through :meth:StepContext.align_state;
  • the static :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect (effect_template) matches the real output schema.

The static metadata is exported as a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.StepCatalogEntry, so the control plane validates specs without importing step code.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
The model plugin contract (plan §5).

A plugin turns a model-stage xr.Dataset into a :class:FitOutput and, later, scores a canonicalised dataset into an xr.DataTree whose predictions group holds the declared outputs in the plugin's :class:~mapi_spec.capabilities.Representation::

draws      (chain, draw, *dims)
quantiles  (quantile, *dims)       quantile coords in (0, 1)
interval   (bound, *dims)          bound coords include "lower", "upper" (+ "point")
point      (*dims)
moments    (moment, *dims)         moment coords ["mean", "sd"]

The platform owns everything around that: binding, CoordPlan, context, canonical coords, inverse transforms, reverse binding and summaries. :class:CustomModel is the base class for hand-written plugins; mapi_pymc.PyMCModel and mapi_sklearn.SklearnModel build on the same protocol.

var_sources maps each output variable to the input variable whose transforms it inherits (y_hat -> y). Inversion stops at to_stage (default: the last RESHAPE stage) or at the first non-invertible step that touched the variable. Point outputs through a non-linear inverse are labelled median (plain inverse) or use Duan's smearing over stored model-space residuals; moments use the first-order delta method (g(mu), |g'(mu)| sd with a central difference).

decompositions name additive decompositions (contributions(component, ...)). They are inverted component by component only through additive steps (Step.additive); through any other inverse (expm1, x * sd + mean) the components would no longer sum to the inverted prediction, so inversion stops right after that step and :attr:InverseResult.kept says why.

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text:
Fitted-model bundles: one bundle.zarr.zip DataTree plus JSON sidecars (plan §8.6).

Layout of bundle.zarr.zip::

/                       attrs: format, bundle_id, role
/spec                   attrs: spec (canonical JSON), resolved (ResolvedSpec JSON)
/schema/raw             attrs: json (dataset-named raw DataSchema)
/schema/model           attrs: json (model input schema, effective policies)
/binding                attrs: json
/preprocess/<step_id>   attrs: state (JSON); children: arrays, context
/model                  attrs: manifest, settings, fit_config, learned (JSON)
/model/<group>          ArviZ-named groups (posterior, sample_stats, log_likelihood ...)
/terminal_state         plugin-owned state for sequential models
/native                 uint8 arrays of safe native artifacts (skops, xgb json, ...)
/derived/<name>         derived quantities cached at fit
/fit_coords/<stage>     coordinates of the fitted data at every stage
/side_tables/<name>     pinned side tables used at fit
/residuals              model-space residuals (point models, smearing)
/thin                   the bundle-wide draw thinning index

Sidecars: manifest.json (content hashes of every file: size, CRC32C and MD5 in the GCS base64 form, SHA-256), diagnostics.json, plots.json and metrics.json. An evaluate_then_refit bundle keeps its train-only evaluation bundle under evaluation/. Pickle is never written and is rejected on read.

  • :class:CoordPlan runs the static checks of :func:mapi_spec.validate.validate_score_request against the bundle's fit coordinates and the actual score payload, raising typed errors (UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, ...).

Reindex model-stage score data to the fit coordinate order.

  • fixed dims: labels must be fit labels (UNSEEN_LEVELS); data is reindexed to the full fit set (padding unrequested labels);
  • new_levels dims: fit labels in fit order, then unseen labels appended (the <dim>__is_new coordinate flags them; strategy error raises);
  • extend dims: labels may not start before the fit range (COORD_NOT_ALLOWED), must continue it without gaps (NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION) and may not exceed max_extension (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT); with pad_extend the full fit range is included so positional models see a contiguous axis.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
Representation-aware summaries, aggregation and draw thinning (plan §5).

Outputs come in one of five representations (see :mod:mapi_sdk.models). Which summaries and aggregations are valid depends on the representation; the rules live in :data:mapi_spec.capabilities.REPRESENTATION_RULES and are enforced here:

  • draws: every summary; any aggregation (applied per draw);
  • quantiles: median/quantiles/ETI (interpolated on the stored quantile grid, never extrapolated); no aggregation;
  • interval: the interval and its point; no aggregation;
  • point: mean/point; linear aggregation only, flagged;
  • moments: mean/sd and normal ETIs; no aggregation.

Summaries are returned as one variable per output with a leading stat dim whose labels read like mean, hdi_90_lower, hdi_90_upper, q5 ... HDIs are computed in numpy (narrowest window over sorted draws).

docs.title: In-process executor
docs.text:
In-process executor (isolation NONE) for notebooks, tests and mapi fit on own code.

Implements the :class:mapi_spec.executor.Executor protocol: submit starts the run in a worker thread, status is the source of truth, cancel is cooperative (checked between pipeline phases) and event_source yields :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent objects. Payloads are JSON only; dataset references are resolved by a resolver.

Supported run kinds: fit (payload spec, data, optional side_tables and raw_schema) and score/evaluate (payload request, bundle - a bundle directory or a key registered with :meth:InprocExecutor.put_bundle - and optional data/scenario/side_tables; otherwise the request's data/scenario refs are used). A counterfactual resolves data as the baseline and scenario as the scenario.

Never use this executor for untrusted code: it runs plugins in the caller's process.

docs.title: Wire formats
docs.text:
Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips, stacking and Arrow IPC.

Encoding rules (plan §3.2), applied by every writer here:

  • any pandas.MultiIndex is reset before persisting (and recorded so readers restore it);
  • string coords and variables are zarr v3 vlen-utf8 (data type string);
  • datetimes are int64 nanoseconds with explicit units and calendar attrs;
  • only the zstd and blosc compressors are written or accepted;
  • :func:stack_rows drops empty rows and records a row mask so :func:unstack_rows restores them.

Pickle (and joblib/cloudpickle) is never used for anything. Readers treat every payload as hostile: zip entries, zarr metadata, codecs, dtypes and sizes are checked before any array is decoded.

docs.text: scikit-learn and xgboost models: write estimator(), get stacking, safe persistence and uncertainty.

docs.title: Base classes
docs.text:
SklearnModel: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators on labelled data (plan §5).

A plugin author implements only :meth:SklearnModel.estimator, returning an allow-listed estimator (a choice from :data:~mapi_sklearn.estimators.ESTIMATORS, a {kind, params} mapping, or an instance of an allow-listed class). The platform:

  1. stacks the rows dims of the model-stage dataset into samples and builds the design matrix from the selected variables and coordinate features (:mod:mapi_sklearn.design), dropping incomplete rows through the SDK row mask;
  2. fits one or more estimators for the plugin's uncertainty kind;
  3. persists them with skops or xgboost JSON (never pickle);
  4. at score time rebuilds the same columns, handles unseen levels (:mod:mapi_sklearn.levels), predicts and unstacks back to labelled arrays in the plugin's representation:

================= ===================== ========================================== base class representation predictions group ================= ===================== ========================================== SklearnModel point y_hat(*rows) (+ contributions) SklearnQuantile quantiles y_hat(quantile, *rows) SklearnBootstrap draws y_hat(chain, draw, *rows) SklearnConformal interval y_hat(bound=[lower, upper, point], *rows) SklearnClassifier point y_hat(*rows) = P(target == positive) ================= ===================== ==========================================

Forecasting is direct only: future features must be supplied (or produced by the pipeline from coordinates); forecast_strategy: recursive raises RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED.

expected outputs are the replicate predictions (uncertainty of the fitted mean); predictive outputs add an out-of-bag residual drawn per cell, approximating the predictive distribution. Draws are joint across cells, so every aggregation is valid.

docs.text:
Settings of the scikit-learn / xgboost model plugins.

A spec's model.settings for sklearn.* plugins looks like::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}
rows: [store, sku, time]               # dims stacked into samples
time_dim: time                         # the row dim that extends at forecast time
columns: {roles: [covariate]}          # which variables become feature columns
coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
uncertainty: {kind: quantile, quantiles: [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]}
forecast_strategy: direct
retransform: median

The uncertainty kind fixes the output representation, so each kind is its own plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles accepts only kind: quantile and so on).

docs.title: Estimator registry
docs.text:
The allow-listed estimator registry.

Plugins never import arbitrary classes. An estimator is chosen by kind from :data:ESTIMATORS, and its hyper-parameters are validated by that kind's Pydantic params model (extra="forbid", bounded values). The platform then builds the estimator with every parameter passed explicitly, so behaviour does not drift when a library changes a default. Parameters the platform owns (seeds, threads, categorical handling and the loss/objective an uncertainty kind needs) are not part of the params models.

In a spec::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}

docs.text:
EstimatorEntry(
    kind: str,
    module: str,
    name: str,
    params: type[Params],
    choice: type[_Choice],
    task: Task,
    persistence: Literal["skops", "xgboost"] = "skops",
    linear: bool = False,
    native_nan: bool = False,
    native_categorical: Literal["xgboost", "sklearn_hist"]
    | None = None,
    quantile: QuantileMode | None = None,
    quantile_setter: Callable[
        [dict[str, Any], float], dict[str, Any]
    ]
    | None = None,
    loss_param: str | None = None,
    quantile_loss: str | None = None,
    seed_param: str | None = "random_state",
    n_jobs_param: str | None = None,
    trusted: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    description: str = "",
)

Static facts about one allow-listed estimator.

linear estimators expose coef_/intercept_ (exact additive contributions); native_nan ones accept missing feature values; native_categorical says how integer-coded categorical columns are declared (xgboost feature types or the categorical_features of sklearn's histogram boosting). quantile says how a quantile model is built: one native multi-quantile model, or one model per level with quantile_setter. loss_param/loss_default/quantile_loss name the loss or objective the quantile mode manages. trusted lists the extra types skops may load.

docs.title: Data schema
docs.text:
Data contract primitives: dims, variables, ragged structure and dataset schemas.

A :class:DataSchema describes an xr.Dataset without any arrays: its dims (each with a :class:DimPolicy saying what may happen to it at score time), its variables (with a :class:Role, dtype, units and missingness) and its ragged structure.

A :class:DataSchemaTemplate is a static JSON function of enumerated settings: plugins export one per model so the control plane can compute the required input schema for given settings without running plugin code.

docs.title: Loading and hashing
docs.text:
Strict YAML 1.2 / JSON loading, apiVersion upgrades, canonical JSON and spec hashing.

The loader is safe for hostile input:

  • size ≤ 256 KB, nesting depth ≤ 32, ≤ 10 000 nodes (all configurable via :class:Limits);
  • YAML anchors, aliases, explicit tags (!foo, !!python/...), %TAG directives and multiple documents are rejected;
  • plain scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema (yes/on/0777/dates stay strings), NaN/Infinity are rejected, duplicate keys are rejected and every mapping key must be a string;
  • JSON input is parsed with the same limits.

:func:load_document returns a typed document (discriminated on kind) after running the apiVersion upgrade chain (the API accepts N and N-1). :func:canonical_json and :func:spec_hash give a normalised, deterministic serialisation for immutable revisions.

The :class:Representation of a model's output decides which aggregations and summaries are statistically valid. docs.title: Schema effects and stages
docs.text:
Step kinds, SchemaEffects, context needs and static schema propagation.

A :class:SchemaEffect is a data-free description of how a preprocessing step changes a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema. Step authors export it as JSON (per image digest); the control plane evaluates it with :func:propagate and never imports step code.

Effects may be templates: strings can reference the step's settings with the :mod:~mapi_spec.template placeholder syntax ("{dim}", "{*vars as v}"). Every referenced setting must be listed in template_params. :func:resolve_effect renders a template with concrete settings into a plain :class:SchemaEffect.

Within one effect, operations apply in this order: renames → drops → transforms_dims → stacks → unstacks → updates → derives → adds.

docs.title: Static validation
docs.text:
Static (JSON-only) validation of ModelSpecs and ScoreRequests.

:func:validate_spec checks a :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ModelSpec against a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.Catalog and the dataset's raw :class:DataSchema:

  1. binding references exist and do not collide;
  2. every use: resolves to a non-yanked version (semver range);
  3. step and model settings validate against their JSON Schemas;
  4. side-table references exist;
  5. the schema is propagated through every step's SchemaEffect, with per-step input checks;
  6. the split stage is resolved (default: end of the stateless prefix), its dims exist there, and LEAKAGE_RISK is raised if a stateful step precedes it;
  7. the model's schema template is resolved and compared with the final stage; spec dim policies may only tighten the plugin's;
  8. recursive forecasting (a target-dependent lag feeding a longer holdout) is rejected unless the model owns recursion; outputs, plots, metrics and resource class are checked.

:func:validate_score_request runs the static CoordPlan checks for a ScoreRequest from metadata only (resolved spec + fit coordinate summaries + dim policies).

Every finding is an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer into the document.

docs.title: Run protocol
docs.text:
See Run protocol for the narrative specification.

The run protocol (plan §8.1, §8.3–§8.7): state machine, bootstrap, events, manifests.

Everything a control plane, an executor and a runner must agree on lives here, as pure Pydantic / stdlib code:

  • :class:RunState, :class:RunTrigger and the transition table :data:TRANSITIONS, with the pure function :func:transition used by the API, dispatcher, events service, reconciler, finalizer and tests;
  • :class:RunSpec — the bootstrap object written to bootstrap/<nonce> before an execution starts (signed URLs, a per-run HMAC key, limits, deadline);
  • :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent payload models, canonical HMAC-SHA256 signing and verification, and the stdout JSONL wire format ({"mapi_event": {...}} per line);
  • :class:OutputManifest (the runner's claim), metadata-only verification against server-computed hashes, and the platform-signed :class:BundleManifest;
  • the runner invocation contract: environment (:class:RunnerEnv) and exit codes (:class:RunnerExit).

Executor-facing shapes (:class:Isolation, :class:ExecutorCaps, :class:Handle, :class:ExecStatus, :class:RunKind, :class:RunEvent, ...) are defined in :mod:mapi_spec.executor and re-exported here unchanged, so both import paths name the same classes.

docs.title: Job payloads
docs.text:
See Job payloads and object names.

Run job payloads: what RunSpec.spec holds for each run kind, plus the input and output object names shared by the control plane (which writes RunSpecs and reads outputs) and the runner (which reads RunSpecs and writes outputs).

========== ============================================ ====================================== kind RunSpec.spec inputs (RunSpec.inputs names) ========== ============================================ ====================================== ingest :class:IngestJob (a bare IngestMapping upload (the raw file; dataset is also accepted) is accepted as a fallback) describe :class:DescribeJob none validate a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> fit a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> score a ScoreRequest document, or bundle, optional :class:ScoreJob bundle.manifest, dataset (the request's data), scenario, side.<name>, history (M3: the fit dataset, for carry_last / seasonal_naive future covariates) evaluate :class:EvaluateJob bundle, dataset, ... derive :class:DeriveJob bundle, dataset, side.<name> render :class:RenderJob plots (a plots.json) translate_ :class:~mapi_spec.calibration.Prior- ``dataset``, optional ``schema``, priors TranslationJob (M3) side.<name>; output priors.json ========== ============================================ ======================================

Datasets are single-object *.zarr.zip files. A dataset's raw schema comes from the schema input, else the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (written by ingest), else it is inferred. bundle is the bundle.zarr.zip of a fit and bundle.manifest the SDK bundle manifest that the fit uploaded as bundle.manifest.json.

This module is pure Pydantic (no numpy/xarray): the control plane imports it.

One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; the other key columns become dims only when they hold more than one distinct value; VariableName values become data variables.

combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

docs.title: UI views
docs.text:
Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

docs.title: Object storage
docs.text:
Object storage contracts (plan §8.6): metadata, the ObjectStore protocol, signed URLs, integrity hashes and the bucket/key naming scheme.

The control plane talks to object storage only through :class:ObjectStore. Two implementations exist outside this package: ShimObjectStore (the local GCS emulator in mapi_gcs_shim) and GcsObjectStore (google-cloud-storage). Both expose GCS semantics:

  • every write creates a new generation; if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist" (write-once);
  • the server computes CRC32C (base64 of the big-endian 4-byte value) and MD5 (base64 of the 16-byte digest) — uploader-supplied hashes are never evidence;
  • signed GET URLs are pinned to a generation and honour HTTP Range; signed PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix + content-length-range) are how sandboxes write, so the executor never holds storage credentials.

Object keys are always built server-side from validated IDs with the helpers at the bottom of this module (never from user-supplied paths).

docs.title: ObjectStore
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Async object-store driver used by the control plane (GCS semantics).

Conventions shared by every method:

  • generation pins the source generation to read (None = live generation);
  • if_generation_match is a precondition on the target: 0 means "must not exist", n means "live generation must be n"; a failed precondition raises :class:PreconditionFailed;
  • missing buckets/objects raise :class:NotFound; denied operations raise :class:AccessDenied.

docs.title: SignedGet
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A generation-pinned signed GET URL plus the server-computed facts about its object.

The URL honours HTTP Range, so zarr zip readers can range-read one object. A reader verifies size/crc32c after a full download (corruption check only — integrity is enforced by the control plane).

docs.title: SignedPut
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A signed PUT URL for exactly one object name.

headers must be sent verbatim (they are part of the signature): typically content-type, x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 (write-once) and x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max_bytes>.

docs.title: PostPolicy
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A V4 POST policy: multipart form uploads of any key under prefix.

The uploader posts multipart/form-data to url with every entry of fields, then key (which must start with prefix), then the file part last. The storage service rejects bodies outside content_length_range and keys outside the prefix.

A create_only policy cannot replace an existing object (its signed conditions carry x-goog-if-generation-match: 0), so the holder can neither overwrite the write-once manifest nor swap an output after it was written.

docs.title: REST DTOs
docs.text:
See HTTP API (v1) for the endpoint tables, conventions and the multi-tenant additions of v0.3.

REST DTOs for the HTTP API (/v1; plan §8.2): M1 (v0.2), M2 (v0.3) and the M3 (v0.4) contracts.

Conventions shared by every endpoint (see docs/reference/http-api.md):

  • Requests reject unknown fields (extra="forbid"); responses ignore unknown fields when parsed by a client, so older clients keep working when the server adds fields.
  • Every resource carries tenant_id and project_id. M1 is single-tenant: both are :data:DEFAULT_TENANT_ID / :data:DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID, but the identity is in every row and key so M2 can add row-level security without migrations churn.
  • Lists return :class:Page (items + opaque next_cursor); errors are RFC 7807 :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Problem documents with stable codes.
  • Timestamps are timezone-aware RFC 3339 strings in UTC.

:data:M1_ENDPOINTS and :data:M2_ENDPOINTS (together :data:ENDPOINTS, what v0.3 serves) and :data:M3_ENDPOINTS (guided mode and integrations) are the machine-readable endpoint tables; :data:ALL_ENDPOINTS is all three. The server's route table and the reference docs are tested against them. :data:ROUTE_ACCESS gives every operation its tenant/project scope and the permission it checks. From v0.3 every M1 resource is project-scoped: the project comes from the path or the X-Mapi-Project header (:func:mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope).

Tenant/project scoping and the permission checked for every operation in :data:ALL_ENDPOINTS (keyed by operation_id).

Acting on other principals' tokens (list_tokens?all=true, revoking someone else's token) additionally needs manage on token. A create_run for a model version (score, evaluate, derive, render) additionally needs run on model. A promote_endpoint with override=true additionally needs manage on endpoint, which no token scope grants (a signed-in admin decides, audited with the reason).

docs.title: IngestMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

How an upload becomes a labelled dataset (Meridian CoordToColumns style).

Tabular formats need a mapping; zarr_zip/netcdf are self-describing and may omit dims/vars. Parsing happens only inside a sandboxed ingest run.

With the mff/bayesinsight presets the long table is first pivoted to one column per VariableName (plus Period and the key columns); vars and wide then pick and rename those variables (column = a VariableName value) and dims may refine the dims the preset derives (column = an MFF column). Without vars and wide every variable is kept under its own name.

docs.title: Tenancy and authorization
docs.text:
See Tenancy and authentication.

Tenants, projects, roles, principals and authorization (plan §2, §8.1, §9).

  • A tenant is the billing, isolation and quota boundary, with a :class:TrustTier that decides where its runs may be placed (:func:placement_allows) and a data-residency region (:func:region_satisfies).
  • A project is a workspace inside a tenant and the RBAC unit. Roles are ordered viewer < editor < runner < admin: editors change datasets and specs, runners may also spend compute (runs, scores), admins manage members, endpoints and plugins.
  • :data:PERMISSIONS is the whole permission matrix; :func:can is the pure check every component uses. :class:AuthContext combines it with token scopes, tenant status and the operator flag (:meth:AuthContext.allows).
  • :func:resolve_project_scope turns the X-Mapi-Project header, path parameters and a token's binding into the (tenant, project) a request acts in.

Pure Pydantic and stdlib: the server, the web app (through OpenAPI) and tests share it.

    resource: ResourceKind | str,
    *,
    resource_name: str | None = None,
) -> bool

  1. internal services may do exactly the internal rules;
  2. operators may do :data:OPERATOR_PERMISSIONS (regardless of tenant status);

docs.title: resolve_project_scope
docs.text:
resolve_project_scope(
    *,
    header: str | None = None,
    path_tenant: str | None = None,
    path_project: str | None = None,
    token_binding: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    member_tenants: Collection[str] = (),
    default: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
) -> ProjectSelector

Decide which (tenant, project) a project-scoped request acts in.

Precedence: path parameters, then the X-Mapi-Project header, then the token's binding, then default (the single-tenant deployment profile only).

  • path and header that disagree → SCHEMA_INVALID;
  • a token used outside its binding → FORBIDDEN (tokens are bound to one project);
  • a bare project id is qualified with the path tenant, the token's tenant, or the only tenant the principal belongs to; otherwise → SCHEMA_INVALID;
  • nothing selects a project and there is no default → SCHEMA_INVALID.

Membership is checked afterwards; a project the caller cannot see is NOT_FOUND (not FORBIDDEN), so ids cannot be probed.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
API tokens: wire format, scopes, at-rest hashing and the token DTOs (plan §8.2, §9).

Token format (all lowercase Crockford base32, 0-9a-z without i l o u)::

mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>
     8 chars  32 chars 7 chars
  • prefix (40 random bits) is public: it is shown in listings and is the lookup key;
  • secret (160 random bits) is shown exactly once, in :class:TokenCreated;
  • checksum is the CRC-32 of mapi_<prefix>_<secret> (ASCII) in 7 base32 digits, so clients and secret scanners can reject typos and random strings without a database call.

At rest the server stores only :func:hash_token of the whole token (HMAC-SHA256 under a server-side pepper) and compares with :func:verify_token_hash in constant time. No API response ever contains the hash or, after creation, the secret.

A token acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes: every request needs both the owner's project role (:func:mapi_spec.tenancy.can) and a scope that covers the action (:func:scope_allows). Tokens are bound to one project of one tenant.

docs.title: Sessions and Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
Authentication protocols shared by the server and the web app (plan §8.1, §8.7, §11).

Browser sessions (BFF). The SPA never sees an OAuth token. GET /auth/login starts an OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce; the transaction is kept server-side, referenced by a short-lived __Host- cookie. GET /auth/callback checks state, exchanges the code, verifies the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry) and sets the session cookie: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ with no Domain. Because the cookie is SameSite=Strict and every state-changing endpoint takes JSON (a CORS-preflighted content type), cross-site requests never carry it.

Programs send Authorization: Bearer mapi_… (see :mod:mapi_spec.tokens).

Pub/Sub push to POST /internal/events carries a Google-signed OIDC ID token; after verifying the signature, the server checks its claims with :func:check_push_claims.

docs.title: Quotas and scheduling
docs.text:
See Quotas and cost.

Quotas, rate limits, priority classes and fair-share leasing (plan §8.3, §8.8, §9).

Three levels of :class:QuotaPolicy apply to every request and run, most specific first: token, tenant, global. Each sets optional :class:QuotaLimits (None = unlimited at that level). :func:evaluate_quota is the single pure decision function: the first limit a demand would exceed yields a :class:QuotaDecision with problem code RATE_LIMITED (request rate; retryable) or QUOTA_EXCEEDED (everything else).

Quotas are expressed in vCPU-seconds because abuse risk is compute, not run count. :class:PriorityClass weights drive :func:plan_leases, the dispatcher's weighted fair-share choice of which queued runs to lease next, so one tenant's 237-task SBC cannot starve everyone else's interactive scoring.

docs.title: evaluate_quota
docs.text:
evaluate_quota(
    levels: Iterable[tuple[QuotaPolicy, QuotaUsage]],
    demand: QuotaDemand,
    *,
    now: datetime,
) -> QuotaDecision

Check demand against every level; return the first violation or an allowance.

Order: request rate at every level first (RATE_LIMITED), then per level from token to global (QUOTA_EXCEEDED): resource class, fan-out width, concurrent runs, vCPU-seconds per day and month, storage, egress. A cumulative limit fails when used + requested > limit and only if the demand asks for some of it, so a subject already over its storage quota can still read and delete. retry_after_seconds is set for windowed limits (minute, UTC day, UTC month).

docs.title: plan_leases
docs.text:
plan_leases(
    candidates: Sequence[LeaseCandidate],
    *,
    capacity: int,
    running_tasks: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    concurrency_left: Mapping[str, int | None]
    | None = None,
    tenant_weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    weights: Mapping[
        PriorityClass, float
    ] = PRIORITY_WEIGHTS,
) -> list[LeaseCandidate]

Choose which queued runs to lease now (weighted fair share; pure and deterministic).

Repeatedly picks the candidate with the smallest virtual finish (load[tenant] + tasks) / (tenant_weight × priority_weight), ties broken by queued_at then run_id. load starts at the tenant's running_tasks and grows with every pick. A candidate is skipped when its tasks exceed the remaining global capacity or its tenant has no concurrency_left (runs). Returns the picks in order.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Price tables, cost estimates and the per-run cost ledger (plan §8.2, §13 cost floor, §14 M2).

Money is integer micros of a currency (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros); unit prices are integer nanos per vCPU-second and per GiB-second, so every amount is exact and reproducible from a ledger row (round half to even at the micro). Every amount names the :class:PriceTable version it was priced with; changing prices never rewrites history.

Usage of an attempt is vcpu × billed_seconds × tasks vCPU-seconds and ram_gib × billed_seconds × tasks GiB-seconds, from :data:RESOURCE_CLASSES; billed_seconds is wall time rounded up to the table's billing increment.

:data:DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE mirrors Cloud Run's published list prices (CPU 0.000018 USD per vCPU-second, memory 0.000002 USD per GiB-second); deployments configure their own. An E33 fit on class M for five minutes costs about 0.03 USD.

docs.title: Operator controls
docs.text:
Operator controls: kill switches and executor health (plan §9 denial of wallet, §11 Admin).

:class:KillSwitches is a single platform-wide document. :func:kill_switch_decision is the pure check the API (at submit) and the dispatcher (at lease) both apply: when untrusted_execution_enabled is off, no run of uploaded (tenant) code is accepted or leased; when the global spend in the current window reaches global_spend_cap_micros, no new compute is accepted for anyone except internal tenants. Both denials use the QUOTA_EXCEEDED problem code at the global scope.

docs.title: Executor conformance suite
docs.text:
The executor conformance suite, as data (plan §8.4, §13 "Executor conformance").

An executor (local-process, docker, docker-gvisor, cloudrun-jobs, ...) is enabled only after it passes every applicable case of :data:EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE. Each :class:ConformanceCase names the behaviour, the fault the harness injects, what the backend must support for the case to apply, and the :class:Expectation on the run's observed trajectory. The server's pytest suite parametrizes over this tuple and checks each observation with :func:check_expectation; the admin API reports results as a :class:ConformanceReport.

docs.title: EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE
docs.text:
EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE: Final[tuple[ConformanceCase, ...]] = (
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.SUBMIT,
        title="Submit runs one execution to success",
        behaviour="A submitted attempt starts with identifiers in the environment only, reports status through the executor API, emits verified events and succeeds.",
        steps=(
            "submit a tiny fit with a fresh nonce",
            "poll status until terminal; collect events",
            "assert argv carries no run id, nonce or credential",
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(
                _S.PROVISIONING,
                _S.RUNNING,
                _S.FINALIZING,
            ),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.1", "§8.3", "§8.4"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.ADOPT_AFTER_DISPATCHER_CRASH,
        title="Orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash",
        behaviour="If the dispatcher dies between the executor accepting an attempt and the handle being stored, the reconciler adopts the execution by nonce instead of starting a second one.",
        steps=(
            "write the intent row, submit, crash before storing the handle",
            "restart the orchestrator; reconciler calls adopt(nonce)",
            "the adopted execution finishes the run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DISPATCHER_CRASH_AFTER_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        title="Duplicate submit is safe",
        behaviour="Submitting the same (run, attempt, nonce) twice never yields two live executions; the second call returns or adopts the first, or its execution is cancelled before it does any work.",
        steps=(
            "submit twice with the same nonce",
            "wait for the run to finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            max_live_executions=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CANCEL_MID_RUN,
        title="Cancel while running",
        behaviour="A cancel during RUNNING moves the run to CANCELLING; the supervisor gets SIGTERM and flushes; the run is CANCELLED only after the executor confirms the execution is gone.",
        steps=(
            "submit a long fit; wait for RUNNING",
            "cancel; poll executor status",
            "assert CANCELLED is recorded after the executor reports a terminal state",
        ),
        fault=Fault.CANCEL_WHILE_RUNNING,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.CANCELLED,
            must_visit=(_S.RUNNING, _S.CANCELLING),
            must_not_visit=(_S.SUCCEEDED, _S.FAILED),
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.TIMEOUT,
        title="Timeout is enforced and classified",
        behaviour="A run that exceeds its timeout is stopped by the backend (hard task timeout as backstop) and ends FAILED with failure class timeout.",
        steps=(
            "submit a run that sleeps past a short timeout",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EXCEED_TIMEOUT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.TIMEOUT,
            attempts=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.STALLED_NOT_LOST,
        title="Event silence raises STALLED, never a false LOST",
        behaviour="When events stop but the executor still reports the execution running, the run becomes STALLED (a warning) and returns to RUNNING when events resume; it is never failed or retried because of silence alone.",
        steps=(
            "submit; drop events beyond K x interval while the execution runs",
            "resume events; let the run finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EVENT_SILENCE,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.STALLED,),
            must_not_visit=(_S.FAILED,),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "Key decisions: liveness"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CONFIRMED_CANCEL_BEFORE_RETRY,
        title="Confirmed cancel before an infrastructure retry",
        behaviour="After an infrastructure failure the reconciler cancels the old execution and waits for a confirmed terminal status before re-queueing attempt + 1, so two attempts never run at once.",
        steps=(
            "submit; report an infra failure while the old execution is alive",
            "observe cancel → confirmed terminal → QUEUED(attempt 2)",
            "attempt 2 succeeds",
        ),
        fault=Fault.INFRA_FAILURE_LIVE_EXECUTION,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.QUEUED,),
            attempts=2,
            max_live_executions=1,
            executions_created=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CHECKPOINT_RESUME,
        title="Checkpoint, PARTIAL and resume",
        behaviour="A SIGTERM after checkpoints were written yields a PARTIAL bundle; resume starts a new attempt from the checkpoints and completes without redoing them.",
        steps=(
            "submit a segmented fit; wait for the first checkpoint",
            "SIGTERM the execution; expect PARTIAL",
            "resume; expect SUCCEEDED with the earlier segments reused",
        ),
        fault=Fault.SIGTERM_WITH_CHECKPOINTS,
        requires=frozenset(
            {Requirement.CHECKPOINT_STORAGE}
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.PARTIAL,),
            attempts=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§5 segmented sampling"),
        budget_seconds=300,
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.OOM_CLASSIFICATION,
        title="Out-of-memory is classified as resource exhaustion",
        behaviour="A worker killed for memory (exit 137) ends FAILED with failure class resource_exhausted and an offer to retry one class up.",
        steps=(
            "submit a memory bomb at class S",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.MEMORY_BOMB,
        requires=frozenset({Requirement.MEMORY_LIMIT}),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
            attempts=1,
            offers_next_class=True,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.5",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.FANOUT_TASK_COUNT,
        title="Fan-out with taskCount",
        behaviour="One execution with task_count N runs N tasks, each mapping its task index to a child spec and writing under tasks/{i}/; status aggregates all tasks and a cancel stops all of them.",
        steps=(
            "submit task_count=4",
            "assert 4 distinct task indexes and per-task output prefixes",
            "assert one backend execution",
        ),
        requires=frozenset({Requirement.FANOUT}),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.6"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.GENERATION_VERIFICATION,
        title="Output generations are verified at FINALIZING",
        behaviour="An output overwritten after the runner's manifest (new generation or hash) or an unexpected extra object fails the run with failure class integrity; nothing is copied into the bundles bucket.",
        steps=(
            "submit; after the complete event, overwrite one output object",
            "let the finalizer run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.TAMPER_OUTPUT_GENERATION,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.INTEGRITY,
            must_visit=(_S.FINALIZING,),
            must_not_visit=(_S.SUCCEEDED,),
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.6", "§9 artifact swap"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF,
        title="429 back-off without duplicates",
        behaviour="When the backend's control API answers 429, the dispatcher backs off (exponential, honouring Retry-After), raises the 429 alarm counter and submits exactly once when the limit clears.",
        steps=(
            "make the control API return 429 to the first 3 submit calls",
            "assert growing delays between calls",
            "assert one execution and a SUCCEEDED run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.BACKEND_429,
        requires=frozenset(
            {Requirement.REMOTE_CONTROL_API}
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.8"),
    ),
)

Every case, in suite order.

docs.title: Guided mode v0.4
docs.text:
See Guided mode.

Guided mode: templates, the question flow, role detection and drafts (plan §11; M3).

Guided mode is organised around tasks. The user picks a :class:GuidedTemplate ("What do you want to learn?"), answers plain-language :class:GuidedQuestion s about their columns ("Which column is revenue?") - pre-filled by :func:suggest_roles from column profiles - and gets a draft: an :class:~mapi_spec.ingest.IngestMapping for the upload plus a ModelSpec document (and its YAML, "View as YAML"), built by :func:build_draft.

Templates are data. Their spec_template is a ModelSpec document with {{placeholder}} strings, filled from answers, template defaults and lookups (:func:render_template); every placeholder is covered by a question, a default, a lookup or a value the builder always provides (:data:BUILDER_VALUES), which a test checks.

Built-in templates (:data:GUIDED_TEMPLATES):

================= ========================== ============================================= id plugin for ================= ========================== ============================================= geo_mmm mmm.hierarchical_geo marketing mix by market (what-if, priors) weekly_forecast````ts.hsgp_trend one weekly series, forecast ahead store_demand tabular.regressor demand per store and week (quantiles) customer_choice````choice.multinomial_logitwhich product customers choose on each trip (a conditional logit with household effects, in plugins/tabular) ================= ========================== =============================================

}

docs.title: GuidedQuestion
docs.text:
Bases: ResponseModel

One plain-language question. Column questions name what the column becomes:

  • dim: the column labels a dataset dim (dim_spec describes it); the placeholder {{<id>}} is the dataset dim name;
  • role (column): the column is a data variable with that role; the placeholder is the dataset variable name;
  • role + wide_dim (columns): the columns become one variable as_var along wide_dim (one label per column, e.g. spend per channel);
  • role without wide_dim (columns): each column is its own variable.

docs.title: Ingest presets v0.4
docs.text:
Ingest presets and file contracts (plan §3.2, §11 Guided task 2, Q8; M3).

An upload becomes a labelled dataset in a sandboxed ingest run. Besides an explicit column mapping (:class:mapi_spec.api.IngestMapping), M3 adds presets for the formats marketing teams already have:

================= =========================================================================== preset file contract ================= =========================================================================== none the explicit dims/vars/wide column mapping mff the MFF long table (:data:MFF_COLUMNS): one row per period, key columns and variable, the value in VariableValue (:class:MffOptions) meridian Google Meridian's CoordToColumns wide table (:class:MeridianColumns) bayesinsight an MFF table plus BayesInsight's metadata.json (:class:BayesInsightMetadata); the model itself comes from model_def.json (:class:BayesInsightModelDef, imported by POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight as a spec for mmm.bayesinsight) ================= ===========================================================================

Wide tables (one column per channel) become one variable along a new dim through :class:WideVarMapping - the shape Meridian and most spreadsheets use.

This module only describes files; every byte of an upload is parsed inside the sandbox. model_def.json and metadata.json are small JSON documents and are validated here.

docs.text:

    "Period",
    "Geography",
    "Product",
    "Outlet",
    "Campaign",
    "Creative",
    "VariableValue",
    "VariableName",
)

The MFF long-format columns, in BayesInsight's order (bayesinsight.lib.constants). Every row holds one value: VariableValue of variable VariableName for one Period and one combination of the key columns.

docs.title: IngestMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

How an upload becomes a labelled dataset (Meridian CoordToColumns style).

Tabular formats need a mapping; zarr_zip/netcdf are self-describing and may omit dims/vars. Parsing happens only inside a sandboxed ingest run.

With the mff/bayesinsight presets the long table is first pivoted to one column per VariableName (plus Period and the key columns); vars and wide then pick and rename those variables (column = a VariableName value) and dims may refine the dims the preset derives (column = an MFF column). Without vars and wide every variable is kept under its own name.

docs.title: effective_mff
docs.text:
effective_mff: MffOptions | None

The MFF options the ingest run uses (defaults for the mff-based presets).

docs.title: DimMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

A dim of the dataset, read from one column of a tabular upload.

docs.title: VarMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

A data variable read from one column (dtype is inferred during ingest).

docs.title: WideVarMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

One variable read from several columns, one per label of dim (a wide table).

{"dim": "channel", "columns": {"tv": "tv_spend", "search": "search_spend"}} gives a variable along channel (plus the table's other dims) with coords tv and search. Several wide variables may share a dim; their labels must then agree.

docs.title: IngestPreset
docs.text: Bases: StrEnum

docs.title: MffOptions
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

The MFF ("model feature format") long-table preset.

One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; the other key columns become dims only when they hold more than one distinct value; VariableName values become data variables.

combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

docs.title: BayesInsight models v0.4
docs.text:
The importer (import_bayesinsight) and the settings of the built-in mmm.bayesinsight (see Built-in models).

BayesInsight model_def.json as a spec for a built-in MMM (Q8, M3).

:func:import_bayesinsight turns a BayesInsight project (model_def.json plus the metadata.json of its MFF data) into a :class:~mapi_spec.guided.GuidedDraft for one of two targets.

target: mmm.bayesinsight - the dedicated plugin, which runs BayesInsight's model as model_def.json defines it (semantics in :mod:mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model):

  • the ingest mapping uses the bayesinsight preset; every row id besides Period becomes a panel dim of its own (Geography -> geo, Product -> product, even with one label, as BayesInsight keeps it), new_levels (pooled) unless some coefficient is estimated separately per level (then fixed); variables keep their MFF names (made safe: Sales -> sales);
  • the spec binds the KPI to y, lags the media (core.lag_tensor, pad: nan - the zero-padded convolution) and carries model_def in the settings, with every analytic name mapped to its variable;
  • what the plugin cannot run falls back to BayesInsight's own default with an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning (an MvNormal likelihood, time transforms, priors with unknown distributions or parameters, coefficient dims that are not row ids); faithful but surprising behaviour is an info issue (no likelihood means Poisson, random effects with partial_pooling_sigma: 0 pool nothing, signs are enforced, carry-overs and curves BayesInsight's code cannot run).

target: mmm.hierarchical_geo (default) - the built-in geo MMM, whose pipeline and settings carry every BayesInsight feature that has an equivalent, and an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning for each one that has none (nothing is dropped silently):

====================================== =========================================================== BayesInsight mmm.hierarchical_geo spec ====================================== =========================================================== exog variable (the KPI) target y, mean-scaled over time per geo media variables spend(geo, channel, time), mean-scaled, 12-lag tensor adstock: delayed / geometric adstock.kind (one kind for every channel) adstock_prior (Delayed) alpha ~ Beta(mu, nu) and theta ~ Exponential(lam), one per channel - exactly BayesInsight's distributions media_transform: hill / linear saturation.kind: hill / none media_transform_prior (Hill) half ~ LogNormal exactly; slope ~ Gamma matching the mean and sd of BayesInsight's 1 + Exponential random_coeff_dims of media pooling: partial (fixed_ind_coeff_dims: none, neither: complete) control variables controls (Global Standardize → core.standardize) season core.fourier (period, n_fourier) localtrend core.trend (a linear trend control; warned) ====================================== ===========================================================

Coefficient and intercept priors are not carried over to the geo MMM: BayesInsight states them in the KPI's own units while the geo MMM works on the mean-scaled KPI, so the same numbers would mean something else (state them as business priors instead, or import for mmm.bayesinsight, which keeps them). Likelihoods other than Normal, Weibull adstock, S-shaped saturation, time transforms and non-linear deterministic transforms have no equivalent there and are reported.

Pure JSON → JSON (no numpy): the control plane runs it on the uploaded documents.

The settings of mmm.bayesinsight: BayesInsight's model_def.json, typed (Q8, M3).

The built-in plugin mmm.bayesinsight (mapi_plugin_mmm.bayesinsight) fits a BayesInsight model exactly as its model_def.json describes it. This module is the contract between the plugin, the control plane (static validation of a spec's settings) and the importer (:func:mapi_spec.bayesinsight.import_bayesinsight with target: mmm.bayesinsight): pure Pydantic, no numpy.

The model (panel = the model's row ids besides Period, in BayesInsight's order Geography, Product, Outlet, Campaign, Creative; t the period)::

eta[p, t] = intercept[p] + sum_media coef_m[p] * sum_l w_m[l] * f_m(z_m[p, t - l])
            + sum_controls coef_c[p] * x_c[p, t]
            + sum_seasons sum_k coef_sk[p] * fourier_k(t)
            + sum_trends  B(t) @ beta_trend[p]
y[p, t] ~ Likelihood(mean(eta[p, t]))
  • Likelihoods (exog.likelihood): Normal and LogNormal use eta itself (identity: y ~ Normal(eta, sigma), log y ~ Normal(eta, sigma)); Poisson, NegativeBinomial, ZeroInflatedPoisson and ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial use a log link, exp(clip(eta, -20, 20)). Without a likelihood, BayesInsight - and so this plugin - fits a Poisson model. MvNormal is not supported.
  • Coefficients in KPI units: every coefficient prior (coeff_prior, the KPI's intercept_prior) is a distribution with its parameters, for the KPI exactly as stored (BayesInsight does not rescale the KPI). fixed_ind_coeff_dims estimate one coefficient per level combination of those row ids; random_coeff_dims add a partially pooled effect sigma * z (sigma ~ HalfNormal(partial_pooling_sigma), z ~ Normal(0, 1) per level combination) when partial_pooling_sigma > 0 - BayesInsight's default of 0 pools nothing.
  • Sign constraints (sign: positive | negative; media are always positive): the coefficient keeps the sign - a real-valued prior is truncated at zero, a positive prior is negated for negative, and random effects become multiplicative (coef * exp(sigma * z)) so no level can cross zero. BayesInsight declares signs but does not enforce them.
  • Media: z = transform(x) / index with index each series' non-zero median (or mean, index_to) over the fit window; the curve f is hill (z^n / (K^n + z^n), K ~ LogNormal(log K_ave, log(K_std / K_ave + 1)), n = 1 + Exponential(1 / (n_ave - 1))), linear (z) or sshaped (BayesInsight's SShaped prior: (b^(alpha^(100 x / x_max)) - b) / (1 - b) with b = beta / 1e8, x_max the series' largest fit-window value, anchored so no spend gives no effect). The curve comes first, then the carry-over over l_max lags (BayesInsight's order): delayed (alpha^((l - theta)^2), alpha ~ Beta(mu=retention_rate_mean, nu=retention_rate_std), theta ~ Exponential(lam=lag_max)), geometric (alpha^l, the same retention prior), weibull (pymc-marketing's PDF or CDF weights, :class:WeibullAdstockPrior) or none; weights are normalised to sum to one.
  • Controls: x = normalize(transform(x)) with the deterministic transforms linear | log | exp(alpha) | indexp(alpha, mean) | power(alpha) and Global Standardize (mean and sample sd over every cell of the fit window, or the stored mean/std).
  • Seasons: n_fourier cos/sin pairs of period period (in periods), computed as BayesInsight does (t spans 2 pi n / period over the n fit periods); one coefficient per component (coeff_prior, default Normal(0, 3); pooling sigma 1).
  • Local trends (localtrend): a B-spline basis (num_knots interior knots, degree order) over the fit window scaled to [0, 1] with Gaussian-random-walk coefficients (:class:LocalTrendPrior), per level of random_coeff_dims around a shared walk, optionally grouped (grouping_map). Forecasts hold the trend at its last fitted level (splines do not extrapolate).

Settings besides model_def tie BayesInsight's names to the model-stage data: the KPI is the canonical target y; variables maps every analytic variable name (TV_Total_Total_Total) to its model-stage variable; media and controls list those in model_def order (the schema template reads them); row_dims maps the row ids to the panel dims. Media variables arrive as lag tensors (core.lag_tensor with pad: zero, BayesInsight's convolution) over lag_dim with l_max lags.

docs.title: Business priors and calibration v0.4
docs.text:
Business priors, lift tests and prior translation (plan §11 Guided task 3; M3).

Guided users state beliefs in business units instead of model parameters:

  • :class:BusinessPriors - per channel an ROI range [low, high] or a contribution-share range, each held with a stated credibility (the probability that the truth lies inside the range), plus an optional baseline share;
  • :class:LiftTest - the result of an experiment (geo holdout, conversion lift): extra spend on one channel over a window and the incremental KPI it caused, with a standard error or a confidence interval. Lift tests are calibration data: the model treats each one as an extra observation of the channel's incremental effect.

Both attach to a ModelSpec through its optional calibration block (:class:Calibration). A model plugin uses them only if its manifest declares the matching capability (Capabilities.calibration); otherwise static validation reports CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

Turning business priors into model-space priors needs the data (spend and KPI scale) and the model's transforms, so it runs in the sandbox as a translate_priors run (:class:PriorTranslationJob → priors.json = :class:PriorTranslationResult), which also samples the prior predictive and reports it in business units (ROI and share distributions, a KPI fan). :func:apply_prior_translation writes the result into a spec.

Pure Pydantic and stdlib (statistics.NormalDist for quantiles): the control plane and the web app (through OpenAPI) share it.

docs.title: BusinessPriors
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

Beliefs in business units, per channel (keys are channel labels as in the data), and/or about the baseline. At least one belief is stated: a baseline belief alone is fine (channels without a belief keep the model's default priors).

docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

What the user believes about one channel: exactly one of roi or contribution_share, held with credibility.

  • roi: KPI units gained per spend unit over the fit window ([1.5, 4] = "every euro returns between 1.5 and 4 euros of revenue");
  • contribution_share: the channel's share of the KPI over the fit window.

A share range (for example of the baseline: KPI that happens without any media).

docs.title: LiftTest
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

One experiment: spend_delta extra spend on channel (optionally in one geo) from start to end (inclusive) caused kpi_delta incremental KPI.

Give the measurement's uncertainty as a standard error se or a confidence interval ci at ci_level. A holdout ("turn the channel off") is a negative spend_delta with (usually) a negative kpi_delta.

docs.text:
sigma: float

The standard error (from ci assuming a symmetric normal interval).

spec is the resolved ModelSpec document (its data.dataset is the dataset input). The runner fits nothing: it builds the model, maps the beliefs to model-space priors and samples draws prior-predictive draws.

docs.title: Scorecard and promotion gate v0.4
docs.text:
The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate (plan §2 Diagnostic, §11 Guided task 5; M3).

A fitted model version carries a :class:Scorecard: plain-language checks in four categories, each pass, warn or fail:

============== ========================================================================= category checks (:data:SCORECARD_CHECKS) ============== ========================================================================= convergence chains agree (R-hat), enough effective draws, no divergences holdout holdout error (MAPE) and interval coverage on the evaluation split; for choice models, the holdout hit rate against always guessing the most popular product plausibility negative or absurd ROI, a channel taking most of the KPI, the baseline share, parameters the data did not inform (prior-posterior overlap) data missing values, years of history, spend that never varies ============== =========================================================================

:func:evaluate_check turns a metric value into a :class:ScorecardItem with the check's message and suggested action; :func:rollup makes the scorecard (overall is the worst item). Templates pick checks and may tighten thresholds (:class:CheckThresholds).

Promoting a model version to an endpoint passes the promotion gate (:func:promotion_gate): pass → allowed, warn → needs an administrator override with a reason (audited), fail → blocked. :func:authorize_promotion applies an override request to a gate decision.

    *,
    fit_mode: str = "evaluate_then_refit",

) -> PromotionGateDecision

Decide whether a model version may be promoted (pure).

  • a partial version (interrupted fit) is blocked;
  • a train_only fit is blocked unless the endpoint's policy allows it (Q13: evaluate_then_refit is the default for endpoints, so context and terminal state come from all the data);
  • breaking input-schema changes (schema_breaks) follow schema_change;
  • no scorecard needs an override; a fail scorecard blocks, a warn one needs an override, a pass one is allowed;
  • an evaluate_then_refit version whose scorecard measured no holdout check (no data.split, or no evaluate.metrics) was never evaluated and needs an override (NOT_EVALUATED), as does every check of required_checks (a guided template's scorecard_checks) that the scorecard skipped or lacks.

The caller audits an override as endpoint.promote_override.

docs.title: What-if scenarios v0.4
docs.text:
Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

What-if scenarios, forecasts and counterfactuals for Guided mode (plan §11 tasks 6-7; M3).

Sliders. A :class:WhatIfScenario scales each channel's spend over the fit window. The browser answers it instantly from the fit's :class:~mapi_spec.views.ResponseGridView with the interpolation contract below; :func:evaluate_scenario is the reference implementation (the web app's TypeScript port is tested against the same golden cases):

  1. a channel without a multiplier keeps 1; multipliers outside the grid ([multipliers[0], multipliers[-1]]) are refused (SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE) - the grid is never extrapolated;
  2. per draw d and channel c, the contribution at multiplier x is the linear interpolation of contribution[d][c] between the two grid points around x; spend is interpolated the same way on spend[c];
  3. per draw, kpi = baseline + sum_c contribution and delta = kpi - kpi(all at 1); summaries (mean and quantiles) are taken over draws after summing, so uncertainty stays joint across channels.

Run exact turns the scenario into a counterfactual :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ScoreRequest (:func:scenario_score_request). Forecasts (:func:forecast_request) and intervention presets ("channel off", "budget x k"; :func:counterfactual_request) build score requests the same way, so the server, the CLI and the docs share one implementation (POST /v1/guided/requests:compile).

docs.title: ResponseGridView
docs.text:
Bases: _View

ui/grids/response_curves.json: per-draw response curves for instant what-if sliders.

For each thinned posterior draw d, channel c and spend multiplier m, contribution[d][c][m] is the channel's total contribution to the KPI over the fit window (periods periods, KPI units) when the channel's spend is scaled by multipliers[m]; spend[c][m] is that spend (spend units). Multiplier 1 is the actual spend (current_spend). baseline[d] is the KPI over the window that no channel explains, so baseline[d] + sum_c contribution[d][c][at 1] is the model's expected KPI. *_by_geo variants add a trailing geo axis (geos order).

Sliders interpolate per draw (see :func:mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario), so uncertainty bands stay joint across channels; "Run exact" submits a real score run.

docs.title: Endpoints and snippets v0.4
docs.text:
See Integrations.

Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (plan §2, §8.2, §11; Q13; M3).

An endpoint endpoint://<project>/<alias> points at one model version at a time. Integrations (the Python and TypeScript clients, Google Sheets, Atlas, BI exports) call the alias, so a new model version can be promoted - or rolled back - without touching them.

  • Promotion (PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}) passes the promotion gate (:func:mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate): the scorecard, the endpoint's :class:EvaluationPolicy (evaluate_then_refit by default, Q13) and the input-schema compatibility with what callers already send (:func:schema_breaks).
  • Every promotion and rollback is an :class:EndpointRevision (the history).
  • Scoring (POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score) takes an :class:EndpointScoreCall: a score request without apiVersion/kind/model, whose data and scenario may be dataset references or small inline XrJSON datasets.
  • GET …/schema describes the input (:class:EndpointSchema, with an example payload), POST …/validate checks a call without running it, GET …/snippets returns code (:mod:mapi_spec.snippets).

XrJSON: small labelled datasets inline in JSON requests (plan §3.2; M3 endpoints).

The shape is xr.Dataset.to_dict()::

{"coords": {"time": {"dims": ["time"], "data": ["2026-11-01", ...]}, ...},
 "data_vars": {"spend": {"dims": ["geo", "channel", "time"], "data": [[[...]]]}},
 "dims": {"time": 8, ...},           # optional
 "attrs": {}}                        # optional

It is for payloads up to :data:MAX_XRJSON_BYTES (one scenario, an endpoint score call), so curl, TypeScript and Apps Script callers need no upload. The control plane checks only the envelope here (names, nesting, sizes, element and string caps, ragged lists) and stores the JSON as a run input; the values are decoded into arrays only inside the runner sandbox (mapi_sdk wire format), which also checks dtypes and the schema.

Code snippets for calling an endpoint (plan §11 Integrations hub; M3).

Pure functions, so the server (GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets), the CLI and the docs render identical code. Every snippet scores POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score with Prefer: wait=60 and an example payload, reading the API token from the environment (MAPI_TOKEN; Apps Script: a script property) - a snippet never contains a secret.

Quoting. Values are embedded with each language's own literal syntax, never by string pasting: Python literals via repr, JavaScript/TypeScript via JSON (with U+2028/U+2029 escaped), shell via single quotes (' → '\''), R via escaped single-quoted strings. The base URL, project and alias are validated first (:class:SnippetContext), so even a hostile value cannot break out of its literal; tests parse the generated code back.

docs.title: Webhooks v0.4
docs.text:
Outgoing webhooks: events, envelope, signatures, deliveries and the SSRF policy (plan §8.2 Integrations, §9 "Webhook SSRF"; M3).

Events (:class:WebhookEventType) are delivered as a JSON :class:WebhookEnvelope::

{"id": "evt_…", "type": "run.succeeded", "created": "2026-10-15T09:30:00Z",
 "tenant": "acme", "project": "growth", "api_version": "v1", "data": {...}}

Signatures. Every delivery carries Mapi-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex> where v1 is HMAC-SHA256 under the webhook secret of "<t>.<raw body>". While a secret is being rotated the header carries one v1 per active secret. Receivers verify with :func:verify_signature and refuse timestamps more than :data:SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_S (300 s) away from their clock, which bounds replays.

SSRF. The server delivers only under :data:SSRF_POLICY: https only, allowed ports, no credentials in URLs, blocked internal host names; it resolves the host itself, refuses if any address is private, loopback, link-local, metadata, CGNAT, ULA, multicast or otherwise non-global (:func:ip_is_blocked, including IPv4 embedded in IPv6), connects to the pinned address it checked (SNI and Host keep the name), follows no redirects, gives up after 5 s and reads at most 256 KiB of the response.

docs.title: Plot sharing v0.4
docs.text:
Saved plots, static rendering and embeds (plan §8.2 Plots, §10.3 items 4-5; M3).

  • Saved plots (POST /v1/plots) keep a plot under a name: either a reference to a plot a model version rendered (a platform recipe or a plugin plot) or a user-authored :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec (sanitized on save and on every read).
  • Static rendering (POST /v1/plots:render) turns a plot into PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox (vl-convert for Vega-Lite, kaleido for Plotly): a render run.
  • Embeds (POST /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds) mint a tokenised, read-only, expiring link for BI tools, Slack and Notion. Plan §10.3 item 4: shared views render platform recipes only - never plugin- or user-authored specs - because a sandboxed iframe can still navigate itself; :func:embeddable decides. The public GET /v1/embeds/{token} returns an :class:EmbedView with every dataset inlined (no URLs).

Embed tokens are mpe_<40 base32 characters> (200 random bits); the server stores only an HMAC (like API tokens) and shows the URL once.

docs.title: Trust lifecycle v0.4
docs.text:
Trust lifecycle: self-service sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and GDPR export (plan §9 "Compute abuse", "Data lifecycle", §14 M3 and cut lines A/B; M3).

  • Sign-up (POST /auth/signup): e-mail, name and accepted terms. The answer is the same whether or not the address is new (no account enumeration). A disposable-e-mail policy hook (:class:DisposableEmailPolicy) refuses throwaway domains.
  • E-mail verification (POST /auth/verify-email) with a single-use token that expires after :data:EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL creates a public-tier tenant with a default project, the signer as tenant admin.
  • Cut line A (M3): public tenants run declarative specs and built-in plugins only - untrusted data, trusted code. Cut line B (M5) opens code upload to public tenants, and only after identity verification (:func:uploaded_code_allowed).
  • Tenant deletion (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion) is scheduled with a grace period (:data:TENANT_DELETION_GRACE, the tenant is suspended and can cancel), then purges every store and reports progress per store (:class:TenantDeletion).
  • GDPR export (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/exports) packages everything the tenant stored into one archive with a short-lived download link (:class:GdprExport).

docs.title: mapi_steps
docs.text:
The built-in core.* steps. For every step's settings, see the generated steps catalog.

Built-in preprocessing steps for modeling-api (core.*).

Every step implements the :class:mapi_sdk.steps.Step contract and exports static JSON (settings schema, templated :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect, context need) so the control plane can validate specs without importing this package. Steps are discovered through the mapi.steps entry point (:func:builtin_steps); :func:registry returns a ready :class:~mapi_sdk.registry.Registry, and python -m mapi_steps.catalog prints the catalog JSON.

========== =========================================================================== Reshape resample, count_events, filter_coords, to_long, to_padded, stack, unstack Value fx_convert, mean_scale, max_abs_scale, standardize, log1p, logit, impute, replace_sentinel, clip Feature fourier, trend, calendar, holidays, lag, lag_tensor, one_hot, encode_levels, missing_indicator, formula Precompute adstock, saturation (point models) Split time_holdout, as_of, leave_group_out, last_per_group, mask_block (:mod:mapi_steps.splits; chosen in data.split, applied by the harness) ========== ===========================================================================

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
The five built-in train/holdout splits (plan §4.1 "Split" group).

Splits are not pipeline steps: a spec chooses one in data.split and the harness applies it at the split stage (:func:mapi_sdk.split.split_dataset), after the stateless prefix. This module gives each split kind a catalog identity (core.<kind>@1.0.0) with its settings schema and plain-language summaries for pickers and docs, plus a direct :meth:SplitStrategy.split for notebooks and tests.

======================== ==================================================================== core.time_holdout hold out the last last periods / a fraction / after a label core.as_of train up to and including as_of; optional gap periods core.leave_group_out hold out whole groups (explicit groups or n random ones) core.last_per_group last last rows of each group with at least min_len rows core.mask_block random blocks over dims covering fraction of the cells ======================== ====================================================================
