docs.text:
Status: available in v0.3 (milestone M2), a private beta

v0.3 makes the platform multi-tenant and gives it a cloud execution backend: one fresh sandbox per run on Cloud Run Jobs. The run protocol (bootstrap object, signed events, verified outputs, signed bundle manifests) is the one that already ran locally in v0.2; v0.3 adds the cloud counterparts of the local pieces. Everything multi-tenant runs on a laptop too (make dev). The cloud pieces are tested against fakes, and a short checklist of cloud behaviours waits for a real project. To use it: Administration, Authentication, Deploy to Google Cloud.

docs.title: One sandbox per run
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph SB["Fresh sandbox (one per run)"]
        direction LR
        SUP["Supervisor<br/><i>trusted · holds credentials</i>"] -->|"inputs"| W["Worker<br/><i>separate uid · runs the plugin</i>"]
        W -->|"outputs (claims)"| SUP
    end
    SUP -->|"signed upload"| OBJ[("Object store")]
    SUP -->|"HMAC-signed events"| EV["Events service"]
    OBJ -->|"server-computed hashes"| FIN["Finalizer<br/>verifies, then publishes"]
  • Isolation. Each run gets a fresh micro-VM sandbox (Cloud Run Jobs, gen2). A trusted supervisor holds the run's short-lived credentials; an untrusted worker runs the harness and the plugin under a different user, with no credentials and no network.
  • No egress. Sandboxes cannot reach the internet, including DNS. Data comes in and results go out only through object-scoped signed URLs.
  • Outputs are claims. The finalizer checks every artifact against the hashes and object generation the store computed itself, then copies it somewhere the sandbox cannot write. A manifest that does not match is rejected as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Progress you can trust. Only the supervisor writes events, each line HMAC-signed and sequence-numbered; the executor's own status decides whether a run is alive.
  • Resumable long fits. Segmented PyMC sampling checkpoints to the run's prefix, so a preempted fit resumes where it stopped. (Checkpoints, partial runs and resume already work locally in v0.2.)
Local (make dev, Compose) On Google Cloud in v0.3 local-process / docker executor Cloud Run Jobs, a fixed inventory of base image × resource class Worker as your user (DEV_MODE_ISOLATION) Worker under its own uid, no_new_privs, in a microVM GCS shim with emulated principals Cloud Storage with IAM, VPC Service Controls Events from the supervisor's stdout pipe Cloud Logging → Pub/Sub push → POST /internal/events EC P-256 key in .local/keys/ Cloud KMS asymmetric signatures, same bytes The development IdP, 127.0.0.1 only OIDC for people, scoped tokens for programs

docs.title: Multi-tenant core
docs.text:
• Tenants and projects with role-based access; row-level security in Postgres on every table (every row and storage key already carries tenant_id and project_id in v0.2).
  • Scoped API tokens with their own budgets; per-tenant quotas in vCPU-seconds; interactive and batch priority classes so one big sweep cannot starve everyone's scoring.
  • A per-run cost ledger shown in the UI.
  • The contracts for all of this are already published: see Tenancy and authentication, Quotas and cost and the multi-tenant HTTP API.
  • Other backends plug in through the same Executor protocol, each gated by an executor conformance suite.
  • The infrastructure is code: Terraform for the control, exec, data and build projects and the VPC Service Controls perimeter, with deploy scripts and a GitHub Actions workflow. See Deploy to Google Cloud and Security hardening on Google Cloud.

The Cloud Run executor, the authenticated Pub/Sub event path, KMS manifest signing and the hardened Cloud Storage driver are described in Cloud Run Jobs executor (tested against fakes; no live cloud yet).

docs.title: What it means for plugins
docs.text: Nothing changes in your code. The contract kit already checks the properties the cloud relies on: no pickle, deterministic bundles, typed errors, evaluate path equals score path. A plugin that passes check_model today is ready for sandboxed execution.

docs.title: Expert plugins, MCP and optimisation jobs next: v0.5
docs.text:
Status: next (milestone M4)

v0.4 opened the hosted platform to declarative specs and built-in models. v0.5 lets allow-listed teams upload their own model plugins, gives AI agents a curated MCP server, and moves budget optimisation and model sweeps into the sandbox. Public code upload for everyone comes after it, behind its own controls (see the roadmap).

docs.title: Plugin upload for allow-listed experts
docs.text:
Today a data scientist's own PyMCModel or SklearnModel runs on a deployment they control, installed into the runner's environment. v0.5 makes it a product feature of a shared deployment, for tenants an operator has allow-listed:

flowchart LR
    A["mapi plugin push<br/>(your package)"] --> B["Overlay build<br/>source + pre-resolved wheels,<br/>pinned by hash"]
    B --> C["Describe run<br/>catalog entry, schema sanitizer,<br/>contract kit report"]
    C --> D{{"Kit passes?"}}
    D -->|yes| E["Runnable in your project<br/>on the pinned base image"]
    D -->|no| F["Readable report<br/>of what to fix"]
  • Overlays, not images. A plugin is built into a hash-pinned overlay (its source plus wheels resolved in advance, including native wheels from a curated mirror) on top of one base-image version. Runs never install anything.
  • The contract kit runs on upload. The same checks you run locally with mapi plugin test decide whether a version becomes runnable, and its report is kept with the version, next to its SBOM.
  • Schema sanitizer. A plugin's settings schemas are sanitized before the web app renders forms from them.
  • Dev overlays for fast iteration: the target is under five minutes from push to a runnable version.
  • A vetted tier: the sibling marketing-mix and HMM models ported as plugins, as the proof that real models fit the contract.

docs.title: An MCP server for agents
docs.text: A curated set of tools, such as listing and describing models, scoring an endpoint, reading a run and fetching a plot, for AI assistants and agents. Every string that came from a user or a plugin is returned as clearly delimited untrusted text, so a model name cannot smuggle instructions into an agent. Tokens and scopes work as for any other client.

docs.title: Optimisation and sweeps as jobs
docs.text:
• optimize runs. Atlas runs next to the model in the sandbox instead of calling the endpoint once per candidate from your machine (today's RemoteModel path), so long optimisations no longer pay a run start-up per batch.
  • Sweep, Backtest and SBC as one parent run that fans out and aggregates: a sensitivity sweep over a prior, an as-of backtest across forecast origins, simulation-based calibration of a new plugin.

docs.title: Exit criteria
docs.text:
• Three sibling models packaged as plugins and passing the contract kit.
  • A dev overlay pushed and runnable in under five minutes.
  • An as-of backtest and a sensitivity sweep each run as a single parent.

Releases are cut when their exit criteria pass; follow the changelog.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
Status: this release (milestone M3), the first public launch

With the multi-tenant core in place (v0.3), v0.4 lets analysts go from a spreadsheet to a trustworthy report and a what-if scenario without writing YAML, and lets other applications call fitted models through stable endpoints. It is the first public launch, cut line A: anyone may sign up and run declarative specs and the built-in models on their own data; uploaded code stays with trusted tiers. To use it: the Guided tutorial, the Integrations hub, Tutorials.

docs.title: Guided mode: organised around tasks
docs.text:
One app, two modes over the same ModelSpec. A header toggle switches between Guided and Expert; every Guided screen has "View as YAML", and Expert edits round-trip back.

journey

    section Set up
      Choose "Geo marketing mix": 5: Analyst
      Upload a CSV, answer "which column is revenue?": 4: Analyst
      Enter beliefs as ROI ranges per channel: 4: Analyst
    section Run
      Watch plain-language progress, with an ETA: 5: Analyst
    section Decide
      Read the report and the sanity scorecard: 5: Analyst
      Drag what-if sliders, see bands update instantly: 5: Analyst
      Share a link or connect a spreadsheet: 4: Analyst
Shipped Where to read about it Four templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice) and a question flow with role detection Your first analysis in Guided mode Sandboxed ingest of CSV, Parquet, MFF and Meridian-shaped tables; the BayesInsight import and the mmm.bayesinsight model From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft, Import a BayesInsight model Business priors (ROI or share ranges) translated in a sandbox, lift tests as calibration Guided modelling The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate Guided mode, Integrations What-if sliders over per-draw response grids, "Run exact", forecast and counterfactual views What if… The persona lock: projects that stay Guided-only The persona lock

docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Self-service sign-up with e-mail verification, disposable-domain blocking, rate limits and Sybil flags for operators to review Sign-up and abuse controls Identity verification and cut line A at run admission Sign-up and abuse controls Tenant deletion that purges every store, and the GDPR export Deleting and exporting data A Cloud Armor policy on every load-balancer backend Security hardening

docs.title: The exit criteria
docs.text:
Criterion Where it stands Five non-technical testers go from upload to report to scenario unaided in under 30 minutes Prepared: an automated run takes 135 s of system time, six usability defects it found are fixed, and the protocol for the testers is written. The sessions themselves are still to run Atlas optimises against an endpoint Met on a laptop: +0.22 % revenue at the same budget against the live endpoint (details) Cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins Met for admission: sign-up workspaces are public, uploaded code is refused; public runs need an executor that enforces egress and DNS (docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs), which this laptop could not run

Everything was verified locally; see M3 verification for the numbers and for what still needs real people, Docker or Google Cloud.

docs.title: The local platform v0.2
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.2 (milestone M1)

The documents the platform accepts (ModelSpec, ScoreRequest), the error codes it returns and the executor protocol it drives were defined in v0.1. v0.2 puts an HTTP API, a job queue, a sandboxed runner, a local object store and the Expert web app around them, and runs it all on one machine. Start with the quickstart.

docs.title: What changed for you
docs.text:
Everything you do in a notebook is also an API call, and the work runs in a sandbox instead of your process:

In your process (v0.1) On the platform (v0.2) validate_spec(spec, catalog, schema) POST /v1/specs:validate, every problem at once with JSON pointers, and the editor's live squiggles fit_spec(spec, data, ...) POST /v1/runs with kind: fit; progress streamed as server-sent events score_bundle(bundle, request, data) POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score with Prefer: wait A bundle directory A model version in a registry, with lineage, metrics, a scorecard, plots and a signed manifest InprocExecutor local-process and docker executors behind the same protocol 
flowchart LR
    C["Web app · CLI ·<br/>Python client · curl"] -->|"/v1 JSON"| API["API<br/>(validates from static JSON)"]
    API --> Q[("PostgreSQL<br/>runs · queue · events")]
    Q --> D["Dispatcher"]
    D --> X["Executor<br/>(local process / Docker)"]
    X --> R["Runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    R -->|"outputs + manifest"| S[("GCS shim")]
    R -->|"signed events"| API

docs.title: Design commitments, kept
docs.text:
• The API never imports plugin code and never decodes your arrays. It validates specs and score requests from the exported catalog JSON and stored metadata. An import-linter contract keeps numpy, xarray and every plugin out of the server, and the server image build checks it against the installed packages.
  • Runs are idempotent and observable. Submissions carry idempotency keys; the executor's status is the source of truth; events drive progress bars, never liveness decisions.
  • Errors are RFC 7807 problems with the same stable codes you see in Python.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 describes every endpoint, and the generated clients are checked for drift in CI.
  • Outputs are verified. A run's outputs are checked against the object store's own checksums and generations, copied where runs cannot write, and signed.

docs.text:

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Each tutorial gets one thing working from start to finish, with the screens or the code you need. The code is not illustrative: every Python snippet runs in the test suite, and the Apps Scripts run against stand-ins for Google's services.

  • Your first MMM in Guided mode

    From a spreadsheet of weekly spend and revenue to ROI per channel, a sanity scorecard and a budget scenario, without code. About ten minutes.

    For analysts. Start

  • Connect Google Sheets

    An Apps Script that writes a model's forecast into a sheet, with its likely range, and refreshes it every morning.

    For analysts and integrators. Start

  • Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI

    A read-only, expiring link to a model's chart for a doc, a dashboard or a thread, and a PNG for tools that cannot show live content.

    For analysts. Start

  • Receive webhooks

    A FastAPI or Flask receiver that verifies every delivery's signature, ignores duplicates and reacts when a model is ready or a run fails.

    For developers. Start

  • Optimise a budget with Atlas

    Turn an endpoint into an Atlas model and let an optimiser split a fixed budget across channels, with batching, caching and back-off.

    For data scientists. Start

  • Import a BayesInsight model

    Bring a BayesInsight model_def.json and its MFF data: check the import, fit it on your laptop, then run it on the platform.

    For data scientists. Start

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A platform to talk to. Everything works against a local stack: make install && make dev && make seed (Quickstart). The Google Sheets and public-embed tutorials need a deployment that the internet can reach, since Apps Script and embedded charts are loaded from Google's and your viewers' machines.
  • A fitted model. The Guided tutorial makes one; make seed loads a demo marketing-mix spec you can fit from the web app.
  • An endpoint, for Sheets and Atlas: put a model live from the Guided Share step or the Integrations hub.

More task-oriented guides are under Guides; the ideas behind them are in Concepts; and Use cases shows which tutorials fit which problem.

docs.title: Import a BayesInsight model v0.4
docs.text:
A BayesInsight project is three files: model_def.json (the model), metadata.json (the keys of the data) and the data itself as an MFF long table. modeling-api imports them as a draft: an ingest mapping for the MFF table and a ModelSpec, plus a report of every feature that did not carry over exactly. Nothing is dropped silently.

In this tutorial you import a project, read the report, check the draft and fit it on your laptop - where you can see that it recovers the parameters the data was simulated with - and then run it on the platform. The code is docs/snippets/bayesinsight_import.py in the repository, which the test suite runs.

docs.title: The example project
docs.text:
The files come from mapi_plugin_mmm.bayesinsight_examples: 60 weeks of sales for two geographies (US, DE) × two products (Phones, Watches), driven by TV (delayed carry-over, Hill curve) and search (geometric carry-over, Hill curve), a price control with a negative sign, an annual season and Normal noise. The MFF table looks like this:

Period,Geography,Product,Outlet,Campaign,Creative,VariableName,VariableValue
2023-01-02,DE,Phones,Total,Total,Total,Price,8.904
2023-01-02,DE,Phones,Total,Total,Total,Sales,240.633
2023-01-02,DE,Phones,Total,Total,Total,Search,26.58
2023-01-02,DE,Phones,Total,Total,Total,TV,102.21

and model_def.json names its variables BayesInsight's way, TV_Total_Total_Total, with priors in the KPI's own units (a TV coefficient around 30 sales per unit of the curve).

docs.title: 1. Choose a target
docs.text: mmm.bayesinsight mmm.hierarchical_geo (default) What it fits BayesInsight's model as model_def.json defines it: likelihoods (Normal, log-normal, Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated), priors in KPI units, Hill/linear/S-shaped curves, delayed, geometric or Weibull carry-over, enforced signs, random effects per row id, seasons, local trends The platform's hierarchical geo MMM, with every BayesInsight feature that has an equivalent mapped onto it Panel dims Every row id besides Period is its own dim (geo, product) One geo dim; several row ids are joined (US|Phones) Priors Kept, in KPI units Coefficient priors are not carried over (they would mean something else on the mean-scaled KPI): state them as business priors instead Guided extras Lift tests (under the model's own likelihood) Business priors, lift tests, what-if grids Use it when You want BayesInsight's results, reproduced and served You want to move to the platform's geo MMM and its Guided tools

docs.title: 2. Import
docs.text:
The import is pure JSON in, JSON out, the same function the API runs, so you can call it offline:

from mapi_spec.bayesinsight import import_bayesinsight
from mapi_spec.guided import BayesInsightImport

request = BayesInsightImport(
    name="bi-sales",
    dataset="bi_mff",  # the dataset the MFF upload becomes
    target="mmm.bayesinsight",  # or "mmm.hierarchical_geo" (the default)
    model_def=json.loads(Path("model_def.json").read_text("utf-8")),
    metadata=json.loads(Path("metadata.json").read_text("utf-8")),
)
draft = import_bayesinsight(request, project="retail")  # pure JSON: no server, no numpy
for issue in draft.issues:
    print(f"{issue.severity.value:7} {issue.pointer}: {issue.message[:70]}…")
print(sorted(draft.mapping.dims), sorted(draft.mapping.vars))

info    /model_def/variable_details/2/adstock: Search_Total_Total_Total: BayesInsight's code cannot run 'geometric' c…
info    /model_def/variable_details/3/sign: Price_Total_Total_Total: the negative sign is enforced (BayesInsight d…
['date', 'geo', 'product'] ['price', 'sales', 'search', 'tv']

Each issue has a severity, a JSON pointer into your files and a message:

  • info: faithful but perhaps surprising. Here, geometric carry-over is fitted as documented although BayesInsight's own code cannot run it, and the price sign is enforced (BayesInsight declares signs without enforcing them).
  • warning: something fell back to BayesInsight's default or has no equivalent. Read every one before you fit.
  • error: the project cannot be imported (no single KPI, no media or control, names that do not match the row ids); the API answers 422 IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED.

The same project imported for the geo MMM warns about what does not carry over:

geo = import_bayesinsight(request.model_copy(update={"target": "mmm.hierarchical_geo"}),
                          project="retail")  # fmt: skip
for issue in geo.issues:
    if issue.severity.value == "warning":
        print(f"warning {issue.pointer}: {issue.message[:70]}…")

warning /model_def/variable_details: mmm.hierarchical_geo uses one adstock kind for every channel; 'geometr…
warning /model_def/variable_details/2/coeff_prior: media coefficient priors are in KPI units and are not carried over; st…
warning /model_def/variable_details/3/sign: Price_Total_Total_Total: sign constraints on controls have no equivale…

The full mapping table is in From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft.

docs.title: 3. Check the draft
docs.text:
Validate the spec against the installed catalog and the schema the mapping promises, as the API does when you save it:

from mapi_sdk.registry import default_registry
from mapi_spec.guided import draft_schema
from mapi_spec.spec import ModelSpec
from mapi_spec.validate import validate_spec

spec = ModelSpec.model_validate(draft.spec)
check = validate_spec(spec, default_registry().catalog(), draft_schema(draft.mapping))
print("valid" if check.ok else [(e.pointer, e.message) for e in check.errors])

valid

draft.yaml is the spec as YAML, the file you would review in a pull request: model.settings.model_def carries your model_def.json, variables maps each analytic name (TV_Total_Total_Total) to its variable, and a core.lag_tensor step with 12 lags feeds the carry-over.

docs.title: 4. Fit it on your laptop
docs.text:
Before you spend platform compute, fit the draft in-process with tiny settings. The dataset comes from the sandboxed ingest's own code applied to the MFF table:

from mapi_runner.jobs import IngestJob
from mapi_runner.worker.ingest import build_dataset
from mapi_sdk.harness import fit_spec

# the sandboxed ingest's own code: the MFF table through the draft's mapping
ds, schema, _ = build_dataset(Path("sales_mff.csv"), IngestJob(mapping=draft.mapping))
quick = spec.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_defaults=True)
quick["model"]["fit"] = {"mode": "evaluate_then_refit", "engine": "pymc",
                         "tune": 100, "draws": 100, "chains": 2, "seed": 1}  # fmt: skip
bundle = fit_spec(ModelSpec.model_validate(quick), ds, registry=default_registry(),
                  raw_schema=schema)  # fmt: skip
post = bundle.model.posterior.mean(("chain", "draw"))
print({v: round(float(post[f"{v}__coef"]), 1) for v in ("tv", "search", "price")})
print("holdout MAPE %:", round(bundle.metrics.values["mape"], 1))

{'tv': 25.9, 'search': 17.5, 'price': -7.6}
holdout MAPE %: 1.9

The data was simulated with coefficients of 30 (TV), 20 (search) and −8 (price): 100 draws on two chains, well under a minute on a laptop, land close, and the eight held-back weeks are forecast within 2%. Keep the draft's own fit settings (500 tuning steps and 500 draws on 4 chains) for results you act on.

docs.title: 5. Run it on the platform
docs.text:
The same import through the API (here with the Python client; the answer is the same draft):

remote = api.guided.import_bayesinsight(request)  # the same draft, from the platform
print(remote.dataset_ref, len(remote.issues), "issues")

Then upload the MFF table with the draft's mapping, save the spec and fit:

version = api.datasets.upload("sales_mff.csv", dataset="bi_mff", mapping=remote.mapping)
revision = api.specs.upsert(remote.yaml)
run = api.runs.wait(api.runs.fit(revision.spec_id, revision.revision).id,
                    raise_on_failure=True)
print(run.output_model_version_id)

The upload is checked in a sandbox with the bayesinsight preset: only the allowed_* key values and the start_period/end_period range of metadata.json are kept, and the necessary_variables must be present. With curl, the import is POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight (the guide).

The fitted version gets the same sanity scorecard as every model; promote it to an endpoint from the Integrations hub, and Atlas, Sheets and embeds work with it like with any other model.

docs.title: Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI v0.4
docs.text:
A chart from a fitted model belongs where decisions are made: the planning page in Notion, the weekly thread in Slack, the dashboard in Looker Studio or Power BI. An embed link shows one chart, read-only, to anyone who has the link, until it expires or you revoke it. Nobody needs an account, and the link can read nothing else.

This is what the link opens: the chart, its plain-language caption, a PNG fallback and the expiry date.

docs.title: What can be shared
docs.text:
Only charts the platform drew with one of its own recipes (core.*, mmm.*, ml.*, ts.*, choice.*): response curves, decompositions, forecast fans, scorecard charts and the like. A chart written by a plugin or by hand is refused (EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED), because a shared link runs the chart's specification in a stranger's browser, and only specifications the platform wrote are allowed to do that. Share those inside the project, or as a PNG.

A link points at one model version, so it never changes under your readers when the model is refitted: share the new version's chart when you want them to see it.

docs.title: 1. Create the link
docs.text:
In Guided modeIn the Integrations hubPythonCLI

On the last step, Share, choose Share a chart, pick the chart and create the link.

Integrations → Plots and links → Save a model plot (or Share in a model version's plot gallery): pick the model, the version and the chart. Then Create link on the saved plot. Optionally give it a label, an expiry (7 to 365 days, 30 by default) and the sites that may frame it.

saved = api.plots.save(
    "EU response curves (v3)",
    model_id="mdl_01jaf3c1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9n0",  # the model version that drew the plot
    version=3,
    plot_id="mmm.response_curves",  # one of its plots: a platform recipe
)
print(saved.id, "embeddable" if saved.embeddable else "not embeddable")

link = api.plots.create_embed(
    saved.id,
    label="Weekly marketing review",
    expires_in_days=90,
    allowed_origins=["https://lookerstudio.google.com"],  # leave out: any site may frame it
)
print(link.url)  # shown once: paste it into the tool now
iframe = (f'<iframe src="{link.url}" width="900" height="520" style="border:0" '
          f'loading="lazy" title="{saved.title}"></iframe>')  # fmt: skip

mapi plots embed plt_01jaf3n1p2q3r4s5t6v7w8x9y0 \
  --label "Weekly marketing review" --expires-in-days 90 \
  --allow-origin https://lookerstudio.google.com

The link and its <iframe> code are shown once: the platform keeps only a keyed hash of the token, like a password. Copy it now.

docs.title: 2. Put it where people look
docs.text:
Tool How Notes Notion Type /embed, paste the link Leave sites that may frame it empty unless you have checked which origin frames the embed (see below) Slack Paste the link in a message or a canvas Slack shows links, not live frames: readers click through to the chart. For an image in the thread, post the PNG (step 4) Looker Studio Insert → URL embed, paste the link Allow https://lookerstudio.google.com if you restrict sites Power BI On a dashboard, Add a tile → Web content, paste the <iframe> code Reports have no built-in web frame: use a custom visual that renders HTML, or the PNG Confluence, internal portals, any web page Paste the <iframe> code (in Confluence, through an iframe or HTML macro) Set width and height to fit the page Slides, PDFs, e-mail Use the PNG (step 4) These cannot show live content

Sites that may frame it. With a list of https:// origins, the embed page draws the chart only when the page that directly frames it is one of them, and shows This plot can only be shown on the sites it was shared with elsewhere. Opened directly, the link always works. Some tools frame embeds through an embedding service of their own; the origin the check sees is then that service's, so if the notice appears, add the origin your browser's developer tools show as the frame's parent, or create the link without a restriction.

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
Open the link in a private window: no sign-in, one chart. From Python, the same public view that the embed page reads, and the list of the plot's links with their view counts:

view = api.plots.embed(link.token)  # what the link shows, fetched without credentials
print(view.title, "| expires", view.expires_at.date(), "|", view.plot.provenance.recipe)
for embed in api.plots.embeds(saved.id):
    print(embed.display, embed.label, embed.status, embed.views, "views")

EU response curves (v3) | expires 2026-11-14 | mmm.response_curves@1.0.0
mpe_7k2m9q… Weekly marketing review active 0 views

The list never shows a token again, only its first characters (display).

docs.title: 4. A PNG, SVG or PDF instead
docs.text:
For slides, a PDF report or a Slack thread, render the chart to a file. Rendering is a small sandboxed run (the runner role), and the file is checked against its checksum when you download it:

render = api.plots.render(saved_plot_id=saved.id, format="png", width=1200, height=600)
png = api.plots.download_render(render, Path("eu-response-curves.png"))  # CRC32C-checked

In the hub, the Download buttons of a saved plot do the same; on the command line, mapi plots render --saved plt_… -f pdf -o chart.pdf. When you create a link with the runner role, a PNG is rendered too, and the embed page offers it as Open as PNG for tools that cannot show interactive content.

docs.title: 5. Revoke it
docs.text:
When the meeting is over, or the link went somewhere it should not:

api.plots.revoke_embed(saved.id, link.embed.id)  # dashboards showing it stop on next load

In the hub: Revoke in the plot's list of links; on the command line, mapi plots revoke <plot_id> <embed_id>. Every dashboard showing the link stops on its next load and says This link has expired or was revoked. Deleting the saved plot revokes all of its links; deleting the organisation revokes every link at once.

docs.title: What a viewer's browser can and cannot do
docs.text: The embed page is served from the plot sandbox's origin, not the app's. It sends no cookie or credential, its Content-Security-Policy lets it fetch the one public embed view and nothing else, the view is validated again in the browser, and every text is written as text. The view carries the chart's data inline (up to 1.5 MB), so the page never touches storage. Per-link and per-address rate limits stop a link from being scraped (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Connect Google Sheets for the numbers behind the chart.
  • Sharing plots: every option of saving, rendering and embedding, with curl.

docs.title: Connect Google Sheets v0.4
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial a Google Sheet holds your model's forecast, week by week, with the actual results it was fitted on and the range the future could fall in, and refreshes itself every morning. Nobody needs to open the platform, and the sheet never holds anything but a token that can score one endpoint.

You need Where to get it An endpoint serving a model that forecasts (a geo marketing mix or a weekly forecast) The Guided Share step, or Promote a model in the Integrations hub A platform the internet can reach Apps Script runs on Google's servers, so it cannot call a stack on 127.0.0.1. Use your team's deployment A Google account that may use Apps Script Any Google Workspace or personal account

docs.title: 1. Create a token that can only score this endpoint
docs.text:
In the web app, open Integrations: the Google Sheets card lists your endpoints. Pick yours and click Create a token: the Tokens page opens prefilled for a score:<alias> token, which can read and score that endpoint and nothing else.

Or from a terminal, with a rate limit and a monthly compute budget:

mapi tokens create sheets-forecast -s score:geo-mmm-prod --rate-limit 60 --budget 600

The secret is shown once. A sheet's script properties are visible to everyone who can edit the script, which is why the token should be able to do nothing but score this endpoint; revoke it at any time on the Tokens page (mapi tokens revoke).

docs.title: 2. Paste the generated script
docs.text:
In the sheet: Extensions → Apps Script. Replace the empty function with the code from the card (it is the endpoint's Apps Script snippet, also on its Snippets tab and from mapi endpoints snippets geo-mmm-prod -l apps_script). For an endpoint geo-mmm-prod it looks like this:

// Extensions > Apps Script. Store the token once under Project Settings >
// Script properties as MAPI_TOKEN.
//
// Input (optional): a sheet named "Input" in long format - a header row naming the
// endpoint's dims and input variables, then one row per coordinate - replaces the
// example's inline data. The answer's summary (mean and HDI per coordinate) is written
// to a sheet named "Result".
function scoreGeoMmmProd() {
  const token = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("MAPI_TOKEN");
  const payload = {
    "future_covariates": "carry_last",
    "horizon": {
      "dim": "time",
      "periods": 8
    },
    "mode": "forecast",
    "output": {
      "kind": "expected",
      "summary": [
        "mean",
        "hdi_90"
      ]
    }
  };
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  const input = book.getSheetByName("Input");
  if (input) {
    const key = payload.scenario && payload.scenario.data_vars ? "scenario" : "data";
    payload[key] = mapiSheetToXr_(input.getDataRange().getValues(), payload[key]);
  }
  const response = UrlFetchApp.fetch("https://api.mapi.example/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score", {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer " + token,
      "X-Mapi-Project": "acme/growth",
      Prefer: "wait=60",
    },
    payload: JSON.stringify(payload),
    muteHttpExceptions: true,
  });
  if (response.getResponseCode() >= 300) {
    throw new Error(response.getResponseCode() + ": " + response.getContentText());
  }
  const result = JSON.parse(response.getContentText());
  const out = book.getSheetByName("Result") || book.insertSheet("Result");
  out.clear();
  if (!result.done) {
    const note = "Still running (" + result.run.id + "): run the function again in a minute.";
    out.getRange(1, 1).setValue(note);
    return result;
  }
  const rows = mapiSummaryRows_(result.summary);
  if (!rows.length) {
    out.getRange(1, 1).setValue(result.run.state + ": no summary in the answer");
    return result;
  }
  const width = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.length));
  const grid = rows.map((r) => r.concat(new Array(width - r.length).fill("")));
  out.getRange(1, 1, grid.length, width).setValues(grid);
  return result;
}

// The summary tables one below the other: a header row ("variable", the coordinate
// columns, the statistics), one row per coordinate, a blank row between tables.
function mapiSummaryRows_(summary) {
  const rows = [];
  for (const table of (summary && summary.tables) || []) {
    if (rows.length) rows.push([""]);
    rows.push(["variable"].concat(table.columns));
    for (const row of table.rows) {
      rows.push([table.variable].concat(row.map((c) => (c === null ? "" : c))));
    }
  }
  if (summary && summary.truncated) {
    rows.push(["(truncated: the full result is in the run's outputs)"]);
  }
  return rows;
}

// A long table (a header row, then rows) as an inline dataset shaped like the example's:
// columns named like its dims hold coordinates, columns named like its variables hold
// values; empty cells become null.
function mapiSheetToXr_(values, example) {
  if (!example || !example.data_vars) {
    throw new Error("this endpoint's example call sends no inline data to replace");
  }
  const header = values[0].map(String);
  const rows = values.slice(1).filter((r) => r.some((c) => c !== ""));
  const column = (name) => {
    const i = header.indexOf(name);
    if (i < 0) throw new Error('the Input sheet needs a column named "' + name + '"');
    return i;
  };
  const cell = (v) =>
    v instanceof Date ? Utilities.formatDate(v, Session.getScriptTimeZone(), "yyyy-MM-dd") : v;
  const coords = {};
  const index = {};
  for (const spec of Object.values(example.data_vars)) {
    for (const dim of spec.dims) {
      if (index[dim]) continue;
      const i = column(dim);
      index[dim] = new Map();
      const seen = [];
      for (const r of rows) {
        const key = cell(r[i]);
        if (!index[dim].has(key)) {
          index[dim].set(key, seen.length);
          seen.push(key);
        }
      }
      coords[dim] = { dims: [dim], data: seen };
    }
  }
  const data_vars = {};
  for (const [name, spec] of Object.entries(example.data_vars)) {
    const i = column(name);
    const value = (r) => (r[i] === "" ? null : r[i]);
    if (!spec.dims.length) {
      data_vars[name] = { dims: [], data: rows.length ? value(rows[0]) : null };
      continue;
    }
    const last = spec.dims.length - 1;
    const empty = (k) => coords[spec.dims[k]].data.map(() => (k < last ? empty(k + 1) : null));
    const data = empty(0);
    for (const r of rows) {
      const at = spec.dims.map((dim) => index[dim].get(cell(r[column(dim)])));
      let node = data;
      for (let k = 0; k < at.length - 1; k++) node = node[at[k]];
      node[at[at.length - 1]] = value(r);
    }
    data_vars[name] = { dims: spec.dims, data: data };
  }
  return { coords: coords, data_vars: data_vars };
}

Then Project Settings → Script properties → Add script property: name MAPI_TOKEN, value the token from step 1. Back in the editor, choose the function and press Run. The first run asks you to authorise the script to connect to an external service and to edit your spreadsheets.

A sheet called Result now holds the answer: the platform ran the endpoint's example call (here an 8-week forecast) in a sandbox and returned the requested summary inline, one table per output variable. Each table has a header row (variable, the coordinate columns such as geo and time, then mean, hdi_90_lower and hdi_90_upper) and one row per coordinate. The payload is the endpoint's own example, generated from its input contract, so it is valid as it stands. If the run takes longer than the minute the script waits, Result says Still running; run the function again to collect it.

To send your own data instead of the example's, add a sheet called Input in long format: a header row naming the endpoint's dims and input variables, then one row per coordinate. The script reads it into the call when the example sends inline data; an endpoint whose example call sends none (a plain forecast) refuses an Input sheet.

The summary is per coordinate, per market and week here. The next step writes a different table: the history the model was fitted on next to the forecast's range, summed over markets.

docs.title: 3. Write the forecast into a table
docs.text:
A forecast run also writes a small JSON table for Guided mode, ui/guided/forecast.json: the history the model was fitted on, then the forecast's quantiles per period. This script fetches it and writes it into a sheet called Forecast. Replace the code with it, and set MAPI_URL, MAPI_PROJECT, ENDPOINT and CALL (the payload of the generated script):

// A forecast from a modeling-api endpoint, written into the sheet "Forecast": the weeks the
// model was fitted on (with your actual results), then the forecast with its likely range.
// Extensions > Apps Script: paste this file. Project Settings > Script properties: add
// MAPI_TOKEN (a token that can only score this endpoint).
const MAPI_URL = "https://api.mapi.example"; // your platform's API address
const MAPI_PROJECT = "acme/growth"; // <tenant>/<project>
const ENDPOINT = "geo-mmm-prod";
// The call: the "payload" of the hub's Apps Script snippet for your endpoint.
const CALL = {
  mode: "forecast",
  horizon: { dim: "time", periods: 8 },
  future_covariates: "carry_last",
  output: { kind: "expected", summary: ["mean", "hdi_90"] },
};

function refreshForecast() {
  const token = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("MAPI_TOKEN");
  // One score run per day: running this again the same day collects that run's result
  // instead of starting another (the platform remembers an Idempotency-Key for 24 hours).
  const day = Utilities.formatDate(new Date(), "UTC", "yyyy-MM-dd");
  const response = UrlFetchApp.fetch(`${MAPI_URL}/v1/endpoints/${ENDPOINT}/score`, {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer " + token,
      "X-Mapi-Project": MAPI_PROJECT,
      Prefer: "wait=30",
      "Idempotency-Key": `sheets-${ENDPOINT}-${day}`,
    },
    payload: JSON.stringify(CALL),
    muteHttpExceptions: true,
  });
  if (response.getResponseCode() >= 300 && response.getResponseCode() !== 202) {
    throw new Error(response.getResponseCode() + ": " + response.getContentText());
  }
  const result = JSON.parse(response.getContentText());
  const sheet = forecastSheet();
  if (!result.done) {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue(`Still running (${result.run.state}): run this again in a minute.`);
    return;
  }
  if (result.run.state !== "succeeded") {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue(`The forecast failed: ${result.run.state}. See run ${result.run.id}.`);
    return;
  }
  const link = result.outputs.find((o) => o.name === "ui/guided/forecast.json");
  if (!link) {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue("This endpoint's model wrote no forecast table.");
    return;
  }
  // A short-lived signed link: fetch it now, never store it. It needs no token.
  const view = JSON.parse(UrlFetchApp.fetch(link.url).getContentText());
  const fan = view.fan;
  const header = [fan.dim, `Actual ${view.kpi}`].concat(
    fan.quantiles.map((q) => (q === 0.5 ? "Median" : `${Math.round(q * 100)}%`)),
  );
  const rows = fan.coords.map((coord, j) =>
    [coord, cell(fan.observed && fan.observed[j])].concat(fan.values.map((row) => cell(row[j]))),
  );
  sheet.getRange(1, 1, 1, header.length).setValues([header]);
  sheet.getRange(2, 1, rows.length, header.length).setValues(rows);
  const units = view.units ? ` (${view.units})` : "";
  sheet
    .getRange(rows.length + 3, 1, 1, 2)
    .setValues([[`Forecast from ${view.split_at}`, `${view.kind} ${view.kpi}${units}`]]);
}

// An empty cell for a missing value (no actuals after the split, no forecast before it).
function cell(value) {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : value;
}

function forecastSheet() {
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  const sheet = book.getSheetByName("Forecast") || book.insertSheet("Forecast");
  sheet.clearContents();
  return sheet;
}

Run refreshForecast. The Forecast sheet then looks like this (the numbers depend on your model):

time Actual revenue 5% 25% Median 75% 95% 2026-09-27 101.5 2026-10-04 98.2 2026-10-11 104.9 2026-10-18 88.0 96.3 101.2 106.4 114.9 2026-10-25 85.1 94.0 99.8 105.2 115.3 Forecast from 2026-10-18 expected revenue (kEUR)

How to read it: in 90% of plausible futures the week of 18 October lands between the 5% and 95% columns; half of them land between 25% and 75%. The KPI is summed over the model's other dims (markets, stores) per posterior draw before the quantiles are taken, which is why these ranges are honest totals and not sums of per-market ranges. Chart the table with Insert → Chart (a line for the median and the actuals, an area between 5% and 95%).

What the script does, and why:

  • One run per day. It sends an Idempotency-Key made of the endpoint and the date. The platform remembers a key for 24 hours, so running the script again the same day returns the same run instead of starting (and paying for) another one. Change CALL and you get a 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT until the next day; rename the key to start over.
  • Still running? Prefer: wait=30 waits up to 30 seconds. A cold start in the cloud can take longer; the sheet then says Still running, and the next run of the script collects the result.
  • Short-lived links. The result's links are signed URLs that expire after 15 minutes. The script fetches the table at once and never stores the link; the link needs no token.

docs.title: 4. Refresh it every morning
docs.text: In the Apps Script editor: Triggers (the clock icon) → Add Trigger → function refreshForecast, event source Time-driven, Day timer, a time of day. Each morning the sheet is cleared and refilled with a fresh forecast from whatever version the endpoint serves that day, so promoting a better model updates the sheet without touching it.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What the sheet or the editor shows Why What to do 401: … No token, or a revoked or expired one Check the MAPI_TOKEN script property; create a new token 403: … The token's scope is not score:<this alias> (or the project header is wrong) Create the token from the Sheets card, check MAPI_PROJECT 404: … The endpoint was deleted or renamed Pick the endpoint again in the Sheets card 409: … with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT CALL changed since the day's first run, under the same key Wait for tomorrow, or change the key's prefix 422: … with MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, or 409: … with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT The call asks for something the model cannot answer: future values it does not have, or more periods than it may forecast Copy the payload from the endpoint's snippet again; shorten the horizon 429: … with RATE_LIMITED or QUOTA_EXCEEDED The token's rate limit, its budget or a project quota Raise the limit or budget on the Tokens page, or refresh less often This endpoint's model wrote no forecast table. The call is not a forecast, or the model's outputs have no KPI to tabulate Use a forecast call; for other outputs, read the result with the Python client
